author: pdarleyjr
body:
## What changes for members

**Home greeting.** Home now reads "Good afternoon, <first name>", "Today is <date> · <verified shift>" and "300 is <rank name>". It uses the 08:00 to 08:00 duty date and refreshes while the page is open. When the roster cannot confirm something, it says so instead of guessing. It only displays: it changes no access, and `card_display_enabled` still turns it off.

**Training Crew Planner.** The manual PDF upload is gone. The planner reads the emailed TeleStaff roster, and the steps are Class, Personnel, Sessions (optional), Review, Publish.
- Simple lists, or several sessions at a station or a custom venue
- Other duty dates, and provisional lists when no roster exists yet
- A warning when the roster changes under a plan
- Drafts saved encrypted in the database for 7 days after the last edit
- Branded PDF and XLSX exports

**One-action publish.** A plan goes to any mix of the 300 card, the Captain 5 card and Department Updates.
- Each destination's existing rule is checked on the server for every send
- Each version of a plan goes to each destination once
- Status is shown per destination, as Sent, Failed or Retry
- Department-wide notices name confirmed members only and count anyone unconfirmed

**Tables.** Operational tables no longer scroll sideways. They use a shared adapter (table, priority columns, then cards), with hidden values in a details panel and 44px row targets on touch. Operational forms use their own container-query cards.

**Fixes found on the way**
- A unit with no designation would have stopped the service ticket list rendering. No production unit is in that state today.
- The phone command bar on operational forms is back to 48px; it had been overridden down to 40px.

## Decisions to review
- **The PDF has employee IDs and is attached to 300 and Captain 5 cards.** Those cards are private. It is never attached to Department Updates.
- **The acting override in the brief no longer applies.** PR 552 retired acting, so the roster alone decides 300.

## Technical notes
- One additive migration: `training_crew_plan_drafts` and `training_crew_plan_publications`.
- No permission grants in migrations, and no worker or manifest changes.
- Removed the PDF upload route, controller and parser, plus their tests, after proving nothing else used them. Poppler stays in the Dockerfile and CI.
- New required gate `ui-browser-suites` runs the responsive tables and Home duty browser suites. A new step in the existing Operational Forms job checks form table widths.

## Test plan
Local results, on this branch unless noted:
- [x] Node `tests/Node/*.test.mjs`: 785/785 before the last main merge, rerun after it
- [x] PHPStan and Pint clean
- [x] Targeted PHPUnit (Training, Home, service tickets): 299/300; the one error is the local `openssl_pkey_export` problem in `HomeQuickActionsTest`
- [x] Service ticket regression test fails without the fix and passes with it
- [x] Vite build, service worker drift check and PWA worker core tests
- [x] Gitleaks on the branch commits: no leaks
- [x] Browser suites, on their own branches before the final merge: Crew Planner 27/27, Home duty 16/16, responsive tables 137/138 with the one failure passing on re-run (hub-support-tickets at 390, cold render)
- [ ] Hosted gates
- [ ] Production checks after deploy

Not covered: the Operational Forms document-history table was not browser-tested, because the fixture cannot create those records. The Ollama proxy Node test in `tests/Node/security` fails locally because `scripts/operations/ollama-ai-proxy.py` is not in main either.

author: pmark
body:
## Problem

At 2026-11-02T00:56:42Z the worker's own launch preflight refused a repair-resume of `arcadia/assert-tmux-temp-launcher-removed` with `session_environment_wall` ("preservation route heartbeat ... is stale (33s old, limit 15s)"). It escalated `environment_wall`, and with concurrency 1 the run stalled. The refusal log shows the same refusal on every later tick.

**Root cause:** `preservation.heartbeat` was re-stamped by a 5s `setInterval` on the worker's own event loop (`src/commands/worker.ts:1025-1035`) and by `heartbeat()` calls between per-Project tick steps (`src/commands/worker.ts:1199-1206`). Launch preparation (`buildLaunchPreview`) is synchronous inside the tick, and it blocked that loop for about 33s before `assertWorkerCapability` (`src/sessions/launch.ts:425`) checked the heartbeat against the fixed 15s limit (`src/sessions/transportHeartbeat.ts:21`, plus the 15s preflight grace). The worker was walling itself. The 25-35s ages seen live were tick-step durations, not the writer's interval.

## Fix (adaptive)

1. **The writer gets its own timer.** The existing out-of-process heartbeat beacon (#617) now also re-stamps `preservation.heartbeat` `at` every interval. Routes and `goRequestsAt` stay untouched, so go readiness still needs a real go pass. The beacon never revives a heartbeat older than itself.
2. **Self-describing heartbeat.** Writers record `intervalMs`, and readers judge staleness by `max(3 × intervalMs, 15s floor)`. A heartbeat without `intervalMs` (an older writer) is judged with a conservative 20s legacy interval, which gives a 60s limit. Changing the cadence needs no change to the probe. The fixed 15s `LAUNCH_PREFLIGHT_JITTER_MS` grace is removed.
3. **Recheck before escalating.** A stale reading that is still within limit + 60s is marked `transient`. The tick records a retryable `session_environment_transient` refusal, with no escalation and no repair attempt, and rechecks on the next ticks. It does not sleep inside the synchronous tick, because that would starve other Actions and the in-process writer. It escalates `environment_wall` only if the reading stays stale for the whole 60s window. A missing heartbeat, or one older than limit + 60s (a dead writer), escalates on the first reading as before.

## Live state (read-only)

- `production_operator_escalations` has `environment_wall` for the Action, and `production_launch_refusal_log` still advances every tick.
- The row is not a hold. On a passing probe, `attemptProjectLaunch` calls `clearOperatorEscalation` and `clearLaunchRefusal` and resumes the `incomplete_resumable` candidate, and no repair attempts were counted.
- The installed runtime keeps blocking itself on each attempt, so nothing clears until this fix ships through the governed protected-release reinstall. No DB edit is needed.

## Tests (written to fail first; 10 failed on base)

- `tests/worker-tick.test.ts`:
  - the beacon keeps the preservation heartbeat fresh while the caller's loop is blocked 10× the interval;
  - the beacon never revives a leftover heartbeat.
- `tests/preservation-heartbeat-freshness.test.ts`:
  - `intervalMs` is published and the limit follows 3× it with the floor;
  - a 30s-interval writer at 33s is not refused;
  - the legacy fallback gives 60s, never 15s;
  - a reading at 33s is transient, and limit + 60s is a durable wall;
  - a missing heartbeat is never transient.
- `tests/production-tick.test.ts`, for both the tick preflight and the launch-side preflight:
  - one transient reading is retried, then launches with no escalation;
  - a reading that stays stale through the window escalates;
  - a durable wall escalates on the first reading.

## Validation

- Focused suites (freshness, production-tick, session-launch, managed-production-policy, session-probe-wall, go-broker-agent-setup, protected-worker-startup, blocker-remedies): 401/401 pass.
- Beacon tests in `worker-tick` pass.
- 14 other `worker-tick` tests fail in the agent sandbox only, before and after this change: `tmux list-panes` gets "Operation not permitted" on the tmux socket, which breaks the Session-ancestry check.
- `tsc --noEmit` and eslint on the changed files are clean.

## Operator QA

1. After the reviewed protected-release reinstall, run `watch -n2 'node -e "const h=require(\"<workspace>/.arcadia/preservation.heartbeat\");console.log(Date.now()-h.at,h.intervalMs)"'` during a long tick. Ages should stay under about 10s and `intervalMs` should be 5000.
2. `sqlite3 "file:<workspace>/database/arcadia.sqlite3?mode=ro" "select kind from production_operator_escalations where action_key='arcadia/assert-tmux-temp-launcher-removed'"` should return no row after the next successful launch.

Reachability: worker runtime only. Nothing is live until the protected release is reinstalled through its governed `/runs` action. Production, launchd and the queue were not touched.

author: panevain
body:
## What and why

A pass over the repo's tooling (mise configs, workflows, composite actions, scripts, Dockerfile, dotfiles) to remove duplication and dead code, followed by fixes from a code review of that pass. No check is added or removed, and no job is renamed, so the rulesets are unaffected.

**Duplication**
- `build:sizes` is gone. `mise run build:budget --brotli` adds the brotli -q 11 sizes to the budget table (`scripts/check-wasm-size.py`). The brotli sizes are still reported on pushes only, and any budget failure is printed before the brotli pass starts. The task passes its arguments through to the script (`--dist`, `--summary`, `--brotli`).
- `scripts/wasm-size-report.sh` reads the wasm-opt level and feature flags from `web/index.html`, even when the link's attributes span several lines. It reads them before the fat-LTO build, and needs them only when wasm-opt is found.
- `scripts/wait-healthz.sh CONTAINER CONTAINER_PORT` replaces the three copies of the `/healthz` wait loop and the host-port lookup in the smoke tests. It prints the host port and gives up after 30 s.
- `prune-images.yml`'s inline script moves to `scripts/prune-images.sh`. The script rejects any argument other than `--dry-run`. It is excluded from `release-plan.py`'s shipped changes and from the Docker build context, as it was while it lived in `.github/`. The job checks out the default branch (`contents: read`), and the reason on the zizmor ignore is updated to match.

**Client tests**
- The client's 11 unit tests (`coverage`, `net`, `regions`, `state`, `ui::regions`) are in its binary, so the old `lib.rs` condition never ran them in CI. They build and pass natively with no extra system packages, so `mise run test` (CI's `test` job) now runs nextest over the whole workspace. CI's unused Bevy apt step is removed.

**Dead code**
- Dockerfile: dropped `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`, because `rustup toolchain install` already installs `rust-toolchain.toml`'s targets.
- The hidden `serve:release` alias is removed. `serve --release` replaced it this cycle, and no stable release had it (it was in the `0.1.0-dev` pre-releases). The CHANGELOG says it is removed.
- Removed `ci-git.sh fetch`, the `smoke` script in `tests/browser/package.json` and the root `/node_modules` in `.gitignore`; none of them was used.
- `check-design-tokens.sh` fails when `theme.rs` is missing, instead of passing after checking nothing.

**Config hygiene**
- `.gitattributes`: `mise.ci.lock`, `supply-chain/imports.lock` and `tests/browser/package-lock.json` are marked generated, `*.ttf` is marked binary, and the lines for the gitignored `dist/` and `target/` are dropped. `git add --renormalize .` changes nothing.
- `.dockerignore` gains `.mise.*.local.toml`, which `.gitignore` already has.
- Comment wrapping is fixed in `mise.toml`, `pins.yml`, `bump-pins.py` and `check-toolchain-sync.sh`; `docs/design.md` is updated.

## Checks

- [ ] `mise run check` passes. mise couldn't be installed in the authoring environment, so CI is the full run. Run instead:
  - `cargo test --locked --workspace` passes natively, including the client's 11 tests.
  - `scripts/check-toolchain-sync.sh` and `scripts/check-design-tokens.sh` pass, and `bash -n` passes on every script.
  - The changed scripts were tested against fixtures or stubs:
    - `check-wasm-size.py`: with and without `--brotli`, with and without a module that has no budget.
    - `wait-healthz.sh`: ready, exited early, the 30 s deadline, and no published port.
    - `prune-images.sh`: which tags are kept and deleted, the DELETE URLs, `--dry-run`, and rejection of unknown arguments.
    - `wasm-size-report.sh`: reading the attributes, including from multi-line HTML.
- [x] Docs and `CHANGELOG.md` updated
- [x] No new environment variables

body:
Closes #164

## What changed

- `terraform/bootstrap/README.md`, line 106: the `source_profile` value of the agent's example plan profile, which held a real twelve-digit AWS account id in the `<id>_SecurityAudit` form the Identity Center CLI gives a profile, is now the placeholder `<management account id>_SecurityAudit`. The `role_arn` line above it already used `<heat-dev account id>`, and line 50 of the same README names that account "the management account id", so the placeholder matches both.

Nothing else changed. One file, one line.

## Why

`docs/standards/terraform.md` rule 4 and `docs/README.md` rule 9 allow no account id in a committed file (decision 0020). The id had been in the file since Issue-36's commit 4dd2170 and was the one `blocks` finding of the first checkup run (decision 0033, third layer; Issue-164).

## Verified

- `grep -E '[0-9]{12}' terraform/bootstrap/README.md` on the branch prints nothing; before the change it printed the one line.
- The diff is the one line, read in the session. The branch is `main` at 6e47500 plus this commit.
- Neither the commit message, this description nor the issue states the id.

## Not verified

- Nothing runs on this change: the file is a README, so "Build and test" and the sandbox apply confirm only that the branch is `main` plus a document.

## The id stays in git history

The id remains in every commit from 4dd2170 to this pull request's base, and the repository is private today. Removing it from history means rewriting `main`, which the `main` ruleset refuses (no force pushes), so it is a decision for the owner, not a change in this pull request. The options, for when the owner decides: leave it, since an account id is not a secret and the repository is private; or rewrite history before any move to public, which would need the ruleset relaxed for the rewrite and every worktree re-cloned.

## Before the merge

- [ ] The review skill's session has run on this pull request (code-changes rule 23).
- [ ] The owner has decided whether the id in history needs attention, or left it as is.

body:
## Summary

The Research Home was a menu of links and a freshness list with no data on it. "More useful" here means: the user's goal on Home is *find something → build a Fund Basket → open the report*, so Home now puts the data that decision needs on the page, with the primary action (Add to basket) on every fund, and folds the plumbing (dataset freshness) behind progressive disclosure.

```diff
 <Index> (/Research)
   <_ResearchNav home>
   hero: title, lead, <_ResearchSearch>, starters
   first-visit steps strip
-  Explore cards: Sectors / World / Funds / Risk
-  Your basket card (chips, starting mixes, Open basket report)
-  Data freshness list (always open)
+  .research-home__workbench            (container query: 2 columns from 50rem)
+    Tracked funds card                 (FundCompareRows.Build, window = 3Y)
+      per role: rowgroup heading
+        fund link + name | return a year | volatility | fee | [Add / In basket]
+      links: Compare all funds · Risk vs return · Correlation · Holdings
+      Unavailable State + Retry when the funds dataset is missing
+    rail
+      Your basket card                 (mixes filtered server-side: data-research-home-mixes-checked)
+      Market backdrop card             (ResearchMarketBackdrop: Fed funds, 3-month T-bill, 12-month inflation)
+      Explore card: Sectors · World · Company lookup   (Company had no link from Home)
+  <details> About this data           (summary shows "N datasets not loaded yet")
   advice line, live region
```

Read path: Home now reads status + funds + fund returns + fund facts + macro in parallel through `IResearchSnapshotCache`; each dataset that cannot be read leaves only its part unavailable (`docs/DIAGRAMS.md` updated).

```text
ResearchController.Index
  ReadAsync × 5 (status, funds, fund returns, fund facts, macro)   // 503/exception → null
  ResearchHomeViewModel(localizer, status, funds, returns, facts, macro)
    FundCompareRows.Build(funds, returns, facts, 3)   // extracted from ResearchFundsPageViewModel
    group by Role (configured order, no role last)
    Presets = mixes whose funds are all tracked (PresetsChecked)
    ResearchMarketBackdrop.From(macro)
```

Responsive thresholds are rem container queries, not pixel media queries: the funds card hides the volatility column under 30rem and stacks each row with its `data-label` headings under 24rem (no sideways table scroll on a phone).

Assumptions kept visible: the funds note says which month the returns run to (or that returns are not loaded), fees show "not filed" when the fund has none, the backdrop shows each figure's month and the inflation definition, and the disclaimer stays.

## Evidence

- **Before / After screenshots** (desktop dark and light, empty and filled basket, phone, ApiService down): https://claude.ai/artifact/8JzzWyCHV3rSdGS8CKYssf
  Checked in the browser pane on the InMemory provider with the E2E fixtures: Add → "In basket" and the nav count update live; partial data ("not filed" fee, "Not loaded yet" backdrop); API stopped → Unavailable State with Retry and "8 datasets not loaded yet"; 375px stacked rows; keyboard order search → starters → Got it → fund links → Add buttons with visible focus; `<details>` opens by keyboard; light and dark both read.
- `dotnet test PersonalFinance.sln`: **3308 passed, 1 failed**. `ResearchPage_InVietnamese_ShowsNoEnglishChrome(/Research)` fails only on the three new strings that have no vi translation yet; it passes once the i18n Translate workflow pushes its commit to this PR (same as #613).
- `dotnet build -c Release -p:EnforceWarningsAsErrors=true`: succeeded, 0 warnings.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors (7 pre-existing `sidebar.js` warnings).
- New `ResearchHomePageTests` (9): grouping by role with the 3Y figures, missing returns/facts, missing funds → Unavailable with Retry on Index, preset filtering, backdrop maths (latest month per series, CPI 12 months earlier) and emptiness, not-loaded count, view shape.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Web-only change; no schema, no API contract change. Revert restores the old Home.

**Blast Radius:** Research Home

Home now issues four more cached API reads per page view (10-minute snapshot cache, failures never kept). Five unused `Research.Home.*` i18n keys were removed from en/vi/lock. The E2E walkthrough's `research-home-search` id and the basket toggle contract are unchanged.

author: ramezgerges
body:
**GitHub Issue:** closes #25478

## PR Type:

🐞 Bugfix

## What changed? 🚀

Navigating away from a page whose `ScrollViewer` had been scrolled left parts of the old page on screen, at their scrolled positions. A full repaint (resize) cleared them.

Partial repaint only redraws the reported damage. A stable subtree (enough visuals, unchanged for enough frames) is recorded once into a cached children picture. Scrolling moves that subtree without changing it, so `RenderChildrenStep` replays the cached picture under the new matrix and doesn't walk its descendants. Their `_lastRenderBounds` therefore stay at the pre-scroll positions. The subtree root keeps `_childrenContentDamageRect` up to date on every moved replay, but `ContributeRemovalDamage` only damaged each visual's own `_lastRenderBounds`. Removing the page repainted the stale positions and never the area its content actually occupied.

`ContributeRemovalDamage` now also damages:
- `_childrenContentDamageRect`, the area a collapsed subtree was last replayed at;
- `_shadowFallbackDamageRect`, the cached shadow recording's area, which is replayed the same way.

Like `_lastRenderBounds`, both flags are cleared once reported, so a visual inserted elsewhere later starts with no stale rects. The descendants' stale bounds are still damaged as before, which is harmless over-damage.

Not covered: a collapsed subtree whose root is an **ancestor** of the removed visual, moved without being re-walked. Scrolling invalidates the pictures above the scrolled content, so the reported scenario doesn't go through that path.

### Validation

- New runtime test `Given_Visual_Damage.When_Scrolled_Collapsed_Subtree_Is_Removed_Then_Its_Current_Area_Is_Damaged`. It builds root → page → scroller → content (enough visuals to collapse), lets the content collapse, scrolls the scroller by 100px, then removes the page and checks the damage covers the content's current position.
  - On `master` it fails: the removal damage only covers the pre-scroll positions (around y = 1 and y = 11).
  - With the fix it passes.
- `Given_Visual_Damage` and `Given_CompositionTarget` on Skia desktop (Win32): 30 passed, 0 failed, 1 inconclusive (WebGPU-only), 1 skipped (minimized-window case).
- Not run: the Wayfarer app from the issue against this build.

## PR Checklist ✅

- [x] 🧪 Added [Runtime tests, UI tests, or a manual test sample](https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/blob/master/doc/articles/uno-development/working-with-the-samples-apps.md) (for bug fixes / features, if applicable)

- [x] ❗ Contains **NO** breaking changes
- [ ] 👀 Reviewed 2 other [open pull requests](https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/pulls) (optional but appreciated!)

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change | OpenSSF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [express](https://expressjs.com/) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express)) | dependencies | minor | [`5.2.1` → `5.3.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/express/5.2.1/5.3.0) | [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/expressjs/express/badge)](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/expressjs/express) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>expressjs/express (express)</summary>

### [`v5.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/blob/HEAD/History.md#530)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/compare/v5.2.1...v5.3.0)

\=====

#### 🐞 Bug fixes

- Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by [@​YuryShkoda](https://redirect.github.com/YuryShkoda) in [#​4893](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/4893)

  Fixed the behavior of `res.send()` to prevent conflicts between `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` HTTP headers in responses. The `Content-Length` header in `res.send()` is now only added when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a `Transfer-Encoding` header - by [@​cuishuang](https://redirect.github.com/cuishuang) in [#​7459](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7459)

* Upgrade `qs` to `^6.16.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-2391](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-2391) ([GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883](https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/security/advisories/GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883)), [CVE-2026-82417](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82417) ([GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g)) and [CVE-2026-82562](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82562) ([GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx)): `arrayLimit` bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled `isBuffer` - by [@​davetashner](https://redirect.github.com/davetashner) in [#​7057](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7057) and [#​7478](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7478), and [@​cyphercodes](https://redirect.github.com/cyphercodes) in [#​7305](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7305)

* Upgrade `proxy-addr` to `^2.0.8`, which fixes [CVE-2026-90711](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-90711) - by [@​lazerg](https://redirect.github.com/lazerg) in [#​7474](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7474)

#### 🚀 Improvements

- Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. `req.fresh` previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by [@​Cherry](https://redirect.github.com/Cherry) in [#​7366](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7366)

  ```js
  // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
  app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
    res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
    res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
  });
  ```

- Improve HTML structure in `res.redirect()` responses when HTML format is accepted by adding `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<title>`, and `<body>` tags for better browser compatibility - by [@​Bernice55231](https://redirect.github.com/Bernice55231) in [#​5167](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/5167)

- When calling `app.render` with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by [AkaHarshit](https://redirect.github.com/AkaHarshit) in [#​6903](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6903)

  ```js
  app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected
  ```

- Upgrade `content-type` to `^2.0.0`, bringing a faster parser (\~1.5x quicker `Content-Type` parsing/formatting in `res.send()`) along with a behavior change: `res.send()` now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a `Content-Type` that fails to parse. `type-is` is upgraded to `^2.1.0` as part of the same change - by [@​blakeembrey](https://redirect.github.com/blakeembrey) in [#​7234](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7234)

  ```js
  res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
  // -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8
  ```

- The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as `Error.cause` and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's `parent`/`original`) are no longer swallowed - by [@​Nitin-Mohapatra](https://redirect.github.com/Nitin-Mohapatra) in [#​6464](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6464)

- Upgrade `content-disposition` to `^2.0.1`, which changes the `Content-Disposition` header emitted by `res.download()`, `res.attachment()`, and `res.sendFile()`: file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by [@​blakeembrey](https://redirect.github.com/blakeembrey) in [#​7233](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7233)

  ```js
  res.attachment('user.html');
  // before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
  // after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html
  ```

- Upgrade `body-parser` to `^2.3.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-12590](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12590) ([GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/body-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6)): an invalid `limit` option value caused request body size enforcement to be silently disabled (fail-open), allowing a denial of service via arbitrarily large payloads. Invalid `limit` values now throw at parser initialization instead of being ignored - by [@​Mayvis](https://redirect.github.com/Mayvis) in [#​7390](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7390)

#### ⚡ Performance

- Avoid duplicate Content-Type header processing in `res.send()` when sending string responses without an explicit Content-Type header - by [@​bjohansebas](https://redirect.github.com/bjohansebas) in [#​6991](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6991)

</details>

author: seanlin2000
body:
## Summary

The MCP server that every tool package registers on lived in `web_search_mcp/server.py`, so web search looked like the server and the other seven packages looked like add-ons to it. This moves the server into its own package, `assistant_mcp`, and turns `web_search_mcp` into a tool package like the others, with a `register_web_search_tools` function. The server's own settings (host, port, Host allow-list) move with it and are now read from `ASSISTANT_MCP_*` environment variables; the command is `assistant-mcp`. No tool changes: the same 22 tools (23 with home coordinates), the same names, descriptions, and output.

## The tool server package

- `assistant_mcp/server.py:36-76` (`build_server`) **One server, every package.** It still builds the search client, the page reader, and the benchmark fixtures, because `reddit_search` shares the search client with web search, then calls each package's register function, web search included, and adds the `/healthz` route.
- `assistant_mcp/settings.py:6-9` (`ToolServerSettings`) **The server's own settings.** Host, port, and the Host allow-list leave `SearchSettings`, since they describe the server, not search.
- `assistant_mcp/settings.py:16-19` (`tool_server_settings_from_environment`) **New environment variables.** `WEB_SEARCH_HOST`, `WEB_SEARCH_PORT`, and `WEB_SEARCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS` become `ASSISTANT_MCP_HOST`, `ASSISTANT_MCP_PORT`, and `ASSISTANT_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`; the search settings keep their `WEB_SEARCH_` prefix.
- `assistant_mcp/server.py:79-86` (`transport_security_for`) **The DNS rebinding guard takes the server's settings.** Same rule as before, now reading the allow-list from `ToolServerSettings`.
- `assistant_mcp/server.py:101-112` (`main`) **Binds from the new settings.** It takes host and port from `ToolServerSettings` and passes the same settings to `build_server` for the health route.

## Web search as a tool package

- `web_search_mcp/register.py:21-44` (`register_web_search_tools`) **The three web tools register like every other package's.** `search_and_read`, `web_search`, and `fetch_page` move here unchanged, with the server handing in the search client and page reader.
- `web_search_mcp/register.py:62-73` (`render_grounded_context`) **The rendering helpers move with the tools.** The ranked result list, the passages block, and the not-found sentence live beside the tools that produce them.
- `web_search_mcp/settings.py:6-33` (`SearchSettings`) **Search settings only.** The host, port, and allow-list fields are gone.
- `dashboard/evidence.py:12-12` ("from web_search_mcp.register import NOT_FOUND_INSTRUCTION") **New import path.** The dashboard reads the not-found sentence from its new home.

## Running it

- `pyproject.toml:25-25` ("assistant-mcp = ") **The command is `assistant-mcp`.** It replaces `web-search-mcp`, and `assistant_mcp` joins the package list.
- `scripts/services.sh:129-129` ("ENV_KEYS=(ASSISTANT_MCP_HOST ASSISTANT_MCP_PORT)") **The launchd agent sets the new variables.** It still binds the server to 127.0.0.1:8765.
- `scripts/services.sh:141-141` ("write_plist mcp") **The agent runs `.venv/bin/assistant-mcp`.** The launchd label `mcp` and its log file stay the same.
- `benchmark/mcp_process.py:45-81` (`McpServerProcess`) **The benchmark's server.** It starts `assistant_mcp.server` with the new port and host variables.
- `ops/deploy.py:47-47` ("wikipedia_mcp/") **Tool server changes restart the server.** The rule gains `assistant_mcp/`, and also `wikipedia_mcp/` and `sports_mcp/`, which it had been missing, so a change to either now restarts the server on deploy.

## How to verify

```
scripts/lint.sh -c
uv run deslop
uv run pytest -q
ASSISTANT_MCP_PORT=8799 WEB_SEARCH_ENGINES=searxng .venv/bin/assistant-mcp &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8799/healthz
```

- All 700 tests pass.
- By hand: started `.venv/bin/assistant-mcp` with `ASSISTANT_MCP_PORT=8799`. It listened on 127.0.0.1:8799, `/healthz` answered `ok` with 22 tools and none missing, and through `HttpMcpToolBox` `calculate("2 + 3.5")` returned 5.50 and `fetch_page` refused a loopback address. No Brave searches were spent: the run used SearXNG only, which isn't running on the laptop, so `web_search` there failed to connect, as expected.

## Review notes

- Moving the server is a `git mv`, so `git log --follow assistant_mcp/server.py` keeps its history; the tool bodies in `web_search_mcp/register.py` are copied unchanged from it.
- Going live on the Mac mini needs `scripts/services.sh install`, because the plist's program and environment variables change. The deploy plan already picks that up, since `services.sh` changed (`reinstall_agents`). Not deployed.
- The handbook pages that name `web_search_mcp/server.py`, `web-search-mcp`, or `WEB_SEARCH_HOST` (Web Search, Hardware, Development, Operations) are being rewritten in the handbook refresh. They are left alone here to avoid conflicting with it. Design docs keep the old names as the record of what was designed.

author: mahboobmonnamd
body:
## Why
The active `implement-issue`, `pr-review`, and `process-review` skills describe atomic claims but previously did not invoke the merged backend (#27). That left multi-agent coordination only aspirational and encouraged blocking or duplicate work.

## What changed
- Add a host-facing `tools/workflow_claims.py` CLI that maps implement→issue and review/process-review→**one PR claim resource**.
- `begin` atomically acquires or resumes the **existing** durable token; `verify` fails closed before mutations; `release` deletes the token only after conditional database release.
- Require one shared private DB, a stable host-provided worker identity and one persisted private token path per worker/resource. No automatic stealing when a token is lost.
- Wire explicit CLI begin/verify/release calls into the three current skills. Hold a claim across active work but *not while waiting for the process-review approval gate*.
- Add subprocess and concurrent-worker tests, and skill wiring regression tests. Include new modules in `make check` compilation.

## Evidence and limitations
- GitHub Quality `make check` on exact PR head, including subprocess contention and resume/token loss tests.
- This provides a working **single-host command adapter and skill integration**, not enforcement inside Cursor/other remote hosts. Consumers must supply common DB and worker identity and must invoke verify from the actual tool mutation layer to be security-authoritative.
- No docs-only PR, new planning gate, Seyal repo changes or commercial dependencies.
- No cross-host coordination; a shared atomic remote backend is required for that.

Refs #28; complete this scoped issue on merge only after successful exact-head CI and independent technical review. **No merge without explicit user approval.**

body:
## What

The live heart-rate card drew a threshold only once it was crossed, and with fewer than three days of history (calibration) there was no usual rate and no awake floor, so neither band nor threshold appeared.

- Both thresholds are always drawn: a thin pale orange line at the high one (usual rate at this time + 20) and a thin pale green line at the low one (awake floor), with the light band between them (this replaces the resting → usual band).
- While calibrating, provisional thresholds come from the resting rate (high = rest + 30, low = rest); the caption says "provisional thresholds".
- Crossing the high threshold while still turns the curve, number and subtitle orange (unchanged); crossing the low one now turns them green (`StrandPalette.statusPositive`).
- The caption under the curve names both thresholds with a line swatch of their colour; no text inside the plot.

The "still" rule is unchanged: no session running, phone still, 3 minutes beyond the threshold.

## Scope

iPhone/Mac app target, display only; design tokens only. Three new strings, translated in the 10 catalogue languages. Android untouched.

- `TodayVitalsTests`: provisional fallback, band between thresholds, both lines always on the model, caption colour on the crossed side.
- `TodayScreenRenderTests`: `4-fc-seuil` (high crossing) and the new `4b-fc-seuil-bas-et-provisoire` (low crossing in green, calibration). Rendered from `render/today-hr-thresholds`.

body:
Owner 2 Nov 2026, run [41361024017](https://github.com/cogan17/Cogan-Kernel/actions/runs/41361024017) (tanpa SUSFS): "Kamu kurang teliti sepertinya, ini bukan bakasu tapi resukisu!"

## Penyebab
- Rilis terbaru di `Baka-SU/BakaSU` adalah `v4.2.0-rc3` (23 Sep 2026). Rilis itu dibuat **sebelum** proyek berganti nama: commit `97c102ba` "treewide: rename project (#461)", 5 Okt 2026. Penggantian nama itu juga mengubah `kernel/Kconfig`, `kernel/Kbuild`, `kernel/setup.sh` dan tanda tangan manager (`kernel/manager/manager_sign.h`).
- `kernel/Kconfig` rilis `v4.2.0-rc3` dan `v4.1.0` masih ReSukiSU; `main` sudah BakaSU (dicek di repo asli).
- Dengan SUSFS, rilis itu gugur di cek kesiapan SUSFS, sehingga `main` (BakaSU asli) yang dipakai. Tanpa SUSFS (PR #102), cek itu dilewati, sehingga ReSukiSU `v4.2.0-rc3` terambil.

## Perbaikan
- `resolve.is_bakasu(repo, ref)` membaca `kernel/Kconfig` rilis. Rilis yang masih ReSukiSU dianggap belum siap.
- BakaSU lalu diambil dari `main` dengan build CI manager resminya, **dengan atau tanpa SUSFS**. Kernel dan manager tetap dari commit yang sama.
- Tanpa SUSFS, cek kesiapan SUSFS untuk `main` dilewati. Kalau `main` tidak punya build CI manager, summary menulis "Tunggu pengembang BakaSU".
- Begitu BakaSU menerbitkan rilis sesudah ganti nama, rilis itu dipakai lagi seperti aturan semula.
- CLAUDE.md mencatat aturan ini.

## Bukti lokal
- `is_bakasu` pada repo BakaSU asli: `v4.2.0-rc3` → False, `v4.1.0` → False, `main` → True.
- Tes:
  - rilis BakaSU dipakai bila memang BakaSU;
  - rilis ReSukiSU membuat resolver beralih ke `main` (manager `ci`);
  - `is_bakasu` diuji pada repo git sementara.
- Semua tes lulus.

Setelah merge: satu run CI BakaSU tanpa SUSFS sebagai bukti.

author: baldur
gokubar
body:
Lane RENDER-AUDIT (Commander kabir-claude). This PR looks for places where the Mac preview's `DL3Renderer` would draw something different from pdfTeX's PDF, in constructs the P3 fixtures do not cover.

## Fixtures: `fixtures/preview-probes` (10 documents, one case per page)

`pv-form-state`, `pv-stroke-text`, `pv-literal-modes`, `pv-colorstack-pages`, `pv-matrix`, `pv-images`, `pv-pdf-inclusion`, `pv-annots`, `pv-fonts`, `pv-page-attrs`. The README lists what each one draws. `preview-parity.yml` passes the directory to `check_positions.py` as a third `--root`. They are not in the parity scoreboard's fixtures tier. Every expected pixel comes from pdflatex's own PDF in CI. No reference is committed.

## Mismatches fixed (each shown from data alone, with no rendering)

1. **A form drawn in a colour, text render mode or pen other than a new page's.** pdfTeX writes no colour at the start of a form, so in the PDF the form inherits the state it is drawn in. A `FORM` in the display list starts black (spec §4.3). The interpreter now flags that `Do` INCOMPLETE. On the 88 parity fixtures the new flag lands only on pages whose forms were already INCOMPLETE (beamer-madrid, beamer-visuals, from `sh`), so the fallback rate does not change.
2. **Stroked text (`Tr` 1 or 2, as the pdfrender package uses it) with a non-default pen or under a scaling CTM.** Without `LINE_STATE` (§11.4) the client strokes with width 1. Now INCOMPLETE.
3. **A glyph that a `\pdfliteral` shows in a code TeX never typeset in that font.** The glyph is not in the PDF's font subset. If the code is past `/LastChar`, its width is 0: the display list put it 5.26 bp off. The new `Env::typeset` reads `pdf_char_marked`, including fonts that share the PDF font object (§801). Now INCOMPLETE.
4. **Palette PNGs.** ImageIO bases the palette on sRGB, or on *linear* sRGB when the file has gAMA 1.0. pdfTeX writes `/Indexed /DeviceRGB`. `deviceSamples` now rebases the palette onto DeviceRGB. `PaletteImageSpaceTests` fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Verified locally (TeX Live 2026, pdfTeX 1.40.29, mac-m5pro-kabir)

- `check_positions.py --pt2` on the 88 parity fixtures plus the 10 probes: 98/98 positions exact, 98/98 P-T2.
- 3 new interpreter unit tests pass.
- `PaletteImageSpaceTests` passes, in a scratch package with only the two preview targets.
- clippy is clean.

The zero-tolerance sweep has **not** been run on these probes yet: rendering runs only in CI. A `preview-parity` dispatch on this branch will measure it, and auto-merge goes on only after that sweep is green.

author: paws-helper[bot]
body:
Fixes PAS-987

## What changed

- **Storage:** new migration `20261102T0055_runner_admin_repositories` adds `runner_repositories.admin_repositories` (JSON array, NULL means all). Only the new admin endpoint writes it. Heartbeats still write only `repositories`, so they never overwrite the admin choice.
- **Placement:** `runnerAllowsRepository` now allows a repository only when both the admin list and the host list allow it. NULL means all, and matching is case-insensitive. A runner whose lists exclude the item's repository is still skipped with "repository not allowed on this runner". There is no new item state.
- **API:** `POST /api/runners/<id>/repositories` takes `{ "repositories": ["owner/repo", …] | null }`. It is admin only, using the same `admin(principal)` check as `setConcurrency`. Invalid names or more than 256 entries return 400, and a non-admin gets 403. Each save writes a `runner.repositories` audit row. `GET /api/runners` now returns `repositories: { admin, host }` for each runner.
- **Runners page:** each runner's Settings shows "Repositories: All repositories" or the chosen list. When the host reports a list, it also shows "Host config limits it to: …". Admins get a form with "All repositories" or checkboxes for the workspace's repositories, then Save. The workspace list comes from `GET /api/workspaces/repositories`, which is already admin only. Unsaved choices survive the page's polling repaint.
- **Docs:** `docs/runner-enrollment.md` explains how the page setting and the host config combine.

The runner daemon, the runner config format, the heartbeat schema and provisioning are untouched.

## Why

A runner's allowed repositories could only be set in `/etc/paws-runner/config.json`, so a repository added later was refused silently until someone edited the host file. PAS-974 sat in `running` for this reason.

## Verification

- `test/runner-repositories.test.ts` covers four cases. Admin NULL with host NULL allows any repository. An admin list excludes a repository the host allows, matching case-insensitively. Real heartbeats leave `admin_repositories` alone. Through the HTTP route, a member gets 403, invalid names and 257 entries get 400, and saving `null` restores All.
- `runners.test.ts` render tests cover "All repositories", an admin list, the host-limit line, the admin form with checked and disabled states, and a revoked runner.
- `bun run check` passed in full, as did every Closeout command check.
- Screenshots at desktop width and at 390 px are attached as visual proof. Neither width overflows, and the page logged no errors.

author: wonny-labs
body:
Refs #142. **Draft. Not for merge.** Nothing in this PR adopts a dependency, a manifest change, an API subset or a licence statement; those are proposals for the owner (below). The full record is [`docs/psa-crypto-qualification.md`](docs/psa-crypto-qualification.md).

## What changed and why

Issue #142 asks for a portable PSA Crypto interface that future TLS and credential consumers can rely on, without a Crux cryptographic wrapper. This change adds only test material, a trial script and documentation:

- `tests/psa_crypto/cases/`: 22 provider-neutral conformance cases (C17, `<psa/crypto.h>` and ISO C only), with negative status cases.
- `tests/psa_crypto/host/` and `tests/psa_crypto/zephyr/`: a standalone Linux Host CMake project and a `native_sim` Ztest app that run the same case list. The composition selects the provider, never the cases.
- `tests/psa_crypto/stubs/`: two test-only stub providers used as negative controls.
- `scripts/test-psa-crypto.sh`: the trial runner (not in any CI workflow).
- The qualification record, the plan and retained evidence under `docs/evidence/psa-crypto/`.

Unchanged (checked against `origin/main`): `west.yml`, root `CMakeLists.txt`, `.devcontainer/`, `.github/`, `zephyr/`, and `docs/native-interface-policy.md`. Provider sources are never stored in the repository.

## Authorisation

Owner approval to start #142 on 2 November 2026 is recorded in [the issue comment](https://github.com/wonny-labs/crux-pilot/issues/142#issuecomment-6565912192). It covers investigation, test-first development, trial builds and this Draft PR. A reviewer PASS does not authorise merging.

## Tested revision, commands and outcomes

Base `origin/main` `f57ff22`. Code revision tested: `1d8ef0b` (the later commit adds only retained evidence). Linux Dev Container image (linux/amd64), Clang 18.1.3, CMake 3.28.4.

| Command | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/test-psa-crypto.sh all` | exit 0. Controls: no provider fails to configure; the `NOT_SUPPORTED` stub fails all cases; the `SUCCESS` stub fails every case that expects an error status. TF-PSA-Crypto on **Linux Host** Debug: 22 of 22. **Host with ASan/UBSan**: 22 of 22. **Zephyr `native_sim/native/64`** via Twister: 1 of 1 configuration passed (22 cases plus a list check). |
| `scripts/check-host.sh` | exit 0 (run at `6531d23`; later commits do not touch the root build) |
| `CRUX_HOST_PRESET=host-sanitize scripts/check-host.sh` | exit 0 (run at `6531d23`) |
| `CLANG_FORMAT=clang-format scripts/check-format.sh` | exit 0 (rerun at `1d8ef0b`) |
| `scripts/check-dependencies.sh` | exit 0 (rerun at `1d8ef0b`) |
| `scripts/analyze-host.sh` | **exit 1, pre-existing.** The same command on a clean checkout of `origin/main` (`f57ff22`) exits 1 with the same four diagnostics in `samples/logging` and `tests/logging_consumer`. Not touched or fixed here. |
| Portable sources include only ISO C and `<psa/crypto.h>` | confirmed by `grep` over `tests/psa_crypto/cases`; Zephyr appears only in the `native_sim` harness |

Retained logs: `docs/evidence/psa-crypto/`. The first Host run against the real provider failed 3 of 22 cases; the record explains the three corrections (two assertions went beyond the documented API, one is a provider limitation) and keeps that first log.

Host, `native_sim`, cross-build, CI and physical evidence are separate. Only Host and `native_sim` were run.

## Not run

- GitHub Actions (this PR will trigger the existing workflows; `scripts/test-psa-crypto.sh` is not in them).
- Any RT1060 build or cross-compilation with the PSA app. Kconfig was resolved for `mimxrt1060_evk@B//qspi` with a **configure-only** run; nothing was built or executed.
- Any physical-board operation (not authorised).
- `psa-arch-tests` (inspected only), TLS, secure storage.
- wolfPSA and any other alternative provider: **blocked on licence review**, not fetched, not built, not run.

## Trial inputs

Zephyr `684c9e8f` (`v4.4.0`); `tf-psa-crypto` `dc575a2ddcc8cb16275d24c42a52eaf79ebe2231`; `mbedtls` module `a3e190fe44c78d1ba67f55979e1257328cc7d0d8` (both match Zephyr's manifest), fetched with `git fetch --depth 1` into `/opt/crux-cache/psa-trial/` and passed to Zephyr through `ZEPHYR_MODULES`. Host and cache disk checked before fetching. The #141 trial directory was not touched. `libclang-rt-18-dev=1:18.1.3-1ubuntu1` (listed in the Dockerfile, missing from the local image) was installed into my throwaway container only.

## Decisions needed from the owner (proposals, not decided)

Details and trade-offs are in the record.

1. **Manifest.** Recommended: add `mbedtls` and `tf-psa-crypto` to `name-allowlist` when a consumer is approved. Both are needed at this pin (the Mbed TLS module hosts the CMake entry). Alternatives: pass modules from a cache (not reproducible); `tf-psa-crypto` alone (not viable).
2. **Linux Host dependency.** Recommended: `FetchContent` with a URL and SHA-256 at Zephyr's pinned commit, like GoogleTest (tarball SHA-256 `1a122bcb91fc7c32060e64feeea29364a7cd894413e0ba89ee200fc5e384f95b`, computed in the trial), plus a check that it equals Zephyr's pin. Host CI has no west workspace. Alternatives: system package (rejected: Ubuntu 24.04 has 2.28.8), west module path, vendoring (rejected).
3. **API subset.** Recommended: the small consumer-driven subset (random, SHA-256 multipart, ECDSA P-256 verify, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256; TLS named, not qualified). **Open point:** `psa_key_derivation_verify_bytes` is unsupported by this provider revision, so credential verification has no provider-supported constant-time comparison. Options: consumer-owned comparison, provider patch or revision, or a different PSA function.
4. **Licence statement.** TF-PSA-Crypto and the Mbed TLS module are Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later (exceptions in `drivers/everest`, one BSD-3-Clause header). Recommended: elect Apache-2.0 if Crux states Apache-2.0. **Owner decision (2 Nov 2026):** Crux is Apache-2.0 and these recommendations are accepted; the `LICENSE` file is added by a separate Draft PR (branch `chore/add-apache-2-license`). Nothing is adopted by this PR. Not legal advice.

## wolfPSA blocker

Blocked on licence review; the feasibility result is not recorded. The review must answer seven questions listed in the record (terms and fitness for a public repository and distributed firmware; whether the trial fetch is permitted; compatibility with Crux's undeclared licence and Zephyr's Apache-2.0; linking obligations; exact project, release and PSA version; a statement that no commercially licensed or employer-owned material is used; sign-off).

## RT1060-EVKB entropy source

Identified from source only: the i.MX RT TRNG (`nxp,kinetis-trng`, `random@400cc000`, chosen as `zephyr,entropy`), driver `entropy_mcux_trng`. **Evidence status: source-read and Kconfig-resolved, not executed on a target.** Target execution needs separate approval. Hardware acceleration is declared unsupported for all three environments.

## Open findings

1. `psa_key_derivation_verify_bytes` is an unconditional `NOT_SUPPORTED` stub in the pinned provider.
2. Zephyr's entropy glue falls back to `sys_rand_get()` (xoshiro on RT1060, non-cryptographic) if the entropy call fails, and still reports full entropy. `ENTROPY_MCUX_TRNG` selects `ENTROPY_NEEDS_PRNG`, so the PSA source is the legacy RNG with HMAC_DRBG.
3. `CSPRNG_ENABLED` does not certify a source, and `native_sim` PSA random output is identical on every run by default (retained probe).
4. TRNG health-check adequacy and entropy rate were not assessed; nothing ran on a board.
5. The provider pin is a commit in Zephyr's fork; its relation to the upstream `v1.1.0` tag was not established.
6. No Crux licence is stated; Host CI has no west workspace.
7. `scripts/analyze-host.sh` already fails on `origin/main`.
8. The local Dev Container image lacks `libclang-rt-18-dev`, so `host-sanitize` does not link in it without the package.

## Acceptance criteria (issue #142)

| Criterion | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Manifes

author: djkianoosh
body:
### 🎯 What
Fixes an arbitrary file overwrite vulnerability in `shelf disable` and `shelf enable` commands where writing to `.geminiignore` followed symbolic links by default.

### ⚠️ Risk
If a repository contains a `.geminiignore` symbolic link pointing to an arbitrary file on the user's filesystem (such as system files or sensitive user configurations), invoking `shelf disable` or `shelf enable` would follow the symlink and overwrite the destination file with shelf-generated ignore rules.

### 🛡️ Solution
- Added `AppError::SymlinkNotAllowed` to represent rejected symlink operations.
- Checked `fs::symlink_metadata()` on `.geminiignore` in both `disable_profile` and `enable_profile` before read/write operations to verify that the file is not a symbolic link.
- If a symlink is encountered, the operation is immediately rejected with an error, preventing writes to target files.
- Added automated integration tests ensuring symlinked `.geminiignore` files are rejected and target files remain untouched.

author: raptium
body:
Three independent breakages were turning every recent run red on `main` and on the Dependabot PRs. This fixes all of them.

## Root causes and fixes

**1. PyPy 3.12 wheels fail to compile** (`linux aarch64`, `musllinux aarch64`, `armv7`, `musllinux x86_64`; run [41364308295](https://github.com/raptium/rusty-zip/actions/runs/41364308295))

pyo3-ffi 0.29.2 gates `use core::ffi::c_int` behind `#[cfg(all(not(PyPy), Py_3_12))]` while the FFI declarations using it are gated only on `#[cfg(Py_3_12)]`, so every PyPy 3.12 wheel died with `cannot find type c_int` / `_PyInterpreterFrame`. All CPython 3.9-3.15t and PyPy 3.11 wheels built fine, which is why only the jobs whose cross image ships PyPy 3.12 failed. pyo3-ffi 0.29.3 fixes the gating.

- `pyo3` 0.29.2 -> 0.29.3

**2. `cargo audit --deny warnings` fails** (run [41364308381](https://github.com/raptium/rusty-zip/actions/runs/41364308381))

`zip` 8.6.0 is affected by RUSTSEC-2026-0367, -0368 and -0369 (all `extract()` issues this write-only crate never hits, but the audit is unconditional). Patched in >= 9.0.0.

- `zip` `=8.6.0` -> `=9.2.1` (still `default-features = false, features = ["deflate", "time"]`; MSRV stays 1.88). zip 9 adds a filename lifetime to `FileOptions`, hence the one-line signature change in `get_file_options`.

**3. `test (3.9)` cannot install Python** (same CI run)

`ubuntu-latest` now resolves to Ubuntu 26.04, where `actions/setup-python` has no 3.9 build: `The version '3.9' with architecture 'x64' was not found for Ubuntu 26.04`.

- The `test` job drops `actions/setup-python` and lets uv provision the 3.9/3.12/3.14 matrix interpreters, so the job no longer depends on runner-image Pythons.

**4. Dependabot's uv updater cannot resolve the lockfile** (`uv in / for maturin, ruff` update jobs, e.g. [40291923527](https://github.com/raptium/rusty-zip/actions/runs/40291923527))

The updater runs `uv lock --upgrade-package pre-commit==4.6.2`, which must satisfy every `requires-python` split; pre-commit 4.4+ needs Python >= 3.10, so the 3.9 split was unsatisfiable (`dependency_file_not_resolvable`). The runtime keeps `requires-python = ">=3.9"`; the dev group now scopes pre-commit with `python_full_version >= '3.10'`.

This is also why Dependabot PRs #15/#16 keep failing: their red checks are just (1) and (2).

## Verification (local, macOS arm64)

- `cargo audit --deny warnings` -> exit 0 (59 crates, 1395 advisories)
- `pytest -q` -> 7 passed on CPython 3.9 and 3.15
- PyPy 3.12.15: `cargo check` passes with pyo3 0.29.3; with pyo3-ffi 0.29.2 it reproduces exactly the CI error (negative control)

author: ashdamle
body:
## What
Suite-wide elimination of the recurring **tight wall-clock timing flake** — the anti-pattern behind repeated false CI failures (and real development friction): a test asserting an externally-measured wall-clock upper bound with too little cushion, so a loaded runner's scheduler starvation crosses the pass/fail boundary even though the mechanism under test worked.

## Approach
Enumerated **every** timing assertion across `tests/` and judged each (verdicts recorded, none left UNREVIEWED):
- **class a** (scheduler-sensitive upper bound) → hardened: widen the discriminating window, all bounds **derived from named constants** (~15s vs multi-second/forever hangs), with the **typed outcome kept as the primary assertion**.
- **class b** (lower bound / generous hang watchdog) and **class c** (virtual-clock / typed data) → left unchanged.

Includes a distinct success-path fix CI caught: a ledger read asserted to **succeed** must not carry the tiny adverse `deadline_s` meant for refusal tests (it falsely raised `LedgerQueryDeadline` under rare starvation). Swept across all `deadline_s` sites in 16 files; tiny deadlines retained only where a refusal is asserted.

## Proof (per changed file)
- ruff clean; both 3.11 and 3.12 green.
- **20–50× repeats under 18 concurrent CPU burners** (50× for the low-frequency 20ms-margin site), on both interpreters.
- **Mutation proofs**: breaking each mechanism makes the typed assertion go RED.

Test files only — **no production code changed**.

## Honestly unresolved (flagged, not hidden)
- `test_codex_lease_progress_reclaim.py`: a dormant test (no entrypoint) exposes a pre-existing production/test mismatch; exploratory edits fully reverted.
- `test_delegate_cancel_process_group.py`: the real `killpg` branch reports `SKIP/UNREVIEWED: EPERM` on macOS — needs a permissive Linux CI host to exercise.
- `test_managed_parser_cache_safety.py`: a pre-existing `_sqlite3` authorizer SIGSEGV observed once under combined load; a fresh faulthandler run passed but the native crash is not claimed fixed.

author: ianmccul
body:
Adds the infinite, zero-field massive XXZ transverse two-spinon spectral density and `bethe-xxz-structure-factor-thermo`. It supplies physically normalized intensity alongside the existing dispersion: both unequal spectral sheets, physical momentum k=pi-Q, S^{-+}(k,ω) with dω/(2π) integration, and absent values at thresholds or numerical failures. Higher spinons and longitudinal intensity are outside this calculation; no sum-rule rescaling or broadening is applied.

The immutable evaluator uses Uni20 theta constants/jets, a restricted RF(x,y,1) inverse map, rationalized Jacobians and a bounded log-kernel tail. It supports binary64, native extended precision, binary128 and explicitly owned MPFR precision. The frontend uses the existing bounded ordered Async grid, declared spectrum/continuum tables and common run metadata/exports.

Sheet arithmetic preserves resolved endpoint distances and reflection symmetry, checks all thresholds before evaluating kernels, and avoids intermediate overflow at large exchange. At a closing sheet, the upper bound is reconstructed from the lower bound and a nonnegative squared difference; separately rounded formulas could otherwise invert the interval. Widths below scalar resolution can round to zero. These changes preserve physical normalization and existing reference tolerances.

Validation at `2d7d39c1b5a8a8c2e855feb5f2fb19404051c3aa`:

- Focused numerical/frontend/export/precision/argument/citation checks: **25/25 native, 39/39 wide, 30/30 Clang ASan/UBSan**. Wide includes binary128 and MPFR128/256; sanitizers use Uni20's existing MPFR cache policy. Existing configured providers were used, not a fresh full repository build.
- Independent original q-product vertex amplitudes and integrated two-vacuum measures; 120/130-digit point values, internal-sheet edges, outer-edge offsets down to 1e-24, and isotropic/Ising limits. The standalone mpmath/NumPy reference needs no private data.
- The identical closing-sheet regression fails the previous header in binary64/80/128 and MPFR128/256, then passes the correction. It probes both closing momenta, six anisotropies and the two reviewer examples. Tiny-momentum, midpoint and near-maximum-exchange controls remain.
- Earlier native/MPFR160 guide examples and a fresh library-only CMake consumer compiled and ran. Current Markdown math, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Compact evidence, source hashes and precisely attributed earlier checks are in `docs/validation/xxz-two-spinon-spectral-weight.json`.

This is the X1 public-port checkpoint. Higher-sector finite-q XXZ machinery (#121) and independent QTM evaluators remain separate. Reciprocal follow-up, completed Claude review, current full CI and final installed/deployed integration remain gates.

## O que muda
Os números de dano se amontoavam sobre o herói e o mecha do LightWolf (lw_3_misseis, lw_4_salto). Causa: `v2/efeitos.gd > numero` abria um número novo a cada acerto; um míssil e a explosão dele, ou uma salva num bando em volta do herói, davam 6 a 14 números no mesmo quadro, quase no mesmo ponto (só um sorteio de +-12 px).

Conserto no ponto único por onde todos passam:
- Acertos da mesma cor e tamanho que pedem lugar a menos de 30 x 20 px de um número nascido há menos de 0,3 s SOMAM nele (soma exata).
- O que não soma sobe 14 px (até 3 vezes) se cairia em cima de outro número recente, medindo a caixa pelo tamanho do texto.
- Não soma: `exato` (armas_novas já agrupa por monstro), texto não numérico ("LIMPOU x14") e cura ("+12").
- Dano de jogo e RNG não mudam; `usados.numeros` continua contando os pedidos e `usados.somados` os que entraram na soma. Constantes `NUM_JUNTA_*` e `NUM_AFASTA_*` no topo de efeitos.gd (o arquivo não lê dados/).

author: zcross00
body:
## Change

Adds an **Early is a miss too** rule under Burn-down and re-forecast.

- Dev process keeps every closed milestone's last due date, its actual close, and the signed error.
- The weekly retro reads the mean signed error (target within ±0.5 days) and the share of milestones closed on their due date (target at least half).
- When the mean drifts, the retro changes the forecast's settings: the pace window, buffer days or rate. Individual dates are not patched to hide the drift.

Adds a CHANGELOG 2.6 entry.

## Reason from use

On the reference project, 12 of the 13 milestones that closed from Oct 28 to Nov 1 closed early, and none closed late. The median error was -2 days. The causes were stacked allowances (a planned rate below measured throughput, plus a playtest day added to every milestone) and dependency moves that didn't check whether the dependency really blocked the playtest. The owner's point was that dates must be commitments they can plan around, so early is as much a miss as late. For Saturday's retro.

author: mbryzek
body:
Notes replaces Approvals. Every note waits on its note page until the member approves it, or until the agent does when auto approval is saved. The member can Edit a note: the edit becomes a new version, both checks run on it, and Learnings are updated from the diff of what passed. Approving and sending are two separate jobs: the agent approves (`digestif note --approve`), and the app's send job signs whatever is approved and unsigned, on every pass.

## Design

DES-37265, approved revision `drv-b21de72217cc4b44becc2bc540034a70` (`dev issues design 37265 --content --revision drv-b21de72217cc4b44becc2bc540034a70`). This PR covers four sections: Approve and Edit; Rules and Learnings; Status and Shared; Approval and sending are two small jobs. It also covers the `notes` and `note` screens of `design/digestif/member.html` in the claude repo.

## What changed

**Node** (`node/web/store.ml` `Notes`, `node/web/api.ml` `Notes`)
- Data model:
  - A note and its versions live in `ui_notes` and `ui_note_versions`.
  - Version 1 is the agent's. Each edit adds a version in the person's voice.
  - A version is shown only once its checks pass. The exception: the member sees the result of their own edit.
- Endpoints:
  - `GET /notes`, `GET /notes/:id?version=`, `GET /notes/:id/log`
  - `POST /notes/:id/versions` (Save, and Save & approve)
  - `POST /notes/:id/approve`
  - `POST /notes/suggestion/dismiss`
  - `GET|PUT /settings/approval`
  - `GET|PUT /learnings`
- Save & approve sends only if the checks removed nothing. If they removed something, the note stays Waiting with "Not sent. The Rules check removed 1 from your edit, in Learned. Approve sends the text below."
- The check hook:
  - It is a new `check` hook (`node/web/behaviors.ml`). It is the nightly's executable with `DIGESTIF_HOOK=check` and `edits` in its handoff.
  - It hands results back with `digestif note checked <version>` and `digestif learnings set --version <version>`.
  - A version handed over and not finished is retried at most once an hour. The note never waits for its Learnings.
- Note time writes nothing while a note waits.
- Sending:
  - The send job runs on every pass (`Api.send_notes`), before the daily run.
  - Shared is the earliest relay sighting's `received_at`.
  - #149's signing backstop returns the note to Waiting with `not_sent`.
- The suggestion:
  - It appears after three member approvals in a row with no change.
  - An edit, Not now, or saving Every note waits restarts the count. Auto approved neither counts nor breaks it.
- Removed: the first five notes, Write a note now's button, Drop/Regenerate/Keep/Change/Decline, and the Removed tab. The approval queue is gone too.

**Behaviors**
- `behaviors/src/edits.ts` and the new prompt `behaviors/prompts/learnings.md`. Both checks run on the member's text through #149's `runChecks`. The Learnings model reads a line diff of the edited version's checked text against the edit's checked text, so nothing a check removed reaches Learnings. Its answer is the whole Learnings, or `NO CHANGE`.
- The writer prompt now carries Learnings.
- The nightly reads `GET /settings/approval` at hand-over and passes `--approve` when auto approval is saved.

**UI**
- `ui/src/routes/(node)/notes`: the list with its suggestion line, the note page, and the Log tab.
- The Approvals routes are deleted, and the nav shows Notes with the waiting count.
- The mock node, the fixtures and `digestif demo` all seed notes the way the node keeps them: two approved, one waiting, two approvals with no change.

## API contract change

`spec/digestif-node.json`, the exact diff of this PR's own commit (the notes resources and models came in with ISS-38773's contract, on main):

author: chloe6888
body:
## Summary
- Extend the existing offline paper-trading simulator with optional liquidity-aware execution based on local yfinance raw daily CSV files.
- Calculate trailing average daily volume (ADV) from recent valid Volume observations, with stale-data and minimum-history checks.
- Add a configurable maximum order participation rate; quantities above the ADV capacity remain explicitly unfilled rather than being treated as executed.
- Record requested, filled, unfilled, liquidity-limited, and cash-limited shares in the order report.
- Add configurable square-root impact slippage: impact_bps = coefficient_bps * sqrt(filled_shares / ADV).
- Preserve preview-only default; local ledger changes still require explicit --commit-ledger.
- Add tests for sell-side ADV caps, buy-side ADV caps, zero whole-share capacity, volume-data freshness, market impact, cash interaction, and CLI ledger behavior.
- Document the new --volume-dir, --volume-window, --max-volume-age-days, --max-participation-rate, and --market-impact-coefficient-bps options.

## Validation
- GitHub Actions on exact PR head `9dbfd9033eaa5d71ce00b13d768797768b26f900` passed: **221 tests passed in 21.53s**. [Workflow run](https://github.com/chloe6888/phase1_risk_analysis/actions/runs/41371384499).

## Limitations
- ADV participation and square-root impact are configurable approximations, not calibrated intraday execution models.
- Does not model order-book depth, queue priority, intraday prices, halts, price limits, broker routing, tax, or real market impact.
- No broker connection or real order placement.

author: ryubara
body:
## Summary

Firing from the hip is now the aim held for a moment, not a second, partial aim (the reopened part of #300, the maintainer's three reports: firing without aiming must put the gun in the aim pose; entering the aim must not teleport the gun; one camera and pose weight, no snap). `PlayerMotionState.holds_aim(hold)` is `aiming or fire_age < hip_fire_hold`; the camera's one aim spring chases it, and the legs and the hands read that same eased weight. The weapon pose is blended by it (`aim_yaw` from the body's heading to the view, `WeaponHandsIK.converge` 0 to 1 instead of a bool), so nothing flips in one frame. Holding the aim button only skips the entry. The hip-fire spring, zoom share and its two frequencies are gone; the turn to the view is the aim turn, slowed to 8 rad/s so the weapon (which turns with the body and with the weight) moves a few degrees a tick. Look steadiness stays on the real aim button with its own ease (a burst from the hip does not slow the view), as the coordinator decided.

Fixes #300

Docs: the shoulder camera and hip fire research pages, the weapon hold design page and the character controller table are updated.

## Issues affected

- #383: its tilt while reloading must read the same aim weight (`ThirdPersonCamera.aim_amount()`); that weight now exists and is the one the hands blend by.
- #405: the sprint pull-back and sprint sway now ease out while the aim is held (a shot too), not only on the button.
- #286: an auto-fire that holds the trigger now holds the whole aim (zoom, turn, pose), as the hip fire research page notes.

## Checklist

- [x] One aim weight (`aiming or fire_age < hold`) drives the camera, the body, the legs and the hands
- [x] The weapon pose eases in and out (yaw, convergence), with no single-frame jump
- [x] Hip fire reaches the same camera placement and weapon pose as aiming, and zooms out after the hold exactly as a released aim does
- [x] Look steadiness follows only the aim button (own spring)
- [x] Docs, tuning notes and tests updated

## Testing

- New `test_aim_weight.gd` (5 tests): hip fire and aim reach the same lens, field of view, grip and barrel; the grip moves under 15 cm and the barrel turns under 25 degrees a tick going in and out of both, with the view 75 degrees off the body; the weight lets go after the last shot along the aim's release curve, `hip_fire_hold` later; pressing aim during a burst changes nothing; the look steadiness follows only the button. `test_hip_fire.gd` and `test_player_aim_move.gd` follow the new API.
- `tests/player` and `tests/night`: see the result line below. One run of `test_player_crouch.gd` failed once under heavy machine load (a 5 mm replay difference) and passed alone on this branch and on main.
- Headless import prints no ERROR.
- Per tick, from `hip_fire_transition.tscn` (60 ticks a second, lever rifle, view 75 degrees off the body):

| | main, hip fire | main, aim button | now, both |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| most the grip moves in a tick | 15.7 cm | 46.6 cm | 12.4 cm |
| most the barrel turns in a tick | 21.0 deg | 78.3 deg | 19.1 deg |
| zoom (field of view 70 to) | 65 | 60 | 60 |
| zoom-out starts after last shot or release | 0.82 s | 0.03 s | 0.82 s / 0.03 s (the hold, then the same curve) |
| 95 percent of the way back after the end of the hold or release | 0.67 s | 0.18 s | 0.18 s / 0.18 s |

Failed first: `test_hip_fire_reaches_the_camera_and_weapon_pose_of_the_aim`, `test_the_weapon_pose_eases_in_without_a_jump_for_hip_fire_and_for_aim`, `test_the_view_lets_go_after_the_last_shot_as_it_does_after_the_aim_button` and `test_pressing_the_aim_button_during_a_burst_changes_nothing` all fail on main (the aim button's hand step was 0.42 m and 72 degrees in one tick, hip fire reached half the zoom) and pass here.

## Screenshots

Frame sheets from the shoulder camera at 1920x1080 (20 frames a second, the view turned 75 degrees off the body first; the trigger or the aim is pressed at 1.80 s, let go at 3.00 s).

- **Before:** hip fire (the gun does not come up, half zoom) ![before hip fire](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c1bd750-4678-44bc-8784-bde5a0b806dd) the aim button (the gun jumps between two frames) ![before aim press](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75ce9b64-4d53-4233-a8cf-553cdd050f68) the trigger let go ![before hip fire release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/651262b9-1eb3-4486-ba5e-d21820f657d0)
- **After:** hip fire (same pose and zoom as the aim, eased) ![after hip fire](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd8575e7-ab21-4d16-969e-0e5b10368952) the aim button ![after aim press](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90d043e4-ccc4-45d1-aefe-045dc20840af) the trigger let go (the hold, then the same release as the aim) ![after hip fire release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eade1c2b-03a4-4e9a-b0de-744cd1a96962)

## AI use

- **Commits written by:** an AI
- **Model:** Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5 (the history carries the earlier commits of the crowbar branch, which were merged in before it landed)

The static ledger stays deferred; only this invocation's effective current-artifact claim can pass.

Protect all validated inputs from output writes, including stage/envelope receipt aliases and normal-mode ledger/source clobbering. Bind the new validator and regression suite into V8, and use the actual gate in CI in place of the separate delivery/bundle calls. Document the separate trace-extractor correction; this PR does not complete V7 or #117.

Validation:
- 113 security gate tests pass, including real RED/GREEN output-clobber regressions; independent DeepSeek Flash development reviews approved the fixes.
- Local full artifact experiment: all 467 library classes, 82 crypto classes, 37 runtime classes and three notices matched; nine origin-checked hybrid handshakes passed per JDK. A one-class altered JAR copy failed with Invalid JVM class and received no effective claim.
- That full experiment precedes the final additional stage-receipt output guard. Its validation module is unchanged; the final guard has a failing-before/passing-after regression and a passing preflight against the real inputs. Exact-head CI will replay the complete pipeline before merge.

JVM timing, cryptographic hardness, running-deployment identity and external expert review remain outside this claim. Part of #117.
