author: darknight11ish
body:
## The bug

In Jarvis Live the owner approves a card for a web search, hears **"Approved. Carrying on."**, and then gets an answer that clearly never used the search: *"approved card, then Jarvis forgets my question"*.

## Measured cause (his own run, 2026-11-01, 15:44-15:47)

**"Approved. Carrying on." is not the model.** It is the app's own fixed sentence (`backend/jarvis_card_words.py:589` `VOICE["approved"]`, `backend/static/card-words.js:97` `CARD_VOICE.approved`), spoken on the SSE comment `: jarvis-status approved`, which `jarvis_agent._Out.card_answered` emits. So it proves only that the gate recorded a yes.

```
15:43:59.514  route          turns=7              the question
15:44:03.109  gate.asked     search_the_web       its card
15:44:17.141  gate.approved  by=phone             the tap
15:44:21.655  agent.chain    web_search ran=true ok=true
15:44:21.746  route          turns=7              the SAME history re-sent, 91 ms later
15:44:25.000  SPEED          rounds=1 tokens=17 tools=False
```

`jarvis_gate.decide()` had already consumed the tap and **NULLed the card's prompt and detail**. The turn then found `out.gone` - the phone had closed its stream while the card waited - so it raised `ClientGone` without running the tool nobody could read (`_one_call`'s `out.gone` branch; `_web_search_call`'s `:13168-13171` in the live file). Nothing on the PC remembered the yes, so the re-sent turn made **one** model round, ran **no** tool and answered in **17 tokens**. The card turns in the same session that *did* finish read `rounds=2`, `~6000` prompt tokens and `first_word_ms` 17-23 s - the working case this one is missing.

The full diagnosis, with the trees it was measured on, is `.dsh-scratch/APPROVAL-CONTINUITY-2026-11-01/EVIDENCE.md` (gitignored scratch, not in this PR).

## The fix

`backend/jarvis_agent.py` + `jarvis-backend/jarvis_agent.py` (whole-file delivery: `jarvis_agent.py` is in `$SHIPPED` and no patch targets it, so the twin is carried byte-identically - see the delivery note).

- both `out.gone` branches - the generic `_one_call` one and `web_search`'s - call **`owed_record()`** before raising `ClientGone`, so a yes that could not be used is kept instead of dropped;
- **`owed_record()` refuses anything that is not a person's approval.** It asks `_a_person_said_yes()` *again* for itself rather than trusting its caller, needs a usable `conversation_id` and the card's own `request_id`, and keeps the call, its parsed arguments, the action name and the card id - in memory, per conversation;
- at the start of the **next `run_local_turn` for the same conversation**, `owed_run_turn()` takes that record once and `_owed_replay()` runs it through the **same `check_call` / `prepare()` / gate / `execute()` contract**, with `pre_approved` set so **no card is raised and `checker` is not called** - the approval already exists;
- the transcript left behind is the ordinary multi-step one - the assistant message that asked for the tool, then its result, with `OUTSIDE_NOTE` above them when the tool was a reading one - so the model answers from it;
- a carried step that fails, cannot run, or raises says so **in code's own words** in the answer, and never claims it ran; a replay that raises never turns the question into a 500.

## What does NOT change

- **One card per action, nothing auto-approved, nothing before the gate's yes.** The carried step runs under the verdict of the card that was really answered; `jarvis_gate.decide()` is not bypassed for anything new, and no tier or `NEEDS_A_PERSON` rule moves.
- Bounded, so it cannot become a queue or a replay loop: keyed by the card id (`_OWED_DONE`, so a client that re-sends twice still runs it **once**), dropped after `OWED_TTL_SECONDS` (ten minutes), never carried into another conversation, never written to disk, never survives a restart, and never created for a denied, timed-out, expired or never-answered card.
- A private turn and a crisis turn run no tool, so they leave the step owed rather than spending it.
- Both the record and the replay are in the audit log as `agent.owed` / `agent.owed_ran` - names and ids only, never the card's words and never the question.

## Delivery note (why there is no new `backend/*.patch`)

`jarvis_agent.py` is a module this repository **ships whole**: it is in `$SHIPPED` in `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` and **no patch targets it**. `backend/jarvis_agent.py` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis_agent.py` are byte-identical (same SHA-256: `7460F663121D59C315B0A4AE3A89E58AA8688949BAFFC625853C3DCB83A888C7`), as `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` requires, so the change is delivered as the whole file in both. Because no patch changed, `tools/build_patch_history.py`, the patch stack's RATCHET, `backend/README.md`'s patch table and the generated plugin catalogue are untouched.

## Evidence: before / after

"Before" is commit `1861485da`'s own two agent files in a separate detached worktree (no fix); "after" is that same tree with only the two fixed agent files copied in.

| run | command | tally |
|---|---|---|
| before - full-file revert (`HEAD` agent files) | `python -B backend/test_approval_continuity.py` | **2 passed, 0 skipped, 17 failed, exit 1** |
| before - pre-fix behaviour (record + replay halves switched off) | `python -B prove_red_without_fix.py` | **8 passed, 6 failing checks** |
| after - same tree, only the two agent files copied in | `python -B backend/test_approval_continuity.py` | **60 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0** |
| after - the CI runner | `python -B backend/run_suites.py test_approval_continuity.py` | **60 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0** |

Related suites through the CI runner (`python -B backend/run_suites.py <suite>`), all exit 0:

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `test_agent.py` | 279 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed |
| `test_agent_plan_wiring.py` | 60 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed |
| `test_agent_retirement_wiring.py` | 73 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_chat_stream.py` | 68 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed |
| `test_approval_contract.py` | 67 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_gate_fixes.py` | 27 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_gate_names.py` | 3 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed |
| `test_gate_risk_words.py` | 17 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_gate_touches.py` | 100 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_web_search.py` | 415 passed, 0 failed |
| `test_asks_first.py` | 226 passed, 0 failed |

Twins / records (whole-file delivery): `python -B backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` -> 135 passed, 0 failed; `python -B backend/test_base_regeneration.py` -> 39 passed, 0 failed; `python -B tools/check_stale_twins.py` -> exit 0 (302 shipped modules + 3 beside-files match). `py -3 tools/roll_changelog.py --check` and `py -3 tools/roll_decisions.py --check` both exit 0.

Direct runs on this PC without the CI runner's throwaway config show 2 **pre-existing** `test_chat_stream.py` failures that reproduce on unmodified `HEAD` too (ambient owner config); under the CI runner, whose state is throwaway, that suite is 68 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed.

## Records

- `changelog.d/2026-11-01-approval-continuity.md` (one bullet) - `CHANGELOG.md` not edited.
- `decisions.d/2026-11-01-approval-continuity.md` (one dated bullet) - `docs/DECISIONS.md` not edited.
- No document is added under `docs/`, so `docs/README.md`'s count is not bumped.

## Not covered, said rather than hidden

- The **attached-file** card's own `out.gone` branch (`run_local_turn`'s file gate) is a different mechanism - no tool call and no per-card id - and is left exactly as it was.
- A stream that dies a **second** time during the replay and before anything ran puts the one record back (it stays owed until its ten minutes end, then drops); the pre-existing client-side cause of the dead stream is not touched.
- This is a bug fix, so there is no new feature row and no `docs/JARVIS-API.md` change: no route, no request field and no API answer changed.

body:
Astra now fills a missing timed-task reminder as one removable preview group and carries optional read-offer intent in the main model call. Read composition no longer waits for a serial offer selector. Moderation has a two-second deadline, and argument-level guidance covers owned parents, goal links, selection reuse and concrete starting actions.

Refs thomasluizon/orbit-tickets#1674.

## Approach and scope

The existing commands, gateway, ownership checks, validators, entity guards and preview revision service remain the write path. The new completion reads structured create arguments only and uses `AppConstants.DefaultReminderMinutes` (15). Explicit false, fixed reminders, repeat reminders, reused habits, edits and removed preview fields keep their existing meaning. Semantic dismissal keys suppress only the matching configuration suggestion.

`ProactiveReadOffer.cs` defines the internal `orbit_offer_intent` control for supported read schemas. `ProcessUserChatCommand.Offers.cs` composes eligible actions from complete successful read rounds and existing account facts; `ProactiveProposal.cs` strips the control before operation execution and read fingerprints. Concrete family actions keep their existing priority. Aim and Calendar intent comes from the model, with no message keyword or regex routing, tool hiding, renamed calls or fixed answer substitution. All 71 tools remain available under the existing capability rules. Preview next actions retain their existing selector.

The shared-file changes are confined to schema declaration, typed offer capture and create completion. No HTTP DTO, domain field, migration, model, reasoning effort, UI repository or eval harness changes. The contract and complete English/Portuguese copy register are in `src/Orbit.Api/OpenApi/AnswerComposition.md`. Fixture provenance and synthetic declarations are documented in the proactive-offer fixture README.

## Findings by gate class

| Class | Cause and fix | Offline evidence and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1: omitted create proposals | The rule at `ProactiveProposal.cs:14` existed only as general instructions; the create fields had no equivalent local guidance. `ProactiveProposal.Create.cs:11` now describes `reminder_enabled`, `reminder_times`, `parent_habit_id` and `goal_ids`; `ProactiveProposal.cs:67` injects those descriptions into offer schemas. `ProactiveProposal.Create.cs:20` completes only a new timed OneTime draft with no reminder configuration. | Both recorded dated-task calls are replayed through the real gateway and previewer. The reminder fields form one editable, removable group; removal, refresh, matching dismissal and unrelated dismissal are tested. Existing bilingual `R9gOfferReplay_FirstRoundIncludesOwnedGoalAndRoutineFacts` confirms owned routines and active goals reach `ProcessUserChatCommand.Ai.cs:77`. Semantic parent and goal matching remains a model decision and requires the coordinator probe. |
| 2: missing aim action | On the starting implementation, `PreferredTypedOffer` excluded aim; the remaining path depended on the selector's interpretation and deadline. `ProcessUserChatCommand.Offers.cs:124` now uses the main model's declared intent, and prefers the goal-list block. `ProactiveReadOffer.cs:9` tells the model to compare the expressed aim with the complete active-goal facts. | Bilingual goal-read replays prove aim attaches with no second `SendWithToolsAsync`, unknown/none cannot imply aim, and control metadata never reaches operation arguments or read scopes. The new intent value is explicitly synthetic test input for our new schema, not an observed provider output. The supplied artifacts do not retain raw selector JSON, so an exact historical choice versus timeout cannot be proven. The pt-BR selector phases near three seconds are consistent with its deadline; this is an inference, not a recovered response. |
| 3: latency | Equivalent-goal windows total 11.283 s and 10.652 s, with main model phases 4.550 + 4.235 s and 4.274 + 3.798 s, plus serial selectors of 2.130 s and 2.230 s. The read selector is removed. `ProactiveReadOffer.cs:9` keeps an aim beside a read from triggering an unrelated habit lookup or planning call. | Replays assert no selector call. Holding all other recorded phases constant, removing that call would give about 9.15 s and 8.42 s. This is a projection, not a live latency measurement. The 12.498 s pick list made three model calls (2.853 + 4.692 + 3.725 s), including a repeated selection read; the 6.857 s window made two (2.350 + 3.903 s). Thus it was not solely provider variance. `QueryHabitsTool.cs:30` now directs reuse of returned candidates before ask. Offline tests cannot measure whether the provider avoids that extra call. The ten-second budget is unchanged. |
| 4: generic starting step | `SuggestBreakdownTool.cs:9` now requires a specific activity, one physical action and a named object; an empty day still needs an immediately doable action. The title and item descriptions carry this guidance, and `ProcessUserChatCommand.Offers.cs:84` appends it to the selected small-step scope. | The recorded starting-step replay preserves the provider's structured step and asserts the concrete-subject description. `SuggestBreakdown_IsAReadOperationWithReadScope` confirms the real catalog declares `IsMutation=false`, read scope and no confirmation. The supplied eval catalog also declares `writes:false`. No API write misclassification is reproduced on this base; the historical declaration used by window 01 is absent. Replays cannot prove the next generated action will be concrete. |
| Moderation | `ContentModerationService.cs:24` defines `RequestDeadline=2s`, applied to account resolution, HTTP send and body read; registration at `ServiceCollectionExtensions.AiServices.cs:40` uses the same deadline. | A stalled handler failed at the test's three-second ceiling before the fix and now returns unavailable after the two-second cancellation. The existing unavailable and caller-cancellation behaviors pass. No retry was added. |

## Test evidence

The unchanged tests were run before changing implementation or tests:

- `dotnet test tests/Orbit.Application.Tests -c Release --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~ProactiveOfferReplayTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProactiveWriteReplayTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProactiveProposalTests' --nologo`: 35 passed. author: forkni
body:
## Summary

Release v0.22.1: two fixes to the no-checks gate in `merge_pr.sh`.

- `91d7682` — `merge_pr.sh` counts only workflows that run on pull requests. v0.22.0 refused a PR with no checks whenever the repo had any active workflow. A repo with only a tag-push release workflow or a scheduled job could merge only with `--skip-checks`. The gate now reads each active workflow's YAML and refuses only when one mentions `pull_request`. A YAML that cannot be read counts as a pull-request workflow, so the gate still fails closed.
- `215e854` — end `gh` option parsing before a repo-controlled workflow name. A workflow `name:` that starts with a dash could be read as a `gh` flag in `cgw_workflow_may_run_on_pr`. The call is now `gh workflow view --repo <repo> --yaml -- <name>`. The `--` goes last because everything after it is positional.
- `05fa6e6` — changelog header renamed from `Unreleased` to `v0.22.1 (2026-11-01)`.

No other `gh` call passes a repo-controlled value as a positional argument.

Sorties (SPEC §6.11): a short auto-battle foray for Scions who stay off the expedition.

**How it works**
- A new `sortie` Year assignment names the Sortie's id. Four Sorties are in `content/sorties.json`, with a schema: Patrol the walls, Hunt the marsh, Escort a caravan, Dig the old mine.
- Each House gets one Sortie per Year, with up to four Scions or Retired. Recruits can't go.
- A Scion who is fielded on the expedition goes there instead.
- Sorties resolve as the expedition comes home, before the Reckoning.

**The fights**
- 1–2 gambit battles a level under the Year's band.
- Injuries are capped at Moderate: a new `Battle.injuryCap` turns a worse roll into the next milder result. Nobody dies on a Sortie.
- A lost battle ends the Sortie.

author: aseeras
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"aseeras"} -->
_Requested by **Alvin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GYuETi31dCTuo3Q4enep9g?thread=cmsg_01GYuETi31dCTuo3Q4enep9gP9Sf97SdZ97VpfwahzjwFT)_

## Summary

The assistant could already look up clients, appointments and dose ranges. But a veterinarian still had to open the right page for most daily work, and the assistant was only reachable from its own page. This PR makes it useful through a clinician's day, especially on a phone between house calls.

**New assistant tools** (`lib/agent/vet-tools.ts`)
- `get_my_day` lists the day's visits in time order. Each one has the client's address, a directions link, phone and visit notes, plus the pet's age, allergies, active problems and vaccines due within 30 days. Only the latest dose of each vaccine counts.
- `search_patient_history` reads the chart (SOAP notes, prescriptions, vaccines, labs, procedures, problems, vitals, allergies) through the same query as the patient history view. Corrected records are excluded.
- `list_medications` shows active prescriptions with refills remaining, plus allergies, to prepare a refill. The clinician records the refill in the chart.
- `get_my_todo` gathers unread client messages, texting-assistant drafts waiting for approval, labs to review or follow up, the clinician's unfinished SOAP drafts, and visit follow-ups that are due.
- `save_soap_draft` turns dictated notes into a SOAP **draft** through the existing draft lifecycle. It never finalizes. It refuses to overwrite a draft that already has content unless the clinician agrees, and it reports finalized notes and closed visits instead of changing them.

**Runner**
- Personal tools (`requiresStaffUser`) are only offered when a signed-in staff member runs the agent. API-key runs never see them.
- Each run tells the model the current date in the practice time zone, who is asking, and which patient or visit is on screen.
- The system prompt now asks for tappable links and says plainly that the agent cannot prescribe, record refills, or message clients. The output budget was raised so a full SOAP draft fits.
- Shared tool types moved to `tool-kit.ts` so tool groups can live in their own files without an import cycle.

**UI**
- An **Ask** button on every dashboard page for admins and veterinarians. It opens the assistant beside the page (full screen on phones) and knows the patient or visit in the URL.
- The chat is shared by the Agent page and the panel (`components/agent/agent-chat.tsx`). It adds browser dictation (Web Speech API, hidden where unsupported) and safe rendering of links and lists in replies, limited to in-app paths and http(s) with no innerHTML.
- When the assistant tries a change that wasn't allowed, the reply shows an **Allow this change** button. The "allow changes" box still turns off after one message.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring / code quality
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Other (describe):

## Target and Risk

- [ ] Feature/fix PR into `development`
- [ ] Release promotion from `development` into `staging`
- [ ] Production promotion from `staging` into `main`
- [ ] Changes auth, billing, migrations, tenant isolation, deployment, or secrets

Risk and blast radius: Only the assistant is affected. There are no schema or migration changes. All new queries are scoped to the practice and run inside the existing tenant transaction. The only new write is a SOAP draft, and it goes through the existing `saveAppointmentSoapDraft` lifecycle behind the per-run write gate and the `records:write` scope.

Rollback or recovery plan: Revert this PR. No data migration is involved, and any SOAP drafts already saved are ordinary drafts that can be edited or discarded in the visit screen.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm type-check` passes (`tsc --noEmit` for apps/web)
- [ ] `pnpm build` succeeds (left to CI)
- [ ] Tested manually in a local dev environment
- [ ] Added/updated E2E tests (if applicable)
- [ ] Preview or staging smoke test completed (for promotions)

The full web unit suite passes: 4615 passed, 45 skipped. New tests cover:
- tool registration and the read-only / write split
- input validation
- `save_soap_draft` outcomes: new draft, existing draft, replace at the current revision, finalized note, lifecycle error, role refusal
- latest-dose vaccine logic and the address / directions helpers
- the per-run context prompt
- staff-only tool gating in the runner
- URL-to-patient/visit hints, link safety, and the approval trigger

## Screenshots

Not captured. This needs a running instance with an AI provider key.

- [x] Code follows the existing style (TypeScript, Tailwind, tRPC patterns)
- [x] No hardcoded secrets or credentials

- [ ] Database changes use backward-compatible expand/contract sequencing (none)

- [x] New API endpoints include Zod validation and role-based access checks (new optional `context` input on `agent.run`; the route keeps its admin/veterinarian gate)
- [ ] Deployment, workflow, auth, billing, and migration changes have an explicit owner review

author: alisonjenkins
body: Supersedes #486. It has the same four commits, rebased onto main. While #486 was open, main took B253/V193 for the audio-session fix, so this PR uses **B254/V194** instead. The docs commit subject still says B253/V193, and the commit after it corrects the citations. #486 could not be rebased in place because force-pushing is blocked here. _Requested by **Alison**_ ## Problem `CookieBackfill` has been on main since 100ad143. It sets `JellyfinAuth` on any 2xx response to a request that authenticated by header **or by `?api_key=`**, and it overwrites a cookie that holds another token. That allows session fixation: - A page on a sibling `*.aliflix` host embeds ``'<img src="https://pharos/Items/…/Images/Primary?api_key=ATTACKER_TOKEN">'``. - The request is same-site, so the browser stores the Set-Cookie. - From then on, the victim's posters, subtitles and streams authenticate as the attacker. Separately, native clients receive a Set-Cookie with their own token on every response. ## Fix - `note_header_credential` records only a header token, never `api_key`. It uses `extract_header_token`, which is split out of `extract_token`. Every extractor tries the header first, so a header token still present after authentication is the one the store accepted. - The middleware sets the cookie only when the request carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` and has no `JellyfinAuth` cookie. It never overwrites another token's cookie; sign-in still replaces it. - Every decision is counted in `pharos_auth_cookie_backfill_total{outcome=set|held|not_same_origin|other_cookie|unencodable}`, which replaces `pharos_auth_cookie_backfilled_total{reason}`. - The bug and invariant are recorded as B254 and V194. ## Tests Each new test was checked by disarming its guard and watching it fail: - `an_api_key_never_sets_the_cookie`: same-site, cross-site and same-origin `` requests with `api_key`. - `a_header_token_from_anywhere_but_the_same_origin_gets_no_cookie`: requests with no `Sec-Fetch-Site`, and with `same-site`, `cross-site` and `none`. - `a_cookie_holding_another_token_is_kept`. `just test-changed` passed 1448/1448 on #486's base. On the rebase, only spec ids and comment citations changed. ## Security review No findings. CORS never sends `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, and page script cannot set `Sec-Fetch-*` headers. ## Out of scope An older path is fixed separately: attachments are served inline with the probed mime type and no `nosniff`. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01PqrfzJDAkduZ2bwMBxLSSs)_

author: loccalgmail
body:
## Qué agrega

Una sección **Informes** en el panel con siete informes. Todos se filtran por período (este mes, mes anterior, este año, año anterior u otro rango) y por cliente, y se descargan en PDF:

- **Ingresos:** lo cobrado según la fecha de cada pago, por medio de pago, por mes y con el detalle de recibos.
- **Margen:** lo cobrado menos el costo de lo revendido, en proporción a lo que se pagó de cada cargo (igual que "Percibido" en el tablero). Lo separa por origen y muestra lo que quedó a cuenta y los cobros de reventas sin costo cargado.
- **Deuda por antigüedad:** foto del día. Muestra los saldos por cliente en tramos de atraso y los cargos vencidos.
- **Clientes:** ranking por lo cobrado, con lo facturado y lo que debe hoy cada uno.
- **Abonos:** vigentes, mensual de los fijos, cobrado y adeudado por abono, variables a confirmar, altas y bajas.
- **Taller:** órdenes ingresadas y terminadas, horas, días promedio de resolución, service externo por proveedor y equipos que siguen afuera.
- **Presupuestos:** emitidos, aceptados, tasa de aceptación y montos.

## Cómo está hecho

- El cálculo está en `app/Support/Reports`, con una clase por informe que devuelve cifras y tablas con los valores sin formatear. Esa misma clase alimenta la pantalla (`app/Filament/Pages/Reports`) y el PDF (`pdf/report.blade.php`, con el diseño de los demás documentos).
- No suma paquetes ni requiere build: la pantalla usa los componentes y las variables de color de Filament (anda en modo oscuro y en el celular), y el PDF sale con dompdf.
- `pdf/layout.blade.php` ahora acepta estilos extra (`@yield('styles')`).
- Hay un grupo nuevo, "Informes", en el menú, y `NavigationTest` pasa a esperar 5 grupos.
- Publica la versión **2.5.0**: CHANGELOG y `config/app.php` actualizados, y la fase 8 anotada en `docs/plan-sistema-admin.md`.

## Pruebas

- `tests/Feature/ReportsTest.php`: los cálculos de cada informe, los períodos, los filtros en pantalla, y que cada página cargue y descargue su PDF.
- Suite completa: 209 tests pasan. `composer analyse` sin errores.

## Después del merge

Poner el tag `v2.5.0` en el commit de merge en `master`.

## **User description** ## 要什么 `internal/ui/framebudget_test.go` 的**满屏播放器**（153 次 / 3377 字节，上限 40 / 1900）和**播放条**（28 次 / 649 字节，上限 18 / 880）两档是红的——而**它们的虚高是测量台自己的问题**，不是界面的问题。 ## 🔴 根因：测量台绕过了 `pageInput()` 的每帧缓存 `pageInput()`（`internal/ui/page_inputs.go`）有一个**每帧缓存**： ```go func (s *Shell) pageInput() pageInput { if s.framePage.Input.Images != nil { return s.framePage.Input } return s.pageSeam().Input // ← 没有缓存时：重建整份 seam } ``` 而 `s.framePage` **只在 `Shell.View` 里被填**（`internal/ui/shell_view.go:101`）。 ⚠️ **测量台把 `Shell.View` 整个换掉了**（`withView`，`internal/ui/shelltest_test.go`）⇒ **`Shell.View` 压根不会被调到** ⇒ `s.framePage` 永远是空的 ⇒ **每一帧都重建整份 seam**。 实测（instrumented，`pageSeam()` 里数，改之前每一帧重建的次数）： ``` 满屏播放器 20 次 评论页 / 评论页·筛选开着 10 次 播放条 2 次 其余各档 0 次 （生产是 1 次） ``` ⇒ 而 **省掉重建之后各档的数有涨有跌**，方向恰恰和直觉相反： - 重建次数最多的那几档（满屏 / 评论页）**跌得最多**（满屏 153 → 39 次 / 3377 → 1556 字节） - 其余各档**反而涨了五次到六次**——因为它们**本来重建 0 次**（它们**不读**共享输入），改之后**多付了一次** `captureFramePage()`（每帧一次，六个状态 = 6 次 / 96 字节） ⚠️ **而那一次正是生产上一直要付的那一次**（生产走 `Shell.View`，那一路**一直**在取那一份）——**测量台之前压根没付这一笔**。⇒ **这不是回归，是测量台之前量到的是一台不存在的机器。** ## 做法 把取那一份的那一行抽成 `captureFramePage()`（`internal/ui/page_inputs.go`），两条路共用它——生产在 `Shell.View` 里调它，测量台在 `withView` 里也调它，而**测量台那一条照抄生产的做法**（画之前取，位置一样）。 ⚠️ **App 被摘掉时不动这一份**：迷你外壳有一条测试会临时把 App 摘掉，而那一次失败**要留在画的那一趟里面**（崩溃兜底要验的就是它）——所以 `s.app == nil` 时这一句什么都不做。 ## 顺带修好：下载记录页那一档压根没量过 `budgetDownloadsMount` 写的队列文件是 `"tasks": null`，而 `internal/service/download/migrate.go` 现在**拒绝 null**（`bdb47939` 改了队列文件的契约）⇒ 挂下载直接失败，**那一档从来没量过**。⇒ 改成 `[]queuedTask{}`（序列化成 `"tasks": []`）。 ## 十二档按实测重写 票 #613 的纪律：「**上限不能顺手改**——要单独立票：查清多出来的字节是什么，要么让它便宜下来，要么重测基线并写清新的数。」⇒ **这一票就是那一张**：十二档的基线与上限全部按实测重写，每档都写清实测值、为什么是这个数、余量为什么是这个数；文件头那张「冷跑 / 热跑」的表也跟着重写。 | 档 | 冷跑（实测） | 热跑（实测） | 新上限 | |---|---|---|---| | 首页列表 | 54 / 1420 | 54 / 1420 | 60 / 1800 | | 播放条 | 22 / 553 | 22 / 553 | 28 / 880 | | 队列抽屉 | 39 / 560 | 39 / 560 | 45 / 800 | | 满屏播放器 | 39 / 1556 | 39~40 / 1553~1639 | 47 / 2100 | | 稍后再看网格 | 56 / 760 | 56~57 / 765~868 | 64 / 1100 | | 设置开关 | 9 / 152 | 9 / 152 | 14 / 200 | | 迷你播放器 | 41 / 945 | 41 / 945 | 47 / 1500 | | 迷你播放器歌词卷帘 | 59 / 1617 | 59 / 1617 | 69 / 2500 | | 评论页 | 23 / 616 | 23~24 / 616~654 | 29 / 900 | | 评论页·筛选开着 | 23 / 616 | 23~24 / 619~645 | 29 / 900 | | 关注页 | 62 / 2297 | 62~64 / 2297~2376 | 76 / 3000 | | 下载记录页 | 306 / 18064 | 307~308 / 18102~18164 | 360 / 22000（不变） | ⚠️ **评论页那两档的下限从 28/35 降到 11**：填上缓存之后它们**真的画得少了**（缓存本来就省东西）⇒ 那不是回归，而下限要按新的实测重定——它们要防的那个回归（每帧重排正文）是 117 次，仍然超得掉上限。 ⚠️ **播放条那残差 4 次不是「三枚带数字的键」**：那一档的夹具里那首歌**还没有 `ArchiveCounts()`**（零 = 「没有这个数」= 不画），所以数字那一格压根没建（实测：把那三枚键整个去掉，那一档仍然是 22 / 553）⇒ 是**上限按旧基线定的**（票 #618 加了第四枚键时定的），按实测重定即可。 ## 验证 - `go build -trimpath -p 4 ./...` —— 通过 - `go vet -trimpath -p 4 ./...` —— 通过 - `go test -p 4 $(go list ./... | grep -v '/internal/ui$')` —— 全过 - `GOGC=10 go test ./internal/ui/ -count=3 -timeout 5m -run 'TestEachScreenStaysInsideItsFrameBudget'` —— 连跑三遍全绿 ## ⚠️ 已知不在本票范围 `TestTheFramesWhileSwitchingTabsCostNoMoreThanTwoPages`（`internal/ui/homepage_transition_test.go`）**单独跑是绿的、跟别的测试一起跑才红**（顺序依赖）。它**既没被这一票修好，也没被这一票弄坏**——另立一票查。 ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Align frame-allocation checks with normal screen drawing** ### What Changed - Performance checks now measure each screen with the same shared state used during normal drawing, avoiding inflated counts from rebuilding it repeatedly. - Updated frame budgets for all 12 screens to match the corrected measurements. - Fixed the download-page test data so its performance check can load and run. ### Impact `✅ Fewer false performance-test failures` `✅ Accurate full-player and comments-page frame checks` `✅ Reliable download-page performance checks`

body:
## ⚠️ Antes do merge

Rode o `supabase/setup.sql` **desta branch** no SQL Editor do Supabase. Se o merge vier antes, a tela "Divulgar serviços" dá erro ao salvar. Os dados não se perdem.

## O que muda

- **Banco de dados (`supabase/setup.sql`):** a tabela `professionals` ganha as colunas `company_id` (ligada à empresa, única, apagada junto com a empresa) e `address`. As regras de insert e update agora exigem que, quando houver `company_id`, a empresa seja do próprio usuário (`is_company_owner`). O arquivo continua podendo ser rodado de novo sem perder dados.
- **Nova tela `#/divulgar` (empresa):** a empresa escolhe as categorias e escreve uma descrição, sem valor. As categorias são: Oficina mecânica, Autopeças, Assistência técnica, Pet shop, Barbearia, Oficina elétrica, Locação de equipamentos, Salão de beleza, TI e Outros. Nome, logo, telefone e endereço vêm do cadastro da empresa. Também há o botão "Parar de divulgar".
- **Painel e Serviços (empresa):** convite "Divulgar serviços" / "Editar divulgação".
- **Encontrar profissional:** etiqueta "Empresa", endereço no lugar do preço, link "Ver empresa", filtro Todos / Autônomos / Empresas e as categorias de empresas no filtro.
- **Pedidos de serviço:** aceitam também as categorias de empresas.
- **Página pública da empresa:** quadro "Serviços oferecidos".
- **Dados da empresa:** quando a empresa atualiza o cadastro, a divulgação é atualizada junto.

## Como foi testado

- **Banco:** num Postgres 16 local, com stubs de `auth` e `storage`, rodei o `setup.sql` atual da `main` e depois o novo duas vezes seguidas, sem erros. Nas regras de segurança, a empresa A divulga a própria empresa (ok). A tentativa de trocar para a empresa de B foi bloqueada, B não conseguiu inserir com a empresa de A nem apagar a divulgação de A, e apagar a empresa apaga a divulgação junto.
- **Telas:** abri o painel, a tela de divulgar, a lista (computador e celular, com o filtro "Empresas") e a página da empresa num navegador automático com Supabase simulado. Não apareceu nenhum erro de JavaScript.

author: visvaya
body:
## What

The installed game on an iPhone drew its bottom buttons (for example "Wróć do oferty" in the squad drawer) under the home indicator. The drawer and the action bar already pad themselves with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, but iOS reports every safe-area inset as 0 unless the viewport asks for `viewport-fit=cover`, while a standalone app still draws to the bottom edge.

- `index.html`: `viewport-fit=cover`, so the existing inset rules (action bar, squad drawer, notification, eviction dialog) take effect.
- `.dd-root` keeps clear of the status bar and, in landscape, the notch (top, left and right insets; all 0 where there is no safe area). The `min-width: 768px` rule that reset its top padding to 0 is gone: it repeated the base value and would now drop the status-bar inset on a tablet.

## Tests

Local: lint, format, text and convention checks; the `smoke`, `focus-invariants` and `offline` e2e specs in Chromium and WebKit (57 passed, 1 skipped). No browser here emulates safe-area insets, so the effect itself needs a check on an iPhone (installed app and Safari, portrait and landscape).

body:
## Problem / Motivation **Goal:** An HTML file added to knowledge is indexed as readable text: `&` reads as `&`, and each heading, paragraph and list item sits on its own line. `html2text` is not a dependency, so `FileReader._read_html` always takes its regex fallback. That fallback strips tags but never decodes entities, and it collapses the whole page into one line. A page with `

Guide

Tom & Jerry

` is indexed as `Guide Tom & Jerry`. ## Why it matters Anyone who adds HTML docs to knowledge gets worse search. A search for `Tom & Jerry` misses the page, snippets show raw `<` codes, and the chunker sees one long block with no line breaks. ## Not a goal - Adding `html2text` (or any parser) as a dependency. - Rendering HTML as markdown (links, tables, emphasis). - Changing the `html2text` path when it is installed. ## What changed (motivation → approach → change) | Input | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `&`, `<div>`, ` ` | kept as codes | `&`, `
`, a space | | `

`, `

`, `
`, `
  • `, `

    `-`

    `, `` | one space | end a line | | a newline inside the HTML source | one space | one space | The regex fallback in `src/kiro_crew/knowledge/readers.py` collapses source whitespace first, marks block tags as line breaks, strips the other tags, and only then decodes entities. Decoding last means an escaped `<b>` in the page stays as the text `` and is never stripped as a tag. Empty lines are dropped. ## Backwards compatibility Compatible: the reader accepts the same files; only the text it returns for HTML on the fallback path is cleaner. Removes nothing: no key, path, record or reader is taken away. ## Tests `test/test_knowledge_html_reader.py` forces the regex fallback and checks entity decoding, an escaped tag staying text, block tags ending lines, source newlines staying spaces, inline tags (`pre`, `brand`) staying inline, and script/style bodies dropped. Proof: PROVEN test/test_knowledge_html_reader.py::test_entities_decode_to_their_characters, test/test_knowledge_html_reader.py::test_an_escaped_tag_stays_as_text, test/test_knowledge_html_reader.py::test_block_tags_end_a_line, test/test_knowledge_html_reader.py::test_source_newlines_are_whitespace (head f4a8670d4142) Related knowledge suites (`test_knowledge.py`, `test_knowledge_formats_parity.py`, `test_folder_watcher.py`, `test_dashboard_file_io.py`) pass, plus flake8, isort, mypy and the flake-pattern ratchet. ## Manual verification N/A — unit coverage sufficient: the change is a pure text transform, and the tests read real `.html` files through `FileReader`. ## Related Issues Fixes #27591 ## Sibling sweep Swept: git grep -nE "<\[\^>\]\+>|<\[\^>\]\*>" -- src/ Sibling: src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/artifacts_parts/library_reads.py:74 -- not affected -- strips tags from markdown artifact previews, not the knowledge index Sibling: src/kiro_crew/messaging/markup.py:47 -- not affected -- trims edge thinking tags, keeps the body as written Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/format.py:1145 -- not affected -- trims the wrapper tags of a block for Slack, no entity text ## Pattern harvest Not generalizable: a hand-rolled HTML-to-text fallback in one reader; no other site turns HTML into indexed text. ## Checklist - [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`) - [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality - [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

First step of « private trackers through qBittorrent ». A torrent from a private tracker (C411) pasted as a magnet never starts in TorLink: qBittorrent won't serve the metadata of a private torrent ([libtorrent `ut_metadata.cpp`](https://github.com/arvidn/libtorrent/blob/RC_2_0/src/ut_metadata.cpp): "don't add this extension if the torrent is private"), and private trackers only allow known clients, never WebTorrent. So Mira will drive the real qBittorrent, under its own profile.

This PR is Core only (nothing calls it yet):
- `Bencode.ReadFile`: a .torrent's info hash, name, size and private flag.
- `QBittorrentSettings`: the keys Mira writes into `qBittorrent.ini` (`.conf` outside Windows): Web UI on 127.0.0.1 behind a PBKDF2 password Mira picks, legal notice accepted, started hidden in the notification area, update check off. Every other line is kept. Downloads folder and port go through `app/setPreferences`.
- `QBittorrentClient`: sign-in (again on 403), add a magnet or a .torrent under the `Mira` category, list, files, pause/resume (`stop`/`start` on 5.x, `pause`/`resume` on 4.x), delete.
- `QBittorrentDownloads`: its states in the downloads page's terms.

Tests: the `.torrent` reader, ini merging, the PBKDF2 format and state mapping, plus an end-to-end run against the real `qbittorrent-nox` (Ubuntu's 4.6.3, installed by the `portable` job, `MIRA_QBITTORRENT`). That run covers Mira's profile and password, a wrong password refused, a private .torrent checked and seeding, and a magnet paused, resumed and deleted. Passed locally: 252/252.

author: bin913
body:
### PR Category

Operator, OP Test

### Type of Change

Bug Fix

### Description

ATen accepts an unbatched `(C, D, H, W)` input for `avg_pool3d` and returns a 4D tensor, but both FlagGems wrappers unpacked five dimensions unconditionally:

```
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 5, got 4)
```

The forward and the backward wrapper both raised for a valid unbatched call.

Promote a 4D input (and its matching 4D `grad_output`) to a batch of one and restore the original rank on every return path, including the empty-output early returns. A 5D `grad_output` paired with a 4D input is rejected explicitly instead of silently unpacking the wrong dimensions. The numerical kernels and the batched code path are untouched — the promotion is metadata only (`unsqueeze` / `squeeze`).

Scope: this PR fixes the shared implementation (`src/flag_gems/ops/avg_pool3d.py`), which is what the issue reproduces on. The vendor-local wrappers under `_metax`, `_iluvatar`, `_hygon`, `_sunrise` and `_cambricon` repeat the same five-dimension assumption and need the same rank handling, but I cannot run those backends from this environment, so they are left for their owners. Kunlunxin already supports unbatched input and is unchanged. Discloses overlap with PR #7799 (which proposes the same change for those vendor copies and supersedes the pooling part of #7795); this implementation and its tests were written independently and validated on the shared path.

### Issue

- Fixes #7797
- Related: #7738, #7743 (same ATen compatibility gap reported on MetaX)

### Progress

- [ ] Change is properly reviewed (1 reviewer required, 2 recommended).
- [x] Change is responded to an issue.
- [x] Change is fully covered by a UT.

### Validation

Environment: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, Python 3.12, torch 2.10.0+cu128, Triton 3.6.0, base `master` 1b9ccb17484ec5041ce3d7f4f5474c9a994702c0.

Issue reproducer:

```python
x = torch.randn(2, 7, 9, 11, device="cuda")     # (C, D, H, W)
flag_gems.avg_pool3d(x, 2, 2)                    # before: ValueError, after: (2, 3, 4, 5)
flag_gems.avg_pool3d_backward(grad, x, 2, 2, 0, False, True, None)  # before: ValueError, after: x.shape
```

`tests/test_avg_pool3d.py` — new unbatched forward and backward cases over all ten existing pooling configurations and all float dtypes, plus a rank-mismatch regression:

| source | result |
| --- | --- |
| unfixed | 60 failed, 61 passed |
| fixed | 121 passed |

The 60 new failures are exactly the new unbatched cases (the batched cases pass in both runs, so the new tests are not vacuous).

### Performance

No performance claim. The unbatched path uses metadata-only `unsqueeze` / `squeeze` and the existing kernels; the batched path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

author: roryprimrose
body:
## Approved outcome

Complete the admitted NOTICES-SCHEDULED-QUIET-HOURS operation within controllable voice interaction and permissioned conversation notices: review and confirm one device-local weekly speech-only quiet interval, preserve its visual completion notice, and never replay suppressed speech when quiet ends ([owning contract](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/Design/Proactive_Interaction.md#scheduled-proactive-speech-quiet-hours)).

## Placement and scope

The host owns explicit zone interpretation, original-channel/session admission, atomic saved intent, trusted audit, no-replay receipts and output joining. This is not a tool, MCP service, model timer or skill scheduler. It reuses the existing completion owner and shared preference store rather than timer-toggling run-only RoutineQuiet ([configuration owner](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/src/Kora.Application/Configuration/QuietHoursConfigurationService.cs), [completion admission](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/src/Kora.Application/Interaction/ConversationCompletionVoiceNotices.cs)).

No reminders, task dispatch/scheduling, background fetch, new observation source, microphone/listening consent, general proactive enablement, call-policy relaxation, requested-answer suppression or hidden questions/approvals. Existing provider qualification and explicit run consent remain authoritative ([scope and operation](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/docs/conversation-notices.md#scheduled-proactive-speech-quiet-hours)).

## User-visible behavior

Native Settings exposes explicit ordered days, 24-hour start/end and installed zone ID, review, separate confirmation and inspection. The standard cog Reset prepares Off for its own confirmation; it does not save immediately. Exact typed and current-name activated voice share the same operation and original-channel review. Model-origin changes are not admitted ([native and typed/voice owner](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/src/Kora.Application/ViewModels/MainViewModel.QuietHours.cs), [grammar](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/src/Kora.Application/Configuration/QuietHoursCommand.cs)).

```text
set notices.quiet-hours to weekly Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri 09:00 17:00 UTC
confirm notices.quiet-hours
get notices.quiet-hours
reset notices.quiet-hours
confirm notices.quiet-hours
```

Default/reset is Off. Start is inclusive, end exclusive; an overnight interval belongs to its starting day. Injected UTC is converted into the selected zone at every actual synthesis and playback boundary. Repeated DST local hours stay quiet inside the interval; skipped times create no replay. UTC rollback holds proactive speech until its watermark is reached ([schedule](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/src/Kora.Core/Configuration/QuietHoursSchedule.cs), [boundary adapter](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/src/Kora.Windows/Audio/WindowsTextToSpeechService.cs)).

Visual Presented/fatigue receipts remain unchanged while observed completion IDs are consumed before speech admission. Schedule/control changes invalidate queued output; cancellation does not claim release before the actual owned output joins. Required questions/approvals and ordinary requested speech remain independent ([behavioral regressions](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/tests/Kora.Application.UnitTests/Interaction/ConversationCompletionVoiceNoticesTests.cs), [requested-speech and decision regressions](https://github.com/roryprimrose/Kora/blob/4e9bbc1ffbd146c7c12f3f5954d4a8fffdd8f6a3/tests/Kora.Application.UnitTests/ViewModels/MainViewModelTests.QuietHours.cs)).

Local validation used SDK `10.0.403` under the repository's `10.0.401`/latest-patch policy. Missing assets were resolved by locked restore through the machine-required feed; no package manifests, lockfiles, source configuration, authentication or administrator settings changed. author: callumalpass
body:
## Problem

Native Core compared an app's seed type (`mode: seed`) with the pack's desired document and `upgrade_from` baselines **byte for byte**, and merged only against a recorded `origin_digest`. Collections set up by the legacy installer (mdbase-rs `type_pack.rs`) have no `origin_digest` in `mdbase.lock.yaml`, and their seed files are often re-serialised by another writer. Core then kept the seed with the reason "no upgrade baseline applies", the SDK reported `setup_unresolved`, and TaskNotes stopped at "Setup can't finish" with only "Try again".

## Change

All of it is in `runtime/crates/core/src/packs.rs` `plan_seed`, the one place seeds are compared:

1. **Semantic comparison.** `same_type_document` compares parsed frontmatter (map order ignored, `1` ≠ `1.0`) plus the exact body. A live seed equal to the desired document is current, and Core records its origin (lock-only write). A live seed equal to a baseline upgrades normally to the exact desired bytes.
2. **Origin inference.** When there is no origin, or an unknown one, Core tries each baseline as the merge base with the existing `merge_type`. It tries the nearest first (fewest leaf differences from live), with manifest order (newest first) breaking ties. It accepts a clean merge only if the result, staged with the pack's managed resources, still has no errors and implements every `(contract, version)` the desired type implements. The upgrade records `origin_digest`. "Nearest first" rather than strictly newest first: for the real TaskNotes `task.md`, the newest baseline merges cleanly but would carry a stale `x-tasknotes-generator.managed_fields` entry. The nearest baseline is the one the file was actually created from.
3. `merge_type` merges equal-length lists item by item (needed for `implements`) and emits only the changed paths via the shared `writer::diff`, moved from `plan/records.rs`. That gives one diff and one equality (`Value::same`) instead of two private copies.

When nothing merges, the seed stays preserved with a reason, as before. The follow-up PR adds the explicit "Use this app's version" choice for that case.

## Tests

- Core (`crates/core/tests/packs.rs`):
  - a re-serialised desired seed is current and records its origin;
  - a re-serialised baseline seed upgrades to the exact desired bytes;
  - a customised seed with no origin merges against the inferred baseline, keeps the customisation and is then current;
  - an unmergeable seed is preserved with a reason;
  - a clean merge that drops `implements` is refused.
- Conformance (`crates/conformance/tests/pack_schema_resources.rs`): the published TaskNotes rc.19 packs (fixtures are type definitions only) with the field-reported legacy files.
  - `tasknotes-scratch-image.md` and `tasknotes-scratch.md` are current, and their origins are recorded.
  - `task.md` upgrades from the `2b6016c3` baseline, keeping its custom status and priority colours.
  - The reinstall is current.
- The spec seed-upgrade conformance cases still pass, including unknown-origin and unlisted-origin preserved.

author: macalinao
body:
Ships the delivery items from the roadmap's "Not yet" lists (docs/delivery.md, docs/assembly.md).

## Chapters and cover art in the MP4 (`mp4-atom`)
- `ffcine_delivery::mp4`: writes chapters and a cover into a finished MP4 without re-encoding. Chapters go in as a Nero `udta/chpl` list and a QuickTime chapter track (`tref/chap` + disabled `text` track), as ffmpeg's muxer writes them. The cover goes in as `udta/meta/ilst/covr` (JPEG/PNG). The file is rewritten once (`ftyp`, new `moov`, chapter `mdat`, then every other box byte for byte), and chunk offsets (`stco`/`co64`) are moved along with it, so the result is also `+faststart`. Re-tagging replaces the previous chapters and cover.
- `ffcine tag MP4 [--timeline T] [--cover FILE|TIME] [--clear]`; `ffcine render` writes the timeline's chapter markers and `--cover` into the master (`--no-chapters` turns this off).
- Verified with ffprobe: `-show_chapters` lists the chapters (also with `chpl` stripped, from the QuickTime track alone), the cover shows up as an attached picture, `framemd5` is identical before and after, and `-xerror` decodes cleanly (`crates/ffcine-delivery/tests/mp4_ffprobe.rs`, on synthetic test patterns).

## Review renders from proxies
- `ffcine render --profile review`: 720p HEVC NVENC p1, with every shot decoded from its proxy. That is the camera's `.LRF` beside the clip, or else one made once into `<cache>/proxy/` (NVDEC + `scale_cuda` + NVENC, with a CPU fallback) and keyed by the source's fingerprint.
- Review segments are keyed apart from preview/master. The other profiles' keys are unchanged, because `proxies` only enters the recipe when it's on.

## Also
- `grade --deliver` outputs (`.mp4`/`.mov`) are made `+faststart` (the delivery.md "Not yet" item for the phone copy).
- mp4-atom 0.17 declares rust-version 1.88. The workspace stays at 1.85: raising it turns on newer clippy lints in other crates. Builds use the dev shell's stable toolchain.

## Summary by Sourcery

Add chapter and cover-art metadata to MP4 deliveries and introduce proxy-based review renders for faster edit review.

New Features:
- Add MP4 tagging for timeline chapters and JPEG/PNG cover art without re-encoding, including the new `ffcine tag` command and render integration.
- Add a 720p review render profile that uses camera or cached proxies with GPU and CPU fallback support.

Bug Fixes:
- Make delivered MP4 and MOV outputs faststart-compatible for progressive playback.

Enhancements:
- Preserve existing MP4 metadata while replacing chapters and cover art idempotently, without changing media packets.

Documentation:
- Document MP4 chapters, cover art, faststart delivery, and proxy-based review renders.

Tests:
- Add unit and ffprobe integration coverage for MP4 tagging, metadata replacement, packet preservation, faststart layout, and proxy rendering.

Chores:
- Update delivery dependencies and workspace documentation for MP4 metadata and review rendering.

author: amazingkman
body:
Executes [planning/WO-006-sigma-calibration-and-decorrelation-diagnostics.md](planning/WO-006-sigma-calibration-and-decorrelation-diagnostics.md), including Addendum 1. The report is [reports/2026-11-wo006/report.md](reports/2026-11-wo006/report.md), and the provenance log is at the end of the WO file.

**All three pre-registered criteria failed.** None was changed after seeing results. These stay on record as failures. The findings below still move WO-003 forward. Everything here is synthetic.

## Results

| Criterion | Verdict | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration, A1 and two-layer | FAIL | A1 coverage 0.997 (limit 0.98); two-layer 0.936; confident wrong sign 0 |
| Directional, L = 4.3 | FAIL | Slope ratio 0.82-1.10 passes at 15-90 degrees; wrong sign up to 0.206 fails; 0 degrees not estimable |
| Gain prediction | FAIL | 61% of 100 cells within 0.25: L = 8 85%, L = 4.3 42%, L = 2 0% (69% of those patches flagged) |

## What was learned

- **The directional estimate removes the sign reversal.** The full estimate reads -0.43 to 1.04 across the same angles.
- **What remains is a Sigma problem, not a bias problem.** Wrong signs at L = 4.3 fall from 20.9% at 1 degree to 1.5% at 10 degrees.
- **No single kappa and f can meet the calibration criterion:** 0 of 16,261 grid points, even on the calibration split.
- **Sigma is about 3.5 times too small under decorrelation,** even where the slope is unbiased. A constant cannot fix that.
- **Processed noise shrinks and never reverses the gain,** as DR-013 predicted. It does break the white-noise calibration at SNR 2: A1 coverage 0.81.
- **`gain_map` separates noise from material on these synthetic pairs,** using void layers. The void correction identifies the cause; it does not improve the gain prediction.

kappa = 2.95, f = 0 were fitted on seeds 0-4 and committed in `d565324` before seeds 5-9 ran.

## Decisions for the Planner

1. **Fit strata (my departure from the WO).** I fitted on A1 and two-layer and reported realistic. Fitting all three gives f = 0.57, and any f above 0.51 means no estimate can ever reach significance. Please confirm or change this.
2. **Status of kappa = 2.95, f = 0,** given that no pair can pass the criterion.
3. **Wording of the directional criterion.** "Every fibre angle" is undefined at 0 degrees, where the truth along the observed direction is about zero.
4. **A data-driven Sigma** from pair-shift scatter looks like the next step. It is new method, so I did not try it.
5. **`docs/method-lpsf.md`** should adopt the 2-D gain tensor, which corrects WO-002's formula between the principal directions.

## Also in this PR

- The separate `docs:` commit requested before this WO: R3 now names `FIGURES.md`, a DR-010 addendum on the email, and the identity scan flags absolute root and temp paths.
- `integrate` now uses calibrated Sigma, as DR-011 item 4 requires. The worst A1 bump RMSE is 0.048 voxels, against 0.049 with raw Sigma.
- `directional` stays off by default until the WO-003 pilot decides. The other frozen WO-002 defaults are unchanged.

## Checks

261 tests, 17 selftest checks, ruff, and the security scan all pass locally. Four new figures are registered in `FIGURES.md`.

Patch-level tables are 8-12 MB and are not committed; `report.md` section 9 gives their SHA-256 hashes, and the seeds rebuild them. The figure palette reuses WO-002's and was not re-validated, because the validator needs `node`.

author: charliermarsh
body:
## Summary

Boxed matches can look up a single named group, but calling `groupdict()` raises `AttributeError`. CPython’s original regex test uses that method to collect the values of two named captures.

We now walk the match’s public capture slots in declaration order and use the existing group lookup to populate a fresh dictionary. For example, `re.match(rb"(?P<x>a)(?P<y>b)?", b"a").groupdict(default=False)` returns `{"x": b"a", "y": False}`. Unnamed groups and internal engine captures are excluded.

author: zhangqiu-ai
body:
## 摘要

把思玥 iOS 驅動器目前使用的 Codex 分支（18 個 commit，0.3.76 之後）經審查併入 `main`，並修正審查發現的、對未啟用 UIKit 探針的目標預設啟用的行為改變。發版 v0.3.77。

維護者已選擇「先審查合併（A）」：思玥的 runner 改以 `main` 擷取原型後，與 Codex 分支驅動器的文字讀法不一致，VER-1793577119097-bd64056b 的 207 個場景中有 202 個結構比對失敗。

## 帶入的 Codex 工作

- UIKit 補充觀測（`--uikit-probe-context`）：文字所有權、圖層順序、flattened parent 範圍、settling 預算、公開編輯選單換頁。
- iOS 響應式擷取（`--orientation`、`--frame app-window`、`--appearance`）與短效 deep link 啟動準備。
- `scroll-to` 的 `value:"start"`／`value:"end"`。
- PNG EXIF 方向。
- `fill`／`clear` 之後接 `scroll-to`／`wait-for` 時保留鍵盤。
- 原生控制項文字只取可見 `staticText` 後代。
- Web 零面積裁切文字。

## 審查修正（本 PR 的 9939f57）

獨立審查找到三個預設啟用、會影響非思玥原生目標的回歸，已修正：

1. **原型的 `.sr-only` 文字**
   - 原本：Codex 分支在所有目標上排除原型裡零面積裁切的無障礙文字。未啟用探針的 iOS 與 Android 擷取仍以無障礙 label 讀圖示按鈕（「Close」），兩邊會不一致。
   - 現在：原型的 `text` 照舊包含這段文字，另外回報不含它的 `visibleText`。只有驅動器回應帶 `textSemantics: "visible"` 時，T1 才改比 `visibleText`；目前只有探針驗證通過的 iOS 擷取會帶這個欄位。
   - Web 與 Electron 目標回到與 0.3.76 相同。
2. **控制項文字**
   - Android 的 `CheckBox`、`RadioButton`、`Switch` 畫出的 text 被丟掉（「Sign in Remember me」變成「Sign in」）。現在把畫出的 text 視為父容器讀得到的文字子節點；控制項錨點本身與 Web checkbox 一樣沒有文字。
   - iOS 分段控制的分段按鈕標題被丟掉（「Stats Day Week Month」變成「Stats」）。現在會讀到各分段標題。
3. **iOS `fill`／`clear`**
   - 原本：一律長按後點「Select All」。中文模擬器、隱藏的編輯選單、錨點在外層包裝時都會失敗。
   - 現在：未啟用探針時先用刪除鍵清空，只有留下文字時才改用「Select All」；啟用探針時維持 Codex 分支的流程。

## 驗證

- 用思玥 3,080 份歷史擷取重算錨點文字：Codex 分支與本 PR 完全相同（0 個差異）。對照組 `main`（0.3.76）與 Codex 分支差 33 個錨點，可見這個比對抓得到差異。思玥走探針路徑，`textSemantics` 的切換由構造保證與 Codex 分支相同。
- `npm run check` 通過。
- `npm test`：修正後 1,143 個測試中原本 3 個失敗，都是以原始碼字串檢查舊流程的測試，已更新。全量重跑結果見 CI。
- `npx playwright test --project=chromium`：250/251，唯一失敗的 Swift 片段編譯測試已修正並重跑通過。這組測試包含真實 `CaptureTests.swift` 的 iOS SDK typecheck。
- CI 第一輪找到兩個 Codex 測試在 Linux 上的問題，已在 5b178f3 修正：
  - 零面積裁切的 Chromium guard 原本在單元測試裡啟動瀏覽器，但 CI 的單元測試工作不安裝瀏覽器，已移到 `tests/e2e/web-clipped-text-guards.spec.js`；
  - 一個 Swift 測試寫死了 `/private/tmp`，已改用系統暫存目錄，並與其他 Swift 輔助測試一樣只在 macOS 執行。
- CI 第二輪只剩 `tests/e2e/web-clipped-text.spec.js` 的「遮罩前後截圖位元組相等」在 Linux 失敗，已在 b16f61d 修正：
  - 兩輪暫時診斷（857a8c1、118b7c6，已移除）顯示，引擎單獨擷取、只套遮罩、只加凍結樣式在 Linux 都是 0 像素差異；
  - 只有測試頁同時帶自己的 adoptedStyleSheet、MutationObserver 與 ariaSnapshot 時，可見段落一個字形邊緣像素變動 1–5 階，屬反鋸齒重繪，不是遮罩殘留；
  - 改為解碼像素、容許每通道最多 8 階；本機量測遮罩若殘留並遮住可見內容，差異為 137–255。
- 新增測試：
  - Android 畫出的控制項文字；
  - iOS 分段控制；
  - 依 `textSemantics` 選擇原型文字；
  - Web `text`／`visibleText` 兩種讀法；
  - 非探針路徑的清空 fallback。
- **NOT_RUN**：
  - 真實 iOS 模擬器上的擷取。依約定不碰模擬器；思玥 runner 下一輪 `runner retry` 即為實測。
  - Android 模擬器實測。

## 需要維護者注意

UIKit 探針寫死了思玥 App 的名稱與版本：
- `SIYUE_CAPTURE_PROBE_*` 環境變數；
- `Library/Caches/SiyueCaptureProbe`；
- React Native 0.86.3；
- `main.jsbundle`。

這部分只在明確 opt-in 時生效，已在 `docs/native-targets.md` 列為待辦。其他 App 要接入前需先改為可設定。

author: gitrasheed
body:
`nns_reg(smooth=True)` was an approximation of `stats::smooth.spline`, up to 8.8% off R. `dy_dx` stepped by the bandwidth's position instead of its value and rewrote boundary estimates after the fit. `nns_diff` solved for h far more tightly than R's `uniroot`, so it hit `max_iter` and reported non-convergence where R converges. We port R's algorithms for all three.

Stacked on #150; merge with a merge commit.

## Changes

- `smooth=True` builds the penalty with R's `sgram` formula (constant .3330), thins knots like `.nknots.smspl` once nx > 49, groups x within R's tie tolerance and solves with a banded Cholesky like `sslvrg`. Before, every one of 8 smooth cases differed from R, with Point.est off by up to 8.8%. Now 7 of 8 agree to 1e-10 relative and the last to 3e-8, a gap that comes from a copula value sitting on a knife edge. `nns_reg(smooth=True, order="max")` at n = 1000 goes from 119 s to 0.4 s. Every `smooth=True` result changes, and with it `dy_dx` and the smoothed `nns_arma` path.
- `dy_dx(eval_point=...)` steps by the bandwidth value, and at min(x) or max(x) it uses the one-sided slope with a NaN second derivative, as R does. For y = x^3 on 500 uniform points at (-1.5, 0, 0.5, 1.5), Python gave (3.859, 3.223, 3.282, 3.900) against R's (3.708, 3.774, 3.679, 3.719) and now agrees to 2e-8. Below n = 16, where R's `dy.dx` fails, the port uses the distinct bandwidths.
- `dy_dx` without `eval_point` raises "eval_point must be provided" instead of a copied data.table message. R's default call crashes too.
- `nns_diff` widens the bracket like `uniroot(extendInt = "yes")`, solves with a port of `R_zeroin2` at R's tolerance, and checks equal intercepts like `all.equal`. On 10 test functions, 8 differed from R before; all 10 now match every output field, including iterations and flags. The derivatives are slightly less accurate than before, because R's root is looser.

## Tests

Parity tolerances for smooth fits go from 5e-4/5e-5/5e-3 to 1e-10, with a new case above 49 regression points. `dy_dx` parity goes from 5e-3 to 1e-10, with random-x bandwidth cases (n = 30, 60, 250) and boundary eval points drawn on a 1/1024 grid so the cache keys are portable. `nns_diff` parity compares every field at 1e-12 on 11 cases. The parity cache encodes unpatched R 13.3.

## Review

GPT-6.1 Sol reviewed this slice and raised one finding, which we took: the inferred-step callback in `nns_diff` raised ZeroDivisionError at a zero step, where R's uniroot replaces the non-finite value and converges. The callback now returns NaN at h = 0, as R's 0/0 does: inferred h, iterations and converged go from NaN, 1, 0 to R's 8.5e-11, 32, 1. The fix commit has not been re-reviewed.

author: arcavenai
body:
One killed test run can leave a stopped tmux server behind, and the next `go test` of four packages then hangs in `TestMain` with `kill-server` clients spinning at full CPU. On a fleet host that read as four such clients at 100% CPU each for about three hours. This bounds the sweep's `kill-server` with a 5 s deadline, so the sweep skips a server it cannot stop and the run goes on.

Refs #805.

What changes: `sweepNames` in `internal/tmux/tmuxtest/sweep.go` runs `tmux -L <name> kill-server` through `exec.CommandContext` with a `killServerDeadline` of 5 s (a variable, so the test can shorten it). The context's default cancel is SIGKILL, so the client waiting on a stopped server ends with the deadline, and the server is skipped like any other the sweep cannot stop. A server that stays stopped costs each later run at most that deadline; this does not resume or kill it.

Not in this PR: sending SIGCONT to the stopped server first, which the issue also suggests. The deadline is the part that stops the hang; resuming is a separate choice about touching a process the sweep did not start.

Evidence:
- `TestSweepNamesGivesUpOnAStoppedServer` starts a scratch tmux server under a scratch `TMUX_TMPDIR`, reads its pid from the server itself, stops it with SIGSTOP, and calls `sweepNames` with a 500 ms deadline. It passes in 0.62 s. A watchdog fails the test, and resumes the server, if the sweep has not returned within 15 s, so the no-fix case is red and not a hang. The test signals only the pid it read.
- Mutant, applied uncommitted and restored with the file hash compared equal: the deadline removed (`WithTimeout` replaced by `WithCancel`). It failed in 10 of 10 separate processes, each with the watchdog message, and left no stopped test server behind.
- Run in a scratch home and TMPDIR, with no `MARVEL_*` variables and the codex binary off PATH.

Cost of merge: test support code only (`internal/tmux/tmuxtest`); no production package changes.

author: obany
body:
## 📝 Description

Adds a new `@3sixty/api-tenant-rest-client` package with a `TenantAdminRestClient` that implements `ITenantAdminComponent` over the tenant admin REST routes. To keep the client free of storage dependencies, the tenant request and response models move from `@3sixty/api-tenant-processor` to `@3sixty/api-models`, and a new route lets the client get a tenant by organization id with a single call. The create and update tenant routes are also fixed, as they rejected every request.

```typescript
const client = new TenantAdminRestClient({ endpoint: 'https://api.example.org' });
const tenantId = await client.create({ apiKey, label: 'node', organizationId: 'org-1' });
const tenant = await client.getTenantByOrganizationId('org-legacy', true);
```

## 🔄 Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] 📚 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Performance improvement
- [x] ♻️ Code refactoring
- [ ] 📦 Dependencies update

## 🛠️ Changes Made

- Added the `@3sixty/api-tenant-rest-client` package with `TenantAdminRestClient`, which makes a single call per method to the `tenants` routes, with examples, and registered it in the release-please configuration, the root `README.md` and `docs/packages.md`
- Moved `ITenantCreateRequest`, `ITenantGetByApiKeyRequest`, `ITenantGetByIdRequest`, `ITenantGetByPublicOriginRequest`, `ITenantGetResponse`, `ITenantListRequest`, `ITenantListResponse`, `ITenantRemoveRequest` and `ITenantUpdateRequest` to `@3sixty/api-models`, with `@3sixty/api-tenant-processor` still re-exporting them so existing imports keep working
- Added `ITenantCreate` and `ITenantUpdate` to `@3sixty/api-models` and used them in `ITenantAdminComponent`, `TenantAdminService`, the request models and the client in place of the inline `Omit` and `Partial` types
- Widened `ITenantUpdateRequest` `body` to `ITenantUpdate` to match `ITenantAdminComponent.update`
- Added the `GET tenants/organization/:organizationId` route with an optional `includeLegacy` query parameter and the `ITenantGetByOrganizationIdRequest` model, calling `getTenantByOrganizationId` with the tenant reader authorization
- Fixed `tenantCreate` and `tenantUpdate`, which guarded the request body with `Guards.stringValue` and so rejected every request, to use `Guards.objectValue`
- Fixed `tenantUpdate` to update the tenant identified by the path `id`, which takes precedence over any `id` in the body

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] I have tested this change manually
- [ ] Testing not required for changes

author: mithr4ndir
body:
## What

Grafana dashboard **pfSense Firewall Logs** (uid `pfsense-firewall-logs`, folder Network) over the pfSense syslog stream that #249 started shipping to Loki (`{host="core.home.arpa"}`).

| Row | Panels |
|---|---|
| Overview | lines/min, blocks/min, gateway alarms, sshguard events, log volume by daemon, blocks by interface |
| Firewall | top 10 blocked destination ports, top 10 blocked sources, blocks by protocol, parsed IPv4 TCP/UDP block log |
| Daemons | everything except filterlog (DHCP, OpenVPN, gateway alarms, sshguard), raw stream |

Variables: datasource, daemon (static list, since `appname` is a parsed field and not a Loki label), interface, action, source IP regex, destination port regex, search.

Also raises Loki `limits_config.max_query_series` from 500 to 5000.

## Why the Loki change

The top-N panels aggregate by source IP and destination port. Measured over the last hour of real filterlog data: 2806 lines, 1031 distinct sources, 1010 distinct ports. Loki rejected the 1h queries with `maximum of series (500) reached for a single query`. At 5000 the panels work for ranges up to roughly 4h, and the panel descriptions say so. Instant-query series are a single sample each, so this is not the memory lever that mattered in #237 (that was bytes scanned over 3h and 24h regex queries). loki-0 sits at 373Mi of its 2Gi limit.

## Verification

- Every panel expression replayed against Loki at 192.168.1.231 with variables at defaults: all return data (gateway alarm and sshguard counters return 0, which is correct for a quiet hour). Top-N expressions confirmed valid at a 15m range; they fail at 1h only because of the 500 cap this PR raises.
- IPv6 leak caught and fixed: pattern-parsed IPv6 lines put the destination (`ff02::1`) where IPv4 has the protocol, so the source and protocol panels now filter `ipver="4"`.
- `kubectl kustomize infrastructure/monitoring/grafana-dashboards` and `infrastructure/monitoring` build. 21 ConfigMaps, all dashboard uids unique. Data key `pfsense-logs.json` is unique.
- `helm template` of the loki chart renders `max_query_series: 5000`.

## After merge

ArgoCD syncs the ConfigMap; the sidecar writes it and Grafana picks it up on its 30s poll (the sidecar reload call 401s, which is known and harmless). The Loki change restarts loki-0, so expect a brief ingestion gap; Vector buffers but does not backfill long outages.

Pre-existing, not touched: `kubernetes-cluster-overview` and `proxmox-cluster-overview` both use the data key `cluster-overview.json`. They land in different sidecar folders so they do not collide today.

author: chinmaymk
body:
## Problem

The ownership-count integration test added in #2294 fails on native Windows AMD64 and ARM64 before its fixtures run. It canonicalizes the repository root and derives the default stats target from it. Rust's Windows canonicalization adds a verbatim `\\?\` prefix, which reaches the nested `ring` build's GNU archiver; archive creation fails and the test receives exit 101 instead of the expected fixture-gate status.

Confirmed on main `846e899b775b1db57b07c8fdc0fced553ffe3960`, run 41373565601: [AMD64 job](https://github.com/manuscript-lang/manuscript/actions/runs/41373565601/job/125051023350), [ARM64 job](https://github.com/manuscript-lang/manuscript/actions/runs/41373565601/job/125051023353).

## Proposed change

Derive the repository root lexically from Cargo's already absolute manifest directory. Keep the default stats target as `target/leak-stats`, relative to the repository working directory, matching the production helper in `tools/lib.ms`. Pass explicit `LEAK_TARGET_DIR` overrides through unchanged.

All existing assertions and fixtures remain unchanged, including both Debug/Release executions, nonzero child status, successful cleanup, compilation failure and an unavailable compiler. This changes test setup only. No workflow, CI setting, dependency, runtime ABI or production gate behavior changes.

## Alternatives considered

Manually stripping Windows path prefixes adds unnecessary special cases for UNC and long-path forms. Selecting another archiver changes toolchain configuration to compensate for a path representation introduced by the test. Preserving Cargo's ordinary path and the existing relative target convention avoids that extra transformation.

## Testing

Existing permanent regression `count_gate_rejects_failed_children_even_with_zero_live_blocks` exercises the affected setup and retains every status/zero-live-block assertion.

On Linux, using fresh matching GNU/musl archives on base main `ffe89f573cbde83a40f0f66f21fcbd00cf4514fb`:

- Default stats directory: focused nextest passes, zero skips (110.971 s including runtime builds).
- Explicit absolute `LEAK_TARGET_DIR` override: the same regression passes, zero skips (36.524 s).
- `cargo clippy --locked -p ms-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `make repo-check` and `make licenses-check` pass.
- Independent read-only review is clear for working-directory/default/override behavior and unchanged assertions.

Native Windows execution of this candidate remains pending. This selected environment runs Linux; cross-compilation is not treated as native validation. This PR stays draft with auto-merge off under the merge hold. Coordinate one Windows AMD64/ARM64 batch with the other source repairs and inspect its actual tested revision, stats archive build and fixture results. No per-PR Windows dispatch was attempted, and no workflow file or CI setting was changed. The broader validation follow-up is #2296; shared guide/localhost and task-trace repairs remain with their existing owners.

Reconciliation: this alternative addresses the same demonstrated Windows canonical-root/GNU-archiver failure already owned by external #2343 at `9341aafabac2757ee791c1aa3b72ff4f2b2819a3`. That implementation strips the local verbatim prefix while preserving UNC; this alternative uses lexical parents and a relative default target. No additional demonstrated source defect requires a second fix. Closed unmerged as redundant, preserving the branch and external ownership. The central validation batch should use #2343. The Linux results above apply to this alternate implementation only and do not establish native Windows validation of either implementation.

author: littlehenderson
body:
Lantern maps Rust apps the same way it maps Python, TypeScript and Go. Built on top of #33 (Go), so this PR's base is the Go branch until #33 merges.

- `lantern/rust_frontend.py`: crates from every `Cargo.toml` (workspaces), modules from file paths and inline `mod`, functions, `impl` blocks, traits. Calls resolved by `name`, `use` (`crate::`/`self::`/`super::`/child modules/`use x::*`), `assoc` (`Type::f()`), `receiver-type` (parameters including axum's `State(state): State<Arc<T>>` patterns, struct fields, `let`, return types — types are canonicalised so a field declared in one module resolves from any other), `trait` (`dyn Trait` / `impl Trait` / `T: Trait` → one `possible` edge per `impl Trait for X`), `callback`. Untyped receivers are counted in `graph.unresolved`; chains on foreign calls are not counted.
- Routes: axum `.route("/p", get(h).delete(h2))` with `.nest("/api", f())` and inline nests; actix `#[get("/p")]`, `web::scope("/api").service(h)`, `.route(p, web::get().to(h))`; rocket `#[get("/users/<id>")]` with `.mount("/api", routes[…])`.
- Outgoing `reqwest::get` / `client.post(url)` / `ureq` calls feed the bridge; `format!` placeholders and module `const`s are folded. A React frontend links to axum routes (`http-exact`).
- `LR-*` rules: `format!` into SQL or a shell command, `danger_accept_invalid_certs`, MD5/SHA-1, `unsafe` blocks. The missing-login check works on Rust routes as is.
- Readiness: axum/Actix/Rocket/warp detection, `Cargo.lock` as the lockfile.
- Sample `tests/fixtures/rustapp` (axum + React): both planted injections are found and ranked critical through the routes; the unprotected DELETE is flagged. 10 new tests; 268 pass; self-audit clean; viewer smoke clean.

Confidence levels for Rust edges are provisional until a Rust benchmark exists (noted in CLAUDE.md Known gaps).

body:
Gives a flowing page a width: `full`, `standard`, `wide` or a number.

**What changed**
- **format:** `PageSize` takes a flowing width of `full`, `standard`, `wide` or a number. Legacy `'fluid'` reads as `{ width: 'full', height: 'auto' }`, exported as `FULL_PAGE_SIZE`. `PAGE_WIDTHS` holds the named measures (standard 1024, wide 1440). `PageWidths` is the host override. `resolvePageWidth` is the one policy for screen, print, render and placement resolution. `FLUID_WIDTH` is removed.
- **Imposition:** a named page in a wider cell is laid out at its measure, centered, and drawn at its own width. Pieces are grouped by the geometry they render: page index, piece size and, for inset pieces, the bleed.
- **frame:** `<segnavia-page>` writes a named page's cap and centering inline, so an `unstyled` page keeps its geometry. Only a full page honors `bounded`. Every element and `printPages` take `pageWidths`, parse it where it arrives, and skip a reload when the widths are unchanged.
- **render:** the page, pages and book renders parse `pageWidths`. A printed named page is laid out at its measure and centered on the sheet. The viewport and placed media use the resolved width.
- **react:** `pageWidths` on props and descriptors.
- **Docs:** architecture.md and vocabulary.md describe flowing widths. The changeset states the `FLUID_WIDTH` removal and the effect on existing data: cover digests change once, and a re-serialized legacy page cannot be read by an older library.

**Why**
A host needs a page that reads at a set measure on any screen, honored the same way by the frame, print and the server render. The named widths are data a host may override, so the screen and the PDF never disagree.

**Gate**
`bun run check --changed` passed on cf936376: architecture, biome, typecheck and every package's unit tests (gate execution 5764). `bottega gate check --enabled --project segnavia` passed.

_Requested by **Oscar** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Kmn22NwE3hxjrazdBQ1TLo?thread=cmsg_01Kmn22NwE3hxjrazdBQ1TLoMha5aP153jFi8XzAU9VXJa)_

## Qué cambia

- **Cuentas**: una tabla nueva con cuentas de débito y crédito, cada una con su saldo o deuda inicial. También se marca cuál recibe los depósitos de Airbnb. Se editan en Ajustes.
- **Gastos**: el campo "¿Con qué se pagó?" reemplaza a la casilla "pagado desde la cuenta del negocio". Las opciones son una cuenta o *dinero propio*; con dinero propio, el gasto queda por reembolsar al socio que lo pagó. El admin elige por defecto la primera cuenta y un socio, dinero propio.
- **Pagar la tarjeta** y **reembolsar a un socio** se registran en Flujo como transferencias, así que no vuelven a contar como gasto.
- **Flujo**: muestra el saldo de cada cuenta, la deuda de la tarjeta, lo que se debe a cada socio y el *disponible real* (débito − tarjetas − por reembolsar). Una compra con tarjeta cuenta como salida el día que se hizo; los pagos de tarjeta no aparecen en entradas y salidas por mes.
- **Importar y exportar**: los gastos traen la columna opcional `pagado con` al importar, y el CSV del contador la incluye.

## Migración de datos existentes

El saldo único que había pasa a la cuenta "Débito negocio", que queda marcada como la que recibe Airbnb, y se crea "Crédito negocio" con deuda 0. Los gastos que estaban marcados como pagados con la cuenta quedan en débito; los demás, como dinero propio.

## Corrección de fechas

El cast `date` de Laravel guardaba `2026-10-31 00:00:00`, y `whereBetween('fecha', [desde, hasta])` dejaba fuera los gastos y reservas del **último día** del periodo. Ahora las fechas se guardan como `Y-m-d` con el cast `App\Casts\Fecha`, y una migración corrige los datos existentes. Agregué una prueba para este caso.

## Pruebas

`php artisan test`: pasan 14 pruebas. Las nuevas cubren el flujo con tarjeta, pago y reembolso, los permisos de transferencias, la importación con `pagado con` y el último día del periodo. También lo probé en el navegador: un gasto de Juan con dinero propio aparece como "por reembolsar a Juan".
