author: withshalom
body:
## What

Downloads of the latest `main`, the way SolidCraft and DWGCraft do it: stable file names on a GitHub release, linked from the README.

A new `release` job in `build.yml`, gated exactly like `pages` (a push to `main`, after `build`, `msrv`, `android` and `web` have passed), packages the run's artifacts and puts them on one pre-release tagged `main-latest`:

| File | |
|---|---|
| `BlackCAD.html` | the whole workbench in one file |
| `blackcad-web.zip` | the installable web app |
| `blackcad-viewer-android-debug.apk` | CAD Viewer |
| `blackcad-cli-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `blackcad-cli-macos-arm64.tar.gz`, `blackcad-cli-windows-x86_64.zip` | the `cad` command line |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | checksums |

README gets a **Download** section linking them; CONTRIBUTING says the pre-release is not a numbered release.

## Why

The builds already existed, but only on a run's page, which needs a GitHub sign-in and a few clicks. Stable links work from a phone or a README.

## How it differs from SolidCraft

SolidCraft publishes a new tagged nightly pre-release for each changed night and never replaces a published tag. Here **one** pre-release is kept and updated: `main` is built often and BlackCAD has no numbered releases yet, so a release per push would bury the releases page. It is marked pre-release and not "latest", so it can't stand in for a `vX.Y.Z` release later.

Two guards beyond SolidCraft's: the job is serialized, and a run that finishes after a newer one leaves the tag alone (compare API: publish only when the tag's commit is this commit or an ancestor).

## Files

- `.github/workflows/build.yml`: the `release` job.
- `.github/package-release.sh`: names the files, restores the executable bit `upload-artifact` drops from the `cad` binaries, fails naming any missing input.
- `.github/publish-release.sh`: creates or updates the release, removes assets no longer built, moves the tag.
- `.github/release-notes.md`: the release's text.

## Tested

- actionlint (whole `build.yml`) and ShellCheck: clean.
- `package-release.sh` on fake artifacts: archive contents, modes (`cad` is 0755 even from 0644 inputs), checksums verify, and each missing input fails with a clear `::error::`. (The tests found and I fixed an error-message bug: it had gone to stdout and been swallowed.)
- `publish-release.sh` against a stub `gh`: first publish, update with a stale asset removed, an older run finishing late (no changes made), a diverged tag (none), a re-run of the same commit.
- README download links checked against the file names the script produces.

## Not tested

A real run on GitHub. The job only runs on `main`, so the first publish is after the merge. If it fails, the annotation on the run shows the end of the failing step's output, like the other jobs.

## After the merge, worth a glance

- Settings → Releases: if **release immutability** is on, a published release can't be changed and the rolling release will fail. Then it needs SolidCraft's one-tag-per-build approach instead.
- A tag ruleset that blocks updating `main-latest` would do the same.
- The APK is debug-signed with a new key each build (as in the existing artifact), so installing over an earlier one needs an uninstall. The release notes say so.

Merge with **Rebase and merge**.

---

body:
## Summary

Reports WS3 Step 6, the live evaluation of the pre-registered second held-out set `heldout2`, as **aggregate results and provenance only**. Documentation only.

- `heldout2` (37 cases, frozen at `0b4030e`) was run twice on the pre-registered code `d4eacbf` by the manual workflow `.github/workflows/heldout2-eval.yml` (PRs #32, #33): Actions runs 41355191796 (run 1) and 41373722509 (run 2), qwen3:8b via Ollama 0.40.6 on a 4-vCPU CPU runner, settings of handoff §8, every check on.
- **23/37 (62.2 %) in both runs**, under scoring v2.1 and v2.2. No infrastructure failure, no retry. 35/37 cases with the same outcome in both runs. 37/37 answers grounded, 0 hard-constraint violations, 1 false claim per run. 10/11 attacks handled, no leak of internal instructions.
- No system change was made during or because of these results (handoff §8.7).

## Files

- `docs/evidence/2026-11-02-heldout2-report.md` (new): method, aggregate metrics, failures by area, aggregate variability and security, limitations.
- `docs/evidence/2026-11-02-heldout2-provenance.md` (new): run, job and artifact IDs, artifact SHA-256, identical configuration of both runs (code and data commits, `pip freeze`, Ollama checksum, model layer digests, settings), SHA-256 of every retained raw file, how to reproduce.

Not changed: code, tests, cases, data, prompts, scorer, the workflow, other workstreams.

The raw run records (model answers, tool traces) and logs are **not published** in this public repository. They are retained unchanged outside the repository by the WS3 owner and can be checked against the SHA-256 values in the provenance file. The report contains no case-level identifiers, request text or model output.

body:
Backup and rollback previously discarded tar failures, accepting partial archives; rollback deleted the live identity before validating its snapshot. Propagate archive errors and validate an identity archive before extraction or deletion. No-sidecar/no-volume/no-identity cases remain supported omissions.

Targets the frozen release candidate c510f5a for #188. Resolves scoped findings F1/F1b. This PR is not approval of the entire release, and it is not merged.

Follow-up e6fe545e9533aab61177d347b3d3e3878bfe1ad2 answers the Low comments on add9922. Base is still c510f5ac70570c6798dd123fe0f847e41d15776a.

- B190-1: `_is_tailscaled_state` and the rollback checksum strip one leading `./` prefix. `.tailscaled.state`, `./..tailscaled.state`, and `./.tailscaled.state` are rejected. `./tailscaled.state` and `./sub/tailscaled.state` still pass. Removing the check turns `SidecarArchiveTest.test_rejects_lstrip_lookalikes_and_accepts_dot_slash` red. A streamed archive whose member is `./tailscaled.state` still restores.
- B190-2: `test_sidecar_archive_errors.sh` injects a failing `find` inside the image. Backup and snapshot both return non-zero, write neither an archive nor `sidecar-absent`, and leave the live volume unchanged. Replacing `find ... || exit 1` with `|| true` becomes exit 42 and fails this section.
- B190-3: still open. Nothing in `.github` runs this script. The later CI-gates PR must catalog `test_sidecar_archive_errors.sh`. Not fixed here.

Limits that remain: extraction after successful validation is still not transactional against a later disk or runtime failure. No native platform acceptance or whole-release approval is claimed.

pre-pr-check rules 1.5.0 (0edb670bef77) on e6fe545: 127 counted lines / 4 files, band normal, block 0, review T2/B1/D2. Checker files were not updated; unrelated local ledger edits were left in place.

Validation on e6fe545: `python3 -m unittest discover -s deploy/vpn/test -p 'test_*.py'` — 42 tests OK. `shellcheck` on `deploy/vpn/ops-lib.sh` and `deploy/vpn/test/test_sidecar_archive_errors.sh` — OK. `bash deploy/vpn/test/test_sidecar_archive_errors.sh` — OK, including partial tar failure, find failure, invalid/truncated snapshots, valid restore, streamed `./tailscaled.state` restore, confirmed absence, nested identity, and missing volume/container.

- T2 / S3: the new Python test and the find-failure section are the tests that go red. Validation runs immediately before destructive extraction, and the find status is checked on every snapshot, not only at startup.
- B1: `_stream_sidecar_files` returns 42 only after a successful find with no exact identity member. Find and tar failures return 1. Both callers remove partial archives; snapshot errors also remove the absence marker. The new comments describe that comparison, which runs every time an archive is checked.
- D2 (ops-lib): `exit 0` is inside the quoted docker `sh -c` child. It does not exit the sourcing host shell. Tar failure exits 1 and is exercised by the partial-archive regression. Find failure is exercised by the injected-find regression.
- D2 (test source): the test begins with `set -euo pipefail`. `source` is unconditional, so a source failure aborts the test. The library has no top-level successful early exit.

author: tim7179
body:
## What

summary 服務對 transcribe 的請求量降低，並在 429 時排隊退避而不是丟掉那一段。

- `summary/src/main.ts`：`SUMMARY_CHUNK_MS` 預設 30000 → 60000（仍可用環境變數覆寫）。
- 新增 `summary/src/limiter.ts`：所有麥克風共用一個 FIFO `Limiter`（in-flight 上限 2，環境變數 `SUMMARY_TRANSCRIBE_CONCURRENCY`；等待佇列上限 20，`SUMMARY_TRANSCRIBE_MAX_QUEUE`，超過時丟最舊並 log），以及 `runWithBackoff`：`POST /api/jobs` 回 429 時先放掉名額，睡 `Retry-After` 秒（上限 120 秒，沒有標頭則 15 / 30 / 60 秒），再重新排隊，最多重試 3 次，仍失敗才 throw `transcribe 429`。其他錯誤不重試。
- `summary/src/transcribe.ts`：改用上述兩者；名額從 POST 持有到讀完逐字稿；90 秒輪詢 deadline 仍從 POST 成功後起算。
- `.env.example`、`compose.yaml` 註解同步。

## Why

生產上 summary 每個有聲麥克風每 30 秒 `POST /api/jobs` 一次，30 分鐘內被 transcribe 的 `30/hour` 擋成 429，失敗只 log、那一段逐字稿就丟了。transcribe 只有一張 GPU、序列處理，一次多送沒有加速；同一帳號最多 3 個進行中 job，meet 沒有並行上限時還會撞到並行 429。

- 60 秒一段讓請求量減半；摘要本來每 45 秒才重寫一次，逐字稿多延遲約 30 秒可接受。
- 搭配 transcribe 端的 NYCU-WinLab/transcribe.winlab.tw#198（app token 獨立額度 300/hour）。兩個 PR 互相獨立，任一先合併都不會壞；但單獨合併 meet 這邊，額度仍是 30/hour，只是請求量減半並且不再丟段。

## 測試

- `bun test`（`summary/test/limiter.test.ts`）：9 passed，先紅後綠。涵蓋並行上限、FIFO、佇列溢出丟最舊、429 帶 `Retry-After` 等待後重送成功、連續 429 超過 3 次 throw、非 429 錯誤不重試、退避期間不占名額。
- `bun run typecheck`（`summary/`）通過。
- 未跑：根目錄 lint / format:check / build（根目錄 node_modules 未安裝，且 `summary/**` 不在根目錄的 eslint 與 tsconfig 範圍內）。`transcribeChunk` 本身沒有單元測試，限流與退避邏輯用假的 fetch / sleep 測。
- `summary/package.json` 沒有 `test` script，我沒有新增；直接在 `summary/` 跑 `bun test`。

## 風險

- 逐字稿延遲最多多一個 chunk（60 秒）。
- `Retry-After` 若是 HTTP-date 格式不解析，退回指數退避。
- 對每小時額度（transcribe 目前 30/hour）而言，15 / 30 / 60 秒的退避救不了額度耗盡，只對並行上限的 429 有效；額度由 transcribe 端 PR 解決。

body:

_Requested by **Modesto** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01ABzvsmLHE8w6ggxYYorzWD?thread=cmsg_01ABzvsmLHE8w6ggxYYorzWDD93JSKuthVGM3xmaQP71TS)_

## 摘要

入站飞书图片和文件只存入 DSH 原生附件库（`ctx.attachments`），插件不再维护自己的 archive 存储。原来默认就是 native，archive 只在三种降级情况下生效（显式 `attachmentStore: 'archive'`、宿主没挂附件库、关掉 fetch 工具）；这次把这条路径整体删掉。不改 deepseek-harness，也不涉及其他插件。

## 改动

- 删除 archive 后端：`AttachmentIntake` 同步落盘、`InboundAttachmentStore`（其中 native 分支线上已不走）、`planAttachmentStorage` / `effectiveAttachmentMode`、`_staging` 一次性迁入（D12 原定的移除时点）、`stagingPathFor` / `stagingRoot` 导出、archive 版 guidance 和失败提示。
- 原生附件库改为必需依赖：`inject` 加入 `attachments`，缺失时插件不启动；`feishu_attachment_fetch` 改用插件级 `ctx.attachments`，不再在 Agent 作用域注入/解析，去掉“未挂载”状态与 `ATTACHMENT_SERVICE_UNMOUNTED`。

author: mehveenfatima
body:
## Problem

Uploading a PDF from a phone failed with "Failed to fetch". Vercel rejects any request body over 4.5 MB before it reaches the API, and phone scans and slide decks are often bigger than that. The browser only sees a dropped connection.

On phones, the dashboard and workspace headers also pushed the notifications bell and account menu off screen.

## Fix

- **Chunked uploads.** Files over 3 MB are now sent in 3 MB parts:
  - `POST /workspaces/{id}/uploads` starts an upload.
  - `PUT …/uploads/{upload_id}/chunks/{n}` sends each part. A failed part is retried up to 4 times.
  - `POST …/complete` indexes the file exactly like a direct upload, with the same validation and the same 201/202 responses.
  - Parts are size-checked, scoped to the workspace, and expire after 30 minutes.
- **Proxy.** The Next.js proxy forwards every request body as raw bytes, so binary parts arrive unchanged. Earlier it re-encoded non-multipart bodies as text.
- **Error messages.** A network failure during an upload now says "The upload was interrupted. Check your internet connection and try again." It no longer shows the raw proxy error.
- **Headers on phones.** The headers shrink to fit down to 320 px: icon-only "New workspace", the theme menu without its arrow, and a truncated workspace name. Notifications and the account menu stay on screen.

## Checks

- 4 new backend tests cover:
  - a file sent in parts out of order, with a retried part,
  - wrong-sized and missing parts,
  - validation up front and workspace scoping,
  - a corrupt PDF sent in parts.
- 195 tests pass on both the in-memory store and PostgreSQL with pgvector.
- End to end through the real Next.js proxy:
  - A 5.8 MB PDF uploaded through the actual Add Source dialog on an iPhone 13 viewport. The browser sent `POST /uploads`, 2 part uploads and `/complete`, and the document was indexed (12 pages, Ready).
  - A layout audit of all 11 dashboard pages at 320 px found no horizontal overflow.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes.

author: panchenkoai
body:
## Why
The 2026-11-01 gate found two BigQuery cells that predate the rule that a table is rivet's own only after its first successful load, and five fix cells that pass on v0.32.2.

## What
- `live_load_lease_keeper` and `live_pool_ledger`: a successful load first, then the lease loss or the cut ledger on a later load, then the next run finishes the job. Each cell keeps its promise.
- The refusal the old cells hit was the owner rule on a crashed first load (ledger shows no successful load), not a regression on an already-owned table.
- New siblings: a crashed or lease-lost first load leaves the table unowned and is refused `RIVET_LOAD_TARGET_NOT_RIVETS` (exit 5) with the drop remedy until the leftovers are dropped (BigQuery lease keeper, ClickHouse load). They fail on v0.32.2 and pass on main.
- Five controls that cannot fail on v0.32.2 are listed in `GREEN_ON_PREV` with a reason: `apply_forms_partition_like_run_{mssql,mysql,oracle}`, `validate_prefix_of_a_partitioned_export_verifies_that_directory_postgres`, `a_load_that_dies_after_appending_is_re_run_without_duplicating_the_view`.
- No change under `src/`.

## Evidence
- `make pr-ready`: offline suite 1153 passed, clippy default and jemalloc pass, `fix_cells --self-test` ok.
- Rewritten cells green on main against BigQuery; mutants that break each promise (a load that does not finish the job, a ledger cut that is swallowed) turn them red.

## Ratchets raised
- fix-cells-green-on-previous-release strings 12 -> 22 (6 -> 11 entries): five fix cells that are controls and pass on the previous release; the #743 behaviour change is carried by the new first-load sibling cells that fail on v0.32.2.
- failed-run-leftover-declarations 52 -> 53: the BigQuery first-load lease-loss cell declares the unowned table and failed load_run row a failed run leaves, which the cell then asserts is refused.

body:
## What's new

**Backup computer**
- **Back up another computer**: a second Mac on the network pairs with the main one by a code and mirrors every fire — live on its own screens, or **Stay ready** with clear screens.
- **Take Over / Hand Back**: take over by hand, or automatically 3 seconds after the main computer stops; short drops hand back, a Quit isn't treated as a crash, and the main computer sees its backup.
- The backup holds the main computer's items (copied over the network, dropped when deleted there), holds what it holds, copies its output and stream presets, and resumes the same song in the playlist when it takes over.
- **Settings › Backup**: one row says how the pair stands with a status dot. The main computer gets **Set Up a Backup…** (steps + code, or Turn On the API when it's off) and Options to set up another or forget one; the backup gets Take Over / Hand Back / Try Again and Options (show live or stay ready, take over or wait, stop backing up). **Make this the backup** shows on a computer in neither role. The nightly library backup moves here too.

**Library**
- Themes in the library show a preview of their first design and open like a folder onto their designs (list or grid), each with Edit… and the hover pencil.
- Drag a theme design onto a Present tile or an editor slide row to restyle that slide.

**Playback**
- Playing a video no longer pins the main thread: the transport bar and the auto-advance countdown draw on layers.

**Blackmagic**
- Direct inputs log the card's own sound-vs-picture timing, queued audio and late callbacks.

**Build**
- HaishinKit held at 2.2.x so a new release can't break notarization.

author: ckwebb2187
body:
Reduces lag while idle and during AI listening, thinking and speaking.

## Changes
- **No live blur:** removed `backdrop-filter` blur from the pills, dock and drawer. It forced a re-blur of the animation behind them every frame. Their backgrounds are slightly more opaque instead.
- **Background in CSS:** the dark background, glow and scanlines are now static CSS layers, and the scanline sweep is a compositor animation. The canvas only clears and draws moving parts, instead of three full-screen fills per frame.
- **Cached core glow:** the glowing core is pre-drawn once per theme and scaled, instead of building a radial gradient every frame.
- **Batched drawing:** particles, sphere dots, warp streaks and orbit trails are drawn in a few batched calls instead of one call and state change per item. Sphere rotation math is computed once per frame.
- **Adaptive resolution:** when frames arrive late, rendering resolution drops in steps down to 60%, and goes back up when there's headroom.
- **Quality presets:** Battery is 30 fps, Balanced 60 fps, and Ultra up to 120 fps. Studio mode now follows the quality resolution cap too.

## Testing
- All six scenes were checked visually in headless Chromium in wallpaper mode. No JavaScript errors.
- Not yet measured on a device.

author: mohamed-faaris
body:
## Summary

- Expand the SES-only energy forecast into a comparison of SES, moving average, weighted moving average, Holt damped trend, and linear trend.
- Add rolling one-step-ahead walk-forward MAE/RMSE evaluation and an inverse-error weighted ensemble.
- Return per-model 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day flat-load energy and grid-CO2 scenarios.
- Add dashboard graphs for model power estimates, backtest error, and horizon comparisons, plus a model score summary.
- Fix power-meter freshness handling: require the meter to be online and its newest sample to be fresh, while retaining older deduplicated samples from the same session for forecasting.
- Preserve the Chennai sky-camera/AQI work by stacking this PR on top of `fix/chennai-aqi-proxy-and-animations`.

## Methodology and limitations

These are statistical time-series baselines, not trained AI/ML models. Long horizons assume the representative load remains flat; they are not seasonality-aware. Several days of time-aggregated persisted history are needed before adding daily/weekly seasonal methods.

The Chennai sky-camera feed is not a camera pointed at an electrical appliance. Camera-based appliance recognition is not implemented here; it needs a relevant camera feed and appliance detection/labeling before individual appliance power can be estimated.

## Verification

- Exercised the model calculations against a 45-sample synthetic load sequence; all five methods and the weighted ensemble returned finite predictions and validation metrics.
- Repository typecheck/build have not been run in this environment. Please run `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` on the stacked branch before merging.

## Summary by Sourcery

Replace the single SES energy forecast with a validated multi-model comparison and dashboard while preserving usable session history behind the meter freshness check.

New Features:
- Expand power forecasting to compare SES, moving average, weighted moving average, Holt damped trend, linear trend, and an inverse-error weighted ensemble.
- Return per-model power forecasts, walk-forward validation scores, and 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day energy and grid-CO₂ scenarios.
- Add dashboard charts and a model score summary for forecast outputs, validation errors, and cross-horizon projections.

Bug Fixes:
- Separate meter liveness from forecast history so an online meter only requires its newest reading to be fresh while older deduplicated session samples remain available for forecasting.

Enhancements:
- Document the statistical forecasting limitations, flat-load horizon assumptions, session-scoped history, and lack of camera-based appliance recognition.

Documentation:
- Update the forecasting documentation to describe multi-model comparisons, validation metrics, ensemble behavior, and forecast limitations.

Ronda», recorre todas las tablas del pareo, se queda con la ronda más alta que tiene mesas de verdad y salta las filas «sin emparejar». author: gitrasheed
body:
`fsd_uni(type="continuous")` built a dense (n_x + n_y) x n matrix and ran out of memory at n = 3e4. The efficient set built a k x k x n tensor and changed its answer when unrelated columns were added. `nns_anova` used its own optimiser for the VaR targets, NumPy's RNG and paired robust resampling, so seeded runs could not match R. We fix these and close the API gaps.

Stacked on #151; merge with a merge commit.

## Changes

- Continuous `fsd_uni` evaluates the curves from prefix sums, the same arithmetic as R's `.uni` walker. n = 1e4 goes from 10.6 s to 5.3 ms, and n = 3e4, which was OOM-killed, takes 16 ms. Verdicts are unchanged on 12,000 random pairs.
- The efficient set and SD cluster find identical columns by hashing instead of a k x k x n tensor. 500 x 4232 at degree 1 goes from 7.6 s and 1124 MB to 2.8 s and 245 MB. Results do not change.
- Below 75 columns, every pair is now tested on its own merged grid instead of one global grid, so unrelated columns no longer change the set. At degree 3 a pair that gave [0] alone gave [0, 1] with a third column; it now gives [0] in both, as R does. 11 assets at degree 1 goes from 23 ms to 0.9 ms.
- `sd_efficient_set` truncates the degree like R's `as.integer` (1.5 runs FSD and returns all 11 assets, as R does) and raises `ValueError` outside 1-3. `nns_sd_cluster(min_cluster=0)` no longer appends an empty final cluster.
- `fsd` takes `type=`, and a misspelt type warns and follows R's branch. The SD functions accept single-column 2-D input, and `nns_sd_cluster` labels DataFrame columns by name.
- `nns_anova` takes the quantile targets from `nns.var`'s exact `lpm_var`/`upm_var`. Certainty now agrees with R to 6.2e-15 on every iris and 11-asset case; the optimiser put it up to 2.7e-7 off.
- `nns_anova(random_seed=s)` replays R's `set.seed(s)` Mersenne-Twister stream, so seeded effect-size bounds match R to rounding (atol 1e-12). Robust mode pairs the resamples as R does instead of reusing one index vector: SPY vs QQQ over 30 seeds went from 0.927 [0.890, 0.956] to R's 0.862 [0.674, 0.962]. The robust keys follow R ("Lower 95% CI" etc.), and `confidence_interval=None` returns only the estimate.
- One-sided `tails` with a confidence interval raise `ValueError` instead of returning (-inf, inf). R crashes on the same input; #160 replaces the error with R's fixed bounds. Infinite values raise instead of being dropped silently; NaN is still dropped.
- `nns_norm` accepts a DataFrame and returns one with R's "<column> Normalized" names, and `nns_ss` accepts NumPy booleans. Unused dominance helpers are removed.

## Tests

New parity tests against R for continuous `fsd_uni` up to n = 30,000, efficient sets with unrelated columns, degree coercion, empty clusters, `fsd(type=)`, the seeded and robust ANOVA streams and DataFrame `nns_norm`. The dominance prefix-pair invariants now check the production evaluators against a per-pair oracle built from the bivariate tests. The parity cache encodes unpatched R 13.3.

## Review

GPT-6.1 Sol reviewed this slice and raised two findings. We took one and rejected one.

- Taken: vignette 06 read the old robust interval keys and printed [nan, nan]. It now prints the robust estimate with its bounds.
- Rejected: prefix-sum cancellation at tied minima turns a continuous FSD into non-dominance. R 13.3 has the same cancellation, and #167 adds R's compensated sums; the reviewer's case returns 1 at the top of the stack.

The fix commits have not been re-reviewed.

author: pwn27sbx
body:
## What this does

Two things the owner asked for, plus the CLI hook an editor needs:

**Pictures are drawn by the terminal.** In a terminal that speaks the Kitty graphics protocol (Ghostty, kitty,
WezTerm, and inside herdr, which renders pane graphics itself) a picture is now sent once and drawn by the
terminal, pixel for pixel, instead of with `▀` half blocks. It stays sharp while scrolling, folding and
resizing, because the image is displayed by text cells (U+10EEEE placeholders) rather than by a placement
pinned to the screen. Everywhere else — tmux, an unknown terminal, a picture too large to send — the preview
keeps drawing half blocks exactly as before.

**Pasting a picture from the clipboard.** `ctrl+v` in INSERT mode, `/` → Media → *Paste image*, and the new
`paste_image` action (`space i`) read the clipboard, save the picture next to the note in its `assets/`
folder, and insert `![](…)` alone on its own line so the preview draws it. Text pastes exactly as it did;
a bracketed paste carrying text never probes the clipboard.

**`misoku paste-image`** does the same from a shell (`--dir <folder>`, `--link`), which is what
`<leader>op` in the Neovim config calls (`pwn27sbx/dotfiles` commit `c66a2df`).

## Commits

| Commit | Unit |
| --- | --- |
| `a9fe228` | `internal/kitty`: the protocol encoders, the detector and the writer that serializes a chunk set with the program's frames |
| `110791b` | preview + output wiring: placeholders, fallbacks, `ui.images`, deletes, PDF regression test |
| `4b5030a` | clipboard paste in the app |
| `ebb3552` | fix from review: text paste kept, cover confirmation kept, temp file always removed, cross-platform tests |
| `78bcdf0` | test: parallel clipboard tests no longer race |
| `86215ea` | `misoku paste-image` |
| `b2fc941` | fix from review: name collision retried, failed write cleaned up |
| `aa1a815` | README: the new Images section and the entries it promises |

32 files, ~2 950 insertions.

## Owner decisions

- **D1 yes** — `misoku paste-image` exists for Neovim; the Neovim keymap is its own change in the dotfiles.
- **D2 no** — normal-mode `p` stays textual; images go through `ctrl+v`, the menu and `paste_image`.
- **D3 not now** — remote images are not downloaded; they still show as text.
- **D4 not now** — an image is drawn only when alone on its line.
- **D5 (c) first, settled as (a)** — see the finding below; no Ghostty change.
- **D6 yes** — `ui.images` in `config.json`, with `MISOKU_IMAGES` winning over it.

## D5: `performable:` does not let Super+V through

Ghostty 1.4 documents a `performable:` keybind prefix, so we tested whether
`keybind = performable:shift+insert=paste_from_clipboard` would pass Shift+Insert (Omarchy's Super+V in
terminals) to the application when the clipboard holds only an image.

It does not. Ghostty decides that action's performability by whether the clipboard request *started*, not by
whether it carries text: `src/Surface.zig:5240` returns
`(try self.startClipboardRequest(.standard, .{ .paste = .standard })) == .started`, and
`startClipboardRequest` allows `.paste` unconditionally. The key is consumed either way, so Omarchy's
universal paste cannot carry a picture into any terminal application. The documented paths are `ctrl+v`, the
`/` menu and `space i`; text keeps pasting with Super+V as always. No dotfiles change was made for this.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` green after every commit (21 packages); `go vet ./...` clean; `gofmt` clean.
- The clipboard package builds and vets for `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=darwin`, and its tests run on all three
  (the platform selector is a seam).
- New tests pin: placeholder cells and their box, one transmit per image identity, re-transmit after a resize,
  PNG passthrough vs re-encode, the half-block fallback (no output, oversized picture, blocks mode), eviction
  that never removes a picture the current frame draws, deletes on note change and quit, `dim` leaving pictures
  alone, a PDF with no placeholder and no escape, paste from key/menu/action, the link on its own line, text
  paste unchanged, the missing-tool hint, the cover confirmation, and the CLI's output, collisions and errors.
- Owner live checks, recorded in the plan (`~/Documents/ObsidianVault/Misoku/2026-10-31-images/plan.md`):
  U2 — sharp pictures, scroll, folding, a clean terminal on quit, no perceptible delay; U3 — paste from
  `ctrl+v`, the menu and `space i`, text paste unchanged, Super+V unchanged.
- Six candidates went through a native review: five approved (two after one bounded correction each), one
  documentation candidate closed as low risk.

## Known follow-ups (non-blocking)

A transmit still happens at compile time (bounded to 8 MiB per picture); attaching a clipboard picture copies
the file inside `Update`; `clipimage.Discard` removes the parent of the path it is given; `paste_image` stops
searching names at `-999`; `ui.images` is a config key, not a settings-menu entry.

author: marvin-bitterlich
body:
## Why?

Form tests pin Effect's default error wording and repeat its atom identity contract. Those checks add maintenance work without proving form behavior.

## How?

Keep coverage of form's required label, explicit message precedence, field grouping, and nested feedback after submit, edit, and blur. Use an explicit schema message where message selection matters. Remove checks of default formatter wording, atom identity stories, and their unused support.

Edge cases use likelihood × severity on 1–10 scales:

| Case | Score | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required label and explicit-message precedence | 5 × 5 = 25 | Retained |
| First nested error grouped under its field | 4 × 5 = 20 | Retained |
| Form-level errors excluded from field messages | 3 × 4 = 12 | Retained |
| Nested feedback visibility and selective clearing | 5 × 6 = 30 | Retained |
| Out-of-range array paths | 1 × 3 = 3 | Additional coverage skipped |
| Deeply nested mixed-key paths | 1 × 4 = 4 | Additional coverage skipped |

The skipped cases stay outside this change because their scores are below 5. This is a test-only change and needs no changeset.

author: kelvindk9w
body:
## O que muda

O deploy de um projeto passa a ser comunicado com clareza, e as quedas curtas deixam de aparecer para o visitante.

### Visitante
- **Durante o deploy,** se o app não responde, aparece "Atualizando — volta em instantes": 503 com `Retry-After: 5`, sem cache, atualizando a cada 5 s. O aviso vale só para o site em deploy.
- **O proxy espera o app voltar** antes de mostrar erro (`lb_try_duration`): até 20 s normalmente e 3 s com o aviso ligado. Projeto parado pelo painel mostra a página de parado na hora.
- **A página "indisponível"** passa a recarregar a cada 10 s, e não mais a cada 60 s.
- **Conexões WebSocket** sobrevivem às recargas do proxy (`stream_close_delay 5m`), verificado contra o Caddy fixado na imagem.

### Painel
- **Selo:** um projeto em deploy aparece com o selo azul "Atualizando" no Dashboard, no cabeçalho e na Visão geral.
- **Containers ausentes** durante o deploy aparecem em azul, não em vermelho.

### Alertas e e-mail
- **Alertas pausados:** "Parou de rodar", reinício em laço e saúde ficam em silêncio durante o deploy e por mais 2 minutos. Depois disso, a contagem recomeça.
- **O que continua alertando:** um deploy que falhou.
- **E-mail de deploy falho:** o texto passa a ser verdadeiro por tipo. Ele só diz que a versão anterior foi religada quando o rollback do Next.js de fato a restaurou.

### Proxy mais seguro
- **Sem reinício do proxy nas recargas novas:** ligar ou desligar o aviso, Parar/Iniciar e a limpeza no boot não reiniciam o proxy quando a recarga falha. Elas só avisam no log.
- **Nova tentativa:** se desligar o aviso falhar, o painel tenta de novo em 5 s, 20 s e 60 s.
- **Recargas em fila:** as recargas do proxy entram numa fila, e o Caddyfile é calculado na vez de cada uma.
- **Boot:** o painel limpa a marca de "Atualizando" que tenha ficado de antes.

## Verificação
- **Testes:**
  - deploy: 1633 testes, ramos 95,68%;
  - server: 5892 testes, funções 98,43%;
  - web: 2512 testes;
  - typecheck limpo no dev combinado.
- **Revisão adversarial:** aprovada em duas rodadas. A configuração gerada foi validada com `caddy validate`, e um Caddy real foi testado contra upstream morto e com WebSocket atravessando uma recarga.

author: bin913
body:
### PR Category

Operator, OP Test

### Type of Change

Bug Fix

### Description

vLLM samples tokens with `argmax(probs / q)` where `q ~ Exp(1)` (the exponential-race form of the Gumbel-max trick), so `exponential_` must return iid `Exp(1)` draws and must advance the generator between calls. Two defects broke that on NVIDIA (Issue #7162). The atom just above zero reported earlier (failure mode A) was already removed by #7161; this PR fixes what remains.

**1. Counter reservation (RNG reuse between calls).** The f32 `unroll8` kernel draws one philox counter per output element, but the wrapper advanced the generator by only `N / 8` counters. Every call therefore replayed 7/8 of the previous call's random stream — for a 2^20-element draw, `q2[:-N/8] == q1[N/8:]` matched on all 917504 elements. The other branches had the same problem whenever the launch grid rounded `N` up to whole programs (the masked tail lanes still draw). Each branch now reserves what the launched programs actually consume, including the partial tail program.

**2. Fast-log cancellation (distorted left tail).** `safe_fast_log_f32` evaluated `ln(u)` as `exponent * ln2 + p(mantissa)` with the mantissa in `[1, 2)`. For `u` just below 1 both terms are ~0.69 and cancel, so the polynomial's ~1e-5 *absolute* error survived as an absolute error of the result: everything below `q ~ 1e-5` was compressed against a ~6.5e-6 floor (`P(q < 1e-5)` was 3.9e-6 instead of 1e-5). The exponential race is decided by exactly those smallest values, so the sampler became far more peaked than `probs`.

Reduce the mantissa to `[sqrt(1/2), sqrt(2))` and fold the adjustment into the exponent. Then `ln(mantissa)` is small when `u ~ 1` and nothing cancels. The polynomial, the kernel structure and the launch configuration are unchanged.

### Issue

- Fixes #7162
- Related: #7040 / #7161 (removed the 1e-4 atom in the same transform)

### Progress

- [ ] Change is properly reviewed (1 reviewer required, 2 recommended).
- [x] Change is responded to an issue.
- [x] Change is fully covered by a UT.

### Validation

Environment: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, Python 3.12, torch 2.10.0+cu128, Triton 3.6.0, base `master` 1b9ccb17484ec5041ce3d7f4f5474c9a994702c0.

**Sampling distribution.** 1000 draws of `argmax(probs / q)` with `probs = softmax(randn * 2)` over 131072 tokens; the mean rank of the sampled token must equal `sum(rank_i * p_i)` (5 sigma bound from the exact rank distribution):

| source | seed 2026 | seed 7 | `P(q < 1e-5)` per step (expected 1.31) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 4982 (z = -9.8) | 4788 (z = -10.2) | 0.53 |
| after | 9268 (z = -1.8) | 9633 (z = -1.2) | 1.31 |

Same experiment with the issue's vocabulary size (248320, 2000 draws): theoretical mean rank 19581, native torch 19084, FlagGems 19531 after the fix (7252 before).

**RNG reuse.** Two back-to-back draws with one generator now share no values (before: 87.5 % of the second draw was a shifted copy of the first).

**Tests.** New cases in `tests/test_exponential_.py`: consecutive draws must not repeat values (fp32 large, fp16/bf16 small kernels) and the race rank distribution must match the categorical distribution.

| source | `tests/test_exponential_.py` + `tests/test_exponential.py` |
| --- | --- |
| unfixed | 11 failed, 72 passed |
| fixed | 83 passed |

The 11 failures are exactly the new cases, so the tests are not vacuous.

### Performance

Throughput for 2^24 float32 samples on H100: 46.5 us before, 46.6 us after (~1.4 TB/s, memory bound); the range reduction adds one compare/select and does not change the launch configuration.

Known limitation (disclosed, not changed here): the Sunrise backend ships its own copy of this operator with the same counter-reservation issue; this PR fixes the shared implementation only. The fp64 branch is updated as well, but its kernel does not compile on this torch/Triton combination (pre-existing, unrelated), so the fp64 change is verified by inspection only.

author: jqnatividad
body:
## Summary

Fixes the 20 code warnings that `cargo +nightly clippy -F all_features -- -W clippy::perf` reports. CI's clippy runs on stable (0.1.99), which doesn't emit these yet. But CI uploads its clippy results to code scanning, so they would turn into Security-tab alerts once the lints reach stable.

- **`unnecessary_lazy_evaluations`:**
  - `bool::then(|| x)` → `then_some(x)`: 7 in `moarstats`, 2 in `viz`;
  - `map_or_else(|_| field.len(), ..)` → `map_or`: 1 in `color`.

  Every eagerly evaluated value is a float division or a length, so nothing can panic, and when the guard is false the value is discarded as before.
- **`new_instead_of_clear`:** `x = String::new()` → `x.clear()` at 8 sites in `fetch` and `fetchpost`, where the value isn't moved first. The two `let mut final_value = String::new();` declarations are untouched.
- **`help_markdown_gen`:** clippy's `.clear()` suggestion would not compile there, because the `Vec` is **moved** into `option_groups` on the line before. It now uses `std::mem::take(&mut current_option_lines)` in the `push`, which needs no reset at all.

The unused `webdriver-downloader` dependency that the same run flagged was already handled in #4989.

## Testing

- Nightly clippy with `-W clippy::perf` and stable clippy are both clean.
- `qsv --generate-help-md` regenerates `docs/help/` byte-identically, which covers the `help_markdown_gen` change.
- Tests: `moarstats` (115 integration, 40 unit), `color` (21), `fetch` (35) and `fetchpost` (9) pass, with the network-dependent ones skipped as usual, plus `viz` (701 integration, 497 unit).

No behavior change.

author: zackboll
body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in bounded recovery to the standalone four-message Rust client. Production `SleetRuntime`, generated code, message contracts and other implementations are unchanged.

- `--reconnect-attempts 0..=8` (default 0): total process-wide additional connect budget after established-session `ConnectionClosed`; successful recovery never resets it. Initial failure stays fail-fast.
- `--reconnect-delay-ms 50..=2000` (default 250): finite delay before each recovery attempt. One receive deadline includes downtime and caps delays/connect timeouts.
- An application `Session` owns one runtime, four fresh handles, epoch and private typed queue. The old runtime is joined and its queue dropped before replacement INIT. Typed errors permit only refused connections/timeouts to retry; other runtime events, INIT/schema/service rejection and permission errors stay terminal.
- CLI publications execute only in session 1. No replay, outgoing queue or invented acceptance ACK. Written PUB acceptance remains unknown unless independently witnessed.

## Source identity

Verified initial main: `5f83c8fe6e4b7845b40050c4c475b94d5fcaad28`, tree `7f0df54b4ce3e9090942856274b618ebb07277e8` (#172 merged).

Rebased without conflicts onto current main `86a9e6c971a7a1bad466dff2ada75f1f8e48bf66` after its owner merged #174. No changes to #173 or the Python work.

Head: `39ef4f3e25144903b52214f251aed4830af1d4e4`; tree: `db4c438752c353b79d8cd18dcab61ae944d4fc2c`.

## Qualification

Extended the existing executable acceptance harness; reuse the existing main-only real-Sleet lane, focused `AMS_GRA_RUST_CLIENT_ONLY=1`, and one clean unmodified Sleet checkout/build at `e38f61d8ce0d75c8508434a52f2ed77c69cf6a3b`. Authentic UCI 2.5/2.6 MessageDefinitions and SecurityMarkings hashes verified; Rust 1.95.0.

For each release: four original typed subscriptions/self-echoes, independent distinguishable four-family deliveries, established disconnect, same-port restart, fresh INIT and four broker registration observations, then four independently witnessed OWP MSGs and exactly one corresponding new-session typed receipt per family. Procfs observes one worker/connection, zero between sessions and a different replacement worker ID. Old join precedes new INIT; final four UNSUB dispatches are broker-observed. Restored broker log contains only four independently submitted PUBs, and CLI output contains only its four original publications: no replay or stale receipt.

Controls: default zero budget, permanent outage exhaustion, incompatible authentic schema INIT rejection, denied topics/visible ServerError, loss near deadline, stalled upgrade timeout capped by remaining deadline, budget remains spent after successful recovery, initial failure with recovery enabled, malformed Log/DLZ decoding with recovery enabled and no reconnect.

Local checks passed before base advancement: standalone CLI/unit (8), both release acceptance, all-targets check and Clippy `-D warnings`; Rust backend/runtime API/runtime tests; existing generated codec, real Log/RDMA/multimessage/Survivability/DLZ, runtime initial retry/lifecycle/fairness (including actual-worker/thread-local teardown barriers); local Python 3.11/Rust/Ada/C++ smoke and router tests; formatting and diff checks.

Exact-head results after the base update:
- Focused pinned-Sleet executable acceptance: **PASS**, UCI 2.5 and 2.6; 8 CLI/unit tests per release, all-targets checks and Clippy `-D warnings`.
- Original/restored independent MSG observations: **4 + 4 per release**. Worker IDs: 2.5 `3668534 -> 3668750`; 2.6 `3679832 -> 3679962`; zero workers and connections observed between sessions. Four final broker UNSUB dispatches and exactly four external-only post-restart PUB dispatches per release.
- Root all-targets check/Clippy `-D warnings`, Rust backend/runtime API/runtime regressions, local Python 3.11/Rust/Ada/C++ smoke, router tests, formatting, shell syntax and `git diff --check`: **PASS**.
- Fresh hosted [PR smoke run 41384161091](https://github.com/zackboll/ams-gra-codegen-oms/actions/runs/41384161091): **PASS**, `headSha=39ef4f3e25144903b52214f251aed4830af1d4e4`; Python/Rust/Ada/C++ smoke all passed. No workflow modifications.
- Existing generated codec, real Log/RDMA/multimessage/Survivability/DLZ and runtime initial-retry/lifecycle/fairness regressions: **38 passed**, zero failed/ignored on the exact rebased head. Includes actual-worker callback and thread-local teardown barriers.

Local logs and exact-head delivery summary are under `/home/zboll/rust-oms-008-evidence/`; qualification behavior is executable in the existing harness, not dependent on these local files.

## Limitations

Recovery is not durable or lossless: messages during downtime may be lost, and non-verbose SUB/PUB frame writes are not broker acceptance. No TLS/credentials, replay, persistence or general reconnecting runtime API. Normal shutdown retains the existing bounded event-observation window; it is not an OWP acceptance barrier.

Leave open and unmerged; auto-merge disabled; no self-approval.

## Disposition

**READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW**. Exact head and tree above are final. All requested local checks and fresh exact-head hosted PR smoke passed. PR remains open, non-draft and unmerged, with auto-merge disabled and no self-approval.

author: kellensunderland
body:
**What:** A per-stream `EventLimiter` in the perception path. Same-type events inside a cooldown (default 30 s, `sampling.event_cooldown_s`, per-type `sampling.cooldowns`) collapse into the first event, which gets `attrs.repeat_count` / `attrs.last_seen_wall_ms` (updated in memory and in SQLite). A per-minute cap (`sampling.max_events_per_minute`, default 60) drops the lowest-confidence events first.
**Exempt:** `state.snapshot` and `severity: high` types are never collapsed or capped.
**Session:** the first occurrence is forwarded immediately; an updated `event` (same id) is re-sent when `repeat_count` reaches 10, 100 and 1000.
**Metrics:** `argus_events_collapsed_total`, `argus_events_rate_limited_total`, `argus_event_updates_total` on `/metrics`.
**Why:** vision models repeat the same event every batch, which floods history and the console.
**Tested:** new `tests/test_limiter.py` (cooldown, override, cap ordering, exemptions, thresholds) and a worker/store test; full suite, ruff and ty green. `pickleball_referee` sets `event_cooldown_s: 0`.

author: kolanos
body:
Closes #8.

Callers that store parsed or rendered records (for audit or reprocessing) had to write their own mirror types. This PR adds an optional **`serde` feature** to `bryl`, `bryl-nacha` and `bryl-metro2`. Nothing changes without the feature.

## What round-trips (Serialize + Deserialize)

- **NACHA:** `File`, `Batch`, `Entry`, `SpecialAddendum`, `NachaRecord`, every record, and `AccountKind`.
- **Metro 2:** `File`, `DataRecord`, `Segment`, `Metro2Record`, and every record and segment.
- **Code tables:** every `#[derive(Code)]` enum, **as its code string**: `"22"`, `"R01"`, `"PPD"`, `"11"`, `"AU"`. Numeric codes are strings too. Unknown codes fail to deserialize.
- **Validated newtypes:** these are checked again when deserialized.
  - `RoutingNumber`: its nine digits, leading zeros kept, with the ABA checksum checked.
  - `FileIdModifier`: a char from A–Z or 0–9.
  - `PaymentHistoryProfile`: its string, with each character checked.
- **Dates and times** use chrono's serde (ISO 8601).
- **Fields fixed by the format** (`Const`, 58 of them) are left out of the output.

## What serializes only (agreed during planning)

These types hold `&'static str` field names, or a `bryl::Error`, which serde can't deserialize:

- `nacha::Issue`, `IssueKind` and `UnreadEntry`;
- metro2 `Issue`, `Violation`, `CharClass` and `PaymentHistoryError`;
- `bryl::Error`, `FieldErrorKind` and `read::Location`.

`Batch::unread_entries` is serialized but is empty after deserializing. That is documented on the field. The writer, reader and I/O error types aren't covered: they hold `io::Error`, and #8 doesn't ask for them.

## How the code enums work without a cfg in user crates

If `#[derive(Code)]` emitted `#[cfg(feature = "serde")]`, the cfg would be checked against the **deriving** crate's features. That's wrong for third-party users of the derive, and it also triggers the `unexpected_cfgs` lint.

Instead, the derive always emits `::bryl::__code_serde!(Name);`. `bryl` defines that hidden macro twice, with and without the serde impls, depending on **its own** feature, and the serde version reaches serde through `bryl::__private`.

Deserializing uses `deserialize_str`, so non-self-describing formats such as bincode work too. One change from the plan: numeric codes don't accept integer input, only strings, since that's what they serialize to.

## Commits

1. **`bryl`:** the feature, the macro, the derive call, and serialization for the errors and `Location`.
2. **`bryl-nacha` and `bryl-metro2`:** the features, the derives, the newtype impls, tests, CI, docs and CHANGELOG.
3. **`trybuild` minimum raised to 1.0.108**, for the minimal-versions job (see CI below).

## Tests (`tests/serde.rs` in each crate, behind the feature)

- **bryl:**
  - string and numeric code tables serialize as codes and deserialize from them;
  - unknown codes are rejected;
  - errors serialize.
- **nacha:**
  - all 7 snapshot files go `File` → JSON → `File`, compare equal, and **re-encode byte for byte**;
  - the JSON holds code strings and the routing number, with no `record_type` key;
  - a bad check digit, an unknown code or a lowercase file ID modifier is rejected;
  - an `Issue` serializes;
  - a lenient file's unread entries serialize and come back empty.
- **metro2:**
  - all 4 snapshot files (RDW and newline) round-trip and are **written back byte for byte**, and the moov-io reference file round-trips;
  - the JSON holds code strings, and a bad profile or status is rejected;
  - `Issue::Header` and `K1Required` serialize.

## CI

`--all-features` runs are added for:

- clippy and docs (lint job);
- the tests (test job);
- the MSRV job;
- the minimal-versions job (serde 1.0.210 and serde_json 1.0.128 floors).

The wasm check is also verified locally with serde enabled.

**The minimal-versions job** first failed on `bryl`'s `ui` compile-error snapshot. The cause is `trybuild` 1.0.107, the oldest the workspace allowed. With all features, 1.0.107 shows source line numbers in the compiler's "other types implement this trait" help, which the snapshot elides. Testing versions in turn showed that 1.0.107 fails and 1.0.108 passes, so a third commit raises the `trybuild` minimum to 1.0.108. The lockfile is unchanged, since it already uses 1.0.119. Under minimal versions, all 594 tests pass with all features.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the same with `--all-features`
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`, with and without `--all-features`
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo test --workspace` (581 passed), and with `--all-features` (594 passed)
- [x] `cargo +1.85 test --workspace --all-features -- --skip ui --exact` (593 passed)
- [x] `cargo test -p bryl-nacha --no-default-features` (187 passed)
- [x] wasm32 `cargo check` without default features, with and without `bryl-nacha/serde,bryl-metro2/serde`
- [x] `./scripts/test-packaged-crates.sh --all-features` (594 passed)
- [x] `cargo check` in `fuzz/`

author: brianckeegan
body:
## Summary

Closes #108.

**Root cause.** `pvalue_method="auto"` switched to the refined normal approximation (RNA, Hong 2013) whenever there were more than 200 artifacts. The RNA matches the first three moments of the Poisson-binomial, but its far upper tail is too light when a pair's expected co-occurrence μ is small, which describes almost every pair in a sparse incidence matrix. The cutoff was too strict on cost (the exact tables were tabulated once per pair of agent-degree classes, not per pair) and too loose on accuracy.

**Measured cost.** In the unconstrained SDSM the exact cost is shared: there is one table per pair of distinct agent degrees, not one per agent pair. The old full convolution cost `n_class_pairs × n_f² / 2`, for example 5.3 s on 2000×2000 and 19.7 s on 5000×5000. With edge constraints (SDSM-EC) the cost is per agent pair.

**What changed**
- **Truncated exact convolution** (`_pb_tail_table`). P(X ≥ k) and P(X ≤ k) only need the law up to k, so each table stops at the largest co-occurrence that can be observed. That is the smaller of the two degrees, or the observed count with constraints. The mass above the cut is accumulated as it crosses it (a sum of non-negative terms), so tiny tails keep full relative precision (tested against the full pmf down to about 1e-30). Tables with similar cut points are grouped in chunks. For k = 0 the SDSM-EC lower tail P(X = 0) is computed as a product. Building the tables is 8–60× faster:

  | input | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | 2000×2000, density 0.01 | 5.3 s | 0.18 s |
  | 5000×5000, density 0.002 | 19.7 s | 0.35 s |
  | 1000×1000, density 0.1 | 5.8 s | 0.73 s |

- **"auto" from measured cost.** The cost model counts cell updates plus a per-step overhead and was checked at 4–6 ns per unit on 6 shapes, including heavy-tailed degree distributions. `"auto"` is exact when the estimate is at most `max(1e9, 25 × n_pairs)` cells: about 4 s, or about the cost of scoring the pairs. For the issue's reproducer that takes 0.02 s.
- **Over budget** (rare: many artifacts and many distinct high degrees). The class pairs with the **smallest expected co-occurrence**, where the RNA fails, keep exact tails in that order while the budget allows. The RNA covers the rest, and a `RuntimeWarning` gives the share of pairs and the smallest μ among them. SDSM-EC over budget uses the RNA for every pair and warns.
- `pvalue_method="rna"` is **unchanged** (R parity). The R-fixture tests already pass `"rna"` explicitly and still pass.
- Docs:
  - `sdsm` docstring: the `pvalue_method` entry, Warns, and a new Notes paragraph with the evidence.
  - Bipartite tutorial: the RNA passage, and section "Scale" now compares `auto` with `rna`. New hidden asserts check that `auto` keeps no noise pairs and is identical to `exact`.
  - "Coming from R" guide: the SDSM passages.
  - `docs/tutorials/bipartite_backbone.rst`, the changelog and the roadmap.

## Results changed

- 2000×500 pure-noise matrix (density 0.01, `default_rng(0)`), default `pvalue_method`:
  - smallest p-value: 5.7e-37 → 3.9e-05 (the issue reported 7.8e-05 for exact; I measure 3.9e-05 on the matrix input)
  - pairs kept by BH at 0.05: **1,498 → 0**
- Bipartite tutorial, section "Scale" (planted group of 30): noise pairs kept with the default: 161 / 1,435 (RNA) → **0 / 0** at 1000 / 2000 agents.
- Davis and every input with ≤ 200 artifacts were already exact. Their p-values change only in the last bit, from the truncated summation; no backbone changes. Les Misérables is not affected (not bipartite).

## Calibration evidence

Null simulation: each replicate draws B ~ Bernoulli(P0) cell by cell, and SDSM refits the BiCM on B. The table gives the share of all agent pairs with p below each level, over 5 replicates per setting. The tests are discrete, so a valid test has share ≤ level.

| setting (seed) | method | p<0.05 | p<0.01 | p<1e-3 | p<1e-4 | p<1e-6 | BH(0.05) kept per replicate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform 600×300, P0 = 0.01 (11) | **before** (auto = RNA) | 5.8e-3 | 2.9e-3 | 1.5e-3 | **7.2e-4** | **2.0e-4** | 136, 123, 123, 128, 120 |
| | **after** (auto = exact) | 1.5e-2 | 8.9e-4 | 4.3e-5 | 1.1e-6 | 0 | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 |
| uniform 300×200, P0 = 0.1 (12) | before = after (exact) | 1.5e-2 | 1.3e-3 | 4.9e-5 | 0 | 0 | 0 ×5 |
| | RNA, for reference | 1.2e-2 | 1.3e-3 | 1.3e-4 | 8.9e-6 | 0 | 0 ×5 |
| heavy-tailed 600×1500, Pareto(2) propensities, mean degree 8 (13; P0 from `default_rng(1)`) | **before** (auto = RNA) | 4.9e-3 | 2.4e-3 | 1.2e-3 | **6.0e-4** | **2.2e-4** | 80, 63, 75, 96, 89 |
| | **after** (auto = exact) | 1.2e-2 | 1.3e-3 | 9.1e-5 | 5.6e-6 | 0 | 0 ×5 |
| | after, budget forced to 2e6 cells (exact for small μ, RNA for the rest) | 1.2e-2 | 1.3e-3 | 1.3e-4 | 1.2e-5 | 1.1e-6 | 0 ×5 |

By expected co-occurrence μ, in the heavy-tailed setting:
- μ < 0.1: the RNA's share below 1e-6 is 2.8e-4.
- 0.1 ≤ μ < 1: 6.1e-5.
- 1 ≤ μ < 10: 0, and its share below 1e-3 is 1.9e-4, so it is valid there.

This supports giving the exact tail to small-μ pairs first when over budget. The new tests in `tests/test_calibration.py` turn the uniform sparse case (300×250, 3 draws) into a fast check: the shares are at most alpha + 4 se for `auto` and `exact`, and the RNA's share below 1e-4 is above 3e-4.

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

These are fixes for 1.8.0, found while testing it on a phone. They are published as the beta pre-release [v1.8.1b1](https://github.com/onoffautomations/yidstore/releases/tag/v1.8.1b1).

- **"Restart required" stuck after a restart.** 1.8.0 stored a restart flag on the package and never cleared it. Updated integrations kept showing "Restart required" and looked outdated, even though the new files were in place.
  - Now only "no restart needed" is stored as final.
  - A pending restart uses the "updated since Home Assistant started" check, so it clears itself after the restart.
  - The fix is in `dashboard.py` and `sensor.py`.
- **Update opened the setup wizard.** Updating an integration that was installed but not yet set up started the wizard. Like the Marketplace, the wizard now only opens after a fresh install. An update ends with "updated to vX".
- **Restart left the page.** When Home Assistant hadn't loaded its restart dialog yet, YidStore opened Settings → System to load it. Now Restart stays on the page:
  - Home Assistant's own dialog when it is loaded.
  - Otherwise YidStore's matching dialog: Quick reload, Restart, and Reboot / Shut down when a Supervisor is present.
  - The actions go through `/api/yidstore/restart`.
- **Configure in place.** Set-up integrations that have settings get **Configure**, which opens their options flow in the same dialog. The flow endpoints take `kind=options`. The forms are translated by the integration, not by the config entry.

## Testing
- Python byte-compiles and the dashboard script passes `node --check`. hassfest passes.
- In a phone-sized browser with mocked endpoints:

author: vasilistotskas
body: ## Problem An operator could not switch the control plane's admin to English, the way a store admin can. Investigating it found three separate causes, and a fourth defect that also hit the store admin. | # | Cause | Where | |---|---|---| | 1 | The platform admin was mounted at the unprefixed `admin/` only. The urlconf has `i18n_patterns`, so `LocaleMiddleware` answers every unprefixed path in `LANGUAGE_CODE` and ignores the `django_language` cookie. `set_language` redirects to `/en/admin/`, which did not exist on that host (404). | `tenant/urls_public.py` | | 2 | `UNFOLD_PLATFORM` has no `SHOW_LANGUAGES` / `LANGUAGE_FLAGS`. It is merged over Unfold's defaults, not over `UNFOLD`, so the platform admin rendered no switcher at all. | `settings.py` | | 3 | Django's `set_language` resolves `next` (here the referrer, since Unfold's form posts no `next`) under the ACTIVE language. The view is mounted unprefixed, so the active language is always `LANGUAGE_CODE`; `/en/admin/` can never be translated back to Greek. This broke English -> Greek on the **store** admin too. | `core/urls.py` | ## Fix, at the roots - Platform admin mounted in `i18n_patterns(..., prefix_default_language=False)` exactly like the store admin: `/admin/` (Greek) and `/en/admin/`. - `ADMIN_LANGUAGE_FLAGS` is one constant shared by `UNFOLD` and `UNFOLD_PLATFORM`; both set `SHOW_LANGUAGES`. - `core.views.set_language` activates the language the posted address already carries and delegates to Django's view; the redirect, cookie and safety checks stay Django's. No migration. The existing "store admin is not reachable on the platform host" guard still passes under both languages, and its "still reachable" test now accepts either address form. ## Verification - `tests_mt/test_admin_language_switch.py` (12 cases): both hosts x both languages. It reads the switcher form out of the rendered page and posts exactly its fields with the page as referrer: address per language, `Content-Language` and ``, Greek -> English and English -> Greek, every language offered. Before the fix it failed on the platform host (no switcher, 404) and on both hosts for English -> Greek; the store-host cases for Greek -> English passed already. - Related lanes: `tests/unit` tenant/core/admin 3674 passed, integration admin/tenant passed, `tests_mt` platform/admin/routing files 77 passed, `ruff`, `ty`, `manage.py check` clean. - The full `tests_mt` run on my machine hit "out of shared memory / max_locks_per_transaction" in the shared local Postgres (79 setup errors, no failures); I re-ran the relevant files serially instead. CI runs the whole lane. - Not done: reproducing on staging. I cannot reach it from here, so this was reproduced against real middleware, urlconf and templates in the multi-tenant lane. Docs: grooveshop-docs PR to follow, draft until this is live. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsrseR5L6psGVfGNSLAzQ5

author: chetan-metrum-ai
body:
## Summary

A localhost synthetic regression reproduced two distinct Responses system-part boundaries colliding in the normalized cache key on a PII-enabled group; the second request received the first cached response. Until #645 supplies a reviewed target-bound identity, this safety-first change bypasses **both reads and writes** of the router response cache for requests evaluated against PII-enabled groups. Other groups retain existing caching. Otherwise-cacheable requests report `cache-pii-filter` as a bounded reason.

Closes #670. This mitigates the cache collision; it does not complete #645 or fix instruction filtering and shadow replay.

## Verification

- Focused localhost tests pass for the reproduced collision, old-entry read bypass and no replacement, a PII-disabled seeded-hit positive control, retry/fallback with an actual redaction, fail-on-match without dispatch, and streaming/tool/client-control telemetry precedence.
- A localhost tool-call/file/result continuation test passed. No hosted provider calls were used.
- Independent security review and re-review completed; diff secret scan passed.

## Limits and cutover

The guard uses the policy captured by each request; it is not an instantaneous activation barrier. For a strict cutover, pause and drain requests and confirm that every replica has loaded the enabled policy. Existing cache entries are not purged and can become eligible again if filtering is disabled, until expiry or cache reset. Upstream call volume and cost can rise for PII-enabled groups. The successful fallback test checks its outgoing synthetic value, not the body of the deliberately failing first target.

author: charliermarsh
body:
## Summary

CPython’s `_pyio` imports `__all__` from `io` and keeps the same list. Imre rejected that import while compiling an ordinary program and raised `ImportError` in a runtime-loaded module.

We now initialize `io.__all__` with the 24 public names in CPython 3.14.5 order. A named import gets the current list, and wildcard imports read the live module binding. The first entry, `BlockingIOError`, resolves to the existing builtin exception in both `io` and `_io`.

```python
import io
from io import __all__ as names

assert names is io.__all__
assert names[0] == "BlockingIOError"
assert io.BlockingIOError is BlockingIOError
```

The unchanged `_pyio.py` import advances to `Reader`. Walking the full list still requires the buffered stream classes, starting with `BufferedReader`. [CPython export list](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/5607950ef232dad16d75c0cf53101d9649d89115/Lib/io.py#L43-L49)

body: Fix remote WebDAV certificate failures without disabling WAN HTTPS trust globally. Add a read-only certificate inspector (no NAS credentials), show system trust reason / SHA-256 fingerprint / host / port in remote WebDAV settings. Allow an explicit, user-confirmed exact leaf certificate pin only after independent NAS-side fingerprint verification; bind it to one host and TCP port in this device's Keychain. Changed certificates fail closed, other remote HTTPS endpoints continue using iOS normal trust. Share the trust handler across foreground and background URLSession. Fix misleading error text previously directing remote users to a LAN-only insecure toggle. Add unit and real self-signed WebDAV CI tests (trusted remote 8766 vs untrusted 8767). No private NAS credentials or ports published.

author: goodsoo
body:
## 한 줄 임팩트
쌓인 녹음을 메모에 바로 연결하고 그 자리에서 다시 듣는다

## 문제 (Why)
회의 녹음은 `_audio` 폴더에 쌓이기만 하고, 전사본을 어느 메모에 붙일지는 터미널에서 손으로 옮겨야 했다. 그래서 녹음 46개 중 메모에 연결된 건 0개였다. 또 메모 폼은 본문만 고쳐도 음성 기록(사이드카)까지 통째로 다시 저장해서, 앱 밖에서 사이드카를 바꾸면 다음 본문 편집이 그걸 덮어썼다.

## Before
![before-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goodsoo/goodsoob-memory/e6a37440fe887eb7f97b72d0e7637900f2d298c5/.github/screenshots/feat-recording-tab-pr1/recording-tab-pr1-before-1.png)
오늘 화면과 탭 바. 녹음은 앱 어디에도 보이지 않는다.

![before-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goodsoo/goodsoob-memory/e6a37440fe887eb7f97b72d0e7637900f2d298c5/.github/screenshots/feat-recording-tab-pr1/recording-tab-pr1-before-2.png)
메모의 음성 기록 탭. 전사 텍스트만 있고 원래 녹음으로 돌아갈 길이 없다.

## After
![after-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goodsoo/goodsoob-memory/e6a37440fe887eb7f97b72d0e7637900f2d298c5/.github/screenshots/feat-recording-tab-pr1/recording-tab-pr1-after-1.png)
오늘 화면 맨 위에 "처리할 녹음 42개". 탭 순서는 ⌘3 녹음, ⌘4 포트폴리오.

![after-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goodsoo/goodsoob-memory/e6a37440fe887eb7f97b72d0e7637900f2d298c5/.github/screenshots/feat-recording-tab-pr1/recording-tab-pr1-after-3.png)
녹음 탭. 행선지별 그룹, 녹음 시각·길이·전사 단계 칩.

![after-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goodsoo/goodsoob-memory/e6a37440fe887eb7f97b72d0e7637900f2d298c5/.github/screenshots/feat-recording-tab-pr1/recording-tab-pr1-after-2.png)
녹음 상세. 플레이어, 행선지 3택(기존 메모 연결 / 새 메모 / 전사만 보관), 전사 미리보기.

## 디자인 결정
- **전사본은 연결하는 순간 메모 옆으로 "이사"한다(복사 아님).** 녹음 파일은 언젠가 지워도 되는 부산물이고 남는 건 메모에 붙은 전사본이다. 그래서 연결 전엔 `_audio/<base>.txt`, 연결하면 `<메모>.transcript.md` 끝에 `## {시각} · {base}` 섹션으로 옮긴다. 모든 전사본을 `_audio` 에 두고 메모가 참조만 하는 안은 기존 사이드카 18개와 두 갈래가 생겨 버렸다.
- **이사는 서버 한 곳에서, 메모 경로 단위 잠금 안에서 멱등으로.** 섹션 추가 → `audio:` 기록 → `moved.json`·`done` → 원본 삭제 순서라, 중간에 끊겨도 다음 진입 때 같은 호출로 마무리된다. 같은 메모에 녹음 둘을 동시에 연결해도 섹션이 사라지지 않는다(통합 테스트).
- **메모 폼은 바뀐 칸만 저장한다.** 연결 직후 열린 폼에서 본문을 한 글자 치면 이사한 섹션이 지워지는 문제를 eng review 에서 코드로 확인하고 이 PR 의 첫 커밋으로 막았다. 그 수정이 만든 회귀(실패한 칸이 다른 칸 저장 성공에 묻혀 "저장됨"으로 보이던 것)도 독립 리뷰로 찾아 고쳤다.
- **오늘 블록은 기간 제한 없이 전체 개수.** 옛 녹음까지 세서 42개로 크게 뜨지만, 큰 숫자가 연결을 재촉하는 장치라 최근 N일로 줄이지 않았다.
- **할 일·루틴 탭은 곧 없어질 예정이라 녹음·포트폴리오를 그 앞으로 당겼다.** 두 탭을 지워도 ⌘1~4 가 그대로 남는다.
- 화자분리·Claude 교정(PR2), 리뷰·적용(PR3)은 이 PR 범위 밖. 해당 단계 녹음은 상태 칩만 보여준다.

## 유저가 얻는 것
- 녹음을 고르고 메모를 고르면 끝. 터미널에서 파일을 옮길 필요가 없다.
- 메모의 음성 기록 탭에서 섹션마다 ▶ 로 원래 녹음을 바로 다시 듣는다.
- 연결을 풀거나 다른 메모로 옮겨도 전사본이 사라지지 않는다(헤딩을 못 찾으면 텍스트는 그대로 두고 안내).
- 앱 밖에서 고친 음성 기록을 본문 편집이 덮어쓰는 일이 없어졌다.

author: angusmcglynn
body:
Clients need a focused view of their own work without the staff planning and administration tools. This adds `/client/` to the existing Plane web app and backend, using native sessions and existing work, page, comment, file and Intake models.

The client UI follows Plane’s project tree, compact toolbar, list/board styling and menus. Work items open in a side-peek frame shared with the staff interface; requests use the existing modal. Home is the default landing view and reuses Plane’s greeting component and dashboard layout. It shows complete scoped work/page counts and links to active work and shared pages. Website performance and attribution panels can be enabled independently per client; they show explicit unconnected states, with no analytics integration or invented results. Status sections use thin dividers without filled backgrounds.

Client accounts have a permanent classification and explicit portal access. Server checks deny staff APIs, API keys, unshared/private content and cross-project file access. Replies are EXTERNAL, document sharing is explicit, protected files are proxied, and request/reply writes have transactional deduplication receipts. Workspace and project admins can manage sharing and Home panels and open a read-only preview. Existing staff comments remain Private by default.

Validation: 64 focused backend tests pass locally, including isolation, revocation, CSRF, malformed rich text, deduplication, attachment boundaries, Home totals beyond list pagination and admin-only panel configuration. Django checks and migration consistency pass. Production web build, TypeScript and lint pass. Chrome verification covers login, sharing and Home-setting persistence, list/board/filter/display controls, pages, requests, replies, upload/download byte equality, side-peek, Home navigation and mobile layout.

This is a draft for review and staging. Additive migrations `client_portal.0001_initial` and `0002_clientportal_performance_panels` must run before serving the new code. Production remains unchanged. Existing Morse client accounts require a separate migration decision; no invitations, email notifications or board migrations are performed. See `deployments/morse/CLIENT-PORTAL.md` for setup and rollout details.

author: icyshadow5
body:
## What this changes

Android release signing is currently validated inline in the workflow: secrets are checked by name, and the keystore is decoded into a fixed path in `$RUNNER_TEMP` right before the build. Failures surface as raw `keytool` output, and a bad secret is only discovered after the SDK setup and unit tests have already run.

This PR replaces that with a testable preflight script, a safer temporary keystore, and an interactive Termux helper for uploading the secrets.

### Signing preflight (`android/scripts/android-signing-preflight.sh`)

Two modes:

- `validate` runs **before** the Android SDK and unit tests. It checks all four secrets, the Base64 payload, the decoded keystore, the keystore password, the alias and private-key access without building an APK. The decoded keystore is always deleted before success is reported, and no path is exported.
- `prepare-signing` runs immediately before `assembleRelease`, validates again, keeps the keystore only on success, and exports its exact path through `GITHUB_ENV` for the build.

The temporary keystore is created with `mktemp` (unique name, `umask 077`, mode `600`) instead of a fixed `melo-release.jks`. Nothing removes, truncates or overwrites a pre-existing file that happens to use the old name, concurrent runs use independent filenames, and a repeated run cannot delete an earlier run's keystore.

Cleanup fails closed: if deletion fails during validation, the run exits non-zero and emits an error annotation instead of printing a success line.

Failures use stable categories so the cause is visible in the Actions annotation: `missing-secret`, `invalid-base64`, `invalid-keystore`, `cannot-open-keystore`, `missing-alias`, `wrong-key-password`, `unusable-private-key`, plus `keytool-missing`, `base64-missing`, `tempfile-error` and `usage-error` for runner problems. Passwords, the Base64 payload, decoded keystore bytes and raw `keytool` output are never printed.

### Workflow changes (`.github/workflows/android-release.yml`)

- Signing validation moves ahead of the Android SDK and unit-test steps.
- The keystore is prepared immediately before the build instead of at an earlier point.
- `Remove temporary keystore` now runs immediately after `Build signed release APK` and keeps `if: always()`. The private key is removed before signature verification, artifact upload and GitHub Release publishing. Those publishing operations are unchanged, and none of them read the keystore path.

### Termux helper (`android/scripts/setup-termux-signing.sh`)

New helper for uploading the four secrets from a phone:

- uses `--keystore`, then `./melo-release.jks`, then `~/melo-release.jks`;
- never generates or overwrites a key;
- verifies the keystore password, alias and private-key access locally;
- prompts for passwords without echoing them;
- uploads the four secrets through standard input, so no `.b64` copy or plaintext password file is left behind;
- reports which secret failed and that an unsuccessful `gh secret set` may still have changed the remote state, so reruns are safe;
- refuses any repository other than `hakosworld-blip/melo` unless the target is passed explicitly with `--repo` and `--allow-non-target-repo` and typed back to confirm; `--yes` does not skip that check;
- does not start a release.

`android/README.md` documents the preflight, the workflow ordering, the Termux flow, and the rule that an existing keystore must be reused rather than regenerated.

### Tests

`android/scripts/tests/run.sh` runs two synthetic suites (no real credentials, throwaway keystores, mocked `gh`):

- every preflight error category and its message;
- redaction of passwords, Base64 and `keytool` output;
- a pre-existing `melo-release.jks` surviving validation byte-for-byte;
- concurrent and repeated runs using independent keystore files;
- successful validation leaving no decoded keystore;
- cleanup failure producing a failed run with no success output;
- workflow ordering: no keystore during SDK setup or unit tests, cleanup immediately after the build with `if: always()`, and before verification, upload and release;
- Termux helper defaults, repository refusal, typed confirmation, and partial-upload messaging.

A new read-only workflow (`.github/workflows/android-signing-scripts.yml`) runs these tests on script changes with `contents: read`.

## Verification

- signing preflight tests: 164 passed, 0 failed
- Termux helper tests: 109 passed, 0 failed
- `bash -n` on all five scripts
- YAML parse of both workflows
- `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check`
- LF attributes applied to all scripts

## Limitations

- **Real signing has not been verified.** The workflow has not been run with the owner's actual keystore and secrets, so a real `assembleRelease` with the production signing key is still unproven.
- **The end-to-end Android release has not been verified.** No APK was built, signed and published from this branch; verification and publishing steps are unchanged but untested here.
- The GitHub Actions workflow itself was not executed; ordering guarantees rest on the script tests and YAML validation.
- If removal of the temporary keystore fails after a successful validation, the run fails and names the file for manual deletion rather than claiming success.
- `cannot-open-keystore` covers both a wrong password and a corrupted keystore, because `keytool` reports the same message for both.

author: eccentricexit
body:
## What

The near-plane fix of the doublet's velocity (#62) left three routines with the old test: `Panel3::doubletBasisPotential()` returned 0 (the in-plane value outside the triangle) for any field point closer than `INPLANEPRECISION`, 1e-6 m, to the triangle's plane, and `sourcePotential()` and `sourceVelocity()` took the in-plane integrals there. They enter the thick surfaces' Dirichlet condition (the doublet's and the sources' potential at the collocation points, the wake's potential) and the sources' velocity on Neumann surfaces.

**Cause.** Off the plane the doublet's potential is -z times the integral of 1/r^3 over the triangle, and the source's normal velocity z times the same: a term of order z/d (d the point's distance to the triangle) that the in-plane value drops. Measured at a point 1e-5 m outside an edge, against an adaptive integration of the kernel (absolute values; the self terms are 2 pi):

| z (m) | 1e-9 | 1e-8 | 1e-7 | 5e-7 | 9e-7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| constant doublet's potential, LE cell 0.14 mm x 115 mm, outside its short edge | -1.7e-4 | -1.7e-3 | -0.017 | -0.086 | -0.155 |
| the same, outside its long edge | -3.0e-5 | -3.0e-4 | -3.0e-3 | -0.015 | -0.027 |
| a 2 mm x 20 mm cell, outside its long edge | -2.9e-6 | -2.9e-5 | -2.9e-4 | -1.5e-3 | -2.6e-3 |

The in-plane routing gave 0 for all of these; the off-plane integrals hold them to 2e-15. The source's normal velocity is the same numbers with the other sign; the source's potential was off by 7e-8 at most.

## The fix

The three take the in-plane integrals only within the coordinates' rounding, `PLANEROUNDING` (1e-12 m), as the doublet's velocity does since #62; the comments of `PLANEROUNDING` and `computeNFIntegrals()` say so for every caller.

## Verification (thick TRIUNIFORM, Dirichlet, inviscid, fixed lift, alpha -2 to 8 by 2; a 1.5 m wing of 0.2 m chord with a dihedral break, alone and with a fin; before = a259de3, after = this branch; build OK)

| meshing | CL | Cm | CDi | derivatives at alpha 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13 TANH chordwise on the wing, 7 on the fin | within 1e-7 | within 2.5e-7 | within 1e-8 | within 6e-6 relative (Cmu) |
| 52 cosine on the wing, 28 on the fin | 0.0008 to 0.0010 lower (zero-lift angle -2.956 -> -2.944 deg; lift slope 4.6390 -> 4.6402 per rad) | 1.5e-4 to 1.8e-4 higher | up to 6.9e-5 lower | not run |

With the fin the changes are the same within 7e-6. Run times within their spread (52 panels: 17.5 -> 16.1 s, 23.8 -> 21.3 s).

**Not changed:** the NASA 4023 routines (`doubletN4023Potential()`, `sourceN4023Potential()`, `sourceN4023Velocity()`) keep their own 1e-6 m test; they were not measured here.

body: Fixes #3467 (task 5402). Three `KindDuration` settings are passed directly to `time.NewTicker` — `daemon.reapInterval` and `daemon.saveInterval` (daemon/server.go:583,585) and `http.ssePing` (daemon/server.go:1563) — and `time.NewTicker` panics on a non-positive period. body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **배포 승인 전 관리자가 `migrations/0006_board.sql`을 먼저 실행해야 해요.**
> 실행하지 않고 배포하면 홈 화면과 게시판이 "불러오지 못했어요"로 나와요 (홈이 새 표 `posts`를 읽기 때문).
> 명령: `npx wrangler d1 execute broadcasting-db --remote --file=./migrations/0006_board.sql`
> 파일 올리기가 막히면 주석을 뺀 SQL을 `--command`로 실행하면 돼요 (SQL 값에는 영문·숫자만 있어요).

## 무엇을 바꿨나요?

- **게시판(`?board`)이 열렸어요.** 선생님 공지와 부원 메모를 한곳에서 봐요. [전체] [공지] [메모] 탭과 20개씩 '더 보기'가 있어요.
- **공지는 선생님만** 쓸 수 있고, 맨 위 고정은 3개까지예요. **메모는 누구나** 써요.
- 학생은 자기 메모만 고치고 지울 수 있어요. 선생님은 선생님 글을 고치고, 모든 글을 지울 수 있어요. 이 권한은 서버에서 확인해요.
- **읽음 확인:** 학생이 공지를 펼치면 읽음으로 기록돼요. 선생님은 공지마다 "읽음 n / m" 버튼으로 읽은 부원과 안 읽은 부원 이름을 봐요.
- **홈:** '새 공지' 카드에 고정 공지와 최근 공지 3개가 나와요. 학생에게는 안 읽은 공지에 빨강 '새', 선생님에게는 '공지 쓰기' 버튼과 '읽음 n/m'이 보여요. 학생의 '내 할 일'에 안 읽은 고정 공지가 붙어요.
- 학생 계정을 지우면 그 학생의 읽음 기록도 함께 지워져요.
- 사용법 화면에 '게시판' 설명을 넣었어요.

## 왜 바꿨나요?

공지와 메모가 사이트 밖(말·종이·메신저)에서 오가서, 선생님이 누가 공지를 읽었는지 알 수 없었어요. (SPEC CAP-3, 스토리 3)

## 확인한 것

- [x] 내 컴퓨터(`npm run dev`)에서 직접 눌러 보며 확인했어요. 로컬 시험 계정과 이 컴퓨터에서만 쓰는 시험용 선생님 비밀번호로 확인했고, 운영 사이트의 실제 계정으로는 확인하지 않았어요.
- [x] 휴대폰 크기 화면에서도 확인했어요 (360px·1280px, 밝은/어두운 화면, 가로 스크롤 없음)
- [x] 학생 계정과 선생님 계정 둘 다 확인했어요 (권한이 관련된 경우)
- [x] 기존 주소 `?scripts`, `?id=`, `?new`, `?calendar`, `?help`, `?accounts`, `?inbox`가 예전처럼 열려요
- [x] `npm test` 29개 통과 (실제 SQLite로 읽음·쪽 넘기기를 확인하는 시험 포함), `npm run check` 통과
- 코드 검토 뒤 고친 화면 부분(빈 탭 문구, 더 보기로 연 글 고치기 등 7개)은 브라우저로 다시 눌러 보지 않았어요.
