author: godardt
body: ## What and why FRAMEWORK-268, fix 4. A lane that calls a member with the mark `reaches_for_item` needed a `kind: "reach"` assumption whose check reads an observation of its role. Assumptions are checked before the run, and the `args` of an observation take no `$ref`, so no such check could read the position of the item that the perception of the run gives. In the chat of the item, the robot session guessed the height of the work surface for `workspace.describe_workspace`. The checker now also takes reach checks in the lane, named before the reaching call on every path (`Workflow::names_before_calls` of `workflow_documents`). The `done_when` of a reach check fails the step when the robot does not reach the item, before the reach. - A reach check is a call whose member gives, on every pin that the role reads, one required boolean result field with the mark `checks_reach` of the same name, with `as` and a `done_when` that is that field of its result, alone or as a term of `&&` (`reach_check_of`, `reach_verdict`, `gates_on`). A `done_when` such as `!near.all_workable`, `near.all_workable || x` or `size(near.results) > 0` is no reach check. - A reach check covers only the items whose position it reads. Each name of a role has a source: the result or the observation that gives it, and, for a loop element, the source of the list of its loop. Each `$ref` of an item id or a position of the reaching call must have the source of a `robot_frame` argument of a reach check before it (`reached_sources`, `checked_sources`). A check of another item leaves the call unchecked, and the error names the source that no check reads. - `may_have_mark` keeps `any` for `reaches_for_item`: a call that may reach is checked as one. - The rule walks the trees of a role once (`Workflow::trees_of`), and reads the reach checks and the names before each call only for a lane that reaches with no reach assumption. - `Cargo.lock` pins public-peppy-libs at f54797a, the merge of public-peppy-libs #180 of this set into `main`. ## How it was tested - `cargo test --lib`: 209 passed. Reach tests: - `a_lane_that_checks_the_reach_of_the_item_before_it_reaches_needs_no_reach_assumption`: the field alone, and as a term of `&&`. - `a_reach_check_counts_only_when_it_gates_the_reach_on_every_path`: refused for a member with no verdict field, no `done_when`, a `done_when` that is no gate on the field (`seen.found`, `reach.margin > 0.01`, `!reach.reachable`, `reach.reachable || seen.found`, `reach.reachable == true`), the check in one branch of an `if`, and the check after the grab. - `a_reach_check_covers_only_the_item_whose_position_it_reads`: a check of another item is refused and names the source of the grabbed item; checks of both items pass. - `a_loop_element_is_checked_by_a_reach_check_of_the_list_of_its_loop`. - `a_reach_check_counts_only_when_every_pin_gives_its_verdict`: refused before a binding when one pin of the fleet gives no verdict field, accepted once the role is bound to the robot whose pin gives it. - `cargo test --tests` with `PEPPY_ZENOHD_PATH`: 24 + 12 passed. - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean. - `test_arm.json5` gives `reachable`, the result field of `check_reach`, the mark `checks_reach`, and the test perception gives the positions of a scan. ## The set (branch `feat/reach-check-in-lane`) - contracts-hub: the mark `checks_reach` on `all_workable`, the boolean field of the result of `check_positions` of `workspace:v1`. - mcp-hub: the `sha256` pins of `workspace:v1` and `item_manipulation:v1` in `robot/robot_control.json5`, whose bytes the contracts-hub change of this set changes. - public-peppy-libs (#180, merged into `main` as f54797a): `CHECKS_REACH`, `Workflow::names_before_calls`, `Workflow::trees_of`, `Workflow::step`, `StepRef::parse`, and the rule in `LANGUAGE.md`. - nodes-hub: the director takes a reach check in the lane that reads the position of each item that the reaching call reaches (its lock pins public-peppy-libs at f54797a). - platform: sim-chat pins public-peppy-libs at f54797a (the prompt reads `LANGUAGE.md`), step 3 of the robot session prompt, and the eval case of fix 3. Plane: FRAMEWORK-268, fix 4. You chose this design: the check goes in the lane, not in the contract or the director. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? author: jddunn
body:
## What changed

A review of #159 found that Settings drops a unit name the person gave a preset leader. Launch Atlas Lab with the first leader's unit set to "East Wing", open Settings again, and the field shows "East Wing" while GET /scenario loads, then turns back to "Lab Alpha" when Atlas Lab's preset arrives. Before #159 the preset branch kept the unit the form already held; #159 replaced it with the preset's unit so that a unit left by another scenario's run would not carry over, and that also replaced units stored by a run of the same scenario.

Settings now keeps the unit of a preset leader when the stored roster was launched on this scenario and the unit is not the fallback scenario's default. A unit stored by another scenario's run still takes this scenario's word, and a unit typed since the page opened still wins.

The same run was also lost when Settings opened again without a reload. Launch moves to the Sim tab, so going back to Settings mounts the form with Atlas Lab already loaded, and the form was built from the preset alone: the first leader's unit came back as "Lab Alpha" and a third leader added for that run was dropped. The form now starts from the last launch's leaders whether or not the scenario has loaded, and the preset goes in by one rule (`withPresetLeaders`) both when the form starts and when GET /scenario answers, so Settings shows the same leaders after a reload and after a tab change.

## Issue

No issue

## Spec, plan and design

None

## Pictures

No visible change in layout: the Unit fields keep the stored words instead of the preset's, and a run with three leaders shows three.

## Docs

No doc describes how Settings fills its leaders, so none changes.

## Tests

tests-e2e/specs/run-control.spec.ts, against the real server with only /setup intercepted; each test was pushed first and failed in CI before its fix:

- "a unit from this scenario's last run stays on a preset leader" launches Atlas Lab with the first unit set to "East Wing", reloads Settings with GET /scenario held, releases it, waits for Atlas Lab's start time to land and checks the unit and the next launch's body.
- "this scenario's last run is in Settings when it opens again from another tab" launches Atlas Lab with the first unit set to "East Wing" and a third leader in "West Wing", goes back to Settings from the Sim tab without a reload, and checks the three units and the next launch's body.

author: shydenmcm
body:
## Summary
Refs #230 (EXT S7b). Two commits, each green alone:

1. **A dividend read is one stock's, and history keeps the period it covers.** Spec §5.1 reads dividends per stock, and §7.1 needs each read's period. Before this, a dividend read named no stock, so an empty page couldn't say whose years it covered, and history dropped the period. The fixture broker now reads the page's stock from its `saham` table and refuses a row of another stock. History version 3 adds a `dividend-reads` store (stock, from, to), written in the same transaction as the rows. Dividends recorded before have no period, so they count as unread until the page is read again.
2. **dividend-growth**, the default strategy, ported from Python with missing versus ineligible, a `chartReach` judgement for the chart case, and a parity harness.

A review needs each stock's dividend read to reach the **advice day**, not only the end of last year. The trailing yield that breaks a spread's tie counts the last 365 days, so a read stopping at 31 December would break ties on partial data. An announced dividend with a later ex-date doesn't count yet, as in Python.

## Criteria
1. Ported with `min_stocks` 15, `max_stocks` 25, `growth_years` 5, a yearly review, and dividends restated in today's shares; `DEFAULT_STRATEGY` is `dividend-growth`. `dividend-growth.test.ts` ports every case of Python's `tests/engine/test_dividend_growth.py`.
2. Missing versus ineligible, one test per case: missing (no read; read starting a day late; read ending before the advice day; every gap listed; memory kept); not judged (a member neither buyable nor held; a holding outside the universe); ineligible (a read covering a year with no dividend; a read with none at all); chart: missing (none, or its range starts late), ineligible (range reaches the start but the first close is later, or there's no close).
3. Chart reads already recorded their range. Dividend reads now name their stock and record their period, and the fixture reader refuses a page with no `periode` or `saham` table.
4. The look-back is 1 January of Y − growth_years − 1; a read starting a day later is missing.
5. `parity-dividend-growth.test.ts`: 71 days from 30 Python journeys (seed 230): 46 reviews, 19 reaching the pay-month spread, 9 with too few passers, 40 with splits. All match.
6. Locally: extension unit tests 2641 passed at 100% coverage; Python unit tests 2578 passed; lint, format, types and pre-push clean. Tests were written first; each new rule had a planted change in the code, every one caught.

author: abslock128w
body:
Defect 5 of the v0.4.2 performance test.

**Problem.** A test of the PR's own counts as change evidence only if its failure on the code before the change repeats in a fresh process. That rerun put all the failing tests in one process. Flask #5928's new `test_robust_teardown` fails on the code before the change and leaves teardown broken, so the 13 tests after it error there too (`ValueError: app_teardown`), and the rerun repeated exactly that. Alone, each of the 13 passes on the merge base. The comment said "14 tests … fail on the merge base"; 1 was true.

**Change** (`shadow._replay`): each failing test is rerun alone in its own process, up to 25 (`ALONE`); any beyond that are rerun together, as before. A test that passes alone is verdict `unstable` ("failed on the code before the change with the other tests, passed there alone in a fresh process") and is not counted as evidence.

**Test (fails on main, passes here):** `test_a_new_test_that_fails_before_only_after_another_one_broke_shared_state_is_not_evidence`. One new test fails on the base and leaves module state behind; the next new test fails only after it. Here only the first is evidence.

Locally `tests/ci` and `tests/core`: 282 passed.

body:
## Description

Fixes five P1 bugs from the 1.2.0 release-candidate QA sweep. In four of them a keyboard command could act on the wrong file; in the fifth, the 10xer folder picker searched outside home.

- **#1993, Columns after Back:** after Back, the ancestor columns had no cursor, so F2 and Delete fell back to the root column's open folder. Now, when Left reaches an ancestor column with no cursor, the cursor goes on the folder that column has open. If the column is still loading, the cursor is placed when it finishes, and if that folder is gone by then, nothing is placed. The "folder you just entered" fallback now applies only to the deepest column. Elsewhere, a column with no cursor gives F2, Delete, copy, cut and Duplicate nothing to act on.
- **#1994, renaming a filter result:** a cleanup pass dropped the renamed result before the index listed its new path, so focus and selection fell to whatever result sat in the old row. In Columns, row labels were also looked up by directory position, so the rename label appeared on the wrong row. The renamed result is now kept under its new path and followed, in List, Icons and Columns. This works whether the rename is committed with Enter or Tab, or made through 10xer's `r` prompt. A rename to a path in another folder (#1512) removes the result instead; nothing else takes its selection, as in the folder listing. Clearing is per rename, so overlapping renames keep the newer one's record. Columns labels are now looked up in the filter results. After a refused rename in Columns, focus returns to the result that was selected; on `main` it went to the first result.
- **#1995, range anchor:** in List and Icons, Strata's selection and GTK's internal list each keep their own range start (anchor), and they drifted apart. Plain Home, End, Page Up and Page Down did not reset GTK's anchor. Plain arrows and h/j/k/l, which GTK handles, did not update Strata's. In Columns, Shift+Home/End went to GTK, whose anchor was never set. Now Home, End and the page keys reset GTK's anchor. Arrows and h/j/k/l move Strata's anchor when the move changes the selection. In Columns, Shift+Home/End extend from Strata's anchor.
- **#1996, keys with focus in the preview:** Delete, Shift+Delete, Ctrl+D, F2/Ctrl+R and Ctrl+Alt+N are now ignored whenever keyboard focus is anywhere inside the preview, whatever kind of preview it is. The existing `PreviewDrawer::owns_focus` check decides this. Before, only text widgets were exempt.
- **#1997, `~//` in the folder picker:** `scope()` joined `"/x"` onto home, and joining an absolute path replaces the base. Leading slashes after `~/` are now trimmed. The other places that expand `~/` already trimmed them.

`docs/keyboard-navigation.md` now covers the rename, range-anchor and Back/Left behaviour. No user-facing strings changed.

Not verified locally:
- `scripts/code-health.sh` did not run, because `CS_ACCESS_TOKEN` was not set. The new functions were kept within the AGENTS.md code-health limits by hand.
- `new-folder-with-selection-groups/columns` fails intermittently on this machine, at line 34 (the clicked folder's column does not take focus). It fails as often on `main` (`ede64d92`), so it is not caused by this branch.

## Visual evidence

N/A. These are keyboard-routing, focus and selection fixes with nothing new to see; the behaviour is described above and in the steps below.

## How to test

1. **#1993:** in Columns, open `alpha/sub/inner` and select a file. Click a sidebar place, press Alt+Left, then Left twice. Press F2, then Escape, then Delete.
2. **#1994:** make a folder with `a.csv`, `b.csv`, `c.json` and `d.txt`, and turn Group by file type off. Press Ctrl+F, type `.`, and select `c.json`. Press F2, type `0.md`, press Enter, then press Delete. Repeat in Icons and Columns, and with 10xer's `r` prompt.
3. **#1995:** open a folder with 200 files. Press Down a few times, then End, then Shift+Home. Next, press Home, then Shift+Down. Then press Home, Down, and Shift+Page Down. Do this in List, Icons and Columns.
4. **#1996:** select a `.md`, `.pdf`, `.docx` or `.csv` file. Press Space, then Right to move focus into the preview. Press Delete, Ctrl+D and F2.
5. **#1997:** turn 10xer on, outside home. Press `g` and type `~//x`. Separately, select a file, press `C` and type `~//zzqa`, where no `zzqa*` folder exists in home.

**Expected result:**

1. F2 and Delete act on `sub`, not `alpha`.
2. `0.md` stays focused and selected, Delete trashes `0.md`, and every Columns row shows its own name.
3. Shift+Home after End selects all 200 files. Shift+Down after Home selects the first two. Shift+Page Down extends from the second file.
4. Nothing happens to the file, and the folder's file count does not change.
5. The searches stay below home: `go` shows only matches under home, and `copy to` finds no folders, so nothing is copied.

## Related issue

Closes #1993
Closes #1994
Closes #1995
Closes #1996
Closes #1997

## **Description**

<!-- mms-check: type=text required=true -->

<!--
Write a short description of the changes included in this pull request, also include relevant motivation and context. Have in mind the following questions:
1. What is the reason for the change?
2. What is the improvement/solution?
-->

**Problem.** When a user subscribes to Money Account Plus with a shortfall, checkout tops up exactly the missing mUSD through MetaMask Pay. That mUSD is deposited into the base Veda vault, and later migrated to the premium vault. The Veda teller mints `floor(amount * 1e6 / (rate + 1))` shares but values them at `floor(shares * rate / 1e6)`, so every deposit loses about 1 part per million plus a few base units.

For a fresh $4.99 subscription, the user funds 4,990,000 units, receives 4,989,995 vmUSD (verified on Monad), and ends at about 4,989,989 after the premium migration. The server balance check is strict (`value >= 4,990,000`), so the subscription stays in `awaiting_funds` even though the user paid the full price.

**Solution.** Pad the top-up with a fixed, rate-independent amount: **0.001% of the shortfall (rounded up) plus 10 base units (0.00001 mUSD)**.

- `getMembershipFundingAmount` (new `utils/membershipFundingAmount.ts`) computes the padded amount.
- `getTopUpAmountUsd` in `useStartProSubscription` now sends it at full 6-decimal precision instead of rounding up to cents. $4.99 funds 4.99006 mUSD; $499 funds 499.005 mUSD.
- The confirmation already truncates the displayed amount to 2 decimals (`formatAmountForDisplay`), and Money Account deposits skip fiat-rate conversion, so users still see **$4.99** / **$499.00**. 0.001% stays under 1 cent for plans up to about $1,000.
- No RPC reads, controller, selector, or UI changes.

The loss needs about 0.0002% plus a few units (two deposits). A unit test simulates the vault math across shortfalls from 1 unit to $1,000 and base/premium rates from 1.0 to 2.0, and asserts the padded funding always covers the shortfall.

**Out of scope (follow-ups):**
- The CHOMP invoice pull transfers the invoice amount as a raw pvmUSD share count, not value. With the premium rate at ~1.003 it can still fail or overcharge; that needs a backend change.
- Renewal and Pro Hub "add funds" top-ups, and users with a partial pre-existing balance, are not padded here.

**Edition:** Open Source
**Spec / task / ADR:** Spec 004 ST10 "The model doesn't answer", task 004-01; D123, D170; ADR 017 for done
**Design files:** product/design/canvas/Model-add-failed.dc.html (title "[Model] wasn't added", reason, "Check the details and try again.")

**What changed**
- `model_registry/registration.py`: when a local model the gateway registered doesn't answer through it and Keeplane removes its entry, the error is now "The model didn't answer through the gateway. Nothing was saved." Because it ends with "Nothing was saved.", the Models dialog adds "Check the details and try again." on its own, the way the other Add failures have worked since #211. The two approval-save failures (cloud and local) now also end with "Nothing was saved." once the entry is removed, in place of "Registration was removed."
- If the entry can't be removed, the message still says the model may remain in the gateway without Keeplane approval, and never says "Nothing was saved" (D170).
- Technical choice: for the cloud approval-save path, "nothing saved" depends only on the gateway entry being removed, as in the gateway-refused and provider-refused paths next to it. The key file is removed in the same branch, so the rule is the same everywhere.

**Checks run**
- `pytest tests/unit/test_models_routing.py`: new MRS-11 (no answer; entry removed and not removed) and MRS-12 (approval can't be saved, local and cloud; entry removed and not removed). 25 passed with the scenario map test.
- Model, registration, gateway, catalog and approval regression across tests/unit and tests/integration: 656 passed, 45 skipped. 2 failures, both outside this change: `test_bkg09` hit a permission error on the local virtualenv path, and `test_rsm_03` I fixed before committing.
- `npm run test:unit` in components/admin-ui: 82 passed, including the new MOD-UI-08 (local runner model: the new wording, and the "may remain" wording without "Nothing was saved"). `npm run lint` is clean.
- `ruff check components/control-plane --select F,E9`: passed.

**Not run**
- Live e2e `tests/e2e/test_model_add.py` (ADD-07 now checks for the exact new message). It needs the Docker preview.

**Docs changed**
- tests/unit/models-routing-cases.md (MRS-11 and MRS-12 added; the ST10 "The model doesn't answer" row now cites MRS-11, MRS-12 and MOD-UI-08), tests/unit/ui/cases.md (MOD-UI-08), tests/e2e/model-add-cases.md (case 7 wording).

**Effect on other repos:** none.

An admin adding a local model that doesn't answer now sees the same failure message as every other Add failure: the model wasn't added, nothing was saved, check the details and try again. Keeplane only says nothing was saved when it actually removed what it wrote to the gateway. Otherwise it still tells the admin to check Models.

body:
## What
The phone apps can open a PC through the Ovis relay since #2514 (shipped in v0.4.22), but the privacy policy still says the app connects only to the PCs you add and the push relay. This names both relay services, as v0.4.22 runs them:

- **`relay.ovis.sh`**: end-to-end encrypted between phone and PC; sees per connection the PC's relay ID and public key, phone-or-PC role, the connecting address, and when and how much passes, never the content; no logs, nothing stored, the address only rate-limits (`docs/relay.md` Trust model, `relay/README.md` What it sees and keeps).
- **`app.ovis.sh`**: the hosted phone app as static release files (Cloudflare Pages); sees file requests (phone address, PC relay ID in the path), never the `#offer=` fragment or the traffic.
- What the phone keeps for a relay PC: its `app.ovis.sh` address, name, and a per-PC key pair (private half non-extractable; the PC keeps the public half).

Files: `ovis-site/privacy/index.html`, `ovis-site/ko/privacy/index.html` (new "The Ovis relay" section, summary, network and on-phone sections, effective date), `app/store/android.md` (listing line, Data safety first route, in-transit note, Device or other IDs row, service providers, Later builds) and `app/store/ios.md` (listing line, review notes, App Privacy note). No Data safety or App Privacy answer changes: the relay adds no data type or recipient (content still goes only to the user's PC, E2E).

Docs-only; no code. Found while testing Android 1.0 (4) against relay.ovis.sh (lane android-relay-build). Follow-up for the app link and relay PC naming: #2599.

- `bun test scripts/ovis-site.test.ts scripts/ovis-site-platform.test.ts scripts/conventions.test.ts`: 45 pass.

author: amitcloudarchitect
body:
## What

Staff Home gets a **summary strip** above its five sections, as the user asked: "one high level widget … on-boarded customer count segregated by AWS and Azure with small, medium, large; total revenue across all the accounts, total margin, target and gap; health of all customers". It also wires the two places #113 left as "no data source yet". ADR 0044, migration 0042.

### The strip (`GET /v1/home/summary`)

The strip has its own date range and follows the customer selector (`ScopeDep`). It is for staff with `inventory.read` only, so a customer never gets it.

- **Customers:** onboarded customers in an Azure/AWS × Small/Medium/Large matrix, using #113's size bands (the same code as the Platform section). A customer on both clouds counts once in the total and once under each cloud, and the widget says so.
- **Revenue and margin:** shown only to roles with `commercial.read`.
  - **Totals:** total revenue and total margin are `/v1/commercial/revenue`'s `totals.reported`, read as served and never recomputed. The widget keeps the revenue table's count of customers left out of each total.
  - **Revenue target:** set in Settings (new). The overall target applies when the scope is the whole portfolio. Otherwise the customers' own targets apply, compared only with those customers' revenue. Each month's target is converted at the rate in force on that month's last day. A yearly target counts a twelfth per month and is shown as modelled. Gap = target − actual. If a month has no target or no rate, the range has no target and the widget says why; it never shows a partial target.
  - **Margin target:** the SOW's `target_margin`. Gap = actual margin − target × manage revenue, computed per customer in the contract currency. In the reporting currency it equals the contract-currency gap converted at the same month rates, because the target is a ratio. Customers without a target are counted as left out.
- **Health:** every customer in scope counted per band. The widget links to `/customer-health` (`GET /v1/home/sections/health`), which lists every customer, least healthy first.

### Revenue targets (migration 0042)

- **`cloudops.revenue_target`:** per customer, `tenant_id` NOT NULL. FORCE RLS with `tenant_isolation`, plus the restrictive `commercial_visibility` and `account_scope` policies.
- **`cloudops.revenue_target_overall`:** platform-wide. FORCE RLS lets only the commercial roles read it.
- **History:** both tables are versioned and append-only. A trigger refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, except #109's purge deleting a purged customer's own rows.
- **Money:** `numeric(18,6)` with its currency.
- **Writing:** the only write path is `access.set_revenue_target` (SECURITY DEFINER), behind the new commercial permission `targets.manage`. The CFO and the Platform administrator hold it by default. Every write is audited.
- **Settings page:** Settings → Revenue targets shows each target's history and, for holders of `targets.manage`, the form.

### Wiring #113 left pending

- **Revenue & margin section (staff):** reads `/v1/commercial/revenue` (in a reporting currency, with its compare range) and `/v1/commercial/project-prices`, broken down by component. "No data source yet" is gone.
- **Top 10:** each customer shows the revenue table's `current.reported.total_revenue`. `sort=revenue` ranks by it, largest first; a role without `commercial.read` gets 403 and sees nothing about revenue.
- **Cloud Services hook (#111):** the health score has a `cloud_services` part. It is not observed and weighs 0 until that source is served and the user sets its weight.

## Numbering

Migration **0042** (chained onto 0041, after #111 and #126) and ADR **0044**, as assigned.

## Tests

- **`services/api/tests/test_home_summary.py`:** which target version is in force, a yearly target's monthly share, per-month conversion in USD and GBP, months without a target or a rate.
- **`db/tests/test_api_home_sections.py`:**
  - each strip widget, and the totals equal to the revenue table's;
  - margin gap in EUR and GBP (+20 overall; −230 EUR = −200 GBP × 1.15 for one customer);
  - revenue targets overall (USD) and per customer (yearly GBP), the delivery-lead "customers" basis, withdrawal, history and audit;
  - refusals and the strip per role;
  - revenue ranking.
- **Isolation of the new tables:** pinned policies, FORCE, no customer grant, non-commercial roles read nothing, a commercial role reads only its own tenants, no direct insert, immutability, and the definer refuses a tenant outside the caller's scope.
- **Structural tests and purge:** the structural RLS tests classify both tables, and #109's purge test passes with a seeded target.
- **`apps/web/e2e/home.spec.ts`:**
  - the strip for admin, FinOps and engineer;
  - no strip and no revenue widget for customer and CXO;
  - setting a target from Settings;
  - the full health list, sorted;
  - staff revenue by component with compare;
  - top 10 by revenue;
  - axe in light and dark at tablet width for Home, `/customer-health` and `/settings/revenue-targets`.
- **Nav lists:** updated for the new Settings entry.

Local runs:
- `ruff`, `mypy --strict` and the full pytest suite pass.
- `home.spec.ts` passed against a production build (67 of 68 in a parallel run; the one failure was a load-related timeout and passed 8 of 8 when re-run alone).

body:
## What changed

Issues 19, 20 and 29 landed together because each builds on the last. Framework code (`Game.Core`, the wire format) changed, so this is labelled `core-change`. It is bigger than the small-PR rule asks for; splitting it afterwards would have meant re-testing three intertwined slices.

- **Defensive skill per class (19):** new ability kinds Dodge, Block and Shield on a fourth Defend button. Dodge dashes with brief invulnerability and fires a counter rider when timed just before a hit. Block cuts damage. Shield absorbs it. Defend pressed up to 0.2 s after a hit still counts (`ServerConfig.DefenseLeniencySeconds`), which also forgives network delay.
- **Class resources (20):** a resource is data on the class (max, start, regen or decay, gain per damage dealt, taken and blocked). Abilities spend it with `resourceCost`. Values travel in snapshots. Defaults: mage focus, tank rage, healer mana (block and shield feed it).
- **Class kits (29):** heal on abilities (allies in the line, caster included, clamped), taunt and threat (`taunt`, class `threatMultiplier`, enemies attack the highest threat).
- **Windups and enemy behaviour:** attacks can have a windup; the hit lands from where it started. Clients draw a filling warning area. Enemies with an aggro range chase and attack.
- **Respawn:** dead players return after 5 s at their spawn point.
- **HUD:** Defend button (labelled Dodge, Block or Ward), resource bar, blink while invulnerable, ring grows while guarding.
- Wire format changed (snapshots, events, a new command), so the protocol version is 2. A phone and a PC must run the same build to play together.
- Docs: `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/extending.md` updated with worked examples.

## Tests run

- `tools\test-core.ps1`: 110 passed.
- Unity EditMode: 113 passed.
- Unity PlayMode: 7 passed (includes pressing Defend and seeing the resource).
- Android dev APK built and installed on the S25 for the dodge, block, ward, resources, telegraphs, respawn and forgiveness. It was not rebuilt after healing and taunt.

## Not verified

- Feel of dodge timing, the 0.2 s forgiveness, telegraph readability and slime difficulty. All numbers (damage, speed, aggro, heal, taunt length, threat multiplier) are untuned guesses.
- Healing and taunt on a phone.
- Two-device play with the new protocol.
- Healing shows only the existing holy hit effect on the target; no numbers or green flash yet.

## Try on a phone

1. Mage: tap Dodge as a slime's red warning area is about to fill. A well-timed dodge fires a counter bolt. Try pressing a hair late.
2. Tank: tap Block when hit and watch the rage bar fill. Use the bash and see slimes turn to you.
3. Healer: stand next to a hurt ally, use the pulse, watch both health bars. Tap Ward as a hit lands and watch the mana bar rise.
4. Die on purpose and check you return after about 5 s.

Part of #19, #20 and #29. Not closing them: block and shield roles and the full kits still need phone testing.

author: milad-alizadeh
body:
Closes #1893

## Summary

The Agents and Shells tabs nest an `InspectorScreen` inside their tab's own one. An active screen asked for `visibility: visible`, which overrides a hidden ancestor, so its page painted over whichever tab was shown.

```diff
 <InspectorScreen active={false} label="Agents">       visibility: hidden
   <InspectorScreen active label="Agent Feed">
-    visibility: visible      paints through the hidden tab
+    visibility: inherit      hidden with its tab
```

Web and desktop only. Native hides with `opacity`, which already multiplies down the tree.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the Agent's title, Finished line and Feed draw over the Changes tab.

  ![Agent Feed drawn over the Changes tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ae577a6-11ff-420b-9273-4eab1b415ce5)

  **After:** the same steps, Agent Feed open, then Changes. Different fixture, from `HidesOpenAgentFeedBehindAnotherTab`.

  ![Changes tab drawn alone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38afd3f0-39b1-4254-992c-9413de851aae)

- **Tests:** three new stories in `session-inspector-tabs.test.stories.tsx`.

  ```text
  open a page in a tab → switch to Changes → the page stops painting
  ```

  | Story | Without the fix | With the fix |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `HidesOpenAgentFeedBehindAnotherTab` | fails | passes |
  | `HidesOpenShellBehindAnotherTab` | fails | passes |
  | `HidesAgentsListBehindAnotherTab` | fails | passes |

  They use `checkVisibility`, because `toBeVisible` walks the ancestors and reports the page as hidden even while it paints. That is why the existing stories missed this.

- **Checks:** the story file passed 8/8 three times in a row. `pnpm verify` passes (168 tests in 32 files) and so does `pnpm quality:lint`. `verify` left the other 39 dependent test files to CI.

- **Not checked:** the Electron shell and a real Session; the after shot comes from a Storybook story.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A one-word style change; reverting it restores the old behaviour.

**Blast Radius:** Inspector

Every `InspectorScreen` on web and desktop. A top-level active screen inherits `visible`, so it draws as before.

- A nested page's pressables now animate `visibility` when its tab returns, through their `transition-all`. So a role query straight after a tab switch can briefly miss them. Four stories needed `findByRole` or `waitFor` for this, and any other story with the same pattern would show up as a flake in CI.
- Pressables on a tab being hidden stay painted for their 150ms transition. Top-level tabs already did this; nested pages now do too.

author: sanskarin
body:
## Bug
The local instruction-model context scanner treated an entire JavaScript/TypeScript template literal as inert string data, even when the cursor was inside an executable `${...}` expression. The resulting hints could say to continue literal text instead of actual JavaScript/TypeScript code.

## Change
- Lexically mask raw template text but scan executable interpolation expressions as code.
- Track nested interpolation braces and nested backtick templates, keeping braces within JS strings, regexes, and comments from prematurely ending interpolations.
- Preserve escaped `\${...}` as raw template text.
- Add regression tests for async hints, nested objects/templates, quoted/commented braces, escaped markers, literal-context fallback and byte-exact native FIM requests.
- Update the README with an explicitly **unreleased** developer note.

## Constraints
No model download or training, no source logging or new editor-network behavior, no new release or publisher migration. Native FIM stays byte-exact. This is a bounded heuristic scanner, not a full parser.

Require all seven existing CI checks, including extension host and VSIX candidate compatibility, before merge.

author: theseydicharyyev
body:
## Summary

On the local agent, the DID list and the offer list now return the page I ask for. Before, they returned every item.

```
                                    before     after
GET /api/dids?offset=0&limit=1      2 DIDs     1 DID
GET /api/dids?offset=100&limit=1    2 DIDs     0 DIDs
GET /api/offers?offset=0&limit=1    2 offers   1 offer
GET /api/offers?offset=100&limit=1  2 offers   0 offers
```

The store passed only the selector to RIDB and dropped `offset` and `limit`. RIDB pages through the options of `find`, so the store now passes them there.

Closes #124

## Changes

- `src/utils/agent/local/database/paging.ts`: `pageOptions` turns the `offset` and `limit` of a query into `find` options. A query without them gives no options, so it still reads every row. It has no SDK import, so it can be tested.
- `src/utils/agent/local/database/index.ts`: `query` passes `pageOptions(query)` to `collection.find`. New `getPrismDIDRows()` reads every Prism DID of the tenant, without paging.
- `src/utils/agent/local/database/types.ts`: `find` in `RIDBCollection` takes the options.
- `src/utils/agent/local/inbox.ts`: the issuer looked for its signing DID in `getPaginatedPrismDIDs(0, 100)`. That worked only because the page was ignored. With paging, a tenant with more than 100 DIDs could miss its issuing DID, so it now uses `getPrismDIDRows()`.
- `src/utils/agent/local/database/paging.test.ts`: 4 tests for `pageOptions`.

## Verification

`npm run lint` is clean, `npm run build` passes, `npm run typecheck` shows the same four old `mediatorDID` errors as `main` and nothing new, and `npm run test` runs 20 tests, all pass.

Live on the local stack, one user:

- The four checks from #124: 0 of 4 before this change (the run in #124), 4 of 4 with it.
- Three more checks of the pages themselves, 3 of 3: page 2 is not page 1, for DIDs and for offers, and pages of one DID each give every DID exactly once.
- The issuance checks from #118 (11), #120 (9) and #122 (10) still pass. They sign credentials through the changed DID lookup.

## What was not verified

- Cloud mode was not run. There `offset` and `limit` go to the Cloud Agent, and this PR does not change that path.
- The store sets no sort order, so a page follows the order of the store. In the runs it was stable.
- More than 100 DIDs was not run live. The signing DID lookup now reads every row, so the number does not matter, but I did not create 100 DIDs to show it.
- The docs: #123 says that local mode does not page. Whichever of the two PRs is merged second will get the update of that line.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran the relevant checks.
- [ ] I added or updated documentation where needed. The docs line about local paging is in #123, see above.
- [x] My commits include DCO sign-off.

author: plicease
body:
## Summary

- `macman export NAME... -o FILE` writes machines to a versioned tar.gz: a manifest plus one `blobs/<sha256>` entry per distinct ROM or disk, so shared data is stored once. Archives hold current private disks, and no builds, caches, locks, or host paths.
- `macman import FILE [--rename NAME]` reports each machine as `imported`, `unchanged`, `conflict`, or `failed`. The others still import, and the exit status is 1 if any is unresolved. It compiles nothing; the first `run` builds or reuses the emulator.
- Machines gain a stable UUID `id`, assigned on `create` and `clone`, and on first export for existing machines.
- Export takes shared locks on all disks before reading any, and refuses disks in use.
- Import treats the archive as hostile: only expected names and regular files, sizes and digests checked, size limits, staging with atomic publication, and cleanup after failures. Nothing is merged or overwritten. Disk paths that Windows can't use safely, such as device names, are refused on every host.
- A ROM registration interrupted before its metadata is recovered on the next import, reported as `recovered rom`, but only for a plain file matching the archive's SHA-256. Anything less clear-cut is a conflict.
- `create`, `clone`, and `import` publish machines through `machine::publish_dir`, which holds `locks/machines.lock` across the existence check and the rename, so a machine directory is never replaced by macman.
- New dependencies: `tar`, `flate2`, `uuid`. Details are in `docs/EXPORT_IMPORT.md`, including the copyright notice for archives.

## Design decisions

- `--rename` needs a single-machine archive, so there's no source-to-destination mapping. The copy gets a new `id`, and repeating the same `--rename` import is refused.
- A ROM name clash blocks the import even with `--rename`, which renames only the machine.
- Limits are 16 MiB for the manifest, 4 GiB per blob, and 64 GiB in total. Export enforces them too.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --all-features`, including 37 tests in `tests/archive.rs`, machine publication race tests, and a lazy-build test in `tests/run.rs`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo check --locked` for Windows and i686, and `cargo test --locked` on the Windows CI job
- [x] Disabled the import safety and recovery checks one at a time and confirmed a test fails for each, except the "metadata already there" check in ROM recovery, whose removal changes nothing because the sidecar write also refuses to replace a file
- [x] Round-tripped copies of a real Plus and a real IIx machine: disk hashes matched and re-import reported `unchanged`
- [ ] Boot an imported machine in the real emulator (first-run build was tested only against the fixture source)

## Known limitations

- Export needs hard links at the destination, so it can't write directly to FAT or exFAT.
- Import temporarily needs about twice the size of the disks.
- An interrupted import was simulated with stale staging, not by killing a running import.
- The machine lock only binds macman. Another program could create an empty directory at the moment of publication and have it replaced, though an empty directory holds nothing to lose.
- If publication fails, removing a newly added ROM could pull it from under a `macman create` that started using it in that same moment.

Fixes #12

author: pocketilmatto
body:
Part of TAS-51. Since the switch, the Worker's log has shown `couldn't import the library: OperationalError: unable to open database file`.

The cause: Fly's database is in WAL mode, and SQLite's backup keeps that mark in the copy's header (bytes 18 and 19 are 2). SQLite can't open a WAL-mode database from memory, which is how `import_rows` reads the copy. I reproduced it with plain CPython sqlite3.

Changes:
- `import_rows` sets those two header bytes to 1 when they are 2. This is safe because a backup copy has nothing waiting in a WAL file. The copy already in the bucket therefore imports as it is, and Fly doesn't need to run again.
- `to_bucket` switches new copies to `journal_mode=DELETE` before uploading them.
- New test `test_a_wal_mode_copy_imports`: it fails without the fix and passes with it, with and without `TASTR_TEST_DO_SQLITE`.

After merging, run deploy-worker. While its library is empty, the Worker retries the import every 2 minutes (#110).

author: dereuromark
body:
Refs markup-carve/carve#4868 (carve-rs)

Implements the ticket's `## Expected` section (ruled option A): a refused `+` is a letter, so the writer spells it `\+` where the block below would otherwise attach, and writes that block at the enclosing content column with no blank line (CARVE-P9-085, CARVE-P11-042). The normative sentence and corpus section 929 are in markup-carve/carve#4877, still open, so the rows are not at this repo's pin yet. The new test pins the same bytes.

**Cause.** The escape-narrowing search relaxed `\+` to `+`. The item's read-back then failed and the writer fell back to its loose form, whose blank line makes the bare letter hold, so the relaxation stuck. A heading never takes that read-back, which is why it already came out right.

**Change.** While the tight source spells the letter bare, the failed read-back no longer falls back to the loose form. The whole-document check then rejects the bare spelling, and `\+` stays. HTML does not change.

Input:

```carve
- - +

  > q
```

Before:

```carve
- - +

  > q
```

After:

```carve
- - \+
  > q
```

Input:

````carve
- - +

  ```
  x
  ```
````

Before:

````carve
- - +

  ```
  x
  ```
````

After:

````carve
- - \+
  ```
  x
  ```
````

Input:

```carve
- - +

  {.c}
  > q
```

Before:

```carve
- - +

  {.c}
  > q
```

After:

```carve
- - \+
  {.c}
  > q
```

Input:

```carve
- foo
  1. +
   > b
```

Before:

```carve
- foo

  1. +

  > b
```

After:

```carve
- foo
  1. \+
  > b
```

`- - +` over `# H` already wrote `\+`, and a paragraph, math block or `-` list below keeps its blank; both are unchanged and tested. No existing corpus row changed.

Variant sweep: 684 documents (12 hosts, 19 block kinds, 3 quote depths), compared on HTML or AST before and after `fmt`, and for idempotence: 0 tree changes, 0 non-idempotent. This compares carve-rs with itself: the spec model has no writer.

Left as it was: `:: t` / `: - +` / blank / `  > q` keeps its blank, because the block's host is a description and the ruling speaks of an outer item. Two adjacent quotes below the letter keep the writer's existing marker-column form, same bytes as before this change.

Codex review: `[codex-router] gmx (weekly 66%)`. "I found no other confirmed regression." Its one finding, `tests/spec` turned into a symlink, was a local scratch link in the review's worktree and is not in the commit: `git ls-tree HEAD tests/spec` still shows the submodule. It read the changed files.

author: izagood
body:
## What

API connectors gain a **token exchange** auth kind for APIs that do not accept a static key directly: the key is posted as a form to a token URL and the returned short-lived `access_token` is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Paths may now contain `%2F` (an encoded `/` inside one segment, e.g. `/api/models/org%2Fname`).

This is PR ① (server + operator). The settings form for the new auth kind is PR ② (desktop, after a design mock-up).

## Changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Migration 156 | `api_connector.auth_kind` adds `token_exchange`; new `token_url` (https), `token_form` jsonb `{grantType, clientId, keyField}`; check that both are set exactly for `token_exchange` |
| `connectorRoutes.ts` | Same secret-ownership check as bearer. `token_url` validated by the same helper as `base_url` (https, no userinfo/query/fragment) with a path allowed, encoded dots/slashes rejected. Form values printable ASCII ≤200, `keyField` must not collide with `grant_type`/`client_id`. Changing `token_url`/`token_form` suspends the connector's grants (like base URL / key changes) |
| `apiGrants.ts` | `safePath` accepts `%2F` and checks twice: raw and `%2F`-decoded segments contain no `.`/`..`, decoded path has no empty segments (`//`). `pathCovered` requires both forms inside the prefix. Judgement uses the wire path after `new URL()`. Grant prefixes cannot contain `%` |
| `apiCalls.ts` / `api-checks` | Operator sends `caps`; a `token_exchange` connector refuses operators without `token_exchange` (`operator_update_required`, 409). Reply carries `tokenUrl`, `tokenForm` and the normalized `path` the server judged |
| operator `turnApi.ts` | Exchange with `URLSearchParams`, `redirect: 'manual'` (3xx = failure), 15 s timeout, 64 KB read cap, `token_type` must be bearer if present, token length cap + header-safe chars, everything but `access_token` dropped. In-memory cache keyed by (agent, base URL, token URL, form, key) fingerprint; TTL `expires_in − 60 s` (short: `max(half, 10 s)`, default 5 min, cap 1 h). A cached token that gets 401 is re-exchanged once per request. Server check still runs on every call. Token is scrubbed like the key (body, `location`, error text). Exchange failure returns only `token_exchange_failed` + status |
| desktop | Type widening only (`ApiAuthKind`); the edit form keeps token fields untouched until PR ② |
| docs | `docs/agent-api.md` section on the new auth kind and `%2F` |

## Tests

author: baverrr
body:
Expands the **Find My** tool into a live **"how close is each device"** view (new **Analysis → Find My radar** sub-view).

## What it does
- Parses the `findmy` BLE stream (MAC / RSSI / name) into a **nearest-first** device list.
- Smooths RSSI (EWMA) and estimates **distance** via the log-distance path-loss model.
- Shows a **proximity band** (Immediate / Near / Far), **signal bars**, dBm, and a **closer/farther trend**.
- **Homing panel**: pick a device for a big distance readout + trend; "It's at 1 m" calibrates the reference.
- Adjustable **1 m reference** (TxPower) and **environment** (path-loss exponent).

## Honest by design
RSSI→distance is rough (multipath, body blocking, orientation → easily ±several metres), and Find My rotates device identifiers, so the UI leans on **bands + trend** rather than false-precision metres. The ESP32 does the sensing — this only parses and presents what it streams.

## Structure
- `frontend/src/lib/findmy.ts` — pure parsing + distance/band/EWMA/trend (no React, easy to unit-test later).
- `frontend/src/components/FindMyView.tsx` — the view + homing panel.
- Wired into `CategoryNav` (new `AnalysisId`) and `App`.

## Verification
`tsc` + `vite build` pass. Driven end-to-end against the **mock bridge** in a browser: devices parse, rank nearest-first, show correct distance/bands, and the homing panel works. The line parser is tolerant of format variants ("RSSI -63", "-63 dBm", …) but is worth a quick recheck against a **real** `findmy` capture.

There was no container runtime in the session, so the image wasn't built here. CI's `base-image` job builds it on amd64 and arm64 runners because the `Dockerfile` changed. The `runtime` stage's `gh --version` check runs in that build.

What the build checks, tested by hand against the release assets:

- **Before:** the pin is `GH_VERSION=2.102.1`.

  ```
  $ gh run view --help | grep -E -- '--(job|log)\b'
    -j, --job string        View a specific job ID from a run
        --log               View full log for either a run or specific job
  ```
  The amd64 output matches the build's check, `grep -qF "gh version ${GH_VERSION} "`. The arm64 binary wasn't run, since the host is amd64.
- `scripts/check` passes: `ok: fmt markdown compose css clippy test doc`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting the commit restores 2.102.1, whose release assets are still available.

## Why and scope

Adds **7 cases and 7 controls** for UTC component construction, normalization and argument presence across declared numeric parameters, tuples, fields, generics and Date returns. The cases assert exact observed values and state transitions so typed routing errors remain visible even when the underlying Date operation works in isolation.

This is **1/5** of the Date route stack, based on `main`. The complete family contains 41 cases and 41 controls: construction 7, setters/getters 11, text 7, time values 8 and shared dates 8. This commit adds only the `construction-*` sources in `tests/typescript/date-routes/` and `tests/typescript/date-routes-controls/`, plus additive family rows, contract links and tag counts in `tests/typescript/FEATURES.md`.

Each file is an independent strict script with test262 front matter and no includes or flags. The controls contain no Date types, objects or APIs: numeric arithmetic, explicit parsing/formatting and plain state compute the actual observations from the inputs. Expected observations are separate literal fixtures checked by pinned Node; controls never copy an expected result into actual state. Times and setter returns are checked with `Object.is` and `typeof`, ISO/JSON strings exactly, and complete recorded sequences against their expectations.

Across the family, the input lists cover epoch and pre-1970 times, leap days, the last millisecond of a year, years 0, -1, 9999 and 10000, both inclusive ±8.64e15 boundaries, invalid values and route-specific fractions, signed zero, infinities, optional arguments or object identities. Every submitted file is at most 50 lines.

## Cases, controls and overlap checks

### construction-utc-parameter-month-carry

- **Case:** [construction-utc-parameter-month-carry.ts](https://github.com/AkisArou/nts/blob/chatgpt/date-routes-construction/tests/typescript/date-routes/construction-utc-parameter-month-carry.ts). Declared numeric arguments and return test positive/negative/fractional month carries, true year 0 reached after remapping, expanded years and invalid inputs. **Strict script: PASS; Node: PASS (103.9 ms).**

Read the same year/month numbers directly; truncate the year, apply the 0–99 mapping, normalize the month with floor division, compute Gregorian days, clip, and derive fields/ISO without a Date. **Strict script: PASS; Node: PASS (103.0 ms).**
- **Existing coverage checked:** `builtin-identity/call-construct-date-call-new-parameter.ts`. Checks exact universal-time construction, normalization, invalidity, UTC fields and ISO output across a declared route; existing coverage establishes invocation-target identity.

An interface parameter and Date return carry leap/nonleap-century days, day zero/negative/fractional values, year crossings and both inclusive clip endpoints with just-outside witnesses. **Strict script: PASS; Node: PASS (129.5 ms).**
- **Control:** [construction-utc-return-day-carry-control.ts](https://github.com/AkisArou/nts/blob/chatgpt/date-routes-construction/tests/typescript/date-routes-controls/construction-utc-return-day-carry-control.ts). Remove the interface parameter and Date return. Compute from the literal input record fields with numeric Gregorian leap-day counts, day carries, clipping, inverse UTC fields and ISO formatting. **Strict script: PASS; Node: PASS (110.8 ms).**
- **Existing coverage checked:** `builtin-identity/call-construct-date-call-new-parameter.ts`. Checks exact universal-time construction, normalization, invalidity, UTC fields and ISO output across a declared route; existing coverage establishes invocation-target identity.

### construction-utc-tuple-clock-carry

A typed seven-component tuple tests hours/minutes/seconds/milliseconds overflowing both directions, separate truncation, leap dates, expanded years and clip crossings. **Strict script: PASS; Node: PASS (103.7 ms).**
- **Control:** [construction-utc-tuple-clock-carry-control.ts](https://github.com/AkisArou/nts/blob/chatgpt/date-routes-construction/tests/typescript/date-routes-controls/construction-utc-tuple-clock-carry-control.ts). author: aoki-taquan
body:
## Summary

Hardening slice H3 (CLI-034, #301 security review L8): `ruster run` no longer validates the operator config with the simulator's `SIM_VALIDATION_LIMITS`. It uses explicit production limits, `ruster_config::PRODUCTION_VALIDATION_LIMITS`. `ruster validate`/`plan` choose their limits from the document's `backend.kind`, so they predict what `run` (af-xdp) or `run-sim` (sim) will accept.

Follow-up from the #308 review, which found a pre-existing per-packet linear-scan issue rated High for availability (tracked as PERF-001, next slice H4): tables scanned on the packet path get a lower interim production bound.

### Limits (coordinator defaults, not owner decisions)

| Limit | `run-sim` (unchanged) | `ruster run` | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_scanned_slots_per_table` (new field): resolution states/actions/dynamic-neighbors/failure-holds, ICMPv4 error states/actions | 65536 | 4096 | A miss scans the whole table. One dynamic-neighbor miss reads 1.5 MiB at 65536 and 96 KiB at 4096; a resolution state scan reads 3.5 MiB at 65536 and 224 KiB at 4096. 4096 equals `MAX_NEIGHBORS`. ICMPv4 error states are per egress interface, so at most 256 are used. |
| `max_slots_per_table`: NAT44 tables, directories and port owners; firewall states | 65536 | 65536 | Home NAT needs many sessions. NAT44 slot reuse is O(live entries) on every new flow (PERF-001). The firewall uses a keyed SipHash probe with occupancy capped at about 75%. |
| `max_runtime_bytes` | 64 MiB | 64 MiB | With every table at its production limit, storage is 35061696 B (33.44 MiB), so the per-table limits are what binds. |

The runbook has the per-table cost table with recommended sizes and the worst-case RSS: storage ≤ 64 MiB of ordinary heap, plus UMEM ≤ 1 GiB memlocked (2 GiB during an `auto` fallback), plus config text ≤ 1 MiB per document (two documents during a reload), plus a few MiB.

### Changes
- `ruster-config`: new `PRODUCTION_VALIDATION_LIMITS` and new field `ValidationLimits::max_scanned_slots_per_table` (public API).
- `ruster-cli`: `config_cmd::limits_for` (af-xdp → production; sim or absent → sim). `validate_bytes` is the single loader behind `validate`, `plan`, and `run` startup and reload. `validate_loaded`/`plan_with` make the commands testable in memory. Output formats are unchanged.
- The run unit tests now build their configs through the `run` loader, with production limits.
- New fixture `fixtures/limits/router-production-max.toml`: every table at 65536, pool 1-65535.
- `scripts/priv-run-smoke.sh`: new `limits` phase. The maximal config is refused as a sim document and accepted as af-xdp; `ruster run` starts it, forwards and NAT-translates host A→B, and exits 0 on SIGTERM.
- Docs: runbook (limits table, memory sizing, known limits, CI), README operator section, requirements CLI-010/CLI-034 updated, new CLI-083 to CLI-086 and CI-008.

### Behaviour changes
- `ruster run`, SIGHUP reload, and `validate`/`plan` of an af-xdp document refuse more than 4096 slots in any resolution or ICMPv4 error table, with exit 2 and `CAPACITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The simulator's limit is 65536. Everything else accepted before is still accepted.
- `run-sim`, sim documents and the golden output are unchanged.

## Tests
- `the_limits_table_is_pinned` and `limits_follow_the_backend_kind`.
- `validate_accepts_the_maximal_production_config` and `plan_loads_each_side_with_its_backend_limits`.
- `the_run_file_loader_applies_the_production_limits`, which goes through `load_validated_regular` on a real file.

author: aviezerl
body:
**Stacked on #202. Merge that first.** Until it merges, this diff also shows #202's commit. The change here is the second commit, 80476662.

`gtrack.import()` used to decode every record of a chromosome into one vector before binning it. Now:
- the bigWig reader returns one data block at a time;
- every source (bigWig per block; WIG and tab files per chromosome, as before) goes through one `DenseBinner` that adds each record to the bins it covers.

Each bin gets the same arithmetic in the same order as the old bin-by-bin loop. The binner also checks that records are sorted, non-overlapping and inside the chromosome. All three parsers already guarantee this; the check makes sure a future source that breaks it can't loop forever writing bins.

**Memory** (n114, mm10, binsize 20, defval 0; R alone takes 148 MB). Time is unchanged.

| file | peak RSS before | peak RSS after |
|---|---|---|
| SRX9311783 (218 MB) | 281 MB | 148 MB |
| SRX11797899 (869 MB) | 677 MB | 150 MB |
| per-base chr1 bigWig | 8.5 GB | 149 MB |

The per-base figures were measured by the optimization pass that proposed this change. WIG and tab files still hold one chromosome at a time.

**Output is byte-identical.** Checked three ways:
- 156 chromosome files from bedGraph, fixedStep and variableStep WIG, and tab inputs match misha 5.13.2 by md5. Settings: sparse, and binsize 1/7/20/1000 with defval NaN/0/2.5.
- An independent review compared 13,650 chromosome files from random inputs against the previous loop. Sources: every text format plus bigWigs from UCSC, libBigWig and pyBigWig. Settings: binsizes up to larger than the chromosome, and a range of defvals. All identical.
- All three ChIP-Atlas bigWigs match their reference tracks, with max abs diff 0.

**Tests**
- New `test-gtrack.import-binning.R` checks dense bins against a mean computed in R from the records. It covers partial bins, defval fill, NaN records, the last partial bin, and a binsize larger than the chromosome.
- The existing bigWig test compares two routes that now share the binner, so it could not catch a binner bug. The new test fails on a binner without the defval fill, on one with an unweighted mean, and on one with a full-size last bin.
- Full suite, file-parallel on n114: 209 files, 22,897 expectations, 0 failures, 0 errors.
- Independent review: two rounds, the last clean.

author: denfry
body:
## Problem

- The guard only read `Grep` and `Bash`. A `codebase-index` command run from Claude Code's PowerShell tool never turned it off, so `Grep` kept being intercepted for the whole session, and PowerShell searches were not guarded at all.
- `install-hooks` skipped an installed guard, so a new matcher could not reach existing installs.
- The guard intercepted searches the index cannot answer: `.git` internals, binaries and paths outside the repository.

## Solution

- Add `PowerShell` to the guard and to both matchers, skip here-string bodies, and read `Select-String`'s named `-Pattern`, `-Path` and `-LiteralPath`.
- `install-hooks` refreshes the matcher of an installed guard.
- Searches over git internals, binaries and absolute paths outside the indexed repository pass, and the index lookup now comes before any search parsing.

Also bumps the version to 2.1.3 with every mirror synced.

## Verification

New tests in `tests/test_hooks_guard.py`, the PowerShell ones failing before the fix. A test ties both matchers to the tools the guard reads. Full suite passes (coverage 86%), ruff and mypy clean, `check_versions.py` consistent.

## Compatibility

Plugin users get the new matcher automatically. Users of `install-hooks` run it again after upgrading; until then their hook behaves as before for PowerShell.

author: jsboige
body:
Grain: DEEP/notebook-lean — lane myia-po-2028:CoursIA-2 — prev: DEEP/notebook-lean #24138

## Objet

Les deux volets de #24143 : la relecture phrase a phrase du miroir `Knots/ArcPartition_en.lean`, et l'organe reutilisable qui rend la mesure rejouable par tout siege (elle ne l'etait par aucun outil du depot).

Cette tete repond aux **cinq points de la revue du 2026-11-02** (Hermes, sur la tete `15798ce1`). Chaque point est traite ci-dessous avec la mesure qui l'etablit ; la section « Mesure » donne le tableau avant/apres, et la section « Preuves » donne les commandes.

## Point 1 — le volet 1 porte sur un miroir HALF-DONE : son « 0 ecart » est structurellement vide

La relecture des 67 paires porte sur une paire que **les deux fichiers declarent HALF-DONE** :

- en-tete FR : « Les docstrings du corps sont, a cette tranche, le texte francais verbatim des deux cotes : la traduction anglaise est optionnelle (`code-style.md`) et n'est pas revendiquee ici — `check_i18n_siblings.py` designe la paire `HALF-DONE`, la seule du lake dans ce cas » ;
- en-tete EN : « The body docstrings are, at this slice, the French text verbatim on both sides — an English translation of them is optional (`code-style.md`) and is not claimed here. `check_i18n_siblings.py` flags the pair `HALF-DONE` ».

Mesure (paires de commentaires de `Knots/ArcPartition`) : **65 des 67 paires sont byte-identiques** entre FR et EN ; seules la paire 1 (en-tete) et la paire 42 different. L'organe compare donc, sur 65 paires, du francais a lui-meme : il ne peut y trouver d'ecart, par construction. **Le « 0 ecart » du volet 1 ne vaut donc pas preuve d'une traduction integrale** : il mesure l'identite des octets, sur une paire dont la convention ne demande pas la traduction.

La ligne de preuve du body precedent s'arretait a `0 unbuilt` et coupait le suffixe que l'organe frere publie desormais :

```
381/389 pairs byte-identical | 8 consumer-pattern | 0 drift | 0 orphan | 0 unbuilt (0 whitelisted) | 10 half-done (advisory)
```

Les 10 entrees `HALF-DONE` sont 9 fichiers de la famille `Godement` (`Grothendieck/Godement*`, `Grothendieck/SheafCohomology/Godement_en.lean`) et `Knots/ArcPartition_en.lean` (32 corps de blocs identiques de 100 caracteres ou plus entre FR et EN).

Ce que reste la relecture du volet 1 : la lecture phrase a phrase de ce qui **est** traduit sur cette paire (l'en-tete et la paire 42), et le constat que le reste du miroir n'est pas destine a etre traduit a cette tranche.

## Point 2 — la « variance stylistique » etait mal decrite

Le body affirmait : « le mot FR « Controle » est rendu `Check` aux paires 40 et 41, et `Control` a la paire 42 ». Mesure sur les blocs committes :

- `Check` apparait **0 fois** dans tout `ArcPartition_en.lean` ;
- la seule occurrence de `Control` est la **paire 42** (`EN L615`) ;
- les paires 40 et 41 sont **byte-identiques** — du francais non traduit des deux cotes.

Deux des trois paires citees n'etaient donc pas des variantes de traduction mais du **francais non traduit** ; la troisieme etait correcte. La conclusion pratique (pas d'edition, variance acceptable) reste bonne, mais elle ne portait pas sur l'etat reel du fichier.

**Correction apportee au body** : la ligne « variance stylistique documentee : 1 (paires 40, 41, 42) » est remplacee par l'etat mesure — « 65 paires byte-identiques (francais non traduit des deux cotes) ; 2 paires reellement traduites (en-tete, paire 42) ; 0 occurrence de `Check` dans le miroir ; 1 occurrence de `Control` (paire 42) ». Aucune edition du miroir n'est faite : la convention rend la traduction de ces docstrings optionnelle a cette tranche.

## Point 3 — l'exclusion d'en-tete ne testait pas que la paire etait un en-tete

`header_anchor = min(shared_anchors)` excluait l'ancre la plus basse de **chaque** fichier, quelle qu'elle soit. Mesure sur les 386 fichiers compares du head : cette exclusion masquait **374 ecarts DURS et 1 089 avis** — soit plus que le total publie (360 DURS). La perte verifiee a la main par la revue (`KNOTS/.../Redraw_en.lean`, paire FR L77 / EN L35) en fait partie.

**Remede applique** : l'exclusion teste desormais les **corps** de la paire, et non sa position. Le miroir EN se declare le miroir du canonique (« English mirror of `Foo.lean` (...) ») ; le corps FR ne le fait pas. Mesure : 61 fichiers du depot portent un en-tete de ce type, et **aucun** d'entre eux ne porte de cote FR qui declare le miroir — le discriminant est exact. La regle exclut donc les 147 paires d'en-tete du depot et **zero** en-tete reel n'est compare. Quand les deux cotes declarent le miroir, la comparaison garde son sens et n'est pas exclue.

Sur le cas verifie par la revue : la paire FR L75 / EN L34 de `Redraw_en.lean` est desormais comparee et publiee. L'ecart porte sur le span FR `` `relabelCrossings f cs = cs.map (PDCrossing.relabel f)` ``, absent du miroir EN (« Per-crossing version of `relabelCrossings` (Conway.lean, link 5). »). Sa severite est **ADVISORY** et non DUR : `relabelCrossings` est declare dans `Conway.lean`, pas dans `Redraw.lean`, et la regle DUR de l'organe est « nomme une declaration du fichier compare ».

**Corollaire** : l'appariement est repare dans une fenetre de 3 jetons de code (97 paires reparees sur le depot), sans jamais casser une paire exacte ni troubler l'ordre. Une paire a toujours **deux corps** : l'ancre fantome signalee par la revue (`pair 1 anchor -1, FR L0 / EN L6`) n'existe plus. Ne restent comme orphelins que les commentaires dont le homologue est a plus de 3 jetons — 500 commentaires non apparies, contre 979 avant (dont beaucoup etaient des artefacts d'alignement).

## Point 4 — les deux faux negatifs du matcher de nombres

**(a) L'exemption « annee presente ».** `number_is_carried_elsewhere` excusait tout nombre de 1-2 chiffres des que l'autre cote contenait une annee a 4 chiffres. Desactivee seule, elle fait passer le corpus de 360 a 389 DURS : **29 ecarts du depot** reposaient sur cette exemption, dont des comptes d'arcs (`0`,`1`,`2`,`3`,`4`,`5`,`18`) et non des dates.

*Remede applique* : un nombre n'est excuse que s'il appartient a une **date complete** d'un cote (au moins deux composantes, dont une annee a 4 chiffres) **et** que l'autre cote porte lui aussi une date complete. Une annee seule n'excuse plus rien : `compare_bodies("il y a 3 aretes", "the set in 2026")` rend maintenant un ecart DUR sur `3`. La date peut etre ecrite dans les deux conventions (`2026-10-27`, `27/10/2026`, `April 7, 2026`).

**(b) Le decoupage des decimales.** `number_parts` decoupait aussi sur `.` et `,`, ce qui rendait `1.5` et `5.1` egaux (parties `{1, 5}` des deux cotes) : `compare_bodies("pi=1.5", "pi=5.1")` rendait 0 HARD.

*Remede applique* : les classes de separateurs sont separees. Un groupe qui porte une annee a 4 chiffres est une **date** et se decoupe sur ses separateurs (`2026-10-27` et `27/10/2026` donnent les memes parties) ; tout autre groupe se decoupe sur sa barre oblique et son tiret (un ratio `0/1`, une plage `65-979`) mais **pas** sur son separateur decimal : `1,5` et `1.5` sont un nombre ecrit dans les deux conventions. `compare_bodies("pi=1.5", "pi=5.1")` rend maintenant un ecart DUR.

Les deux regressions de la revue sont **ajoutees aux tests** ; les trois tests qui encodaient l'ancien contrat (decoupage des decimales, exemption par annee, groupe « 0/1 ») sont mis a jour.

## Point 5 — unites melangees et couverture

Le body melangeait des **fichiers** (389) et des **paires de commentaires** (755 « paires porteuses d'un ecart ») : la ligne etait arithmetiquement impossible telle qu'ecrite. Le tableau est desormais etiquete par unite.

*Remedes appliques* :

- `pairs_compared`, `pairs_excluded` et `pairs_repaired` par fichier, plus un total dans le `SUMMARY` ;
- une ligne explicite `NOTHING COMPARED` pour un fichier dont aucune paire n'a pu etre alignee — un « 0 finding » y signifie « rien n'a ete mesure », pas « rien n'a ete faux » ;
- `fr_line` rapportait la **derniere*

body:
Creating a large smart group (~2,300 members) with `jamfplatform_device_group` can take longer than the CDN waits. The POST gets a CloudFront `504` after about 30 seconds, but the platform still makes the group. Terraform has no ID for it, so the next apply fails with "Name already in use".

In one case a single apply made **two** groups with the same name (with different Jamf Pro IDs). The provider sent one POST, so something behind the CDN seems to replay it. That part might need a fix on the Jamf side.

This PR:

- **172e170**: if the read after create fails, record the group with a warning instead of dropping it. A warning, not an error, so the group isn't tainted and re-created.
- **f2466e9**: before the POST, list groups with the same name. If the POST fails with a 5xx or no response, poll that list and record the new group. If there is more than one, keep the highest Jamf Pro ID and list the others in a warning. Nothing is deleted.

Unit tests cover both cases and fail on `main`. `make fix fmt lint test` is clean. I haven't tested this against a live tenant.

Side note: the 504 error text says "the request never reached the Jamf API and nothing changed", which isn't true for a timed-out POST.

author: zanix
body:
This pull request adds a bunch of new features:

- **New "mealie" template:** Shows meals grouped by day and meal type, with responsive day columns above 400px and rows below. "Today" uses Mealie orange (by default).
- **More display options:** Added `groupByDay`, `showTodayLabel`, and `fontSize` configuration options.
- **CSS customization:** Added theme-specific CSS classes and variables for colors, spacing, borders, and image sizes. Custom CSS targeting the previous classes may need updating.
- **Image proxying:** Recipe images now load through the MagicMirror server, which can avoid browser cross-origin issues with Mealie.
- **Safer configuration:** Config values are validated and sanitized, with warnings for corrected values and visible errors for invalid required settings.
- **Date-range correction:** Current-week meal requests now respect the week boundaries and configured day limits more reliably.
- **Updated documentation and screenshots** for the templates, configuration, and styling.

This also add several improvements to the developer experience, CI/CD workflows, and documentation. The main changes include updating and simplifying developer commands, modernizing and streamlining the GitHub Actions workflows for testing and releases, updating documentation to match new practices, and removing (now) unused configuration files and tools.

**Developer Experience and Commands**
- Updated all documentation and templates to use `node --run` commands instead of `npm run`, and clarified developer commands for linting, testing, and releases in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and issue templates.
- Added `.versionrc.json` to configure version and changelog bumping for releases.

**CI/CD Workflow Improvements**
- Rewrote `.github/workflows/automated-tests.yaml` to use a single `test` job with a faster runner, improved Node.js setup, and explicit lint and test steps using `node --run`.
- Overhauled `.github/workflows/release.yaml` to trigger on tags, extract release notes from `CHANGELOG.md`, and use `ncipollo/release-action` for GitHub Releases.
- Updated permissions and removed unnecessary steps from workflows for clarity and security.

**Documentation and Standards**
- Added a Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct at `.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`.
- Updated `.github/SECURITY.md` (renamed from `SECURITY.md`) to clarify supported versions and reporting steps.
- Improved the structure and formatting of `CHANGELOG.md` for consistency and clarity.

**Configuration Cleanup**
- Removed unused configuration files: `.commitlintrc.json`, `.markdownlint.json`, `.husky/commit-msg`, `.husky/pre-commit`.

**Tooling and Linting**
- Updated linter and formatter usage to rely on Prettier (with ESLint bundled) and clarified configuration locations.

These changes collectively modernize the project's tooling, clarify contributor guidelines, and streamline the release and testing processes.

> Esta rama está construida encima del rediseño (#4). Si fusionas este pull request primero, entra también el rediseño y GitHub marca el #4 como fusionado solo.

## Qué incluye

### Precios referenciados (paso 1)
- **Pantalla propia por insumo**:
  - Precio de costeo con su costo por kg, L o pieza, y los días que tiene sin revisarse.
  - **Cotizaciones** de varias tiendas comparadas por unidad, con las etiquetas "Más barato" y "En costeo". **Usar** pasa una cotización al costeo.
  - Enlace al producto en la tienda.
  - **Historial del costo** con gráfica y el porcentaje de cambio.
  - En qué recetas y servicios se usa.
- **Actualizar precios**: lista lo que pasó la vigencia (30 días por omisión, en Ajustes → "Vigencia de precios"). Enter guarda y pasa al siguiente; Enter con el campo vacío confirma el precio vigente.
- Aviso con número en el ícono de Insumos del inicio y en el tablero.
- Los datos de ejemplo traen cotizaciones de referencia para comparar.

### Importar factura (paso 2)
- Lee el XML de facturas CFDI 3.3 y 4.0.
- Sugiere el insumo de cada concepto (por nombre o por una relación ya recordada).
- Calcula el precio con descuento e impuestos, con la opción de sumar o no el IVA y el IEPS.
- Puede crear insumos nuevos.
- Cada precio queda como cotización y, si se marca "Usar", pasa al costeo.
- Recuerda la relación de cada concepto con su insumo para la siguiente factura del mismo proveedor.

Ningún precio externo cambia el costeo sin que alguien lo confirme.

## Pruebas
- `node tests/prueba_costeo.js`: pasan las 13 pruebas.
- Recorrido de precios en Chromium:
  - Usar la cotización de Costco cambia el costo a $27.00/kg y lo anota en el historial.

Both lockfiles resolve it only because Flatpack 0.1.332 requires it: ``` flat_pack (0.1.332) view_component (>= 4.14, < 5) view_component (4.20.0) ``` On `main`, dummy `flat_pack (0.1.207)` required `view_component (~> 4.12.0)` and the lock resolved `view_component (4.12.0)`. The 4.12.0 to 4.20.0 move is that Flatpack floor. Admin 2.8.1 and Root Switchable 0.11.3 declare the same `view_component (>= 4.14, < 5)` range in the dummy lock. Nothing bumps `view_component` directly. `openai` is not named in any Gemfile or gemspec, and it is absent from the root lock. The dummy lock moved from `openai (0.94.0)` (AI `0.11.0`, `openai (~> 0.78)`) to `openai (0.115.0)` because `recording_studio_ai (0.19.5)` depends on `openai (~> 0.103)`. The merge did not add other lock changes. Both locks still show `recording_studio_web_search (0.6.0)` depending on `recording_studio (~> 6.1)`. ### Docs, views, and config - `CHANGELOG.md`, `UPGRADING.md`, `MIGRATION_NOTES.md`, and the gem-template install and configuration docs describe the `~> 6.1` floor and the layout changes. `0.6.0` is recorded above main's `0.5.3`, `0.5.2`, and `0.5.1` entries. - Dummy shell uses `helper RecordingStudio::LayoutHelper` and layout `"recording_studio/default_layout"`. `UsesDefaultLayout` and `recording_studio_page_nav` are gone in core 6. - Dummy Admin sets `config.layout` and `surface.layout` (`engine_layout` is gone in Admin 2.8). Dummy Root Switchable sets `config.layout` to the layout name. A symbol is not a layout setting. - Flatpack cards use `background:` instead of `style:`. - The run show page renders `FlatPack::PageTitle` with the plain query and subtitle. The default layout strips `content_for :title` and then escapes it again, so the query is not passed through that slot and is never marked `html_safe`. The results column is `FlatPack::Stack` with `gap: :lg` (Stack is always a column; `:lg` is the largest named gap). The close anchor defaults to `RecordingStudioAdmin.configuration.surface_for(:admin).path`. - Dummy `dummy_page_nav` and the admin root view draw `FlatPack::PageTitle` the same way, with no `html_safe`. ### Ruby and audit locks Main pins non-matrix `ruby/setup-ruby` steps to `ruby-version: '3.3'`. This branch also sets `.ruby-version` and `test/dummy/.ruby-version` to `3.3`. Bundler Audit scans `test/dummy/Gemfile.lock`. That lock has `crass (1.0.8)`, `net-ssh (7.3.8)`, and `rack (3.2.8)`. Those three were the only audit bumps. No Gemfile constraint was added for them. [Run page heading shows the query with an apostrophe and a script tag as text](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-3978a0ad-39bf-5782-81e9-dfc29f1cb9e3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Frun-show.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: xuefeng-zhu
body:
Based on production 043081c (`track-d/src/main.rs` unchanged since cb9c687, PR #42).

**Change**
- `zeros()` keeps one first writer per 2 MiB page (the de693db race fix), but all threads write them, each taking every `threads`-th page, instead of the main thread alone.
- The parse picks an edge's bucket with `(u as u128 * inv >> 64)`, `inv = 2^64 / block_len + 1`, instead of `u / block_len`. Exact for every u32 id because `block_len < 2^32`.

**Why**
A timer around each `zeros()` call showed the main thread spending 3.3-5.1 ms per run zeroing ~25 huge pages in the kernel while the other threads waited. The parse did one 64-bit divide per edge (5M per run).

**M risk**
None expected: same arrays, same huge-page advice, still one first writer per huge page. VM cgroup peak 70.31 -> 70.21 MB (seed 1 median), 69.56 -> 69.77 MB (seed 2).

**S**
389 -> 392 (official `static_axes.py` on the VM).

**Local (not official)**
Team x86 VM, CPUs 0-11, interleaved random-order rounds, every output hash-checked:

| Run | Seed 1 | Seed 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| final source, 40 rounds | -3.05% (126.35 -> 122.04 ms) | -2.87% (128.05 -> 124.34 ms) |
| same edits, two earlier 40-round batches | -2.74%, -3.07% | -3.40%, -2.98% |
| parallel first touch alone | -2.15% | -2.88% |
| multiply instead of divide alone | -1.98% | -0.90% |

This VM has overstated CPU-side gains for the board by about a third, so expect about -2% T, roughly +0.9% K after the 3 lines. That is inside the board's 3-5% noise, so two runs may not resolve it.

**Correctness**
- Full seeds 1, 2, 3 (seed 3 from the official generator and reference) byte-identical, with CPU affinity 0, 0-1, 0-2, 0-4, 0-6, 0-7, 0-11, 0-15.
- PR #42's `checks.sh` suite, run natively (`dcheck.sh`): checked build passed the random oracle, exhaustive, same-bucket, u32 cutoff, 2^21 boundary, max-weight chain and repeated/unreachable suites, the first three also pinned to 1 and 3 CPUs; release build matched the official reference on tiny seeds 2, 17, 4242 and sample seeds 2, 7.
- `rustfmt --check` clean.

Also screened and not kept (VM): rank prefetch in `relabel`, branch-free relaxation, owner-span `relabel` with few atomics. None added anything on top of this change. Details in `experiments/track-d-parallel-touch44/README.md`.

## What
gim-home/longarm (the Microsoft-internal copy) had no releases ("tags not mirrored: gim-home never releases"). Now:

- **gim-release.yml** (manual): re-publish a tag (default: the latest release) - for releases from before this, e.g. v0.1.28, or a failed run. Downloads this repository's GitHub Release and uploads the same files.
