body:
Browser text metrics can understate faint fallback ink, allowing a complete window title to select a size whose glyph rows are clipped. This change observes the complete shaped request through guarded bounded queries before truncation, preserves the nominal pen/baseline and shadow coverage, and shares metrics-only preparation and destination-bounded painting with procedural frames. Unusable measurements in prefix, marker and procedural paths now raise `TitleCoverageUnavailableError` consistently. The unused private full-title raster adapter is retired.

The modern P1 policy assumes a finite envelope around signed actual bounds and queried-pixel equivalence at the chosen guarded placements. These are explicit supported-renderer assumptions, not arbitrary-font certification or original typography evidence. Coverage uses one canvas of at most 4096×32 and one bounded readback: at most 1,048,576 bytes across the two explicit RGBA planes. Destination output, input, opaque host memory, GC and cumulative traffic are separate.

Validation:

- Theme extraction, library build and repository gates passed. Final guarded gates recorded 1,368 passing tests and zero failures.
- Independent source/built verification: 32 checks each in Firefox, WebKit and Chromium, plus four unchanged Firefox procedural contracts: **100/100 passed**. Tests cover full-request fallback ink, guarded placement, colors, numeric/native measurement failures and resource bounds. Preserved failures drove the corrected implementation; the final methods and clean-room author provenance were independently reviewed.
- Four page-3 goldens restore seven negative-bearing shadow pixels. Independent composition matched all 6,776 title-region pixels and discriminated six alternatives. The four PNGs are exact retained native-CI actual attachments; all other PNGs and the global manifest remain unchanged. Acquisition differences and the bounded approval are recorded in [golden REVIEW](tests/rendering-options/goldens/REVIEW.md#reviewed-substitute-title-bearing-delta--637-2026-11-02).
- A predeclared Firefox trial retained 56 baseline and 56 final renders over 14 fixed conditions, one warmup and three measured samples each, without errors or retries. PM and independent reviewer accept the measured correctness/storage tradeoff. Some extreme 16k-character cases are materially slower: source ordinary median 7.263→12.537 s and utility 13.865→17.623 s, with a maximum current sample of 22.109 s; built ordinary 6.991→8.817 s and fallback 8.389→10.260 s. Modest fallback cases also regress. No general speedup or latency guarantee is claimed; prefix work can remain quadratic. Complete-request host-call medians do not measure the whole resolver or explain total latency. Utility readback traffic is about 66.55 MB per render, distinct from live scratch planes and RSS.

Runtime growth replaces full-title raster allocation with shared metrics, bounded observation/publication, guarded placement geometry and explicit numeric/error handling. No parallel legacy raster path remains. Measured against the merge-base with `origin/main`:

author: skyscs
body:
Connected paths qualified offline can now be read through a strict typed service and protected GET endpoints. The API returns two default paths or one selected path, plus four-entry-point pages with complete original support, explicit incomplete coverage and generation/projection identities. It preserves saved-tree verification, relevant alternative blockers and whole-path admission; internal fact/resolution vectors stay private.

One connected read runs per catalog. Busy, client disconnect, shutdown, source/inventory changes and corruption release or reject pending work explicitly. A newer unpublished inventory does not replace the retained published one; concurrent SQLite writes conservatively reject the pending response and allow a stable explicit retry. Existing static-flow, answer, candidate and correction consumers, schema and frozen experiments remain unchanged. The collapsed browser view is the next phase.

Validation: full `pnpm check` passed 482 tests and builds, followed by a passing real TCP cancellation regression and targeted strict recheck (483 tests now defined). Twenty-one added tests cover normalized qualified-reference parity, independent SHA-256 trees, bounded root pages and citations, HTTP validation, unavailable/empty states, busy/cancel/shutdown, corruption, revocation, eviction and historical restart. The TCP case uses an owned ephemeral loopback listener and verifies a successful read after client abort. Reviewed the complete port, API/lifetime boundaries and documentation links; no model requests or corporate sources.

author: sanderverkuil
body:
## Summary

Cards and thumbnails used to download full-size box art and photos. On `/catalog`, 9 covers came to 3.24 MB, including a 1.77 MB PNG shown about 250 px wide.

This branch makes WebP renditions of every image that may be shown, in the background, once it is approved. It records them per source blob, deletes them with their source, and serves them only as URLs behind the source's own publication gate.

- **Ladder:** 480, 640 and 960 px. The first rung the source does not exceed holds a WebP at the source's own width instead. A rendition is kept only when it is at most 90% of the source's bytes.
- **Encoding:** made from the clean blob through the pipeline's input guards. Metadata-free (checked on every output), alpha kept, and downscaled with an area filter, so fine detail does not alias.
- **Storage and lifecycle:** a new `imageRenditions` table. Every slot counts as referenced in `blobReferences.isReferenced`. Renditions are scheduled on every approval path (pipeline, re-screen, admin approve, waive, restore) and deleted on every reject, quarantine, delete, erasure and metadata-strip path.
- **Serving:** `srcSet` and `thumbUrl` on the public catalogue and the landing plank, every member card grid, thumbnail fields (480 px), the copy photo strip and cover cards, the member's own submissions and the add-copy picker. The web cards set `srcset` and `sizes`. Detail views, zoom, the lightbox and admin views keep the original.
- **Backfill:** internal, dry-run by default, cursor-batched, create-only and idempotent, per table (`boxArt`, `copy`).

Round 2 (review fixes): added the 640 rung, the WebP at the source's own width and the byte check, which close the gap at DPR 2+. `listMyContributedPuzzles` now returns `imageSrcSet`, and the picker's 40 px thumbnails pick a rendition.

### Measured on /catalog (9 live covers, real network loads on a DOM replica)

| Viewport / DPR | Originals | 480/960 (round 1) | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 390 px, DPR 1–3 | 3.24 MB | 0.53 MB | **0.46 MB** |
| 820 / 1440 px, DPR 1 | 3.24 MB | 0.53 MB | **0.46 MB** |
| 820 / 1440 px, DPR 2 | 3.24 MB | 3.06 MB | **0.78 MB** |
| 820 / 1440 px, DPR 3 | 3.24 MB | 3.06 MB | **1.33 MB** |

## Findings

| ID | Status | How fixed | How verified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PERF-C1 | Partial | Renditions for box art and copy photos, plus srcset/sizes and thumbnail URLs on every member and public surface that shows them small (see summary). | Tests written first in renditionEncode, imageRenditions, boxArtRenditions, copyPhotoRenditions, publicCatalogRenditions and memberSurfaceRenditions, plus web component tests. Byte measurements above. Screenshots unchanged at 1440/820/390. Full CI green. |
| P-42 | Partial | Item 1 (renditions, reference registration, deletion with the source, backfill, srcSet/sizes) is done for box art and copy photos. | Same as above. |

Still open:

- **PERF-C1:** message photos (`messageAttachments.thumbFileId` is still not produced), completion photos and circle icons are still served at full size. Follow-up, see decisions.
- **P-42:**
  - Item 2 (the CDN route) is an owner decision.
  - Item 3's `fetchpriority` belongs to perf-web (PERF-C2).
  - Blurhash placeholders for box art are deferred (perf C4 is not assigned to any package).

## Owner decisions

1. **CDN-cacheable `/img/box/:puzzleId/:version/:w` route (P-42 item 2).**
   - Options: defer until the trigger; build it now as a Convex httpAction plus a Vercel rewrite; or a TanStack Start proxy route.
   - **Recommendation: defer.** Renditions already deliver the byte cut. When the trigger fires, use the httpAction, keyed by puzzle id and version, never by storage id.
2. **Renditions for message photos, completion photos and circle icons.**
   - Options: a follow-up PR after this stack; defer until real-user metrics show the bytes; or skip circle icons.
   - **Recommendation:** a follow-up for message photos (produce `thumbFileId`, with a `by_thumb_file` reference index coordinated with SEC-92) and for completion photos; skip circle icons.

## Post-deploy steps

1. Deploy. The schema adds the `imageRenditions` table (indexes `by_source`, `by_small_file`, `by_medium_file`, `by_large_file`). No existing documents change, and reads fall back to the originals until renditions exist.
2. Box-art dry run: `npx convex run lib/imageModeration/renditions:backfillRenditions '{}'`. Check `candidates` in the `imageModeration.backfillRenditions` event that has `done:true`.
3. Real run: `npx convex run lib/imageModeration/renditions:backfillRenditions '{"dryRun":false}'`. Re-run if `failed > 0`; it only picks up what is missing.
4. Copy photos: `'{"table":"copy"}'` (dry run), then `'{"table":"copy","dryRun":false}'`.
5. Spot-check `/catalog` on a 2x screen: cards should carry a `srcset` with 480w/640w WebP candidates, and Network should show the 640 px WebP renditions.

## Testing notes

- **Tests:** Backend tests are written first and seen failing before each fix. They cover:
  - eligibility, recording, idempotency and retry, isReferenced, and deletion on every lifecycle path;
  - the dry-run default and paging of the backfill;
  - gated serving: no rendition for pending, unscored, rejected, quarantined or hash-pending images;
  - no `_storage` id in any response.
- **Test helper:** the helper re-runs a generation that convex-test forced into a retry ("Write outside of transaction" while a Workpool loop runs). Production code is unchanged by this.
- **Live checks:** The dev deployment runs main's backend, so live pages show no srcset. Byte savings were measured with DOM replicas, using renditions encoded by the branch's encoder from the live covers and the routes' own `sizes`. Read-only live checks of `/catalog`, `/my-puzzles/add` and `/my-puzzles/add/quick` showed no console errors.
- **CI mirror** (`format:check` + `turbo run lint type-check test build arch:check --force`): green. Backend 2972 tests, web 1319, domain 1739.

---

**Stack:** layer 14 of 26, based on `fix/perf-backend-models`. Findings are from the [review of 29 October 2026](https://github.com/SanderVerkuil/JigSwap/blob/main/docs/review/2026-10-29/README.md). Any commit SHAs quoted above predate the stacking rebase; each commit's message names its finding IDs and carries an `Intent:` paragraph.

author: viraladmedia
body:
Stacked on #8, so merge #1 through #9 in order.

## What changed
Before this PR, the customer chat followed a fixed script (problem, then address, then photo) and couldn't answer anything else. Now every customer message runs a short **plan, look up, answer** loop (`src/lib/agent.js`). It makes at most 3 lookups, then answers.

| Tool | Reads |
|---|---|
| `check_calendar` | Real open slots in the next 7 days, optionally for a named day |
| `rate_card` | Published roofing rates per m² and labour per hour (never a total), or the med spa menu |
| `business_facts` | Name, service area, first visit and facts confirmed at setup; anything else is reported as "not on my record" |
| `customer_history` | Earlier enquiries from the same address |
| `storm_reports` | Weather-service storm reports on record |

- **Proven facts only.** A coded grounding check holds back any clock time or dollar figure that doesn't appear in a lookup, an earlier message or an approved quote. An unverified, held range is not counted as evidence.
- **Questions aren't mistaken for answers.** "How much do you charge?" is not taken as the job description or the address. After answering, the desk carries on qualifying the job.
- **The customer sees what was checked.** Small chips under a reply, such as "Checked the calendar".
- **The owner sees how it answered.** A new "How the desk answered" panel on the lead shows each plan, each lookup and what it found, and whether the reply passed grounding.
- **Providers.** On Meta, Muse Spark makes each step with a strict JSON schema (`agentStep` in `prompts/prompts.md`). The mock provider is deterministic. Any provider without `agentStep` falls back to `converse`. Every step is logged in the AI-calls table with model, tier, tokens and time.

## Checks
- `npm test`: 68 pass, including 9 new agent tests:
  - calendar and price lookups
  - a question isn't taken as the description
  - unknown facts are reported as unknown
  - customer history
  - the med spa menu
  - the grounding check catches an invented time
  - the step limit holds
- Playwright: 8/8, with a new "smart desk" journey that runs from chat to the owner's trace panel.
- `npm run build`: OK. ESLint: clean.

body:
Step 1 of simplify-core item 4 (`commitUse` out of TurnEconomyProvider). Test only, no production change.

`tests/unit/commit-use.characterization.test.tsx` pins, through the real provider, the property the sealed `commitUse` must keep. A use changes the sheet and the turn, one undo puts both back, and one redo replays it. Cases:
- a bow shot that spends an arrow
- Cunning Action: Dash
- a healing potion
- Rage
- Dodge, solo and on your turn in a fight (fills the Action slot)
- an Opportunity Attack, solo (logged only) and in a fight (spends the reaction)

The comparison covers the whole character doc and every data field of the combat store. Today's undo leaves harmless traces, normalized in the test and listed in its header. They go away once the undo is one whole-state seal: a restored inventory row gains an `instanceId`, an undone tracker spend leaves `{ used: 0 }`, and an empty map comes back absent.

Proven by breaking the code on purpose: dropping the ammo credit, the Dash restore, the equipment restore, the activation restore on the use path, or the log-line removal each turns a case red. The cast paths (`commitCastOption`, reaction spells) aren't driven here; they get their own characterization next, with spell setup.

author: owine
body:
## Summary

Node 26 entered Active LTS ("Lithium") with v26.13.0 on 2026-10-28. This adds it as a supported runtime and moves development onto it.

- **`engines.node`**: `^22.19.0 || ^24.0.0` → `^22.19.0 || ^24.0.0 || ^26.0.0`, so `npx` on Node 26 no longer prints `EBADENGINE`
- **CI**: new `26.13.0` entry in the test matrix on the shared preset's `node-lts-26` lane (capped to 26.x, like the 22 and 24 lanes)
- **`.nvmrc`**: 24.22.2 → 26.13.0. The release build reads `.nvmrc`, so published tarballs are now built on 26
- **`@types/node`**: 24.19.2 → 26.6.6. This replaces #353, which bumped the types before 26 was a supported runtime
- README prerequisites and CLAUDE.md updated to match `engines`

Node 22 and 24 stay supported and tested. Dropping either would be a breaking change, so that's left for a later `feat!:`.

## Verification

Run locally on Node 26.13.0:

- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run build` all pass
- `pnpm test`: 30 files, 1,357 tests passed, exit code 0
- `pnpm run test:package`: smoke test passed (read-only and read-write modes, oversized upload refused)

CI covers 22.19.0 (the `engines` floor), 22.23.4, 24.22.2 and 26.13.0.

Note: with `@types/node` on 26, typecheck no longer flags APIs that exist only in Node 26. The 22.x matrix legs are the guard against them, but only for code paths the tests exercise.

## Summary by Sourcery

Support Node.js 26 as an additional runtime while retaining Node.js 22 and 24 compatibility.

New Features:
- Add Node.js 26 as a supported runtime alongside Node.js 22 and 24.

Enhancements:
- Update development and release tooling to use Node.js 26 and align Node.js type definitions with the supported runtime.
- Document Node.js 26 in the project prerequisites and development guidance.

Build:
- Expand the package engine declaration to include Node.js 26.
- Update the lockfile and development dependencies for Node.js 26 support.

CI:
- Test Node.js 26.13.0 in the CI runtime matrix.

Documentation:
- Update README prerequisites and development guidance to reflect Node.js 26 support.

author: loliba92
body:
## Pourquoi

Sur la page Annonces, l'étiquette (« Dans les prix », « Pas cher »…) compare l'annonce au prix du site, mais le trait de la barre marquait la médiane des annonces actuelles. Un rond à gauche du trait voulait dire « moins cher que la moitié des annonces », alors que l'étiquette disait « dans les prix » : les deux semblaient se contredire (exemple : Le Tombeau du Vampire, 7,90 € contre 7,79 € au site, mais 12,10 € de médiane des annonces).

## Changement

`web/revue.js`, fonction `thermometre` :
- le **trait** marque le prix du site (même état), le **rond** est l'annonce ;
- l'échelle va du moins cher au plus cher des annonces, élargie au prix du site pour que le trait reste dans la barre ;
- le mot affiché sous les extrêmes reste « Le moins cher » / « Le plus cher » ; au milieu, il suit les mêmes seuils que l'étiquette (10 % autour du prix du site) : « Sous le prix du site », « Au prix du site », « Au-dessus du prix du site » ;
- sans prix du site : pas de trait, seulement le rond ;
- l'infobulle donne tout : rang, annonces de X à Y, médiane, prix du site.

## Vérification à l'écran

Page Annonces, ordinateur (1100 px) et téléphone (390 px), connexion sorcier simulée avec les vraies données du dépôt (58 barres) : aucun mot coupé, aucun débordement. Le Tombeau du Vampire : trait sur 7,79 €, rond juste à sa droite (+1 %).

À savoir : pour 39 barres sur 58, le prix du site est sous la moins chère des annonces, donc le trait est au bord gauche. Les annonces sont affichées avec leurs frais (prix livré) alors que le prix du site est calculé sans frais.

_Requested by **Thomas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Y7EHC6facJJuWYEB68vSoi?thread=cmsg_01Y7EHC6facJJuWYEB68vSoi6ua1E7utDgNmRFHTb4w5hB)_

Splits `schemas/commands/catalog.json` (4,428 lines) into one file per command, as planned and reviewed on #528.

- `schemas/commands/<name>.json` holds the entry exactly as before (cut out of the source text, not re-serialised; no `$schema`). `catalog.header.json` holds `reqseq-catalog`, `description` and `order`, the command names in today's catalog order. `catalog.json` is deleted.
- `scripts/contracts/load.mjs` `loadCatalog()` assembles the same catalog object. It reports every folder problem at once: JSON syntax errors with the file name, a listed name without its file (spelled as on disk), unlisted command files, duplicates, names equal ignoring case, `name` ≠ file name, a name ending in `.schema`, and a stale `catalog.json` with a message saying how to move its entries. Header keys other than `order` pass through, so the meta-schema reports a misspelt one.
- `validate-schemas.mjs` checks each command file against the entry schema and the header against the root, and every message names the file (also `checkCatalog`).
- Tests no longer read `catalog.json`: `contracts.test.ts` compares the bundle's commands with the command files (names and each entry), `local-path-fields.test.ts` counts `$ref`s over the command files, `views.test.ts` uses `loadContracts()` of core, `app.spec.ts` reads `order`.
- Commit 2 changes the texts that named `catalog.json` and regenerates. The header description now ends "A change to a command file is a contract change, announced in the stage epic (ADR-0002)" instead of "needs-human change", which CLAUDE.md no longer has. This is the one intended difference from "byte-identical" in the issue.
- Commit 3: ADR-0002 rule 1 and consequences (incl. how to resolve a conflict in `order`), ADR-0003, ADR-0009, ADR-0010 views, core README (incl. where the pre-split history is), CLAUDE.md, `.ignore`, comments, and the `invoke` error text. `verification/SR-073.md` stays as a record.

**Why the size cannot be split:** about 9,300 changed lines outside generated files, almost all the move of 4,428 lines into 49 files (git finds no rename, since no file reaches 50 % similarity). The move, the loader and the readers must change together, or `schemas:check`, `contracts:check` and the tests break on the deleted file.

**Deviation from the plan:** `App.test.ts` and `restore-buffers-app.test.ts` run under happy-dom, where core's index cannot load (`model-cache.ts` needs a `file:` URL). They read `schemas/commands/<name>.json` for each called command instead of using `loadContracts()`.

No open PR touches `schemas/commands/` (checked 2026-11-02 before the push).

Closes #528

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

The merge queue sat empty for hours, and nothing paged a person. The depth alert in `babysit-next.py` fired only with five consented PRs waiting, read one timeline per open PR (over 268 seconds at about 150 PRs), and reached only a babysitting session.

Now `_pr_queue.depth_shortfall` owns the floor, and `babysit-next.py` and the hourly `queue-health.py` both call it. It reads at most `QUEUE_DEPTH_READS` timelines. The new `shallow` page fires when fewer than `QUEUE_DEPTH_MIN` entries are queued and a consented PR outside is held by more than a recent check round.

Before (origin/main copy, live run):

```
set     WORK    ALERT merge queue depth: 0 of 149 PRs a person consented to are queued, and at least 3 should be. Not queued: #9153 (draft; …), #9154 (draft; …), … (149 entries)
```

After (this branch at dc1df1451, live run, 1:02 total, two PRs queued):

```
set     WORK    ALERT merge queue depth: 2 of at least 7 PRs a person consented to are queued, and at least 3 should be. Not queued: #9159 (armed and green, so the queue has not taken it yet; claude-owned), #9200 (unfinished required check: CI; claude-owned), … Adopt each with --adopt N …
```

## Decisions made

- The alert names a PR whose checks still run, or whose only red is the consent check, with that blocker. The deleted row skipped both instead.
- A consented draft is not counted. The alternative named drafts, which no session may mark ready.
- The no-consent row is a person row. As a work row it would keep every idle run at exit 1.

## Review focus

Read `queue_depth_rows` in `.github/scripts/_babysit_queue.py` first. The least-sure part is deleting the stale-main row for an empty queue, with `checks_running` and `awaits_consent`; the depth alert now covers that case.

The depth alert now fires whenever fewer than three PRs are queued while a consented PR waits outside, with no five-PR trigger; `QUEUE_DEPTH_READS` caps its timeline reads.

For the pager, read `shallow_finding` and `outside_blocker` in `.github/scripts/queue-health.py`. The least-sure part is the grace: a PR round counts as runner wait only while a run on its head started inside `QUEUE_ENTRY_MAX_AGE_MINUTES`, and `gh pr list` can name a head that a push replaced minutes ago.

TLA+: nothing a spec asserts moved; the `shallow` finding only reads and pages, and no modeled merge-queue transition changed.

Doctrine: `babysit-prs` step 3 now asks for two things. It merges fixes that each go red on another's cause onto one `red-fix` branch. Once `main` fixes an eviction's cause, it merges `main` into each `requeue-held` PR. At 500 sessions both rules stay bounded: each fires once per shared cause and adds one head per held PR.

author: krokicki
body:
## Summary

Two related changes for OME-Zarr 0.6 datasets:

**Fix: axis table crash on OME-Zarr 0.6.** OME-Zarr 0.6 (RFC-5) wraps the scale transform inside a `type: "sequence"` coordinate transformation. `getScaleTransform` only matched a top-level `type: "scale"` entry, so `getResolvedScales` returned an empty array and `ZarrAxisTable` threw `TypeError: can't access property "toFixed", e[i] is undefined` for every axis. The transform lookup now searches inside `sequence` transformations, and the axis table renders "Unknown" instead of throwing if a scale value is ever missing. This also fixes Neuroglancer state generation, which resolves scales through the same code path.

**Feature: show capability-incompatible viewers.** Viewers rejected by their capability manifest (e.g. `Viewer does not support OME-Zarr v0.6 (supports: 0.4, 0.5)`) were silently hidden, with the reason visible only in the console. The manifest may be wrong or out of date, so they now appear in a collapsed "N incompatible viewers" section under the main tool row, still clickable, with the rejection reasons shown in each button's tooltip. `ViewersContext` returns both compatible and incompatible viewers with reasons, and `useZarrMetadata` generates URLs for incompatible viewers too so opening them works through the normal data-link flow.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests for `getResolvedScales` with direct (≤0.5) and sequence-wrapped (0.6) scale transforms, using the metadata shape from a real 0.6 dataset
- [x] New component tests: incompatible viewers render in the collapsed section with reasons; no section when all viewers are compatible
- [x] Full frontend suite passes (676 tests)
- [x] Manual check on a 0.6 dataset: axis table renders with correct scales, incompatible viewers listed collapsed

body:
[LIN-24](https://linear.app/sesv/issue/LIN-24) · Spec MIRROR, task T2 · Covers MIRROR-R1, R2, R3, R4, R7

## What

- `apps/web/src/server/env.ts`: per-command environment. `parseEnvFor(command, env)` validates only what `serve`, `migrate` or `scheduler` uses and lists every missing or invalid name without printing values. New names: `DATABASE_URL`, `LINEAR_CLIENT_ID`, `LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET`, `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `SESSION_SECRET` (≥32 chars), `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (32 bytes, standard base64, `openssl rand -base64 32`), optional `SIGNIN_ALLOWLIST` (comma-separated emails, case-insensitive). `ELECTRIC_*` stay reserved. `scheduler`/`migrate` in `cli.ts` are unchanged (still reserved, exit 2); T1 and T5 switch them to `parseEnvFor`.
- `apps/web/src/server/linear/urls.ts`: OAuth callback `/auth/linear/callback` and webhook `/webhooks/linear`, built from `PUBLIC_URL` only.
- `apps/web/src/server/linear/token.ts`: client-credentials token of the OAuth app (`read,write`), cached until an hour before expiry, one in-flight request for concurrent callers, invalidated on authentication failure, optional store so the scheduler can reuse one token across runs (Linear caps active app tokens at 1000). Errors never contain the secret.
- `apps/web/src/server/linear/client.ts`: thin fetch-based GraphQL client. Backs off on HTTP 429 or `RATELIMITED`, honouring `Retry-After` or the exhausted budget's `X-RateLimit-*-Reset`, else exponential up to 60 s; at most 5 retries and 15 min per wait, then a typed error. Retries once with a fresh token on 401 / `AUTHENTICATION_ERROR`.
- `apps/web/src/server/linear/budget.ts`: the bootstrap's query shapes and page sizes with the arithmetic against the app actor's hourly budget (fixture bootstrap ≈ 14 requests, ≈ 39.5k complexity points of 2M).
- Playwright `local` webServer and the container smoke give `serve` placeholder values; the smoke also checks that `serve` with no environment exits 1 naming `DATABASE_URL`.
- `docs/deploy.md`: environment table per command, Linear OAuth app section (URLs, webhook categories, scopes, egress).

No new dependency: a thin client keeps request counts and complexity explicit instead of `@linear/sdk`.

body:
## Summary

Investigates the blank Cost Curves charts reported on the Ubuntu VM.

**Not reproducible in Chromium** (headless Chromium 153). Both charts render under every condition tested: direct load and in-page navigation, 800–2560 px viewports, DPR 1/1.25/1.5/2, software GL, reduced motion, dark mode, theme toggles, resizing while hidden. Firefox (Ubuntu's default browser) could not be tested: Mozilla download hosts are blocked by the session network policy, and running a conda-forge Firefox build was not permitted in this session.

**Evidence from the symptom.** `drawEconomics()` writes its dynamic notes *after* creating the first chart. A throw while building that chart gives exactly the report: controls and static text visible, both canvases blank. The two blank charts are the only ones with logarithmic axes.

## Changes

- `chart()` guards Chart.js construction. A failure renders in the chart box and in a red diagnostics banner, with the user agent, and one failing chart no longer aborts the rest of a view. A post-render check detects a zero-size canvas or plot area and retries one resize.
- Canvas colours are `rgba()` instead of CSS `color-mix()`, which not every engine's canvas colour parser or Chart.js's colour helper accepts.
- New footer button, **Check charts in this browser**: visits every chart view and reports, per chart, canvas size, plot area, painted %, any error, and the user agent.
- New `tests/e2e/visual_check.cjs` checks **rendered pixels** on every tab over `file://` with network blocked (light/dark, 1400/1024 px, direct load and in-page navigation): non-zero size, ≥ 1% painted, and every visible dataset's colour present.
  - **Negative control:** drawing is suppressed in Cost Curves, and the check must flag both charts.
  - **Diagnostics control:** Chart.js's log scale is made to throw, and the error must be visible in both chart boxes and in the banner.
  - `npm run test:e2e` runs both browser checks.
- No data, model or measurement changes.

## Validation

- `npm test`: 25/25 JS, 22 Python OK.
- `npm run test:e2e`: dashboard check OK; visual check 148 canvas checks OK; negative and diagnostics controls OK.

author: ehsanulhaquesiam
body:
## Problem

Many sections went straight to a paid X API call even when the session had already seen what they needed. Targets and the Leads list builder were empty until a paid click, Picks ignored what you scrolled past, and Competitors were blank until a fetch. When the free session lane couldn't take a click (the human pace, or no desktop), the click just failed. Some prices were wrong too: Analyze's refresh showed "cached, free" while it could still charge, and "Write 3 for today" said free while it could buy trends. Queued posts with media drove the session with nobody clicking, which breaks AGENTS.md rule 1.

## Change

- **Free first:** Targets, Daily Picks, Staff picks, the Leads list builder and Competitors read what the session saw before any paid call. The paid action stays beside them with its price.
- **Live updates:** free reads update as you browse X (a shared debounced `observedAtom`).
- **`createdAfter` filter:** observation queries can filter by age before the row limit, so old posts seen again don't crowd out new ones.
- **`cacheOnly` reads:** a free read can never turn into a paid call, because a cache miss answers empty.
- **Library free search:** understands `from:`, phrases, `OR`, `-word`, the min counts, since/until and `filter:`.
- **Never stuck:** when the session pressed nothing (paced, no desktop), replies, likes and DMs in Engage and Leads offer **Try again** free or the API now at its price. A click that may have pressed offers no paid retry, so nothing double-posts.
- **Queued media:** waits at its time for the user's Post now. One notification goes out, once a client is listening (`Events.listening`). The Publisher refuses unattended media.
- **Honest prices:** Analyze refresh always prices its later pages, "Write 3" shows the trends price when it needs it, and Plan's confirm says free when the post is free.

## Verification

- `pnpm check:changed` passes after the rebase. Every bug fix has a focused test that I confirmed fails without the fix:
  - Engage targets: dedupe and age filter
  - Treg `cacheOnly`
  - Costs: Analyze refresh price
  - Library: picks and staff picks
  - `observedMatching` and `observedAuthors`
  - Engage and Leads: paid fallback, and no fallback after an ambiguous timeout
  - Scheduler: queued media waits and reaches a late client
  - Engage screen: Try again / Send now
- Reviewed with sol-loop: 5 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved.
- Dev app (seeded data, fake treg, nothing spent):
  - Targets listed observed posts on open and added a new one live.
  - The list builder showed "1 found · seen on X · free" before Preview.
  - A reply with no desktop offered Try again / Send now ($0.015), and the paid path posted.
- Not checked: the desktop-only Search on X buttons and the OS notification. No captures attached, because the states need clicks a route capture can't reach.
- Declined: native list paging while a short list's end is on screen. It matches x.com, is throttled, and changing it needs the live engine bench.

author: zizzfizzix
body:
Turns `@typescript-eslint/await-thenable` on for every TypeScript file. Until now it covered extension code only, and the test and e2e hits were held in `DEFERRED`. That list is now empty. Refs #282.

## What changed

- **Config:** the rule moves into `PROMISE_RULES`. The extension-only block is gone.
- **207 `await`s removed.**
  - Almost all are `await act(() => …)` with a synchronous callback.
  - The rest are the `focusField` / `press` / `editSelector` helpers that wrap the same call, plus three `await expect(value)` lines in e2e.
- **`bootstrap.test.ts`:** `broadcast` no longer wraps `trigger` in `Promise.all`. `trigger` already settles each listener's promise. Its type doesn't say so, so `broadcast` is annotated `Promise<unknown[]>`.
- **`analytics.context.test.ts:101`:** replaces an `as any` with the file's `stubBackgroundPostHog` helper. This `no-explicit-any` error was already on `main`, left over from #369 and #370.

## Behaviour of a bare `act`

In React 19.3, `act` with a synchronous callback is typed `void`. At runtime it still returns a thenable, and awaiting it waits one macrotask and flushes pending React work. So the `await`s this rule rejects did wait for something.

Where an assertion depends on async work the callback started (a storage write, a message reply), the test now waits explicitly with `await settleEffects()`. That covers:

- 10 tests in Settings, consent and onboarding that failed without the wait.
- Negative assertions that would otherwise pass before the work they rule out could land. Two of these, "stays locked after four clicks" and "forgets a partial click run", passed with the unlock threshold lowered to 4. They now fail with it, and they also assert that the synchronous unlock event wasn't sent.

CLAUDE.md now describes this rule next to the test-harness notes.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm fmt-check` and `pnpm compile` pass.
- `pnpm test:coverage` passes: 1818 tests, 100% on every metric, fidelity check passed.
- Two review passes traced every assertion after an `act` that no longer has `await` back to the code under test. The riskiest SidePanel negatives were also checked by mutating `TabPanel.tsx`.
- E2E was not run locally. Its only changes are three `expect` calls on plain values, which were synchronous already.

author: gyuro-dev
body:
## What changes

An outside review of 0.2.1 listed security, data and keyboard problems. Each one was checked against the code. The ones that really happen are fixed here, and the full list is in CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.

**Security**

- Deleted board items in an imported file skipped `cleanEl`. If a merge brought one back, an unchecked `color` could reach the page as HTML. They are now checked, and anything malformed is reduced to the deletion mark.
- The conflict list's "Use their value" put unchecked values from an imported file on the object, which is the same kind of hole. This one was not in the review, and a temporary test reproduced it before the fix. The value now goes through `normalize` first. `id`, `ts`, `bt` and names such as `__proto__` are refused outright, because `__proto__` passes `safeId` and could replace an item's prototype.
- A field name in an imported file became part of a conflict's ID, and `data-id` drew that ID unescaped. One crafted file with the same ID twice made a conflict and ran its markup when the conflict list was opened. CodeQL flagged this on this PR, and a temporary test reproduced it. The code predates this PR; the alert appeared because this PR changed the line. Such fields no longer create conflicts, and the ID is escaped when drawn. Alert #76, on the same line, was earlier dismissed as a false positive because IDs were assumed to be checked by `normalize`, which does not cover IDs built during a merge.
- Tables with no cells and malformed text formatting are repaired on import, so they no longer stop the board from drawing.

**Data**

- Deleting a row or a sheet now marks its evidence as deleted, so images and files leave the saved file. Undo brings them back.
- A merge that keeps a deleted row also brings back the evidence deleted with it. Items deleted before the row stay deleted.
- A merge that finds live rows or board items on a deleted sheet now keeps the sheet, with what was deleted along with it, and the conflict list asks what to do.
- "Open comments" in the summary no longer counts comments on deleted rows.

**Drafts**

- A draft held back with Esc can be applied from "⋯ → Unsaved drafts…" until the test is edited.
- Picking a file with "Open" now offers its draft.
- Opening a draft from the list no longer rewrites it when nothing was edited.

**Keyboard and table**

- Ctrl+S, F, M and H no longer act behind an open dialog.
- The conflict list takes the focus and closes with Esc.
- `Alt+↑/↓` no longer moves rows while sorted.
- Dragging a column edge no longer shrinks the table by 40 px.
- Replace no longer counts cells it did not change.
- The table of contents and "Go there" now reach rows hidden by a filter or a folded group.
- With an issue link template set, an apostrophe no longer becomes a link to issue 39, and a template with both `{n}` and `{key}` no longer rewrites its own links.

## Review points not followed

- **Dropping images at save time:** rejected, because a row kept by a later merge would lose its images. Evidence is marked as deleted instead, which is what deleting a run already does.
- **`#cfpanel` lacks `.dlg-back`:** it already has it. The focus problem behind the claim was real and is fixed.
- **The table of contents misses folded groups:** it does not, because the first row of a folded group stays visible. Column filters were the real cause.

## Known limits

- Files saved before this change keep the images they already contain for deleted rows.
- A draft held back with Esc is still overwritten by the next edit, as the 0.2.1 CHANGELOG says.
- If someone deleted one evidence item after another person deleted the row, and the row is then kept by a merge, that item comes back. It cannot be told apart from one deleted with the row, so this keeps the data.

## Tests

`test\run.ps1`: 220 OK (24 new, in `test/tests/feat-review3.js`). The README counts and CHANGELOG are updated, and `samples/` was regenerated. Goldens did not change.

## Performance, compared with main

Headless Edge, medians, with the order rotated each round. "main" for link generation and for opening 100,000 rows shows two identical copies of main as a control.

| | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| Link generation, no template, 1.5M calls (ms) | 98 / 103 | 102 |
| Link generation, `{n}` (ms) | 397 / 394 | 367 |
| Link generation, `{key}` (ms) | 337 / 341 | 346 |
| Link generation, both (ms) | 679 / 676 | 545 |
| Open 100,000 rows (ms) | 840 / 865 | 847 |
| Open 500,000 rows (ms) | 3,252 | 3,315 |
| Peak memory, 500,000 rows (MB) | 2,037 | 2,012 |
| Open 3,000 images (ms) | 3,612 | 3,649 |
| Peak memory, 3,000 images (MB) | 3,085 | 3,086 |

- **Link generation:** `{key}` alone read 1–3% higher here, and 1–2% lower in the previous round on the same `issueLinks` code, so this looks like noise.
- **Opening:** the 500,000-row and 3,000-image differences are smaller than the spread between runs of the same version.
- **What was measured on which commit:** link generation and opening 100,000 rows are from the final commit. 500,000 rows and 3,000 images are from the commit before the last one, whose change touches only conflict creation and the conflict list.
- **Edit, result, search and summary:** on 100,000 rows these stayed within the spread between the two copies of main. They were measured before the last rewrite of `issueLinks`, which those paths do not use. `bench.js` does not cover the delete or merge paths this PR changes.

**One difference remains.** After opening 100,000 rows, the heap before GC reads 136 MB against 115 MB on main, and building the saved file 313 ms against about 300 ms. Peak memory reads 813 MB against 791 and 814 MB on the two copies of main. After a forced `gc()`, measured on an uncommitted version from before the `issueLinks` rewrite and the two later XSS fixes, the heap was 68 MB in all 27 runs, across main, main with the same amount of added comment text, and the branch. main also reaches about 136 MB in some runs, and 500,000 rows and 3,000 images show no difference. This looks like GC timing, but why the branch lands on the higher value every time was not found.

body:
Fixes the two `core-checks` jobs failing on `main` (`Bedrock.tls.test.ts`, `llm/llm.test.ts`). One is a real product bug.

**Bedrock API keys (real bug).** `_clientAuth()` returned only `{ token }`, but the AWS SDK can still select SigV4 and consult the default credential chain. An API-key-only setup therefore failed with `CredentialsProviderError: Could not load credentials` unless the machine also had AWS credentials. Reproduced by running the TLS tests with `AWS_*` unset (7 of 11 failed), now 11/11 pass. Added a unit test that asserts bearer auth is selected and the credential chain is never consulted, independent of the environment.

**`llm/llm.test.ts`** calls real OpenAI/Anthropic/Mistral/Gemini endpoints. The skip switch (`IGNORE_API_KEY_TESTS`) is only set for forks/Dependabot PRs, so a push to `main` here ran them with no secrets. Each provider's tests now skip when its key is missing (and a placeholder test keeps the suite non-empty); with keys they run as before.

author: andersonfariaas
body:
A IA explica o resultado do motor, mas não o decide. Classificação, pontuação e nível continuam vindo das regras. Se a IA falhar ou responder algo fora do contrato, o usuário recebe o texto determinístico.

- Provedor atrás de uma porta (ProvedorIa). O adaptador usa o SDK oficial @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.135.0 e traduz erros sem repassar corpo de resposta.
- Modelo padrão claude-opus-5-5 (IA_MODELO permite trocar). Timeout de 15 s.
- Só o host e as evidências seguem para o modelo, nunca a URL completa.
- Prompt versionado (analista-v1), com as evidências entre marcadores e a regra de não seguir instruções que venham nos dados.
- Resposta validada por contrato (Zod, campos extras recusados) e por consistência com o motor: ids de evidência reais, sem afirmação de segurança, sem legitimidade quando há sinais, sem pontuação diferente.
- Resultado gravado com provedor, modelo, versão do prompt e evidências citadas.
- Sem ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, o sistema responde só com texto determinístico.

Testes: 158 unitários no back-end (incluindo injeção de prompt, timeout e contradição) e 19 de integração. Não houve chamada real à API da Anthropic: não há chave configurada neste ambiente.

author: jdwyah
body:
## Why
`verify-sdk-boot/boot_check_go` and `verify-dev-injection/inject_check_go` required `github.com/quonfig/sdk-go v0.0.0` with `replace => ../../../sdk-go`, which is outside the repo. That caused three problems:
- **`ssdlc / deps` fails on every open ITD PR** (#29-#34). osv-scanner's govulncheck call analysis can't load the packages (`replacement directory ../../../sdk-go does not exist`), and since #28 osv-scanner exits 127 on that instead of continuing.
- **GitHub's dependency graph never indexed either go.mod** (qfg-ao5h4), so no Dependabot security alert could fire for a Go advisory there.
- sdk-go is now `github.com/quonfig/sdk-go/v2`, so the replace no longer matched the sibling checkout's module path either.

## What
- `go.mod` / `main.go`: require and import `github.com/quonfig/sdk-go/v2 v2.1.0`, with no replace. `x/sys` is 0.44.0 in both.
- `run.sh`: the new `run_go_check` builds against the sibling `../../../sdk-go` through a temporary `go.work`. It fails loudly if `sdk-go/v2` resolves from anywhere else, such as a sibling on an old pre-v2 branch.
- `dependabot.yml`: drop the sdk-go ignore. Bumping the pin is harmless.
- READMEs updated. No YAML test definitions changed.

## Verified
- `go build` and `govulncheck ./...` now load both modules (no called vulns; the only findings are uncalled stdlib advisories for the local toolchain).
- With a scratch root whose `sdk-go` is a worktree at `origin/main`, the sdk-go checks in both `verify-dev-injection/run.sh` and `verify-sdk-boot/run.sh` print `OK sdk-go` against the local checkout.
- With the real sibling on an old pre-v2 branch, `run.sh` now prints `FAIL sdk-go: resolved sdk-go/v2 from …/pkg/mod/…@v2.1.0, not …/sdk-go` instead of silently testing the published release.

author: akoita
body:
Closes #2046.

## What changes

New runs record `cli-critic-v10`: v9's critique prompt (v6's text) with the separate omission check widened to every retrieved chunk, and every omission it finds blocking.

- **Scope.** `omissionCheckInputs` builds the check's calls for a scope: `cited-chunks` (v9, unchanged: one call over the chunks the plan's themes cite) or `every-chunk` (v10: every retrieved chunk in slices of at most 32, each slice with the CV's text, every supported theme and the cuts). A chunk carries the themes the plan cites it for, or none; the parser keeps an omission from an uncited chunk only when it names a theme the call was sent. Instructions `omission-check-v2`.
- **Weight.** `mergeOmissionChecks` joins the slices' answers once per chunk and accomplishment, at most twelve per round, and `capBlockingOmissions` takes a limit: twelve for v10's check findings, the contract's three everywhere else. The critique's own omission findings are still dropped on a run with the check.
- **Cost accounting.** The agent runs the slices in sequence on the guarded adapter with the critic's profile output budget, sums their bills with the providers' `addBilledUsage`, and a guard refusal of a later slice or of the critique carries what the earlier slices billed. The critic execution record sums every slice and the critique.
- **Unchanged.** The author's prompts, the critique prompt, the compact evidence table, the cost guard. Resumed v9 runs keep the v9 check on the cited chunks; the default critic version moves to v10.

## Why

On the 2026-11-02 run of private reference G, v9's check read the 20 chunks the plan's themes cite of 316 retrieved and named one of the twelve accomplishments the draft left out: eight of them sat in chunks no theme cites. With at most three blocking per round, two rounds could add at most six accomplishments where the bar needs seven. Details are in the architecture doc and the roadmap's decision log; no model call was made, and the next #1307 scoring run on G measures it, at a $7 cap over two rounds, after the 2026-11-14 credit.

## Tests

- `critic-omission-check.test.ts`: every-chunk inputs (every theme, uncited chunks without a theme, v9 scope unchanged), slicing by the slice size, empty without a theme or a chunk, uncited-chunk parsing, merge dedup and round cap, the blocking limit per version, the prompt's slice wording, the v10 default and version predicates.
- `provider-critic-agent.test.ts`: a 34-chunk run makes two check calls then the critique, with the profile budget and no prompt cache on each; four distinct omissions over two slices all block and the critique's own one is dropped; the record sums three calls; a refusal of the second slice carries the first slice's bill, of the critique both slices', of the first slice nothing.
- `capBlockingOmissions` keeps its default in the existing tests; version pins move to v10.
- Local gate: `pnpm validate` and `pnpm test:postgres` (results in the PR's checks and below).

## Documentation

`docs/architecture/drafting-and-review.md` gains the v10 paragraph; `docs/roadmap.md` records the decision of 2026-11-02.

author: bu5hm4nn
body:
## Why

The photos-only frontend discovered multiple GPUs but stereo still ran on one. This PR distributes both PHOTO and GEO work, groups compatible shared inputs, and preserves full-resolution float32 quality and the explicit single-device path.

Backlog: Story 30 — Quality-preserving multi-GPU distribution and input-reuse-aware scheduling

Advances installed multi-device execution, affinity grouping, separate VRAM/aggregate-host admission, sequential admitted batches, unique output ownership and cancellation. Broader hardware qualification and 1/2/4-GPU scaling remain separate work; this PR does not mark the whole story complete.

## Delivered

- Deterministic phase-specific placement, balancing work against padded PHOTO source-bank reuse.
- One native process with per-device owned workers and immutable host PHOTO exchange after a complete PHOTO barrier; no duplicate PHOTO computation or pooled VRAM.
- Separate device limits and one aggregate host envelope, including retained maps and staging. No silent resizing, precision reduction or source removal.
- Device-set and resolved-placement approval/report binding; exact `--gpu-index` keeps the single-device path.
- Invocation-wide first-error cancellation and join/drain, including partial owner-thread launch failure and cohort retirement.

## Proof

Current head `1a59926b8`. Earlier GPU qualification used native `36683d0` with Python `4917ad8` (five photos) and `435bde7c8` (eight photos). The test-only `4de3b064` control correction also passed on GPUs. Automatic mixed-compute-capability placement is now refused; homogeneous selection and exact overrides remain intact.

The latest native candidate `3d1eec2f`, with Python pin follow-up `c193f5da`, has the same tree as this head. It replaces per-float map writes with bounded little-endian bulk writes, preserving headers, float bits and the existing big-endian fallback. Actual native compilation, ten CTests, fourteen Mat tests and 63 parent frontend/source tests passed. The new writer also passed three matched GPU pairs, with all 96 output-map comparisons literally identical to the retained pre-fix control.

- Actual native compile/relink/install; eight native CTests, 61 source tests, 29 installed-launcher tests and six installed multi-GPU binding tests passed. Real CPU-only CUDA refusals remained refusals; hardware skips are not GPU passes.
- Installed full-resolution **photos-only CLI completed on two L40 GPUs**, including extraction, matching, SfM, undistortion, PHOTO/GEO and fusion: all five original images registered, 1,817 output vertices. Original images are 6204×4132; geometric undistortion dimensions are explicitly recorded, not silently downscaled.
- Minimal no-cap plan-only invocation discovered both devices and created no requested workspace. Reconstruction used explicit user capacity caps (24 GiB aggregate host / 32 GiB per GPU), default scientific settings and no internal allowance override. This is not automatic physical-fit calibration.
- Actual `cmp` confirmed **22 output files identical** between one- and two-GPU execution: ten GEO depth/normal maps, five warped JPEGs, five sparse-model binaries, PLY and visibility. Comparer code and per-path results were independently inspected with retained artifacts.
- Same-process useful stereo Sweep overlap was verified separately for PHOTO (12.718 s) and GEO (12.267 s) on the two device UUIDs.
- Repaired constrained-bank GPU regression passed: all 64 references compared literally against full-bank multi-GPU and closed-cluster single-device controls, with useful GEO outputs. Two successive PHOTO banks per device were observed; cohort-retirement cancellation also passed.
- Overlap-rich CPU regression verifies lower predicted source-bank payload at equal assigned work. Completed bank-build counts are observations; calculated payload totals are **not measured PCIe traffic**.
- Five-photo matched profiled full-CLI runs: **138 s on two GPUs / 151 s on one**, one diagnostic observation only. A separate unprofiled single-GPU run took 144 s.
- A fresh, explicitly selected eight-photo full-resolution subset registered all eight images and produced 2,279,102 vertices. Its frozen geometry was used for three matched stereo pairs, two workers per GPU, with all 16 GEO maps literally identical in every arm and frozen inputs unchanged. Old-writer native-command speedups were **1.726×, 1.685× and 1.722×**; the first single-GPU arm overlapped preservation I/O. First-pair GPU kernel spans scaled **1.862× PHOTO / 1.918× GEO**, while roughly 21 seconds outside kernels diluted native-command scaling. These are old-writer measurements, not measurements of the new bulk writer.

## Final GPU-stage scaling

Three matched profiled pairs on two L40 GPUs, eight frozen full-resolution references, **two workers per GPU**. Values are means; speedup is the ratio of means.

| Measurement boundary | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PHOTO useful Sweep kernel span | 91.004 s | 48.778 s | **1.866×** |
| GEO useful Sweep kernel span | 99.913 s | 52.042 s | **1.920×** |
| Entire stereo GPU-kernel span | 191.597 s | 102.392 s | **1.871×** |
| Native stereo-command wall | 199.150 s | 110.518 s | **1.802×** |

PHOTO ratios ranged 1.849–1.885×; GEO 1.910–1.928×. Native-command ratios were 1.802×, 1.795× and 1.810×. All six runs used the admitted two-owner limit per device, preserved all eight references and ordered scientific inputs, and passed literal comparisons of all 16 GEO maps against the retained pre-fix output bodies. Frozen input hashes remained unchanged.

GPU kernel spans are **not** complete phase-wall or whole-reconstruction timings. Native wall includes native loading, transfers, execution, joining and output; it excludes SfM, frontend Python validation, fusion and profiler startup/export. Both sides were profiled identically. The production single-GPU path and distributed two-GPU path are compared; no historical-run timing is used as a matched baseline. This is bounded repeat evidence, not universal scaling or cost optimality.

## Failures retained and corrected

- Initial plane fixture had insufficient camera baseline for the unchanged 3-degree filter. Camera spacing and rendered disparity were corrected together; filters, seeds, source order and validity checks were retained.
- The 64-reference legacy control exceeded its original pitched-snapshot accounting margin. Closed four-reference controls preserve global identities and compare every output; the original 3% physical-copy refusal remains tested, not weakened.
- Default resource-policy fingerprints became stale after the native closure changed; the two Python bindings were corrected and tested without bypassing admission.
- Historical A6000 reconstruction outputs differ from the fresh L40 runs, including sparse geometry. No historical-oracle equivalence or cause is asserted; the direct same-build/same-hardware one-/two-GPU comparison is the accepted equivalence proof.

## Limits and review

Measured GPU-run RAM/VRAM peaks are unavailable; plan peaks are forecasts. All PHOTO exchange maps are retained under host admission, so oversized scenes can refuse. No GEO resident cache, cross-cohort cache, heterogeneous-GPU equivalence, Blackwell qualification, four-GPU scaling or arbitrary-scene guarantee is claimed.

For the earlier five-photo run, the 22 scientific outputs, comparisons and traces were retained, but the feature database, undistorted model, stereo configs, alias bindings and single-GPU planning tree were lost. That archive is not a complete replay package. The subsequent eight-photo run preserved its complete bootstrap/replay inputs, database, models, configs, alias bindings, output bodies and six-arm timing/trace records; the earlier loss remains disclosed.

Independent source reviews found no remaining blockers. CodeRabbit's heterogeneous-default-selection finding was addressed in `435bde7c8`, whose review completed with no actionable

author: tauceti-ai-for-science
body:
This PR gives `TauCeti.GTPattern n` its pointwise additive structure and proves that the polynomial (nonnegative) patterns form a finitely generated monoid. Its generators are the `2 ^ n` row-subset patterns, the patterns of the flag-minor diagonals. Patterns become an `AddCancelCommMonoid` with an entrywise `PartialOrder` and `IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid` instance. The nonnegative part is therefore Mathlib's `AddSubmonoid.nonneg (GTPattern n)`, and no separate carrier is introduced. `GTPattern.const n m` is the constant pattern, and `shift_eq_add_const` shows that the existing determinant shift `P.shift m` is `P + const n m`. `exists_zero_le_shift` shows that some natural shift makes any integer pattern nonnegative. `zero_le_iff_isPolynomial` shows that `0 ≤ P` exactly when the top weight is polynomial. `GTPattern.rowSubset I`, for `I : Finset (Fin n)`, is the 0/1 pattern whose row `j` has `#{r ∈ I | r < j}` ones. `rowSubset_univ` identifies the all-rows pattern with `const n 1`, the determinant, whose addition is `shift 1`. `rowSubset_injective` shows that the `2 ^ n` patterns are distinct. `mem_range_rowSubset` shows that they are exactly the patterns with entries in `{0, 1}`. The main theorem, `closure_range_rowSubset`, says they generate `AddSubmonoid.nonneg (GTPattern n)`, and it gives `fg_nonneg`. The proof splits a nonnegative pattern into its threshold patterns `[λ_{c,j} ≥ k]`. These are again patterns, because thresholding preserves the interlacing inequalities. It then reads off a 0/1 pattern's row set from the places where its row counts increase.

Milestone: [GroebnerGeometry/README.md, G5 "Minor, flag-minor and invariant algebras"](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/GroebnerGeometry/README.md#g5-minor-flag-minor-and-invariant-algebras), specifically "Identify its initial exponent monoid with the nonnegative part of native `GTPattern n`, constructing the complete pointwise `AddCommMonoid` API, its nonnegative `AddSubmonoid`, and `shift m` as addition of the constant pattern", together with "The row-subset generators number 2^n−1, including the determinant. Prove finite generation" and "its multiplication is `GTPattern.shift 1`". The flag-minor initial monoid is generated by the diagonal exponents of the row-subset flag minors. Under the roadmap's map `λ_{c,j} = Σ_{r<j} e(r,c)` those exponents become the `rowSubset I`, so `closure_range_rowSubset` is the pattern side of that identification. After this PR, the milestone still needs that exponent-to-pattern map with its successive-difference inverse and the additive equivalence with the generated diagonal monoid, which needs the generic-minor diagonal leading terms of open PR #25671. It also needs the diagonal SAGBI and standard-monomial theorems, saturation, the determinant localization to all integer patterns, and the Rees degeneration.

Add `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/GelfandTsetlin/AddMonoid.lean` (475 lines), which sits beside the `GTPattern` definition and its `Shift.lean`. Two general counting lemmas join their sibling `Finset.card_filter_castSucc_lt_succ` in `TauCeti/Data/Fin/Basic.lean` (+22 lines). They are `Finset.card_filter_val_lt_le`, which says at most `j` indices have value below `j`, and `Finset.card_filter_val_lt_add_one`, which says raising the bound to `j + 1` adds the index `j` when it is present. The instances come from Mathlib's `Function.Injective.addCancelCommMonoid`, `PartialOrder.lift` and `Function.Injective.isOrderedCancelAddMonoid`. The nonnegative submonoid is Mathlib's `AddSubmonoid.nonneg`, and finite generation uses `AddSubmonoid.fg_iff`. The module cites Miller–Sturmfels, *Combinatorial Commutative Algebra*, Chapter 14, and Kogan–Miller, *Toric degeneration of Schubert varieties and Gelfand-Tsetlin polytopes*. No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored. No open or merged PR touches the additive structure of `GTPattern`. The open GroebnerGeometry PRs (#22101, #24914, #25096, #25196, #25229, #25546, #25671, #26538) concern other targets, and this PR depends only on main.

I read the shared protocol and all ten rubrics: scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation and proof-quality. The self-review made four changes. It factored an entry bound that two proofs had duplicated into one private lemma. It moved the generic `Finset (Fin n)` counting facts to `Data/Fin/Basic.lean` rather than leaving them private here. It turned the 0/1 classification into the iff `mem_range_rowSubset`. It restated `topRow_rowSubset` unapplied, because Batteries' `simpNF` flagged the applied form. Local checks: both changed modules compile under the lakefile's lint options (`mathlibStandardSet`, `warningAsError`). Batteries `#lint` reports no findings for them. `#print axioms` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` for the main theorems, and `lake exe module-system` passes. A full `lake build` could not run here because the sandbox's pinned Mathlib build directory is read-only, and `scripts/lint-env.sh` needs `uvx`, which is not installed. CI is the authority for both.

Roadmap: GroebnerGeometry

author: stuartc
body:
## Description

Refactoring our API to have a uniform error response shape ([RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457.html)), additionally changing our authorisation and response code patterns to match select Google AIP conventions.

## What Changed

- **Errors are problem documents** (AIP-193).  
Every error on `/api`, `/collections`, `/adaptors/catalogue`, webhooks and the channel proxy is an RFC 9457 body with a fixed `code` and `detail`, and entries that point at the request key at fault.  
Clients branch on `code` instead of parsing messages. The token endpoint keeps OAuth's format.
- **Permission comes before the lookup** (AIP-211).  
Without access you get 403 whether or not the record exists, so the API stops telling strangers what's there. Only callers allowed to see that kind of record get 404. A number of previously 404s become 403.
- **`PUT` on an id creates or replaces (upsert)** (AIP-133, AIP-134).  
Projects, credentials and collections get `GET` and `PUT` by id, and a repeated `PUT` writes nothing. 
- **Credential lists page** (AIP-158), 10 by default, like the other lists.  
Added pagination.
- **Each status means one thing.**  
401 for failed login; a bad `Bearer` header is 400 and a missing grant/authorisation is 403 `insufficient_scope`.  
A duplicate is a `taken` entry in a 422, not a 409.  
Unknown body keys are 422, a non-object body is 400, limits are 402 `exceeds_limit` (webhooks keep 429), and an adaptor catalogue while it's still loading returns a 503.
- **The service account reaches more of the API** through three new grants.  
It must send `project_id` on the runs, work orders and log lines lists, and `/api/users` refuses personal access tokens with 403.
- **Bad certs & keys stop the app from booting.**  
A public key in `WORKER_RUNS_PRIVATE_KEY`, a placeholder or multi-block `GITHUB_CERT`, or a PEM with a stray character; all get detected early.

## Breaking Changes (most likely to bite)

- Every API error body has a new shape.
- `PUT /collections/:name/:key` with a value that can't be stored now returns 422, not 200 `{"upserted": 0}`. So any jobs that weren't reading the response body (and losing writes) will start failing.

## Agent context and docs

`.claude/rules/api.md`, `api-tests.md` and `policies.md` maintain the contracts we've set, cite the AIPs, and load automatically when an agent touches API code.
We've also added 3 Credo checks to help enforce it: 

- changeset errors carry a code (this is new, changesets have an atom that is mapped against http status codes)
- controllers don't set error statuses (also new, the changesets and return values from the context modules inform how something failed)
- and API controllers don't query. 

`API.md` and `SERVICE_ACCOUNTS.md` are new, with tests that fail if they drift from the router and the code.

## Notes

The service account scopes are still under development, and are likely to change.

## AI Usage

Please disclose whether you've used AI anywhere in this PR (it's cool, we just
want to know!):

- [x] I have used Claude Code
- [ ] I have used another model
- [ ] I have not used AI

You can read more details in our
[Responsible AI Policy](https://www.openfn.org/ai#pull-request-templates)

## Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I have performed an AI review of my code (we recommend using `/review`
      with Claude Code)
- [x] I have implemented and tested all related **authorization policies**.
      (e.g., `:owner`, `:admin`, `:editor`, `:viewer`)
- [x] I have updated the **changelog**.
- [x] I have ticked a box in "AI usage" in this PR

author: andrewmadson-pplx
body:
Fork draft for Andrew's review. Do not merge here. The upstream route is: open the feature request below, then open the upstream PR from `andrewmadson-pplx:pplx/agent-model-provider` with the "Upstream PR description" pasted. This branch and openclaw#2 (Embeddings) both edit `extensions/perplexity/index.ts` and `openclaw.plugin.json`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Brief

- **Gap:** the bundled Perplexity plugin registers only web search. OpenClaw users cannot run agent turns on the Agent API (`/v1/responses`), even though models.dev already lists a `perplexity-agent` provider.
- **Provider id `perplexity-agent`:** matches models.dev. The `perplexity` id stays for web search, whose setup env vars include `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. A separate id keeps model auth on `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` only, so an OpenRouter key is never sent to api.perplexity.ai.
- **Mirrors:** DeepSeek and Moonshot (models plus web search in one plugin), Kimi (more than one `setup.providers` entry), Particle and LongCat (`provider-catalog.ts`, `onboard.ts`, manifest `modelCatalog`), NVIDIA (endpoint-owned `X-Pplx-Integration` attribution through `providerEndpoints`).
- **Seed catalog:** `openai/gpt-5.5` (default) and `perplexity/sonar`, with prices and limits checked against live `/v1/models` and models.dev.
- **Tool schema normalization:** the Agent API rejects object schemas that have no `properties` key (for example a pure `additionalProperties` map) with 400 "invalid request". `normalizeToolSchemas` adds `properties: {}`, which does not change what the schema accepts.
- **Left out:** `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`. Its stream opens a message item at index 0 and starts a function call at index 1 before closing the message, and OpenClaw's Responses parser rejects that ("Responses stream changed output item identity"). Reported to the API team; can be added once fixed.

## What to test

Check out `pplx/agent-model-provider` and run `pnpm install` (Node 24). Run `pnpm test extensions/perplexity` (expect 39 passed). Run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice perplexity-agent-api-key`, paste a Perplexity API key, and confirm the default model becomes `perplexity-agent/openai/gpt-5.5` only if you had no primary model. Start an agent session on `perplexity-agent/openai/gpt-5.5`, ask for something that needs a tool (for example reading a file), and confirm the tool runs and the turn finishes. Switch to `perplexity-agent/perplexity/sonar` and repeat. Last, unset `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, set only `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, and confirm `perplexity-agent` reports a missing key instead of sending the OpenRouter key. Optional: `PERPLEXITY_LIVE_TEST=1 LIVE=1 pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts extensions/perplexity/perplexity-agent.live.test.ts` (expect 4 passed).

## Gate evidence (Nov 2, commit 51226b799dd on main 81cf32d9976, Node 24.22.1)

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Focused tests | `pnpm test extensions/perplexity` | 39 passed (5 new provider tests plus existing web search tests) |
| Contract tests | plugin-registration contract, provider env vars, provider auth aliases, provider attribution (3 files), model-auth env aliases | 29, 93, 17, 38, 5 passed (182 total) |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:core` | all exit 0 |
| Lint | `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/perplexity` plus changed `src/` files | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| Format | `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <changed files>` | all files formatted |
| Generated docs | `pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`, `pnpm config:docs:gen` | regenerated inventory, Perplexity reference page and config baseline hash; `plugins:inventory:check` exit 0 |
| Pre-commit hook | `git commit` | passed |
| Live call | `perplexity-agent.live.test.ts` against api.perplexity.ai | 4 passed (text turn and tool round trip for each model) |
| Full `pnpm check` and full `pnpm test` | not run | Blocked: the sandbox disk (25 GB) cannot hold the full build and test artifacts. CI on the upstream PR covers it |

Adversarial review: Perplexity Agent API (openai/gpt-5.5) over the full diff. The first two attempts hit a transient credential denial; the third ran. It raised 8 findings and I rejected all of them after checking:
- `register` is unsupported next to `provider`: `defineSingleProviderPluginEntry` accepts `register`, and the registration contract confirms web search still registers.
- The `<[]>` preset type drops credentials: the onboarding test confirms `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` is applied.

- Attribution is never stamped: `providerEndpoints` sets the endpoint class, and the attribution tests cover native vs proxy.
- OpenRouter key leakage: env candidates are per provider id, and a test asserts `perplexity-agent` lists only `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`.

## Feature request draft (open first, upstream)

Template: Feature request.

- **Problem:** OpenClaw cannot use Perplexity's Agent API as a model provider. Users who already set `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` for web search need another vendor for agent turns.
- **Proposed solution:** the bundled Perplexity plugin registers a `perplexity-agent` model provider (the models.dev id) on `https://api.perplexity.ai/v1` with the OpenAI Responses transport, seeded with `openai/gpt-5.5` and `perplexity/sonar`, plus an onboarding auth choice `perplexity-agent-api-key`.
- **Alternatives:** a custom OpenAI-compatible provider works only after manual config, gets no catalog or pricing, and hits a 400 on tool schemas without `properties`. A third-party plugin is possible, but the Perplexity plugin is already bundled and owns the auth and attribution policy.
- **Impact:** opt-in only. No change for existing users or for Perplexity web search.
- **Prior art:** DeepSeek and Moonshot plugins (models plus web search), Particle and LongCat model providers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider uses the existing OpenAI Responses transport against `https://api.perplexity.ai/v1` with a manifest catalog, following the Particle and LongCat providers. It uses the models.dev id `perplexity-agent` so model auth reads only `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`; the web search provider also accepts `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, which must never reach api.perplexity.ai. `X-Pplx-Integration` attribution is endpoint-owned, as for NVIDIA, so it is sent only to the native host. Tool schemas get `properties: {}` on object schemas that lack it, because the Agent API rejects those with a 400.

author: lavan96
body:
## What this does

Key audit **A1**. The owner decided on 2 Nov 2026 to re-check the September `missing` ledger rows against each project's own list, and correct them, **dry run first**.

`clone_backend_secrets` records what Mission Control wrote, when it wrote it. It is not a live record of what a clone holds. Measured on 2 Nov:
- **414 rows** on the four September clones read `missing`, with no set time, exactly as provisioning wrote them between 4 and 19 Sep: the dashboard has 100, the CRM 102, NPC Test 106 and Preflight 106.
- Orrimere has **109** more from its rebuild on 30 Oct.

#445 corrected the link key and the Turnstile secret against the project's list. This is the same reading for every other name.

### The rule (`ledgerRecheck.pure.ts`)
The project's list is the fact, and the ledger is corrected to it. The list reports a digest of each stored value (`secretWriteDiff.pure.ts`). Mission Control's own value is compared as a digest too (`valueDigests`), so neither side reads a value.

| Ledger row | Project lists the name? | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `missing`, `failed`, `authorised_no_value` | yes, with Mission Control's own value | `correct` to `inherited` |
| same | yes, another value, or Mission Control holds none | `correct` to `set` (the clone's own, `byok`) |
| same | yes, Mission Control holds a value, the digest is unreadable | `unresolved`: reported, never guessed |
| `set`, `inherited` | no | `unlisted`: **reported only**, because rewriting it would change what the forward sweeps owe |
| anything else | | left alone |

**Not this rule's** (`recheckExclusion`), each owned elsewhere:
- the Mission Control link names, and the Turnstile pair (#445);
- the email identity's key and sender;
- the owned secrets minted per clone;
- the model keys Mission Control mints;
- prime-only names (the prohibited sweep);
- brokered names;
- every row already `minted`, `federated` or `withheld`.

### Dry run first
- `LEDGER_RECHECK_MODE` is `dry_run`, and a test pins it there.
- The half-hourly prohibited-secrets sweep already reads each clone's list. Now it also reads the digests, and records what it **would** correct in `clone_ledger_reconcile_findings`, replaced by every pass. **No ledger row is written.**
- After merge, I'll read those predictions back, clone by clone, and show them to the owner. Going live is that one constant, in its own pull request.
- It never blocks the removal. A failure comes back as the re-check's own error in the sweep outcome, never as a clean pass.
- The findings hold names and statuses only. A test pins that no value or digest reaches them.

### The table (`20261102180000`)
- CHECKs:
  - a `correct` finding names `set` or `inherited`;
  - a reported finding names no status;
  - `applied_at` is only ever set on a live correction.
- It is service-role only, with the default grants revoked, and listed in `check-rls-policies.mjs` with its reason.

**Dry run on Postgres 16.** I tried every allowed and refused shape. My first draft accepted a correction that named no status, because `null in (...)` passes a CHECK. It is now written out, and refused. A second apply skips, browser roles have no reach, and a deleted clone takes its findings with it.

## Tests
- `ledgerRecheck.test.ts` (29 tests) covers each finding, each exclusion, the mode, and a source contract that a ledger write sits behind `mode === "live"`.
- It also runs the sweep end to end against a fake database that keeps a findings table, with a listing that holds a client's own key and a copy of the platform's value. The dry run records three findings (`set`, `inherited`, `unlisted`) and writes no ledger row.
- `cloneProhibitedSecrets.test.ts`: each outcome now carries the re-check's summary. On those fakes, which keep no findings table, it reports its own failure without changing the sweep's outcome.

**Run locally:**
- the full suite: 12,102 tests passed, 1 skipped;
- the typecheck and the build;
- lint on the changed files;
- every CI check, including `check:discarded-errors` (each new write branches on its `error`), `check:rls` and `check:supabase-types`;
- `migrations:assertions`, regenerated.

**None of these rows can move money on its own.** Usage is rated from a ledger status only when a clone reports a call on that name. The rated names among the 414 are client-only, where `missing` and `set` both bill nothing.

## Note for merging
`src/server/migrationAssertions.generated.ts` is generated. #497 and #498 also add migrations, so each later merge takes `main` and regenerates it (`npm run migrations:assertions`).

author: jesusvilela
body:
**Phase173 — exact existing binary quarter, then conditional scalar separation.** This is a bounded numerical/arithmetical bridge, **not** a new field cutoff.

The source-checked Phase165 univariate binary exponent satisfies `4*binaryNullGramExponent R S >= R^2*S`. For positive R,S, normalize using the **same** comparison scale `R^2*S` to prove `log(2)/4 <= binaryLambda*log(2)/(R^2*S)`. No new prime, derivative, metric or support is introduced.

For `u>=237/10` the previously used affine expressions have a strict gap:
`U(u)+98/1000 < L(u)+log(2)/4` with `L(u)=999997*u/1000000-5739/1000` and `U(u)=4*u/5-1849/2000`. This becomes a contradiction **only if** both inequalities bound the SAME normalized log determinant. That source-exact lower remains draft #91 and the full analytic upper on D>=377^4 is still missing.

[Lean proof](lean/TenthDiscriminant/BinaryGap377.lean) · [Human guide](research/thin_integrated/PHASE173_BINARY_GAP_377.md) · [Issue #82](https://github.com/Dojo-1/tenth-discriminant/issues/82).

**H until exact-head focused and whole-root Lean/source/axiom/negative controls pass.** Stronger field-bound claims forbidden until same-source-Gram upper and field-chart proof; independent semantics #50 still open.

author: pgarrett-scripps
body:
Two declared floors in the extras named versions no installer can supply.

## `zstd>=1.5.5` -> `zstd>=1.5.5.1`

zstd 1.5.5 was never published to PyPI. The whole 1.5.4/1.5.5 range on PyPI is:

```
['1.5.4.0', '1.5.4.1', '1.5.5.1']
```

The floor named a version that does not exist. `1.5.5.1` is the only 1.5.5.x release.

## `rapidgzip>=0.14.0` -> `rapidgzip>=0.14.2`

**0.14.0 and 0.14.1 are yanked on PyPI** (no yank reason given), so PEP 592 keeps a resolver
off them unless they are pinned exactly — which is why `>=0.14.0` has always resolved to
0.14.2. 0.14.2 is the oldest installable release in that line.

Worth recording, because the sweep that found this attributed it to wheel coverage: that is
not the cause. All three releases ship the same CPython wheel tags and all three have an
sdist, so wheel coverage cannot be what excluded 0.14.0 and 0.14.1:

| version | CPython wheel tags | sdist | yanked |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.14.0 | cp36–cp312 | yes | **yes** |
| 0.14.1 | cp36–cp312 | yes | **yes** |
| 0.14.2 | cp36–cp312 | yes | no |
| 0.14.3 | cp37–cp313 | yes | no |

(cp313 wheels arrive in 0.14.3, so under `requires-python >=3.12` a 3.13/3.14 user builds
0.14.2 from its sdist. That is a separate question from the floor and is not changed here.)

## Scope and verification

- Both floors corrected in `[project.optional-dependencies]`, and in the `dev` group, which
  duplicates both, so the file no longer names `1.5.5` or `0.14.0` anywhere.
- `just lock mzmlpy`: **the two specifiers moved and nothing else** — no resolved version
  changed, which is the direct evidence that installs are unaffected.
- `just check mzmlpy` and `just isolated mzmlpy`: both pass (ajs 2121, 40.7s, non-exclusive).
  Isolated run 769 passed, 8 skipped (optional-dependency skips, expected in that env).
- No version bump, no source change.
