body:
A version PR (`changeset-release/*`) only bumps versions and changelogs, and every change in it already passed CI on its own PR. So for those branches:

- **`check`**: the whole job skips. A skipped required check counts as passed.
- **`e2e (…)`**: the job runs, but every step skips. A matrix job skipped as a whole reports one unexpanded name (`e2e (${{ matrix.name }})`), and the six required `e2e (core 1/3)`… checks would then wait forever.
- **pkg.pr.new**: no preview publish. The real publish follows the merge.
- **Dependency audit**: skipped. A version PR changes no dependency.

Every other branch runs exactly as before.

author: ifsnop
body:
## Qué trae

Los dos CSV que genera la aplicación siguen ahora el idioma de la interfaz (no el del sistema):

- **Inglés:** campos separados por coma y decimales con punto.
- **Español:** campos separados por punto y coma y decimales con coma (lo que Excel espera en una configuración regional española).

Commits:

1. **CSV del perfil de una ruta** (`790ef62`): `csvDialect(lang)` deduce el dialecto de `Intl.NumberFormat` (un idioma con coma decimal usa punto y coma: también fr, de). `csvCell`/`toCsv` aceptan el dialecto (por omisión coma y punto); solo un `number` de JS se reescribe con la marca decimal, se entrecomilla el separador del dialecto y la defensa contra fórmulas no cambia.
2. **`.claude/rules/i18n.md` versionado** (`aeac02a`): era el único archivo de reglas sin seguimiento (`.claude/` está en `.gitignore`); el README y `CLAUDE.md` lo citan.
3. **CSV de la tabla de atributos** (`62be5c1`): mismo dialecto. Los atributos son texto del archivo y no se tocan, salvo un decimal llano (`3.5` o `3,5`) de una **columna numérica**, que se escribe con la marca del idioma para que la hoja de cálculo lo lea como número (en un Excel español `3.5` es una fecha). Enteros, ceros a la izquierda, exponentes, `1.234.567` y cualquier texto salen tal cual.

## Pruebas

- `KITE_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 node tests/run-all.js`: 115 de 115 suites.
- `tests/profileexport.js` y `tests/attrtable.js`: los dialectos, el mismo contenido, el entrecomillado y `attrCsvValue`.
- `tests/browser/elev-profile.mjs` y `tests/browser/attr-table.mjs`: el CSV descargado de verdad, en español y, cambiando el idioma, en inglés con las mismas cifras.

## Documentación

Manual (7.9 y 7.15), estudio de seguridad (exportar el perfil), README, `tests/README.md` y las reglas (`elevation-dem`, `style-dialogs-ui`, `i18n`). Sin cambios de aspecto, sin capturas nuevas.

body:
## Resumen

Primera tanda de mejoras del fork, centrada en DeepSeek, Windows + Chrome y la gestión de MCP.

### Base del proyecto
- `PLANNING.md`, `TASK.md` y `LOG.md` (decisiones con fecha), `docs/CONTEXTO_IA.md` para compartir el contexto con otras IA.
- `server/bridge.log` deja de versionarse; `*.log` en `.gitignore`.

### Parser y DeepSeek
- La reparación de JSON (barras invertidas que el Markdown deja sueltas, comillas tipográficas) pasa de `chatgpt.js` a `utils.js`, así que la aprovechan todos los adaptadores.
- Adaptador DeepSeek:
  - filtro de razonamiento (DeepThink) más preciso;
  - filtrado de mensajes anidados con coste lineal;
  - caché de la lista de mensajes.
- Prueba en Chromium con DOM simulado: `npm run test:browser`.

### Instalación en Windows
- `INSTALL.md` y `scripts/windows/install.ps1`, probado en Windows con Python 3.14. Se puede volver a ejecutar sin problema: detiene el puente anterior y comprueba que responde el puente real.
- `install_service.py` detiene los puentes anteriores en Windows (al instalar y al desinstalar).

### Detección de MCP y recarga en caliente

- `npm run test:browser`: adaptador DeepSeek con DOM simulado.

author: controgon
body:
Adds policy exemptions to `azure_policy_assignments` (0.3.0 → 0.4.0).

- Every exemption in effect on the subscription in `results.policy_exemptions`: its own, inherited from a management group, and on resource groups and resources inside it, expired ones and Defender for Cloud recommendation exemptions included.
- Each one is joined to the assignment it exempts and, for initiatives, to the named members' resolved effects. It records scope, category (Waiver or Mitigated, whatever case Azure stored), description, metadata, creator and expiry, plus `expired`, `no_expiry`, `days_until_expiry`, `on_defender_benchmark_assignment` and `lifts_enforcement`.
- Exemption records carry free text written in Azure (`description`, `metadata`) and the user principal names of who created and last changed each one (`created_by`, `last_modified_by`), which serve as its approval trail.
- An unknown `lifts_enforcement` carries `lifts_enforcement_unknown_reason`. The reasons are an assignment that isn't listed (usually deleted, its exemptions left behind), unread assignments or initiative members, a member the initiative's current definition no longer has (`in_initiative: false`), or an unresolved effect.
- Each assignment gains `exemption_count`. The summary gains 24 fields: exemption counts by category, expiry, scope and enforcement, `exemptions_read_status`, and the exclusion boundary.
- Exemptions exist only in preview api-versions, and `azure-mgmt-resource-policy` 1.0.0 has no exemption operations. They are read by a raw ARM GET through `_shared/arm_rest.py`, pinned to 2024-12-01-preview. Any failed read fails the run with every exemption count null. `exemptions_read_status` says `api_version_unavailable` when ARM refused that version (InvalidApiVersionParameter, NoRegisteredProviderFound or InvalidResourceType), so a retired preview version shows up as a failed run, and `failed` otherwise.
- When the assignment list fails, the existing assignment summary counts now read null instead of 0, and so do `active_exemptions_lifting_enforcement` and the counts that join exemptions to assignments. The run still fails, as before.
- Adopts `resource_exclusions` for exemptions only, by the scope they were made at (rg:/id:). location: never matches an exemption. Assignments are unchanged.

Tests: 51 new unit tests on synthetic fixtures. Read-only sandbox runs covered no patterns, an rg: pattern and a location: pattern, all exit 0.

Fixes FDE-310

author: delwing
body:
Feedback on the Char.Login v2 / OAuth work (#482): sign-in worked, but the token was never kept, so every visit meant signing in again.

## Why

The game is told `token_storage` before it signs anyone in. That answer came from whether the credential vault was open at that moment, and:

- with no vault, it was always `false`, with nothing telling the player why;
- a vault locks on every page load and was offered for unlocking only when it already held something for the profile, so a first sign-in told the game `false` and no token was sent.

## What changes

**Ask to open a locked vault before answering** (c5a3068)
- v2 game, a sign-in method on offer, and a locked vault with nothing saved for this profile: ask to unlock first. The prompt says why ("…to keep <profile> signed in next time").
- "Not now" signs in without saving, and it isn't asked again this visit.
- With no vault at all: a one-time output line, "Want to stay signed in next time? **Set up saved logins**". The link opens vault setup.
- Branded builds have no vault and show neither.

**Keep the vault unlocked on this device** (ef9508d)
- Opt-in "Keep unlocked on this device for 30 days" on the unlock and setup dialogs.
- The master key is wrapped under a non-extractable AES-GCM key kept in a new IndexedDB database, `mudlet_vault_device`. Script can use the key but never read it, and the vault reopens before the first render, so a cold auto-connect finds the token readable.
- The entry is tied to its vault and expires after 30 days. "Lock now", deleting the vault, or "Ask every visit" in the manage view drops it.
- What it gives up is shown when the box is ticked: anyone who can use this browser profile can open the saved logins.
- Imported only through `main.tsx`, like the rest of the vault, so nothing reaches `dist-lib`.

## Testing

- `yarn typecheck`, `yarn test` (5694 passing). New tests cover the ladder rung, the controller's prompt, "Not now", the setup hint, and remember/restore/expiry/replaced-vault/forget in the vault.
- On a production build in Chrome:
  - ticking the box and reloading opened the vault with no prompt, and the stored key is non-extractable AES-GCM;
  - "Lock now" then reload asked again, with the entry gone;
  - a fed v2 `Char.Login.Default` with no vault posted the link, which opened setup.
- Not tried against a real game's OAuth sign-in.
- `yarn build:lib` fails on Windows on a spec map fixture path (`stale-label-keys.dat?inline`). That's unrelated to this change, so CI's build is the check for the lib.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: vhata
body:
## Why

`start-work.sh <queue> <slug>` documents the queue as one of `todo`,
`review`, `roadmap`, `fix` or `task`, and uses it as the branch prefix
and the worktree name. It accepted any word, so `start-work.sh TODO
<slug>` made `TODO/<slug>` in `.worktrees/TODO-<slug>`.
`check-pr-markers.sh` requires no claim marker on such a branch,
`pr-labels.sh` gives it no queue label, and `claim-check.sh` does not
match its worktree directory. On a case-insensitive filesystem the
`refs/heads/TODO` directory also collides with `refs/heads/todo`, and
renaming one branch to the right case fails until the refs are packed.

## What changed

`start-work.sh` exits 2 with "queue must be one of todo, review,
roadmap, fix, task" for any other word, including another case of a
queue name, before it checks claims or creates a branch or worktree.

This is review finding `start-work-queue-unvalidated`, listed in the
`start-work-inputs-and-paths` backlog entry. The entry's other findings
are separate work, so the entry is not claimed and stays queued.

## Validation

A fixture in `tests/scripts.sh` runs `start-work.sh` with `TODO`,
`Todo`, `tasks` and `feature` and expects each to be refused with no
branch or worktree left behind; it failed before the change.

Type: fix
Resolves review finding: start-work-queue-unvalidated

author: cassiozen
body: Stacked on #66. Milestone 2d of Spaces with Agents: queued runs now run. With this, the server-side triggers work end to end: new note done, note edit done, note deleted, moved in and moved out. ## Runner (`internal/agent/runner.go`) - **Workers:** one per account, started at boot and on first wake. It runs the queue in order, editor triggers first, one run at a time, which is also one at a time per note. - **Shared limit:** at most 4 provider calls at once across accounts. - **Waking:** on every note write (`Registry.OnNote`), when the sweep ends a session, and on AI settings saved or removed (new `api.Config.OnAIChanged`). Otherwise a worker checks once a minute, and sooner when a retry is due. - **Paused:** while AI isn't set up. The queue waits rather than failing. - **Restarts:** a run left `running` by a stopped server goes back in the queue once. It fails as `interrupted` if it already changed something or was interrupted before. - **Shutdown:** `serve` stops the runner and waits for it before closing databases. A run in progress is recorded even as the server stops. - **`RunNext`:** runs one run synchronously, for tests. ## A run - **Prompt:** notesd's instructions (rules, Markdown, tag syntax), the date and time in the account's time zone, the space's prompt, the trigger's prompt. The user message is the event, with the note. - **Deleted and moved out:** these get the stored snapshot instead, and are told they can't open the note. - **Skipped without calling the model:** | Reason | Failure code | | --- | --- | | Agent turned off, or no prompt for the trigger | `agent_off` | | Note deleted | `note_gone` | | Note moved to another space | `note_moved` | | Note locked | `note_locked` | | Daily token cap reached | `daily_cap` | - **Run limits:** 20 tool calls, 150k tokens and 5 minutes per run; 90 seconds per call. - **Provider failures:** retried once after 30 seconds, only if the run changed nothing. ## Tools (`internal/agent/tools.go`) - **Read:** `get_note`, `search_notes`, `list_notes`, `list_tags`. - **Write:** `set_title`, `edit_note` (`find` must match exactly once), `insert` (start or end), `create_note`. - **Not yet:** `get_cursor` and `insert` at the cursor answer that no editor is open; they come with the socket in M4. - **Boundaries:** everything is bound to the run's space. Locked notes are refused and left out of searches and lists. A bad call is answered with an error the model can act on. - **How writes happen:** ordinary store updates with operation ID `agent::` and `agent: {runId, only: true}`, based on the revision the run read, so they never start a session or a trigger. - **Note changed underneath:** the run starts over once from the note as it is now, then gives up with `note_changed`. ## Record (migration `0015_agent_activity.sql`) - **Each run:** status, failure, outcome (`edited`, `created`, `no_change`), the model's last line or what went wrong, model, tool calls and tokens. - **`agent_run_edits`:** each note a run changed, before its first change and after its last, with revisions. Activity's diff and Undo (M3) read it. - **`agent_usage`:** tokens per day in the account's time zone. - **Purge:** finished runs older than 30 days are deleted hourly, with their edits. ## Also - **Short API keys:** a key under 8 characters gets no hint. Its last four would give much of it away; a 4-character key was shown whole. This is a fix to #62. - **Docs:** architecture §7.8 Agents and the schema; the agents guide says which triggers act now. ## Tests - **`internal/agent/runner_test.go`:** a scripted in-process model over the store wired as the server wires it. Covers: - auto-tagging end to end: the prompt, the event, list_tags, the write, the edit record and usage; - the agent's write starting no session; - each tool refusal; - each reason a run is skipped; - the tool and token caps; - a note changed underneath: starts over, then gives up; - the provider retry and its timing; - paused without AI; - the deleted and moved-out snapshots; - create_note; - restart recovery, purge, and the worker loop. - **Against the real binary:** with a fake provider, deleting a note woke the runner, and the model's `create_note` made a Digest note. The run was recorded with its tokens. - `mise run check` passes. --- ## Summary by cubic Queued agent runs now execute on the server: the runner picks up runs, the model acts on notes through tools, and each run is recorded for the activity log. Server-side triggers work end to end for new note done, note edit done, note deleted, and both moved triggers. **Runner and runs** - One worker per account runs the queue in order, editor triggers first, one run at a time; at most 4 provider calls run at once across accounts. - Workers wake on note writes, ended writing sessions, and AI settings changes; the queue waits rather than failing while AI isn't set up. - Runs are skipped without calling the model when the agent is off, the note is gone, moved, or locked, or the daily token cap is reached. - Each run is limited to 20 tool calls, 150k tokens and 5 minutes; a provider failure is retried once after 30 seconds if the run changed nothing. - A note changed underneath a run makes it start over once from the current note, then fail as `note_changed`. - Runs left `running` by a stopped server re-queue once; `serve` stops the runner and waits for it before closing databases. **Tools and record** - The tools are `get_note`, `search_notes`, `list_notes`, `list_tags`, `set_title`, `edit_note` (find must match exactly once), `insert` (start or end), and `create_note`. - Everything is bound to the run's space; locked notes are refused and left out of searches and lists; cursor tools report that no editor is open. - Agent writes are ordinary store updates marked `agent: {runId, only: true}`, so they start no session or trigger. - Each run records status, failure, outcome, message, model, tool calls and tokens; `agent_run_edits` keeps each note before and after for the activity diff and undo, and `agent_usage` tracks tokens per day. - Finished runs older than 30 days are purged hourly. - API keys under 8 characters no longer get a hint, since the last four would give away nearly the whole key. Written for commit 93061649a91c1c870b2ebc8bf40de0550138f0bd. Summary will update on new commits.

author: deesmo
body:
Fixes the npm advisories Dependabot reports for `web/package-lock.json`. Same approach as #153 (api/). Only `web/package.json` and `web/package-lock.json` change.

## Audit, main → this branch (`npm audit --package-lock-only`, distinct advisories)

| | critical | high | moderate | low |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, dev included | 4 | 22 | 15 | 3 |
| this branch, dev included | **0** | **3** (all sharp) | **1** (minimatch, dev only) | **0** |
| main, `--omit=dev` | 4 | 15 | 10 | 2 |
| this branch, `--omit=dev` | **0** | **3** (all sharp) | **0** | **0** |

## What moved (smallest fixing version for direct deps, inside the current major)

| package | from → to | why |
|---|---|---|
| `next` | 15.5.19 → 15.5.28 | 3 critical (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4, GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw), 4 high, 7 moderate. 15.5.28 is the current 15.x `backport` release. |
| `eslint-config-next` (dev) | 15.5.19 → 15.5.28 | kept in lockstep with `next`, as in c13d9fec |
| `dompurify` (via posthog-js) | 3.4.12 → 3.4.17 | 1 critical (GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7), 1 high, 1 moderate, 2 low |
| `js-yaml` | 4.2.0 → 4.3.2 | 3 high |
| `postcss` (also forced onto next by the `$postcss` override) | 8.5.15 → 8.5.23 | 1 high, 1 moderate |
| `nanoid` (via postcss) | 3.3.15 → 3.3.20 | 2 high |
| `source-map-js` (via postcss) | 1.2.1 → 1.2.2 | 1 high |
| `fflate` (via posthog-js) | 0.4.8 → 0.4.9 | 1 moderate |
| `brace-expansion` override pins (dev) | 1.1.13 → 1.1.21, 5.0.6 → 5.0.12 | 5 high, 1 moderate. The old pins were what kept it vulnerable. |
| `browserslist` (dev) | 4.28.1 → 4.29.5 | 2 high. Its data deps come along: caniuse-lite …779 → …820, baseline-browser-mapping 2.10.8 → 2.11.34 (1 moderate). |
| `@humanfs/node` (dev) | 0.16.7 → 0.16.8 | 1 moderate |
| `postcss-selector-parser` (dev) | 6.1.2 → 6.1.5 | 1 moderate, 1 low |

### Release notes read for anything beyond a patch bump
- **next 15.5.20–15.5.28** ([releases](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases?q=v15.5&expanded=true)): security fixes, plus three behaviour changes. 15.5.22 rejects TypeScript ≥ 7; we lock 5.9.3. 15.5.24/15.5.25 ([#97954](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/97954)) only optimize AVIF images when sharp's libheif is the patched version; this app does not enable AVIF and has no `next/image` usage. 15.5.26 hardens `next/og`, which this app doesn't use.
- **js-yaml 4.3.x** ([CHANGELOG at 4.3.2](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/4.3.2/CHANGELOG.md)): adds a `maxTotalMergeKeys` limit and removes the 4.2-only `maxMergeSeqLength` option. `js-yaml` isn't imported anywhere in `web/src`.
- **browserslist 4.29** ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/browserslist/browserslist/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)): query parsing fixes and a new multi-line query syntax. The caniuse-lite data refresh can change autoprefixer output slightly, and it removes the build's "browsers data is 8 months old" warning.

## Left on purpose
- **sharp 0.34.5: 3 high** (GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj, GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c, GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w, all in bundled libvips/libheif/librsvg). These are fixed only in sharp 0.35.x. For a 0.x package that minor bump is breaking: [0.35.0](https://github.com/lovell/sharp/releases/tag/v0.35.0) drops Node 18 and removes deprecated APIs. So it's out of this PR's in-major rule. `next@15.5.28` already declares `sharp: ^0.34.3 || ^0.35.5`, which makes it a one-line follow-up (`npm update --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts sharp`). I checked that follow-up separately on a scratch copy: clean `npm ci` and `next build` pass (19/19), sharp 0.35.5 loads, and the prod audit drops to 0. sharp only backs Next's image optimizer.
- **minimatch GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249: moderate, dev only.** It is fixed only in minimatch 11.0.1. eslint 9.39.x needs `^3.1.5` and typescript-eslint 8 needs `^10.2.2`, so the fix requires eslint 10. npm counts this one advisory as 14 eslint-chain packages.

## Verification
Both lockfiles ran side by side, each in its own scratch copy outside the repo (rsync without `node_modules`/`.git`/`.next`), on Node 24.14.0 (`.nvmrc`). The lockfile was regenerated with npm 11.19, the version that wrote main's lock. An older npm would have dropped its `libc` fields.

| check | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `npm ci` | ok (427 pkgs) | ok (428 pkgs) |
| `next build` | ok, Next 15.5.19, 19/19 static pages, 18 routes, shared JS 102 kB | ok, Next 15.5.28, 19/19 static pages, same 18 routes, shared JS 103 kB |
| build warnings | caniuse-lite data 8 months old | none |
| `next start` on 11 routes | 10×200, `/nope` 404 | same codes and same page sizes (only chunk-hash differences) |
| `npm run lint` | can't run: `next lint` opens an interactive setup prompt because `web/` has no ESLint config (exit 1) | same |
| ESLint, scratch-only Next flat config (`next/core-web-vitals` + `next/typescript`) | 50 errors / 12 warnings | 50 errors / 12 warnings, same rule breakdown |

The lint errors exist on main already: `no-explicit-any` 27, `no-unescaped-entities` 18, `no-unused-vars` 10, `jsx-no-comment-textnodes` 5, `exhaustive-deps` 2.

## Note: web/ appears not to be deployed
- `render.yaml` defines one service, with `rootDir: api`. Every workflow (`deploy`, `test`, `security-gate`) runs in `api/` only, and `security-gate` audits only `api/`, so these `web/` advisories aren't gated anywhere.
- `AGENTS.md` describes `web/` as the "Next.js marketing site", a client that isn't needed to run the API. README and DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST don't mention `web/`.
- The repo tracks a stale `web/.next/` build from 2026-03-16, built with Next **14.2.35**, which is older than the Next 15 migration. It also tracks `web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. That's why all builds above ran in scratch copies. Untracking them would be a separate cleanup.

Not merged; review and merge are yours.

author: arndrosemeier
body:
## Cave search on top of #533

#533 rolls for a cave every 15 m along a cliff. Each roll made up to 16 whole searches, each about 4 to 9 ms, so a run through country without cliffs would hitch every few seconds.

- A place's ground rule can take an accepting test (`near.accept` in `dungeonFor`). The cave tool passes "mouth in a cliff, off the towns, in view, facing the hero", so the best spot that fits wins instead of the best spot overall failing the filter afterwards. Three looks are enough (was 16).
- The cone ahead of the hero is 70 degrees each side (was 40), so a cliff along their way, not only straight ahead, gets caves.
- Measured on 48 runs out of the start town: the first cave came after 285 m on average (was 460 m), at about 9 ms per roll (was about 35 ms at 8 looks).
- Tests: a run along a cliff meets a cave within 600 m on several headings, one of them well off the way. Scanned hero spots in two older tests moved.

author: medsidd
body:
Answers "How long will I actually wait at my stop?" (metrics plan WP4).

## What it adds
- `core/fct_stop_headway`: one row per stop visit a vehicle made.
  - It gives the observed headway since the previous vehicle of the same route and direction at that stop that service day, the arriving trip's scheduled headway, the delay, the day type and the period.
  - A visit counts if it was timed from a crossing or an origin departure, or from the last prediction when the trip had a vehicle. Ghost trips are therefore dropped and leave the gap riders saw.
  - Incremental `insert_overwrite` over 3 days, rebuildable from `fct_stop_visit`.
- `marts/realtime/mart_wait_by_stop_period`: stop × route × direction × day type × period over the last 28 service dates.
  - Columns: `service_class` (frequent or infrequent), expected, scheduled and excess wait, `pct_bunched`, `pct_gap`, `pct_on_time` (1 min early to 5 late) and `p90_delay_sec`.
- `marts/realtime/mart_wait_by_route_day`: the same per route and day, with wait, bunching and gaps over headways scheduled every 15 minutes or better.
- Both marts are `allow_in_app: false` until the stop-visit review.
- Also: schema tests, a glossary section, counts, lineage and as-built notes.

## Testing
- `tests/sql/test_wait_time.py` runs in DuckDB. It uses a hand-computed sequence:
  - headways of 600, 120, 1740 and 540 s against 600 scheduled;
  - expected wait 615.6 s, scheduled 300 s, excess 315.6 s;
  - 25% bunched and 25% gaps;
  - a ghost trip dropped and a skipped stop ignored.
  - Both marts are checked.
- `make lint`, `make test` (88 passed) and `make test-ingest` (44 passed).
- Dry runs:
  - fact: 98 MB;
  - each mart with the fact inlined: 89 MB.
- Read-only check, 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-01:
  - weekday network excess wait was 68–69 s per frequent headway, with 3.6–3.8% bunched and 9% gaps;
  - route 15 had 2.6 minutes of excess wait, with 15% bunched;
  - EWT averaged above 0 on every day, as the plan's check requires.

Pausing for user input previously dropped the accepted token subtotal, and invalid tool calls reported one reason for six parser rejection branches. Preserve the partial accepted usage in a narrow schema 8 receipt and add a fixed parser category only to opt-in failed-request logs.

author: williem3
body:
## Fix: wrong output size for DLSS in D3D12 games with differently sized views

### The problem in plain terms

When a game asks DLSS to upscale an image, it passes a "settings bag" (NGX parameters) that says, among other things, how big the finished image should be (`OutWidth` / `OutHeight`).

Some games reuse **one** settings bag for every DLSS feature they own. The size written in it is whatever the game set last, which isn't necessarily the size of the feature being run right now. Cheeky already guards against this: before processing, it temporarily puts the feature's real size (the size it was created with) back into the bag, then restores the game's values afterwards (`NgxEvaluationExtentScope`).

That guard was applied on the regular D3D12 `EvaluateFeature` routes, but **not** on the `EvaluateFeature_C` entry point. That's the one NVIDIA's helper `NGX_D3D12_EVALUATE_DLSS_EXT` calls, so games using the helper skipped the guard.

### Where it showed up

Assetto Corsa EVO with quad views ([ace-quadview](https://github.com/Williem3/Sim-QVFR)'s QVFR mode) renders four views per frame at two different sizes: two large outer views and two smaller, sharper focus views. ACE creates four DLSS features, then evaluates all four through the same settings bag and `NGX_D3D12_EVALUATE_DLSS_EXT`.

After creation, the bag's `OutWidth`/`OutHeight` still held the size of the last feature created (a focus view). So when Cheeky's quad mode processed an **outer** view, it believed the output was the focus view's size. The peripheral DLAA result was composed at the wrong size, and the outer view appeared shrunk into the top-left of its area with blank space around it: a "picture in picture" effect in the headset. Turning Cheeky off made the image correct again.

Ordinary stereo games never hit this, because both eyes are the same size, so the leftover value happens to be correct.

### Fix 1: the `_C` entry point

`runtime_evaluate_d3d12_c` now uses the same `NgxEvaluationExtentScope` as `process_d3d12_evaluation`, with the same conditions:
- only for native DLSS evaluations (`recognizable_d3d12_dlss_evaluation`)
- not inside Streamline (which supplies its own sizes)
- only on the outermost call, so Cheeky's own private evaluations are untouched

The game's parameter values are restored after the evaluation, exactly as on the other routes. One file, about 8 lines.

### Fix 2: features created before Cheeky's lower hook is installed

The guard above can only restore a feature's real size if Cheeky recorded that size when the feature was created.

With the lower hook path (`D3D12LowerHook`, the default), the core create hook deliberately leaves that recording to the hook on `nvngx_dlss.dll`. Cheeky installs that hook only after it has seen the DLL loaded for three scans (about 1.5 s here). ACE creates its features right as `nvngx_dlss.dll` loads, about 0.4 s before the hook went in. So no size was recorded, the guard had nothing to apply, and the outer views were shrunk again. The log shows only `FEATURE_CREATE … route=D3D12-core` lines in that case.

`hook_core_create_d3d12` now records the created output size itself when nothing has recorded it yet:
- only for the game's own DLSS features, not inside Cheeky's interception
- with the same handle the lower hook would record, so the values match if that hook also sees the create

### Testing

- Assetto Corsa EVO, D3D12, Pimax headset, ace-quadview QVFR with DLSS on, Cheeky quad mode with manual roles (outer views → Periphery, focus views → Center), outer DLAA at 0.75 and 1.0.
  - **Before:** the outer views rendered shrunk inside their area (confirmed with frame captures): to 75% with the `_C` problem, and to 87.5% (the focus views' size) when the features were created before the lower hook.
  - **After both fixes:** all four views correct, the outer and focus views line up, including launches where the features are created before the lower hook is installed.
- Cheeky's test suite (`scripts/build.ps1` list, run with failures continuing):
  - 269–276 cases pass across runs.
  - `CheekyOpenXRBindingTests --fg-gpu-validation` and `--fg-shader11`, and `CheekyCoreDiscoveryTests dx11-ota`, fail on this machine. They fail identically on unmodified v0.6.3 (`master`), and the two binding tests don't compile `hooks.cpp`.
  - `CheekyOverlayTests` (F8 polling) failed once while the game had focus; that test reads the live keyboard, doesn't compile `hooks.cpp`, and passed in the earlier run.
- The changed `_C` route is covered by the UEVR `dx12-c` cases, which pass.

A build with both fixes: https://github.com/Williem3/CheekyFoveatedDLSS/releases/tag/v0.6.3-ace.2

`crb` clears `d.M` immediately before `_M` overwrites every stored CSR entry. Remove that redundant clear and prefill `M` with infinity in the existing dense/sparse `crb` tests to check that rebuilding the matrix overwrites its previous contents.

At 8,192 humanoid worlds on an exclusive L40S, this removes one 7,962,624-byte memset per simulation step. The removed memset takes 3.65 µs on average in the MuJoCo Warp profile and 3.63 µs in Newton; `_M`'s compiled code is unchanged.

| Full GPU simulation workload | Median paired time reduction |
| --- | ---: |
| MuJoCo Warp humanoid | 0.318% |
| Newton humanoid using the MuJoCo solver | 0.046% |

These are four alternating baseline/change pairs against `f7ce310d`, with 1,000 MuJoCo Warp steps (discarding the first 10) and 100 Newton frames of 10 substeps after warmup. All four pairs improved in each workload; the Newton effect is very small. Timing covers the complete simulation graph, excluding host setup, graph capture, and control updates. The separate Nsight capture confirms one fewer memset per step; its duration is not the end-to-end saving because timings of other operations also shift. Toolchain: Warp 1.20.0.dev20261028, NVRTC 13.4.92, MuJoCo 3.17.0, driver 615.71.10.

author: gugrimm
body:
## Related Issue
Closes #913 

## Description
Renewable support mechanisms are central to electricity markets, but so far we did not use or showcase ASSUMES features. This PR adds an example notebook that simulates 5 identical 1000 MW solar units, competing on the EOM. Support instruments are auctioned monthly on a pay_as_bid_contract market, settled retrospectively weekly from actual generation and realized EOM prices:
- a naive bidding strategy - no support, full price risk (reference)
- a Contract for Difference - two-sided difference payment against EOM price
- a Power Purchase Agreement - fixed strike price per MWh generated
- a fixed market premium - one-sided top-up, only paid when the EOM price is below strike
- a feed-in tariff
Full year 2019 simulation with one week per season evaluation.

While bulding the example a small bug appeared: contracts sharing the same buyer (demand / the state / ...) and same start time overwrote each other's settlement futures, because of a non-unique key. The fix is included here.
- execute_contract now builds unique reply keys ({contract}_{buyer}_{seller}_{start_time}), so contracts sharing a seller and start time no longer overwrite each other's futures. Tested in tests/test_concurrent_contract_settlement added in tests/test_policies_contracts.py

author: gildesmarais
body:
One PR to replace the open Dependabot PRs: dependencies are brought current and unused ones are removed.

## Removed
- `cross-env` and `nodemon`: no script or config references them. (`depcheck` also flags `@nuxtjs/pwa`, `@nuxtjs/style-resources`, `sass`, `sass-loader` and `jsdom`, but those are false positives: they are used through `nuxt.config.js` modules, SCSS, and Nuxt's `renderAndGetWindow`.)

## Bumped
- **ava 6.2 → 8.3 (major)**: ESM-only now, so the CommonJS test uses `require('ava').default`.
- **jsdom 25 → 30 (major)**: jsdom 27 removed `VirtualConsole#sendTo`, which Nuxt 2's `renderAndGetWindow` calls by default. The test now passes `{ virtualConsole: false }`.
- sass 1.83 → 1.107
- sass-loader 10.4 → 10.5.2. It stays on 10.x because Nuxt 2 runs on webpack 4 and sass-loader 11+ needs webpack 5.
- Lockfile refreshed, so the transitive `pbkdf2` (3.1.7), `sha.js` (2.4.12) and `cipher-base` (1.0.7) resolve to patched versions.
- **Node**: `engines.node` is now `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, and both workflows run Node 22, up from 20. ava 8 and jsdom 30 don't support Node 20, which is EOL anyway.

## Nuxt: staying on 2.18.1
We stay on Nuxt 2 for now. Nuxt 4 is a full framework migration, not a dependency bump:
- Vue 2 → 3 and Vuex → Pinia (or `useState`): `pages/index.vue` uses `mapState`.
- `@nuxtjs/pwa` has no Nuxt 3/4 version. Moving to `@vite-pwa/nuxt` means porting the workbox precache list that `nuxt.config.js` builds from `static/*.json`, and the PWA's offline behaviour would need checking by hand.
- `@nuxtjs/style-resources` would be replaced by Vite's `css.preprocessorOptions`.
- The test uses Nuxt 2's programmatic `Nuxt`/`Builder` API. It would be rewritten with `@nuxt/test-utils`.

The app is only about 440 lines, so the migration is realistic as a separate, focused PR. It's out of scope here so this PR doesn't land half a migration. Until then #504 (nuxt 4) and #437 (sass-loader 16) can't be merged as they are.

## Verification (local, Node 22.23.2)
```
rm -rf node_modules .nuxt dist
yarn install --frozen-lockfile
yarn test        # 2 tests passed
yarn build       # exit 0
yarn generate    # exit 0, dist/ generated
```
The repo uses yarn (`yarn.lock`, CI). Sass prints deprecation warnings for `lighten()` and `@import`. They aren't errors and are left for a follow-up.

Supersedes #437 #468 #472 #473 #485 #486 #496 #497 #503 #504

The last `ignore_errors` section that matches `tests.*` leaves `mypy.ini`, and so does the ratchet comment:

```diff
+[mypy-aiobotocore.*]
+ignore_missing_imports = True
+
 [mypy-tests.*]
 disable_error_code = comparison-overlap
-# Ratchet for iossifovlab/gain#2083 ...
-[mypy-tests.small.genomic_resources.*]
-ignore_errors = True
-[mypy-tests.small.genomic_resources.genomic_position_table.*]
-ignore_errors = False
-[mypy-tests.small.genomic_resources.gene_models.*]
-ignore_errors = False
```

The test changes fix types only. Two wrong annotations in `test_vcf_info_score.py` change from a list to `dict[...] | None`. The `**counted` dict in `test_position_score_get_plane.py` becomes explicit keyword arguments.

## Acceptance evidence
Run each command from `core/` of the worktree.

- `ruff check . ../scripts` prints `All checks passed!`.
- `pytest -q tests/small/genomic_resources` passes.

## Merge Danger
**Door:** two-way: the diff changes test annotations and mypy configuration only.
**Blast radius:** small: a later test file that does not type-check now fails the mypy CI job.
**Sensitive areas:** none: no secrets, auth, data or deploy files change.
**Error detection:** the mypy step of CI fails on a new type error in `tests`.

- No test compares a wrong value. No test behavior changes.
- The new `[mypy-aiobotocore.*]` section ignores missing imports for a package that the newly checked tests import.

author: mikavohl
body:
JIRA ID : AIHPBLAS-5435

## Motivation

Currently, YAML `compute_type` values can be silently converted to the wrong compute type. Only names with the `c_` prefix (e.g. `c_f32_r`) are defined as compute types, but a bare name like `f32_r` is still accepted without an error. This happens because the members of the `hipDataType` and `hipblasComputeType_t` enums are stored in the same dictionary. A bare name passed as a compute type therefore picks up its `hipDataType` value, which is then read as a compute type. For example, `f32_r` is `HIP_R_32F` = 0, and 0 as a compute type is `HIPBLAS_COMPUTE_16F`, so the bench logs `compute=f16_r`.

Other effects:
- `compute_type: f64_r` becomes `COMPUTE_16F_PEDANTIC`, `i32_r` becomes `COMPUTE_32I_PEDANTIC`, and `bf16_r` becomes 14, which is not a compute type.
- The reverse also happens: `a_type: c_f32_r` becomes `HIP_R_16F`.
- A `Known bugs` entry with `compute_type: f32_r` never matches a `c_f32_r` test, so the bug is not skipped.
- `matmul_conv3d_kernels` in `matmul_gtest.yaml` uses `compute_type: f32_r` and has been running as 16F.

On the CLI (`--compute_type f32_r`) and in the bench log, `f32_r` means `HIPBLAS_COMPUTE_32F`, so the same text means different things on the CLI and in YAML.

## Technical Details

- `hipblaslt_gentest.py`:
  - Enum members stay inside their enum class; only the classes go into the shared dictionary.
  - New `enum_value()` resolves a field's value, and any `Known bugs` value, only against that field's enum. Integers pass through unchanged. Any other name exits with the field, its enum, and the valid names.
  - Member aliases such as `{half: f16_r}` are added to every enum that has the target member.
- `hipblaslt_common.yaml`: `hipblasComputeType_t` also accepts the names the bench prints for compute types: `f16_r`, `f32_r`, `f32_f16_r`, `f32_bf16_r`, `xf32_r`, `f64_r`, `i32_r`. All but `f16_r` are also accepted by `--compute_type`. These aliases are only safe because of the scoping above; without it, the later enum would overwrite `f32_r` and every `a_type: f32_r` would become `HIP_R_16F`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: one entry under Changed, one under Resolved issues.

Behavior changes for existing YAML:
- `compute_type: f32_r`, `f64_r` and `i32_r` now give 32F, 64F and 32I.
- `compute_type: f16_r` and `half` now give 16F; previously they gave 32F.
- `compute_type: xf32_r`, `f32_f16_r` and `f32_bf16_r` previously failed with a TypeError and now work.
- A name from the wrong enum, for example `compute_type: bf16_r` or `a_type: c_f32_r`, now exits with an error instead of producing a wrong value.

## Test Plan

1. All five gtest YAMLs (`hipblaslt_gtest`, `matmul_gtest`, `smoke_gtest`, `auxiliary_gtest`, `rocroller_gtest`) and the `scripts/performance/problems` bench YAMLs.
2. Single-test bench YAMLs, through the same `--template` command line that `hipblaslt_parse_data` runs, with each compute spelling, `half`, an integer, an unknown name, and wrong-enum names for `a_type` and `compute_type`.
3. A YAML with a `Known bugs` entry using `compute_type: c_f32_r`, `f32_r`, and `bf16_r`.

## Test Result

1. Records are byte-identical to the `develop` baseline for all five gtest YAMLs (143,277 records for `hipblaslt_gtest`, 135,378 for `matmul_gtest`) and for `matmul_probset1`–`6`. `matmul_conv3d_kernels` now generates `HIPBLAS_COMPUTE_32F` without editing its YAML. `matmul_example_bench.yaml` fails the same way on `develop`, because of an undefined YAML alias unrelated to this change.
2. Every case produced the values listed under Technical Details. Unknown and wrong-enum names exit with the list of valid names.
3. The `f32_r` known-bug entry now marks the matching test `known_bug`; on `develop` it never matched. `bf16_r` exits with an error.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

author: xdoubleu
body:
Part of #2775 (first slice: the host checks; token minting, push and PR come next).

## What
After the agent says it is done, the runner checks the work on the host before reporting success:
- the branch has commits that change something (empty and net-zero histories fail);
- no commit, merges included, touches `.github/workflows/` (any case);
- none of the secrets (device token plus `JobRunner.Secrets`) appears in any commit's changes, message or author, or in the outcome text.

A failed check fails the job with `Not published: <reason>` ahead of the agent's own outcome, so the task goes to Needs you with the reason. The secret value is never repeated.

## How it stays safe
The clone belongs to the agent, so nothing runs in it. The branch is fetched (objects verified, `core.hooksPath` off) into a throwaway bare repo made from the mirror, and every check reads that copy. A rejected commit therefore never reaches the mirror that later jobs clone from. A clone whose `.git`, `objects`, `objects/info` or `refs` is not a plain directory, or that has alternates, is refused.

## Not in this PR
Secret values are passed to `git log -S` on the command line, so a same-user process can see them while it runs. Searching in Go would need the whole diff in memory; left as is.

## Manual review needed
Security-relevant code: `factory-runner/internal/runner/hostcheck.go`.

## Summary

Three fixes in one integration PR, as three thematic commits:

1. **Safety Score v10.42: premiums are penalised less than discounts.**
   - Only an open **below-peg** event can trigger the active-depeg caps (≥10% → 49, ≥25% → 25, ≥50% → 10). A premium never caps.
   - The Safety peg input counts premiums at **0.25×** (policy `pegPremiumWeight`) in three terms: off-peg time, severity, and the active penalty (both floor and cap). Spread stays below-only.
   - The public Peg Score (`computePegScore`, `/api/peg-summary`) is unchanged.
   - Side fixes: audit-excluded open events no longer feed the cap inputs; the Peg Score methodology table now says spread uses below-peg events only.
2. **Daily digest: live deviation uses the current peg reference.** USD-quoted open events were measured against the reference latched when the event opened. For gold, silver and FX pegs that sign-flipped results, so XAGM's 41-day open event was never flagged.

author: yukiemiona
body:
### Summary

Fix an issue where images returned by model tools (such as `read_image`) were dropped or stripped before reaching the Google Gemini API, and resolve API invariant violations where offloaded/degraded image placeholders could corrupt the `functionResponse` turn.

### What Changed

1. **Multimodal Tool Result Support**:
   - Extract `image` content blocks from `role: 'tool'` messages.
   - Attach resolved `inlineData` parts alongside `functionResponse` in the same user turn according to Google Gemini's multimodal function calling specification.
   - Safely append placeholder text (for offloaded or omitted images) to `responseText` inside `functionResponse.response.result` rather than creating illegal sibling text parts that trigger Gemini API 400 errors.

2. **Code Simplification & Performance**:
   - Perform a single-pass check using `.some(b => b.type === 'image')` before image resolution to avoid unnecessary array allocations on text-only tool results.
   - Cleanly handle orphaned tool results (where `id === undefined`) by degrading both text and image parts to standard user parts.

3. **Comprehensive Test Coverage**:
   - Added unit tests in `tests/adapter.spec.ts` covering:
     - Tool result image blocks converted to `inlineData` alongside `functionResponse`.
     - Appending placeholder text to `functionResponse.response.result` when tool images are offloaded.
     - Handling pure image tool results without text descriptions.
     - Graceful degradation for orphaned tool results.
   - All 187 tests passing.

body:
## Özet
Lojistik Regresyon, Rastgele Orman ve XGBoost aynı 5 katlı katmanlı CV'de karşılaştırıldı. Ağaç modelleri için ölçeklemesiz ön işleme eklendi ve yedi ablasyon varyantı (`day`, yaş grubu, log dönüşümü) ana modellere göre katman katman ölçüldü. 5. hafta raporu üreticisi ve kaptan rotasyonu (H5-H9) eklendi.

## Değişiklikler
- `src/preprocessing.py`: `build_tree_preprocessor`, LR dalına `include_day` ve `use_log` ablasyon seçenekleri (varsayılanlar değişmedi)
- `src/modeling.py`: `build_random_forest`, `build_xgboost`. Rastgele Orman, tekrar üretilebilirlik için tek iş parçacığında çalışır (çok iş parçacığında 1e-16 düzeyinde sapma vardı)
- `src/evaluate.py`: karşılaştırma tablosu, ablasyon karar kuralı (ortalama artış std'yi aşmalı ve katmanların 4/5'inde iyileşme olmalı), katman bileşimi
- `src/model_plots.py`: model karşılaştırma çubuk grafiği ve PR eğrileri
- `src/report_text.py`, `src/notebook_build.py`: H4 betik ve raporundan ortak parçalar taşındı
- `notebooks/build_model_karsilastirma.py`, `reports/hafta5_rapor.py`, `hafta5_ozet.json`, 2 grafik, notebook
- Docs: yol haritası (H5 sonucu, rotasyon), gereksinim durumları, ön işleme kararları, README (macOS için `brew install libomp`)

## Sonuçlar (hafta5_ozet.json)
| Model | PR-AUC | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|
| Lojistik Regresyon | 0,409 ± 0,011 | 0,770 ± 0,004 |
| Rastgele Orman | 0,447 ± 0,019 | 0,796 ± 0,006 |
| XGBoost | 0,453 ± 0,013 | 0,801 ± 0,002 |

XGBoost ile Rastgele Orman arasındaki fark katmanlar arası standart sapmanın altında. Ablasyonda aday çıkmadı, ön işleme varsayılanları korundu. `day` ağaç modellerinden çıkarılınca PR-AUC 0,016-0,019 düştü.

## Nasıl Test Edildi
- `pytest`: 125 test geçiyor
- H5 betiği iki kez çalıştırıldı, özet JSON birebir aynı
- H4 betiği yeniden çalıştırıldı, `hafta4_ozet.json` ve H4 rapor metni değişmedi
- Kod incelemesi bulguları düzeltildi

## Notlar
- Birleştirirken **"Create a merge commit"** seçilmeli, squash zincir branch'leri bozar.
- Rapor Bölüm 2 kutucukları taslak olarak ✓, kaptan (Mesut) teyit etmeli.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Refs #6284. This ports gauntface/agent-factory `cbb51bbcef` (#67), "repeat done --self re-emits review to the orchestrator".

## The problem
An item session that pushes review fixes and runs `af backlog done --self` again, with the same PR, changes nothing that `queueOrchChanges` can see: the status is already `review` and the PR is the same. So af never wakes the orchestrator. The skill text #6621 shipped worked around this by telling the orchestrator to poll with `orchestrate --self --stay` and check the PR itself.

## The change
- **The re-queue:** in `SetItemStatus`, an agent's done on an item that is already in review queues a `review` event itself (`backlog/service.go`). An agent can only ever send its item to review (`checkAgentReview`), so this fires only on a repeated `done --self`.
- **One event for a new PR:** a repeat with a new PR is seen by both paths, and both build the same event (`Kind: review`, the item, no message). `QueueOrchEvent`'s dedupe against events not yet sent keeps it to one.
- **The skill text:** the orchestrator section's `review` line now says to ask the item's session to run `af backlog done --self` again after it pushes, and that af then wakes you with a new review event. The polling advice is gone.

## Tests
- **From the fork:** `TestServiceRepeatDoneSelfQueuesReview` (a repeat with the same PR queues review, with no duplicates while one is pending) and `TestServiceRepeatDoneSelfDuringDelivery`.
- **New here:** `TestServiceRepeatDoneSelfWithANewPRQueuesOneReview`. A repeat with a new PR, where both paths fire, still queues exactly one event.
- **Mutations,** each run and seen to fail:
  - removing the re-queue fails both of the fork's tests;
  - giving the re-queued event a distinct message, which defeats the dedupe, fails the new-PR test and the fork's first test.
- **The usage golden:** regenerated.

Security: there is no new route, auth path or command execution.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Small improvement or alignment, with no change to how a feature works

## What changed

Agents with no photo now show the bloub plush bot (`@norbert_bodziony/bloub/plush` 0.6.1) in place of the flat drawing.

- **Moods:** the plush shows them on its face. There are no orbit rings and no glow round it. A working agent looks up while three felt dots pulse. An agent that waits shows a felt dot. A failed turn lowers the eyes and shakes "no" one time. An asleep agent closes its eyes and shows z's.
- **Hover:** when you point at a resting agent or focus it, the eyes change to a random friendly face (wink, wide eyes, curious). The eyes go back when you move away.
- **Avatar editor:** separate **Shape** (10) and **Eyes** (16) pickers, a shuffle button, and one row of 8 colours plus Automatic. No schema change: a pick searches the seed that draws that pair. If the colour is Automatic, new eyes keep the colour that shows, and it becomes the chosen colour.
- **Face changes:** a new face pops in. The picker tiles change with no animation, to keep the CPU load low.
- **Photos:** they show as a plain circle crop, as on mobile. A busy agent's photo breathes, and an asleep agent's photo is dimmed.
- **Alignment:** the plush body sits low in its box (0.14 × box size). The working line, the waiting line, the sidebar, search, agent tags in messages and the direct conversation header now correct this.
- **Performance:** when an avatar changes, an open conversation no longer builds all its agent tags again. Before, one pick built 744 chip nodes again; now it builds 0.
- **CSP:** no change. Bloub 0.6.1 tints with a `data:` URL, so `img-src` needs no `blob:`.
- **Where the flat bot stays:** the composer token and other synchronous static clones (`createStaticAvatarSvg`), the app loading screen, the marketplace script and mobile.

Surfaces: desktop renderer, `packages/ui`, `packages/brand`, `apps/auth-api` (web client and openbot.run render the plush on the client only), and i18n (13 languages). No changes to IPC contracts, migrations, mobile or `PRIVACY.md`.

- `typecheck:renderer`, `types:ratchet`, `i18n:check`, `knip:check`, `test:changed` (7 tests), Biome on the changed files. The pre-commit hook ran the type checks.
- Dev app smoke, light and dark: sidebar, conversation, working and waiting lines, agent tags, avatar editor, hover faces (6 hovers × 2 rows), and 0 CSP errors.

Left to CI: full lint, the aggregate typecheck, and the full test suites.

None. There is no change to permissions, IPC, persistence or network access. The CSP stays as it was.

author: amer-omar-bamazrou
body:
## Phase 18 R-6: dual control on bank details, only where two admins exist (DR-23)

**Decision applied:** DR-23 (D-6), decided 2026-10-27 as recommended and confirmed by the owner 2026-11-01: "Dual control only where two admins exist." H-8 (IBAN validation, the recorded change) and H-9 (the change-then-pay finding) built the rest; notification waits on B1. Scope and readings: register §11.98, written before any code; §11.99 and §11.100 record what changed after the first red and after the mutants.

### What it does
- In an organisation with **two or more usable admins** (G03's definition: an active admin membership and an active account), a **bank-detail change** is held as a pending request: a change of a supplier's IBAN, of a company bank account's IBAN, or an account becoming the default (the IBAN printed on future invoices, G30), by update or at creation. The rest of the request is written.
- **An admin who did not ask for it** approves it. The approval writes the change in the same transaction, through the owning service and its audit record, so H-9's finding sees a supplier change dated at the approval. An admin may reject; the requester may withdraw; a decision is final; a request whose stored value moved since is refused as stale.
- **Below two usable admins** nothing changes: the write applies at once, as before.

### My readings, for review (§11.98)
- **Not covered:** a new supplier's first IBAN; a new non-default account; clearing the default or deleting an account (they remove the printed details, never redirect them); employees' IBANs (outside DR-23); a bank account's `bankName` and `accountNumber`. DR-23 names IBANs, so the last is a **named gap for the owner**, not a silent default.
- The first default of a company with two admins also waits: it is a change of the printed details.
- No expiry for a pending request (none decided); no cooling-off period (alternative (b), not chosen).

### How it is enforced
- **Migration 0151 (custom, refusing pre-check):** `bank_detail_change_requests` with RLS, the company arm, and G04 keys `(organization_id, vendor_id)` and `(organization_id, bank_account_id)`. It adds `bank_accounts_org_id_unq`. The request's role gets SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE, never DELETE or TRUNCATE.
- **One definition of a usable admin:** `org_usable_admin_ids` and `org_usable_admin_count` (SECURITY DEFINER, not executable by the request's roles). The triggers read them, and so does the service through `membersRepository`. The proof pins them equal to G03's count.
- **The database is the boundary:**
  - a request is inserted only as pending, by the connection's declared actor (T1b);
  - it is decided once, by the declared actor, at `now()`;
  - an approval comes only from a usable admin who is not the requester;
  - a supplier or bank-account write that changes an IBAN or makes an account the default is refused (`bank_detail_dual_control`) unless a matching request was **approved in the same transaction**.
- **One pending request** per supplier, per account IBAN, and per company default (partial unique indexes). The index is the rule; the service does not repeat it.
- **The refusals** live once, in both languages, in `lib/dbRefusals`; the UI keys on the code.

### API and screens
- Spec first, then codegen:
  - `GET /companies/current/bank-detail-changes`;
  - `PUT /companies/current/bank-detail-changes/{id}/decision` with `{ "decision": "approve" | "reject" }`.
- The decision is a PUT because the seeded matrix gives `companies` only read, update (admin) and delete. Every POST under it is refused for every role, and **the matrix is not touched** (DR-13 is R-11's; §11.99).
- The supplier PATCH answers `VendorUpdateResult`, which adds `pendingBankDetailChanges`. The bank-account create and update answer it too; those routes are not in the spec today, and their page reads the field with the generated `BankDetailChange` type rather than widening its pinned hand-written interface.
- **Company settings:** a "Bank-detail changes" section, shown only when there is a request. It lists before → after and who asked, with Approve and Reject for admins and Withdraw for the admin who asked.
- **Bank Accounts:** "Use on invoices" and create-as-default say when the switch waits for a second admin.
- The supplier IBAN has no edit screen today; that change is API-only, as before.

### Proof
`apps/api/src/tests/phase18-r6-dr23-dual-control.test.ts`, 16 cases on sl_test.
- **Red ×2 on main**, runs 3 and 4, on the final proof shape: 13 failed and 2 passed. Runs 1 and 2 used POST routes and are kept as the route-shape record (§11.99).
- **The two cases passing on main** are the one-admin control and the inactive-admin case. The second is vacuous on main and gets its meaning from mutant D1.
- **Four cases were added after the proof commit** (§11.100): a default switch with no request, a requester's approval at the database, an approval reused from an earlier transaction, and the Arabic text on two refusals.
- **Green ×2 on the final tree, 16/16.**

### Mutants
| Set | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Service, first tree | 7 of 8 caught; S8 survived, so the duplicate checks were removed |
| Service, final tree | 7/7 caught (`mutants/second/`) |
| Database (functions and the index) | 6/6 caught (`mutants/db-run-4.log`), each restored identical by definition hash |

Three database runs are void and kept, with the reason for each (§11.100).

### Verification (local, sl_test on PostgreSQL 16.15; foreground, `--maxWorkers=2`)
- **API suite:** 349 files in 18 pieces. Piece 16 failed once: `single-currency-boundary` called the bank-account create outside a request, and an empty held list still needed one. That was a real defect, fixed in `08b1a15d`; the piece was re-run green, 20/20. The other pieces were green, with 2 usual skips.
- **Adjacent suites:** 20/20 files (G03, G04 keys, G30, H-8, H-9, the identity boundary, the FK ratchet, RLS coverage, the permission seed, the privilege map, route reachability, rate-limit budget, org seed, and more).
- **Other stages:** DB 10, ZATCA TLV 1, web 20, build: all exit 0. Typecheck exit 0, browser specs included.
- **Migration 0151:** dry run rolled back (24 statements), hash recorded in the apply's own command, applied through the gate. The catalog was read afterwards: grants, triggers, function privileges, RLS.
- **gitleaks:** CI's container on a fresh clone at `08b1a15d`, no leaks.
- **The browser spec** `phase18-r6-dr23-dual-control.spec.ts` runs in CI only (its own tenant; EN desktop and AR phone).

**Assertions changed:** none.

author: jpduchesne
body:
Closes #369.

The decision dev#369 was opened to make, recorded as an amendment to ADR-0009 in `docs/DECISIONS.md`: an installed tree is read-only to its consumers — its owner is whichever uid published it and that is a fact, not a role; a tree that writes into itself at consume time is patched so it does not, or it is not an installed tree.

The engine case that forced it turned out to be fixed upstream: Unreal's `SetupDotnet.sh` ran `chmod u+x` unconditionally through 5.6 (the css repack's `0001-setupdotnet-chmod-guard.patch`, plans#26); 5.7+ carries the same guard, so `d3mlabs/unreal-engine` `5.8.0-wine-N` needs no patch. Verified on the box today — `runner` (non-owner, in `dev`) runs `RunUBT.sh` against the operator's `jpduchesne:dev` tree, and stage run [40971188564](https://github.com/d3mlabs/cellbound-3d/actions/runs/40971188564) built Win64 from it as `runner` on 10-29. Details on the issue.

Docs only; no code, no test change. Rejected alternatives are in the amendment (dedicated owner behind a sudo seam; operator-inside-only, which `ContainerUserAligner` makes moot; a per-uid overlay, the named fallback).

author: seevee
body:
**Hold until 0.8.0 is tagged.** This touches `custom_components/`, so merging it during the rc.3 soak would mean an rc.4 and a soak restart.

Closes #373.

**Merge last of the four held PRs.** Each pair merges cleanly, but with #376 and #379 already in, `_fetch_one_feed` conflicts. #376 widened the `except`, #379 made the branch an `elif`, and this PR moves the parse into the executor. The resolution is the executor call with `except (ET.ParseError, DefusedXmlException)`. All four merged that way pass the gate together: 2,073 passed, 0 xfailed.

## Problem

CAP bodies were parsed in the executor, but each NAAD host's Atom feed was parsed on the event loop, and so was the envelope pre-filter that turns every entry's GeoRSS polygons into float rings. The issue guessed this was tolerable on x86 from a parse-only timing on a lighter feed. A Pi measurement says otherwise.

## Measured on a Raspberry Pi CM4

The real provider code (0.8.0-rc.1) was run read-only inside a production HA core container against the live feeds on 2026-11-02:

| Per host | Size | Entries | Feed parse | Envelope pre-filter |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| alertready | 6.44 MB | 316 | 294 ms | 967 ms |
| pelmorex | 6.19 MB | 236 | 247 ms | 911 ms |

That's about 2.4 s on the loop per poll, for every ECCC entry using the default two-host union. A profile puts the cost in the polygon parse: alertready alone carried 12,590 polygons and 309,528 vertices. Point-in-polygon is about a tenth of it.

## The fix

The feed parse (`_parse_feed`) and the pre-filter (`_prefilter_entries`, now a pure function) run in the executor, the way the CAP bodies already did. The CPU work is unchanged; only where it runs changes.

| Live ECCC poll, x86 laptop | Longest event-loop stall |
| :-- | --: |
| before | 893 ms |
| after | 84 ms |

A new test records which thread the parse and the pre-filter run on and fails if either runs on the loop's. One existing test, `test_heartbeats_do_not_end_a_restored_alert_the_seed_missed`, had been racing the resync backfill, which HA schedules as a background task that `async_block_till_done` doesn't wait for. It only won because the backfill used to finish inside the loop turns. It failed on the HA floor once the work moved off the loop, and it now awaits `async_refresh()` (`202b10b`): 10/10 on 2026.4.3 and 2026.10.4. Making the polygon parse itself cheaper is possible, but I've left it as a separate, optional step.

```
verify @ c31a4dc: pytest 2060 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 warning; cov 98% (floor 96); flow cov 100%; ruff check ok; ruff format ok; mypy ok; flow_walk skipped
```

author: uthree
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"uthree"} -->
_Requested by **uthree** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011S9a7PZ7dtkFAqkJLhskgA?thread=cmsg_011S9a7PZ7dtkFAqkJLhskgAHcW3rghZhTXavraeAS1Pvg)_

## What

Comments for music, the way source code has them. A comment is a position and some text, and nothing ever plays it.

**Document** (`auris_core::Comment`, `Comments` trait)
- `Track::comments` are pinned along the lane in song time.
- `MidiClip::comments` are pinned in clip time and can optionally sit on a piano-roll pitch row. Because they belong to the clip, they move, copy and split with its notes. A front trim clamps them to the new start instead of dropping them.
- Ids are unique within their holder. The new fields are serde-defaulted and skipped when empty, so no format bump is needed.

**Session**
- `CommentHost::{Track, Clip}` addresses a comment's holder.
- `add_comment`, `set_comment_text`, `move_comment` and `remove_comment` are each one undo step (`Edit::SetComment` / `MoveComment`).
- No engine rebuild happens and no note is touched.

**Window** (`ui/comments.rs`)
- A comment shows as a small tag with a pin stripe on its moment. On a track it sits at the foot of the lane, above the linter strip. In the roll it sits just above its pitch row, so the note it is about stays visible.
- Hover shows the full text in a tooltip.
- Drag moves the tag on the grid; hold the secondary key to move it freely.
- Double-click edits the text, and right-click opens Edit or Remove.
- A tag stops its press from reaching the surface under it, so pressing a tag never writes a note or starts a rubber band.
- **Add Comment Here…** is in the lane menu, the clip menu (where it pins the comment to the track) and the piano-roll menu, next to Add Note (where it pins the comment to that row).

**Agents**
- `inspect_project` returns a `comments` list in song order, with bar, beat, pitch and text.
- The new `edit_comments` tool does add, edit and remove, positioned by bar and beat. Removing a comment requires confirmation.
- The desktop selection context includes `comments_on_selection`.
- The instructions tell the model to read the comments in a passage before editing it, to follow them unless the current message says otherwise, and never to remove or rewrite a person's comments unless asked.

**A reason for linter ignore rules** (follow-up to #133)
- `LintSuppression::reason` is saved with the project. Rules are matched by rule and scope only (`same_rule`), so retyping a reason never adds a second rule.
- After choosing an ignore option, an optional "why?" sheet opens; Escape skips it.
- The ignore-rules list shows the reason under each rule, with a **Reason…** button to write or retype it. Each change is one undo step.
- `lint_project` returns `ignore_rules` along with their reasons, and its description tells agents never to undo or work around them.

## Testing
- `cargo test` for auris-core, auris-session, auris-toolbox, auris-i18n and auris-mcp: all pass. New tests cover:
  - comment ids and text cleaning, the serde round trip, undo, and how comments follow copies and splits
  - placing comments by bar and beat through the agent command
  - an ignore-rule reason annotating the rule without duplicating it, saving with the project, and undoing
- `cargo test -p auris-gpui --bins`: everything passes apart from the two Linux-only `window-close` tests, which are unrelated. New window tests:
  - add a comment from the lane menu, type it and drag it one beat
  - a roll tag sits on its row, and pressing it writes no note
  - remove a comment from its menu
  - ignoring a problem asks why, keeps the reason, and retyping the reason is one undo step
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo doc` passes with warnings denied.
- The real window was checked on Linux (weston): screenshots are in the project thread.

author: lionsr
body:
## Summary

The chapter *Ground states of gapped chains in polynomial time* had grown to one web page of about 9,000 source lines. This splits it into three consecutive chapters, keeping the order of sections:

1. **Viable sets and their trimming** (`ch:gapped_chain_algorithms`, label unchanged): approximate ground-state projectors, gluing at a cut, size and bond trimming, error reduction.
2. **Successive viable sets and a matrix product state** (`ch:gapped_chain_construction`): the sampled and Gaussian successive constructions, the final matrix product state, and product-state extension.
3. **Two-window polynomial filters and regional replacement** (`ch:gapped_chain_polynomial_filters`): the operator Schmidt rank of polynomials of a two-window family, the common middle family, Chebyshev improvement of viability, and the frustration-free regional replacement.

The only references between the three groups go from the second to the first, so the split adds no forward references. No label is renamed. The Part VIII introduction now describes all its chapters.

## Roles

`scripts/blueprint_roles.py --check` reported 41 mismatches on main from results added since the last role pass. This PR:

- makes 28 supporting results lemmas (mostly in the gapped-chain files and in the matrix-product-unitary gauging and cocycle chapters) and fixes 12 reference words;
- lists `thm:physical_dg_interval_entropy_bound` (interval entropy bound for a degenerate ground space, the interval version of ALVV Theorem 4.9) as a main theorem of `ch:aklv_entropy_approximation`, since no later result uses it and it is a headline area-law statement;
- regroups the gapped-chain entries of `blueprint/roles.json` under the three new chapter keys.

## Checks

- `python3 scripts/blueprint_roles.py --check`: OK.
- Every `\label`, `\lean`, `\uses`, `\leanok` and proof environment across `blueprint/src` is conserved against main; the only additions are the two new chapter labels. (`--verify` reports the moved tags and the new labels, as expected for a split.)
- `scripts/check_reader_facing_prose.py --base origin/main`: no violations.
- Formatted with `scripts/latexindent`.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the merged #99. This extends `scripts/dead_code.py` beyond module-level definitions and removes the three orphans the wider scan found.

### Guard coverage
- **Class methods**: non-dunder, non-decorated methods are scanned. `sideband_progress` (pygit2 `RemoteCallbacks`) and `extendMarkdown` (Python-Markdown) are allowlisted with their reason, because a foreign framework calls them.
- **`scripts/`**: module-level definitions in `scripts/*.py` are scanned too. Entry points referenced from their own `__main__` block stay live.
- **Config keys**: `DEFAULT_CONFIG` is parsed and flattened; every distinctive key must be named outside `_default_config.py`. Generic keys (`enabled`, `allow`, …) are exempt. This reports zero today.

### Removed (found by the wider scan)
- `scripts/build_rules_index.py`: `PAGE_INDEX_RE` (unused compiled regex).
- `scripts/corpus_provenance.py`: `HEX_RE` (unused).
- `scripts/gen_historical_holdout_fixtures.py`: `SYNTHETIC_DIR` (unused).

### Documentation

author: 1mentat
body:
## Summary
A test-only PR adding a hidden regression test for a data race in CutSurface's area-of-interest filter. The fix follows in #270, which will remove the tag; this split follows the tests-first rule.

`priv::set_skip_for_out_of_aoi` sets per-face skip flags in a `std::vector<bool>` from inside a `tbb::parallel_for`. `std::vector<bool>` packs flags into shared words, so concurrent writes are lost and faces outside the projected bounds survive, nondeterministically. Both `its_cut_AoI` and `cut_surface` go through this function.

## Test
`its_cut_AoI drops every face of a mesh outside the projected bounds` cuts a flat 100 x 100 grid (20000 faces), entirely outside the bounds, 50 times in one test case. It requires every result to be empty, and on failure reports the first failing run and how many faces it kept. The grid size means every face writes its flag and TBB splits the range across workers.

## Known bug (tagged)
The test is tagged `[.]` (hidden) with a `// Known bug:` comment. It fails only when TBB runs two or more workers, so a single-CPU runner would pass it on main. That rules out `[!shouldfail]`, because an unexpected pass fails the run.

Reproduce:
```
libslic3r_tests "its_cut_AoI drops every face of a mesh outside the projected bounds"
```

Measured in the container (5 CPUs), 10 invocations each:

| Build | Default threads | Pinned to one CPU (`taskset -c 0`) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 10/10 failed (first failure at run 1, 17 faces kept) | 0/10 failed |
| with the #270 fix | 0/10 failed | 0/10 failed |

## Verification (container m119, Linux)
- Explicitly running the hidden test on main: 10 of 10 failed.
- `libslic3r_tests "[CutSurface]~[.]"`: all 82 assertions in 12 test cases pass.
- `libslic3r_tests` (default, hidden test skipped): 2117 cases, 2092 passed, 5 skipped, 20 failed as expected. Same counts with `--order rand --rng-seed 7`.
- `fff_print_tests`: 383 cases, all passed.
- `sla_print_tests`: 21 cases, all passed.
- `filament_group_tests`: 3 cases, all passed.
- `libnest2d_tests`: 21 cases, all passed.

author: vriesdemichael
body:
Closes #132.

The site sends people to the repository, and the README was written for whoever builds it. It now opens with what this is, a link to the site, and a clip of one setting changing the diagram.

**The clip.** An attacker has copied the code, from an app with no secret, and gets the tokens. "Protect against a stolen code" turns on, and the same arrow says "Refused: they have no verifier". Both are real answers: `attack-public` got tokens and `attack-public-pkce` got `400 invalid_grant`. `pnpm build`, then `pnpm clip`, makes it again, with nothing to install. It's an animated PNG of about 2 MB per theme, with a still for anyone who asks for reduced motion. GitHub picked the right one of the four in each theme and motion setting, on this branch.

**Also on the page:**
- What it does, and what it is not, including a line someone looked for: it is not a library.
- The recordings: where they are, how they are made and how they are checked, each under its own heading, which keeps the promise of the home screen's link.
- Two short issue forms, and search's "you can suggest this one" opens the first. It doesn't carry over what was typed, because search sends nothing anywhere.
- The description and topics, already set on the repository.

**Your call, on the live page:** how it says who builds this. The issue asked for one plain line, and it became a short section, "How far to trust it", near the top:
- "An AI agent, Claude, writes the explanations, the words on the diagram and the code here. The maintainer decides what it should be and judges it once it is live."
- It goes on to say that a test checks a phrase is in the cited RFC section, "not that the sentence is right. So check what you will rely on against the specs it links to."

Both fresh readers stopped on this, on a security topic with no stars yet. The first found it buried under the contributor sections, and the second asked who checked the words. That's the honest answer, and it's blunter than you may want, so overrule it if you like.

**A small change to the site:** the home screen's "you can run yourself" now opens that page. Nothing in simple mode led to it.

**Not fixed, for you to weigh:**
- Search finds nothing for "docker" or "run it yourself". A search result can only be a state of the one screen (ADR-003), so I didn't add the page to it.
- The state in the picture has "On a server" selected with "Client type: Public" as a small chip, which both readers stumbled on. It's a valid combination and the sentence under the picture now says "an app that has no secret", but the screen could say it better.

**Yours to do:** no API sets the social preview image, so it's a manual upload. How is on the issue.

**A limit:** "without scrolling" can't be met by the README. GitHub draws the file list first, so only the sidebar shows without scrolling. That's why the description now says the most.

**A real bug the audit found, and it was mine from #131.** The app in the page never looked at its ID token, though the step says it does and the recorder promises that a success means it looked. It now checks issuer, audience, expiry and nonce in the page, and leaves out the signature, as the step says the spec allows. Breaking the nonce check on purpose stopped the run. `browser-app` is recorded again.

**The audit also found overstatements, now corrected,** all in words I had just written:
- "Every request and answer... from a real Keycloak": some are the demo app and API, and the screen says so.
- Both-way checks and the click-through's full comparison: both are only that strict on the authorization code flow.
- "A test holds it to the RFC": it checks that a chosen phrase is in the cited section.
- "Someone copied the code and gets the tokens": only with an app that has no secret. A reader tried it on a server app and got "Refused: they have no secret".

**A small fix the clip showed:** a choice in the settings that wraps now carries on under its own words, not under the button. That changes 74 screenshots, because every choice with a radio button moved slightly. I read two of them.

**Tried from a clean clone, in a fresh container of CI's image, following the README:**
- `corepack enable pnpm`, `pnpm install` and `pnpm verify` passed.
- `pnpm dev` printed its address, and a real browser opened three pages there with no errors.
- Storybook's smoke test passed.
- That image runs Node 24, not the 22.20 in `.node-version`. So I also ran `pnpm dev`, Storybook's smoke test and the browser tests in this checkout on Windows with 22.20, and they pass, though that isn't a clean clone.

**Tried from a clean clone on this machine, because it needs Docker:** `pnpm record --check` said what the screen says still holds, and `pnpm record` wrote every recording again. The unit tests pass on what it wrote, run in the container, because that folder is too deep for Windows to run them there.

**Slips:**
- I told the fresh reader to follow the README, whose `corepack enable` replaced the `pnpm` launchers in your global Node folder and added `yarn` ones. The README no longer tells anyone to run it blindly. Your folder is still changed.
- One commit here was pushed in the same command as a failing test of the README. The next commit fixes it.

author: suica
body:
A station started outside an interactive shell can miss a runtime installed through a version manager or a custom shell configuration. For example, it can report Codex as missing and offer to install another copy even though the user's shell can already run it.

On Unix, when the command is absent from the station's PATH, look for it on the user's interactive or login shell PATH. Resolve directory links while the shell is alive, so temporary links such as fnm's remain usable. The lookup is time-bounded, caches concurrent reads briefly and imports only the resulting PATH. Commands already on the station's PATH keep priority.

Use the same lookup for software checks, account and machine logins, runtime probes, updates and agent runners. A sign-in cancelled or replaced during the lookup does not start afterward. Terminal-wrapped sign-ins look up the actual program rather than the terminal wrapper.

Validation:
- [GitHub-hosted station checks](https://github.com/suica/still.fail/actions/runs/41574848846) on the code at `2b511b96`: TypeScript check passed; 88 tests passed and 5 platform-specific tests were skipped on Linux. The tests include a real Bash startup file, temporary directory links, bounded shell lookup, sign-in replacement, a terminal-wrapped login, updates and the runner.
- The generic shell lookup was previously checked against the affected coder-b environment, where it found the installed Codex and reported its version. The earlier fnm-specific version also completed an app-server handshake there through the station runner.
