author: wangjohn
body:
## Problem

Since #755, a confirmed `backfill --harness muse` batch skips an entry when its final read refuses it, and prints "entry N skipped: reason". The skip was never saved, though. The preview only reads startup records, so the next preview selected the same session again, and a later run confirmed a batch that just skipped it again.

## Behavior

- When the batch skips an entry, it now writes the skip to its batch file under the new optional member `native_import_skipped`. Each record holds the native ID, the selected binding digest, the reason it printed and the `cli.Version` that refused it. `AddNativeImportSkip` replaces an earlier record for the same entry. No new store is added.
- The next preview gathers skips from every saved batch. If a candidate's binding digest still matches the skip and the version is the same, the preview lists it as `refused` with the reason the batch printed, so `--yes` confirms no new batch. The binding digest covers the whole-file checkpoint, so any change to the file selects the session again. So does a different agent-archive version, which means an upgrade that supports the record will import it.
- Resuming an interrupted batch works as before.
- Updated the help text, `docs/reference/cli.md`, `docs/guides/backfill.md`, CHANGELOG (Fixed) and `dev/maintainers/versions.md`.

**Compatibility:** the batch file is a closed object when it carries `native_import`. Older binaries reject the new member rather than misread it, so after a downgrade, a batch that recorded a skip is unreadable until you upgrade again. Batches with no skips are written exactly as before, and older batches still read normally. No filter, adapter, parser or schema version changes; nothing is uploaded.

## Validation

- New test `TestBackfillNativeImportPreviewLeavesOutAnEntryABatchSkippedUntilItChanges`: imports a batch with a refused entry, previews again, and asserts the entry is refused with the recorded reason and that `--yes` creates no second batch. It then rewrites the recorded version and asserts the entry is selected; then restores it, changes the file, and asserts it is selected again. It fails with the preview check disabled.
- `go test -race -short -count=1 -timeout 40m ./internal/archive ./internal/backfill ./internal/cli`: archive and backfill pass. In cli, `TestHelpDescribesEveryFlag` failed on a help line over 100 columns, which a follow-up commit fixed. `TestRecoveryReviewMakesOneDecisionForAllKeysAtExactCwd/skip` failed under the full load. Both pass on a rerun at the final head; the recovery test is a Codex recovery test this change doesn't touch.
- `go vet`, `golangci-lint run --disable=revive` (changed packages), revive `--new-from-merge-base=origin/main`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Levenshtein `verify pre-merge`: **did not complete locally.** The container was killed with exit 137 (out of memory) twice, in go-vuln and then in levenshtein-lint, while other sessions were building on this machine. A native `levenshtein-lint` run with the container's check flags (GOOS=linux) found nothing in the changed packages. CI's Levenshtein job has to confirm the rest.

## Motivation

`RustServer.gather_server_endpoints` publishes each attention-DP listener at the bound host, or, when the bind address is unspecified (`""`, `0.0.0.0`, `::`), at the address the node's interfaces answer on. That choice was inlined in the collective, so a deployment whose service discovery publishes a different one of the node's addresses (for example a container that is reachable from other nodes only through an address assigned by its orchestrator) had no way to advertise that address short of replacing the whole gather.

- Move the host choice into a new `RustServer._advertised_host()` classmethod (a classmethod because the gather runs before any server instance exists) and have `gather_server_endpoints` call it. A subclass can override the hook to advertise another address.
- No behaviour change: the default is still the bound host, else `get_local_ip_auto(fallback="127.0.0.1")`; the IPv4-bind/IPv6-address error still reads the bind host; the multi-node loopback warning is unchanged.

author: doriancollier
body:
## What happens

A new chat was refused with "Maximum session limit reached (50)" while only 8 to 16 chats were running. The server keeps one record per chat, idle records live 30 minutes, and a busy hour of room turns, spin-offs and beats filled the 50 slots. Spin-off starts then failed silently.

## Fix (DOR-3682)

- At the cap, a new chat reclaims the least recently used **idle** record instead of being refused. The reclaim is synchronous with the insert, so two starts at once cannot overfill or drop a live record.
- A record is never reclaimed while it holds work: an open or booting turn, a parked question, a session lock, an in-progress turn or pending interaction on its projector, an open sign-in card, or background work on its pump. Every alias of a record is checked and retired together, and its process and pump are released the same way the idle sweep releases them.
- Only when all 50 are live is a chat refused, with a plain message: "All 50 chats are busy. Wait for one to finish, then try again." The turn's error event carries code `session_capacity_reached`, and `running_chats` gains a `capacity` block (`limit`, `records`, `live`, `available`, `message`).
- A reclaimed chat resumes with its durable settings and transcript.
- Docs (`docs/concepts/sessions.mdx`, OpenAPI) and a changelog fragment included.

## Tests

By path, 6 files, 126 pass: `session-store-capacity.test.ts` (QA's 4 cases), `session-eviction-reaps-pump.test.ts`, `running-chats.test.ts` (server and shared), `guard-turn-errors.test.ts`, `session-tools.test.ts`.

Proven to bite: with the old refusal restored, 7 of 8 capacity tests fail; with the busy check disabled, the open, parked, all-live and protects-work cases fail. Server and shared typecheck, lint (0 errors), `check:max-lines` and the OpenAPI regen are clean.

Security: light review (runtime change).

author: nathanjgaul-agile
body:
**Merge this PR with a MERGE COMMIT (never squash): a squash drops the restored upstream history again.**

## Intent

Restore upstream's commit history in the fork's main so future syncs merge cleanly.

- The previous sync (#9) was squash-merged, so `upstream/main` was not an ancestor of the fork's main and every sync re-conflicted on the same files.
- This branch records the already-merged upstream commit (`c61646ff`) with a history-only `-s ours` merge, then merges the newer `upstream/main` normally.
- The fork's own changes are kept; the tree is the fork's main plus only the new upstream changes.

## What changes in the tree

`git diff origin/main HEAD` touches 16 files, all from the 12 upstream commits after `c61646ff` (crew-state run attribution, remote steering and `--resolve-key` handling, local second mate respawn, piped stdin in timed commands, wake-drain and secondmate-liveness fixes, plus their tests and docs).
One real conflict, in the header comment of `bin/fm-crew-state.sh`, kept both the fork's team-review paragraph and upstream's run-attribution paragraph.

<details>
<summary>How to test this</summary>

Get the code:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nathanjgaul-agile/firstmate.git && cd firstmate
git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:pr<n> && git checkout pr<n>
git remote add upstream https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git && git fetch upstream
```

Prerequisites: bash, git, tmux, jq, shellcheck (as the repo's tests already need).

Prove the ancestry is restored (both must print `ok`):

```bash
git merge-base --is-ancestor upstream/main HEAD && echo ok
git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD && echo ok
```

Prove only new upstream changes arrive:

```bash
git diff --stat origin/main HEAD
git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD | grep -vxFf <(git diff --name-only c61646ff upstream/main)   # prints nothing
```

Run the tests for the touched scripts (each should exit 0):

```bash
for t in fm-classify-corr-token fm-crew-state fm-inactive-reconcile fm-secondmate-liveness fm-send-inbox fm-send-remote-delivery fm-send-resolve-key fm-timeout-lib fm-wake-drain-open-decisions fm-wake-drain-outcome-backstop fm-wake-drain-unread-status; do bash tests/$t.test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "$t $?"; done
```

Negative check: before merging, `git merge upstream/main` on the current fork main conflicts in the same files as before; after merging this PR with a merge commit it is already up to date.

Known gap: `bin/fm-lint.sh` and the full `fm-test-run` need actionlint and ruby, which were not available on the machine used here.

body:
## User impact
A retry previously cleared `sessionFinals` and disabled complete-session copy before microphone permission or the selected STT provider had started. If the retry failed, the previous confirmed conversation could no longer be reviewed or copied.

## Change
- Defer the new transcript boundary until `sttProvider.start()` completes and the foreground session remains current.
- Stage early partial/final callbacks during startup; replay in order after success, discard them if the attempt fails/cancels.
- Keep prior finalized captions and full-session copy available during pending permission/token/socket startup, and retain the prior visible final on failed startup.
- Extend synthetic Chromium E2E with successful first caption, rejected retry, pending retry cancellation and successful fresh restart. No physical mic, cloud audio or playback.
- Synchronize cache-busted web assets/build ID.

## Safety / verification
No changes to Gemini model, MN4 broker, capture gain, audio DSP, Bluetooth routing, output volume or hearing-output permissions. M04 acoustic and ear SPL gates remain BLOCKED. Require CI and Chromium E2E before merge.

body:
> ⚠️ **Draft PR이에요.** V006은 `ops.alerts`(V005, #31)를 참조해서 머지 순서(V004_1 → V004_2 → V004_3 → V005 → V005_1 → **V006** → V008)상 V005가 develop에 들어간 뒤에 머지해요. 그 전까지 CI의 `ApplicationContextTest`·DB 테스트는 **실패가 예상**돼요(Flyway가 `ops.alerts`를 못 찾음). 리뷰는 지금 먼저 받고 싶어요. ## 🔗 Jira - [SCRUM-48](https://dajaba.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-48) — V006 cases 마이그레이션 + Case JPA 매핑 - WBS 2.9.1 `AttachDraftToCase` (채영님 str 작업 선행 조건) 포함 — 3주차 리뷰 "할 일 3"대로 `findForUpdate`·버전만 올리는 기능까지 한 PR에
## ⭐ Key Changes 1. **V006** `cases`·`case_history`·`case_summaries`·`case_no_seq` - 상태 9개(REPORTED 포함) CHECK. 상태와 칸을 같이 묶는 CHECK: 반려 코드는 REJECTED일 때만·반드시 / 종결 사유는 CLOSED일 때만·반드시 / 담당자는 OPEN에만 없음 / 초안은 OPEN·REVIEWING엔 없고 DRAFTED~REJECTED엔 반드시 - `alert_id` UNIQUE(경보당 케이스 1개), NOTE는 같은 `case_version_before`에 한 번만, 이력 사유 코드는 REJECT·CLOSE에만 맞는 값 - `app_backend`: `cases` DELETE 회수, `case_history`·`case_summaries` UPDATE·DELETE 회수 - `current_draft_id` FK는 V008(#28)이 검 — #28의 `cases_current_draft_fk`와 칸 이름·타입 맞춤 2. **`Case` JPA 매핑** (3주차 리뷰 질문 2 반영) - `BaseEntity` + `@Version`, `final` 제거 + `protected Case() {}`, CASES 명세 §8.1대로 `account_key`·`entity_id` 추가(`Case.open` 시그니처 변경) - **이력 컬렉션을 엔티티에서 뺌**: 업무 메서드가 만든 이력은 `getPendingHistories()`에 쌓이고, 유스케이스가 `save(c)` 뒤 `histories.saveAll(c.takePendingHistories())` - 재배정 가능 상태를 `CaseStatus.isReassignable()`로(전이표와 한곳). 재배정 거부 메시지 "OPEN → OPEN" → 동작 이름(`notAllowedIn`) - JPQL에서 `CASE`가 예약어라 엔티티 이름은 `InvestigationCase` 3. **str에 주는 cases 기능** (둘 다 `Propagation.MANDATORY` — str 트랜잭션 안에서만) - `CaseRepository.findForUpdate(id)`: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` - `AttachDraftToCase.execute(caseId, draftId, expectedVersion)`: 404 `CASE_NOT_FOUND` → 409 `CONCURRENT_UPDATE` → 403 `NOT_ASSIGNEE` → 409 `INVALID_CASE_TRANSITION`. 허용: ESCALATED, DRAFTED(재생성), REJECTED+NEED_REVISION(반려 코드 지움) - `BumpCaseVersion.execute(caseId, expectedVersion)`: 상태·이력 그대로 `version`만 +1. 수정본 저장처럼 초안 행만 바뀌는 작업에서 불러 동시 승인 요청과 부딪히게(NFR-APR-02, 미결 20) - `CaseNotFoundException`(404), `NotAssigneeException`(403, `ForbiddenException` 상속 — SCRUM-67)
## ✅ 확인 방법 - 실행 환경: Linux, Java 17, Docker 29 + Testcontainers PostgreSQL 16. **V005(#31 `feat/SCRUM-72`)의 마이그레이션 파일을 로컬에만 복사해서**(커밋 안 함) 실행 - `./gradlew test` → **289개 통과, 1 skipped** (`ArchitectureTest` pass, `ApplicationContextTest` pass) - 새 테스트 - `CaseSchemaDbTest` (12): 매핑 저장·이력 분리·낙관적 락, CHECK·UNIQUE(SQLSTATE 23514/23505), `app_backend` 권한(42501), 시퀀스 - `AttachDraftToCaseDbTest` (15): 정상 3(ESCALATED·재생성·보완 반려) / 실패 7(REVIEWING·NOT_REPORTABLE·담당 아님·version·404·트랜잭션 밖·롤백) / **동시 1**(같은 케이스 두 요청 → 뒤 요청이 잠금 대기 후 409) / `BumpCaseVersion` 4 - `CaseTest`·`CaseStatusTest`: 새 시그니처 + 재배정 메시지·이력 꺼내기·`isReassignable` 테스트 - Docker 29를 쓰면 Testcontainers가 `Could not find a valid Docker environment`로 실패할 수 있어요 → `~/.docker-java.properties`에 `api.version=1.44` 한 줄 - 변경: main 15파일 +482 / test 4파일 +804 / docs 4파일
## 👪 To Reviewers - **400줄 넘어요(main +482).** 리뷰 "할 일 3"이 V006 매핑 + `AttachDraftToCase` + `findForUpdate` + 버전 올리기를 한 PR로 하자고 해서 묶었어요. 커밋 3개로 나뉘어 있어서 커밋별로 보시면 편해요(V006·매핑 → CHECK 수정 → str용 기능). - **테스트로 찾은 버그 하나:** 이력 사유 코드 CHECK를 OR로 묶었더니 `reason_code`가 NULL이면 결과가 NULL이 돼서 **CHECK를 통과**했어요. `case` 식으로 바꿨어요(커밋 2). - **`BumpCaseVersion`이 `PESSIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT`인 이유:** `findForUpdate`로 이미 `FOR UPDATE` 잠금을 쥔 행이라 `OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT`는 Hibernate가 "더 약한 잠금"으로 보고 무시해요(테스트로 확인). 바로 UPDATE하지만 트랜잭션이 롤백되면 같이 되돌아가요. - **`case_history`는 `CreatedOnlyEntity`를 상속하지 않았어요.** `created_by`가 로그인한 사람이 아니라 업무상 행위자(승인자, 생성 배치는 SYSTEM)라서 업무 메서드가 받은 값을 넣어요. `03_shared.md`에 한 줄 적었어요. 의견 주세요. - **담당자 검사는 application에** 뒀어요(`AttachDraftToCase`). 리뷰 체크리스트 5번(`assertAssignedTo` 위치)은 이 방향으로 확정하자고 제안해요. - **안 한 것:** `case_history.action` CHECK의 `REPORT`(모의 제출 이력 이름이 API 12-2에서 정해짐 — 그때 ALTER), `CaseStatus.allows(CaseAction)` 전체 통합(메모 편집 상태가 생기는 API-05 때), `case_summaries` 엔티티(API-12 때). - 채영님: `AttachDraftToCase`·`BumpCaseVersion`만 부르시면 돼요. `expectedVersion`은 AI 호출 전에 읽은 `cases.version`(재생성·수정본이면 요청의 `case_version`)이에요.
## 📎 참조한 문서 · 규칙 - CASES API·도메인 설계 명세 v0.7 §2(상태 9개·전이 표), §6.2(str 공개 기능), §8.1(저장 구조), §8.3(동시성) - 3주차 설계·코드 리뷰(11/2) 질문 2, PR별 리뷰 › 지윤(V006 체크리스트), 할 일 3 - `docs/05_flyway.md` §1·§3, `docs/01_code_rules.md` 원칙 2·3, `docs/03_shared.md` §2(예외 → HTTP), SCRUM-67 `ForbiddenException` - #28 V008 `cases_current_draft_fk`, #31 V005 `ops.alerts`

author: ralph
body:
Investigates #223, "Audio key error: 1" on Premium while the official app plays the same track. The full write-up is in `plans/open/audio-key-refused.md`.

## Findings

Measured on 2026-11-02 on Ralph's account (DE, Premium), with Debug diagnostics added here, and in the web player.

- **Not relinking.** In DE, `spotify:track:41FNZsY7w7KaTQ2bjxdR6w` has four files of its own, no restriction and no alternative. These are the reporter's file ids. The web player plays the exact id, with `linked_from_uri: null`. So does the Full Moon Edition's MOON MUSiC, `4mEWgqYOEiygF1mzEn901R`.
- **The keys are given here.** Three Debug runs got every key and played. One of them was Ralph's own attempt to reproduce the failure. On a known relinked pair (The Letter), a key came back under the original's gid, the substitute's and an all-zero gid. Whether these are the same key was not checked.
- **The web player uses another key path.** It plays MP4 files decrypted through Widevine and never asks the accesspoint for a key. So official clients playing a track tells us nothing about accesspoint keys.
- **The refusal goes with the account, as in librespot#1649.** Some accounts are refused every key by librespot and go-librespot too, and back-off doesn't help them. Older accounts get passing storms, which a 3/5/10 s back-off stops (librespot#1844).

No client-side change makes a persistently refused account play. That would take getting around DRM, or Spotify's Soloist SDK.

## Changes

- `d3b5e2e` **Debug diagnostics:**
  - The track's metadata in detail.

author: olivertgwalton
body:
Stacked on the path-ids PR; review that first.

## What and why

A JSON handler read its body, answered its error and wrote its reply by hand, and its route named the body and reply types again beside it. `a.handles(route, fn)`, a generic method (Go 1.27), takes `fn(r, req Req) (Resp, error)`: it reads the body into `Req` unless `Req` is `none`, answers the error through `answered`, writes the route's status with `Resp` as JSON unless `Resp` is `none`, and fills the route's `body` and `reply` from the types. `notFoundAs` replaces `answeredAs` for a handler that returns its error.

The playlists are its first routes, all nine: `playlists.go` goes from 303 to 225 lines. The remaining resources follow in the next PR.

## How it was verified

- `go test ./internal/httpapi/` and `golangci-lint run` pass.
- The generated OpenAPI document is byte-identical before and after (219,843 bytes): the adapter fills each route's description exactly as the hand-written fields did.

## Checklist

- [x] It needs to exist now: no code for a future need, no knob nobody turns, no interface with one implementation.
- [x] It is not already here: the repo and the standard library were searched, and nothing now does the same job twice.
- [x] The shape is idiomatic: concrete returns, consumer-side interfaces, ctx first, enums for modes.
- [x] Each error is handled once: handled or returned, wrapped only where the words help.
- [x] Every goroutine has an owner and a stop; tests pass under `-race`.
- [ ] A test fails without this change, and it tests behaviour a client or operator would notice, not the code restated. *A refactor: the playlist tests pin behaviour, and the description is unchanged.*
- [x] It is one concern and small; refactors are in their own PR.
- [x] Comments only where something is surprising; every `//nolint` names its linter and says why.
- [x] Any new dependency is justified in this description. *None.*
- [x] Nothing here needs a later PR to undo or complete it.

## Out of scope

Handlers that stream, serve files, redirect, upgrade to a websocket or answer more than one success status keep their `http.HandlerFunc` shape; the adapter is for JSON in and out alone.

author: jomilu93
body:
## What this does

**Everything personal is now encrypted before it's stored.** That covers names, emails, account names and last-4 digits, balances, transaction descriptions and amounts, notes, tags, categories, rules, goals, budgets, income, bank tokens and the new activity log.
- It uses AES-256: AES-256-GCM in general, and AES-256-SIV for the few fields the app looks up by exact value (sign-in email, category name, re-import checks).
- The key lives only in Render (`ADULTING_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), never in the database or in git.
- Someone with a copy of the database or a backup sees only scrambled text.
- Dates, ids and kinds stay readable, so the database can still pull up a month of transactions.

**Security hardening**
- **Recent activity** (More tab): sign-ins with the device, first sign-ins, imports, and bank connections and disconnections.
- **Website:**
  - strict security headers (Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, no framing)
  - session cookies that page scripts can't read
  - sign in again every 30 days
  - attempt limits on sign-in codes, sign-in emails and the household password
  - changes must come from the site itself (blocks cross-site requests)
  - API responses never cached
- **Backend:** database connections must use TLS outside dev, and the API docs pages are hidden in production.
- **CI:** secret scanning (gitleaks), known-vulnerability checks (pip-audit, npm audit), and weekly Dependabot updates.
- **Guard test:** a test fails if a new column could hold personal data unencrypted.

**Written policies** in `docs/policies/`:
- a compliance assessment: what applies today, what would apply if Adulting is opened to others, how Plaid's Developer Policy is met, and the gaps in priority order
- information security
- privacy (data inventory and service providers)
- incident response
- AI and data

Every commitment is labeled In place, Partly or Planned. `SECURITY.md` has the short version, including how to change the key and what to do if something leaks.

## What happens on deploy

- **Migration 0004 encrypts your existing data in place.** It also moves Plaid tokens from the old Fernet format to the new one. Afterwards the tables are rewritten, so no readable copies stay on disk. The log says "Encrypted your existing data."
- **Migration 0005 adds the activity table,** with row-level security.
- **Every deploy now checks that the key can read the stored data.** If it can't, the deploy stops and the previous version keeps running.
- **Changing the key:** `ADULTING_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS` lets you switch to a new key with no downtime (steps in `SECURITY.md`).

## Before / after merging

1. **Save `ADULTING_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in your password manager** (Render → `adulting-api` → Environment). Without it the data can't be read.
2. Work through `docs/DEPLOY.md` §6:
   - turn on 2-step verification for Render, Supabase, GitHub, Plaid and both email accounts
   - in Supabase, turn on "Enforce SSL" and set sign-in codes to expire after 15 minutes
   - protect the `main` branch
   - fill in the security lead and the incident contacts in `docs/policies/`

## Testing

- 164 backend tests pass on SQLite and Postgres. New ones cover the encryption format, tamper detection, key changes, the deploy key check, TLS, the activity log, the migration (up and down) and the encryption guard.
- I upgraded databases filled by `main`'s code with the new code:
  - every number matched before and after (monthly totals, goals, budgets, balances, the Plaid token)
  - a `pg_dump` contained zero readable names or merchants, and after the rewrite no Postgres data file did either
  - `alembic check` reports no changes on Postgres or SQLite
- A browser run of the full flow on a production build (household setup, imports, accounts, goals, budgets, overview, categories, More) passed with no console errors under the new headers.
- With curl: cross-site POSTs are blocked (403), and the password lockout starts after 10 wrong tries (429).
- **Not tested:**
  - gitleaks: I couldn't download it to run locally, so the first CI run is its first test
  - the 30-day re-sign-in and code limits against the real Supabase project
  - the migration against Supabase itself (the steps it uses work on local Postgres)

author: albertogonzalezolmos
body:
Real bug, found while reproducing a user report that the catalogue looked empty.

## Symptom
A browser holding an **expired or revoked token** — i.e. every user after a session expiry, and every user after a database reset — logged:

```
Uncaught (in promise) Error: Sessionen er udløbet — log ind igen.
```

The login screen did eventually render, but the rejection was uncaught: the browser gate classifies `Uncaught` as a hard failure, and the in-flight catalogue load was aborted rather than ended cleanly, which is what makes the app *look* empty.

## Cause
`api()`'s 401 branch clears the token, dispatches `hcrm-session-expired`, redirects to `#/login` and then throws — deliberately, to stop the caller's continuation. A boot-time caller (the initial items load) has nowhere to catch that, so it surfaced as an unhandled rejection.

## Fix
- The thrown error carries `sessionExpired: true`; a narrow `unhandledrejection` guard calls `preventDefault()` **only** for that flag. Anything else still surfaces, so the console gate keeps its meaning — this is not a blanket swallow.
- The boot/route loads that can hit a 401 now end cleanly instead of leaving a half-rendered view.
- Tests: the 401 branch marks the error and still redirects/clears; the guard suppresses exactly that flag and not an ordinary rejection; an ordinary 500 still propagates.

## Verified in a real browser
Against a copy of the live database, with a bogus token in `localStorage` and `/#/catalogue` as the target: **zero console records**, login screen rendered. Before the fix, the same run produced the uncaught rejection above.

## Gate
`uv run pytest -q` → **1047 passed** · `node --test tests/js/*.test.mjs` → **98 passed** · `scripts/i18n_check.py` → 0/0 · `build_i18n --check` clean · `ui_check --self-host` → 4 targets green.

## Summary by Sourcery

Handle expired-session control flow cleanly so authentication teardown reaches the login screen without triggering false browser failures.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent session-expiry redirects from producing uncaught promise rejections that make the catalogue appear empty.
- Ensure boot and account-loading flows stop cleanly after session teardown while preserving propagation of genuine failures.

Enhancements:
- Add narrowly scoped handling for session-expiry control-flow signals without suppressing ordinary rejected promises.

Tests:
- Add coverage for expired-session signalling, redirect and cleanup behavior, selective rejection suppression, and propagation of ordinary errors.

body:
Fixes found while testing #317 on every target, and from playing the 26.3 Fabric build.

- **Easter eggs 9 and 19: drawn where they stand.** `GameFire` loads its block display's saved data, which puts its last position at the world's origin, then moves it with `setPos` only. A block display never ticks, so every frame drew it somewhere between (0, 0, 0) and its spot: it leapt about. It now sets its last position too (`setOldPosAndRot`). The `eggs2` scenario checks it for 9 and 19 (`Egg19.standsStill`), and failed without the fix: "ee9's campfire drawn moving from (0.0, 0.0, 0.0) to (9022.0, -60.0, -182.0)".
- **Easter egg 11 reworked, as asked in play.** Once seen through the player's spyglass, it is gone as soon as it is no longer looked at: the spyglass lowered, or turned away from it for more than 5 ticks. While looked at, it never moves. It scopes the player for 3 to 8 s, lowers its spyglass for 1.5 to 5 s, and raises it again, at random. The walk-off is gone. `Egg11` checks all of it.
- **Easter egg 15's held copies are ticked every tick.** `MobMemory.tick` looks at a still, settled copy only once in sixteen ticks, and `MobMotion.held()` never clears `settled`. So a far herd caught standing still turned in jerks: a head still 93 degrees off after 35 ticks in the 1.21.8 `eggs2` run. The skip now leaves out `Herd.holds(...)` copies, as the hidden-freeze check above it already does. One line in CLAUDE.md's still-mobs entry says so.
- **Changelog:** `## Unreleased` → `### Client` had `#### Fixed` / `#### Corrections` twice, in both files. Merged into one. `changelog-check.js` passes.

No changelog entry for the easter eggs, as for every easter egg.

Tests:
- `./gradlew :1.21.11:build` passes, unit tests included.
- `stillmobs` passes on 1.21.11.
- `eggs2` passes on 26.3 for easter eggs 9, 11 and 19 (`LH_EGGS=9,11,19`), and for easter egg 15 on 1.21.11 and 1.21.8.
- The jerky turn of easter egg 15 could not be made to happen on demand, since it needs a copy settled at the moment the herd is held.

author: pedroboy975
body:
## O problema

No notebook, depois do PR nº 11, "esperei alguns segundos mas não houve bipe nenhum".

O `_play_beep` do Windows chamava `winsound.PlaySound(wav, SND_MEMORY | SND_ASYNC | SND_NODEFAULT)`. O `winsound` do CPython recusa essa combinação: ele não toca uma imagem WAV da memória de forma assíncrona e levanta `RuntimeError("Cannot play asynchronously from memory")` ([PC/winsound.c](https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/python/cpython/+/f03c5148cfc6873df855bd0edca2940f9a5d8fd5/PC/winsound.c)). O `except` engolia o erro e só registrava no log de depuração. Resultado: **nenhum bipe tocava no Windows**, nem o de início nem o de fim, nem antes nem depois do PR nº 11.

## A correção

- Cada bipe toca de forma síncrona (`SND_MEMORY | SND_NODEFAULT`) numa thread própria (`jarvis-beep`), então quem chama continua sem travar.
- Erros de reprodução continuam só no log de depuração.
- `dictation.spec.md` documenta a regra do `winsound`.

## Testes
- Novo `tests/test_windows_beep.py` (3 testes) com um `winsound` falso que reproduz a recusa do CPython: os dois bipes chegam ao `PlaySound` sem `SND_ASYNC`, numa thread própria, e um erro de áudio não escapa. Os testes dos dois bipes falham no código anterior e passam com a correção.
- Suíte completa: as mesmas 76 falhas e 242 erros pré-existentes, nenhuma nova; 5723 passam.

author: ghostofgoes
body:
# feat(sel): discover RTAC engineering access tunnels from RTAC configuration

## Description

tl;dr: Find RTAC access points, access point routers and SEL servers in exports and the database as engineering access paths.

**I20 (RTAC discovery half): "communicating to relays via a RTAC engineering tunnel; flesh out the 'gateway' standards"**

Before this PR, PEAT parsed the RTAC's access points and access point routers (#21), but nothing interpreted them. The pull dropped the `Eng_Access_*` remote devices and ignored the engineering access tables it already reads from PostgreSQL. Connecting through the tunnels (transport, `WHO`/`PORT n`, child devices) is #62. This PR is the discovery and the gateway hook it consumes.

- New `peat/modules/sel/rtac_engineering_access.py` (pure functions, no I/O):
  - `discover_from_export(device_info)` reads #21's parsed export:
    - `AccessPointServer` devices give the `Network Connection Type` and `Local Port Number`.
    - `AccessPointRouters` give the routes. PEAT takes the access point to be whichever endpoint is an access point, `Source` or `Destination`, so the reversed layout in #21's synthetic test also works. It also handles the `Destinations` list (see `rtac_parse` below) and AP-to-AP routes (e.g. to a serial access point).
    - Destinations resolve to devices with or without the `_TAP`/`_AP` suffix and the protocol (`Feeder_1_SEL_TAP` resolves to `Feeder_1`). The route is `interleaved` for `_TAP` or type `TAP`, and `direct` for `_AP` or type `AP`. This also works when the export lists the device access points (`Feeder_1_SEL_AP`) as devices. A route to an access point of the RTAC itself (e.g. `Serial_AP`) gets route `null`.
    - SEL servers (SEL protocol with `server` in the protocol or connection type, e.g. `Server - Ethernet Tunneled Serial`) give `Server IP Port`, `Serial Tunneling Mode`, `Perform Authentication` (forced for SSH), `Termination String` (`<CTRL-D>`, `^D`, `<CR>` etc. become the actual characters; the default is `\x04`), `Enable Port Command`, `Disable Remote Access`, `Allow Anonymous SEL IP Clients`, `Client IP Address`, `Verify SSL Certificate`, `Enable File Transfer Monitor` and the pre/post-termination timeouts.
    - SEL client devices become the targets of each SEL server. The `PORT n` number is the serial port number for serial devices when the export has one, otherwise the `Virtual Port Number`.
    - A DNP3 server tunneled over TLS is not treated as engineering access. A SEL server without a `Serial Tunneling Mode` (e.g. for an HMI) only gets a service, with a debug message instead of a warning.
    - A router whose destination PEAT can't find (no destination, an endpoint without a name, or in the database an ID that isn't in the tables) gives its access point an entry with `name`, `device_name` and `route` set to `null`, and a warning. If PEAT can't tell which of a router's listening access points the client connects to, each of them gets one. The route may be direct, so these ports aren't probed.
  - `discover_from_postgres(tables)` maps the `schema_fw` tables (`access_points*`, `access_point_ethernet_settings`, `access_point_routers`, `sel_server_*`, `sel_client_*`, `sel_virtual_ports`, `serial_port*`, `local_tcp_network_port*`, `connections`, `remote_connections`, `remote_devices`). Column names aren't public, so matching is tolerant:
    - Setting and column names are compared case- and punctuation-insensitively (`local_port_number` matches `Local Port Number`), with a few variations.
    - Rows of related tables are joined on specific ID columns (`connection_id`, `access_point_id`, `remote_device_id`, `serial_port_id`, `local_tcp_network_port_id`, ...). Two rows join only if they share a value in one of these columns and no shared column has different values. `device_id` can't join rows by itself (it may be the same in every row), but a different `device_id` keeps rows apart. Generic columns like `id` or `project_id` aren't used, and two rows from the same table are never merged.
    - Each access point, SEL server and SEL device needs a row in a table of its own kind. `sel_virtual_ports`, `serial_port_connections` and `serial_ports` only add the serial port to SEL devices, and `local_tcp_network_port_connections`/`local_tcp_network_ports` only add a missing TCP port to access points and SEL servers. These tables also have rows for DNP3 devices, other servers and unused ports, and those rows are ignored.
    - Router columns `source*`/`src*` and `destination*`/`dest*`/`dst*` may hold names, IDs (looked up by the rest of the column name, e.g. `source_access_point_id` in `access_point_id`) or lists of either. An ID that isn't in the tables is a destination PEAT can't find (see below).
    - When a mode or type is a number (an enum ID), PEAT logs a warning with the row's column names, so a real dump shows what to fix. A column like `serial_tunneling_mode_id` is also used for this when the exact column isn't there.
  - Every entry has exactly the cross-PR contract keys (`ENGINEERING_ACCESS_KEYS`): `name, rtac_ip, tcp_port, transport, kind, sel_port, device_name, route, needs_rtac_login, termination_string, source`.
- `SELRTAC`:
  - `_process_engineering_access(dev, discovery)` runs from #21's `_process_export` and from `pull_postgres`. It writes:
    - `dev.extra["engineering_access"]`, merged and deduplicated across sources and repeated pulls;
    - `dev.extra["engineering_access_devices"]` with the `Eng_Access_*` names, which are recorded now instead of dropped (they still aren't added to `related.hosts`);
    - one `Service` per listener: `configured_port`, protocol `telnet`/`ssh`/`tls` (none for raw TCP and UDP), role `engineering_access` when the listener reaches devices (otherwise `access_point`/`sel_server`), and `extra` with the destinations (router, route, SEL port, legacy port command settings; a SEL server lists them only if it reaches them) and the SEL server security settings. Services are looked up by port and transport, so different Telnet ports don't merge into one service.
    - The ports land in `related.ports`. A failure in this processing is logged and doesn't stop the parse or the pull.
  - `pull_postgres` also keeps every row of these tables. `pulled-postgres-config.json` keys rows by their first column, so rows with the same first value overwrite each other there. The JSON output is unchanged. A `remote_devices` row without a name no longer raises.
  - `downstream_targets(dev)` is the duck-typed gateway hook: the tunnel PR #62 calls it with `getattr(module, "downstream_targets", None)`. It returns copies of the entries that have an RTAC IP and a port, with one entry per path, so a path in both the export and the database (same port, transport, kind, SEL port, device and route) is returned once. `needs_rtac_login` is set if any copy of the path has it. The results include `direct` and unknown (`null`) routes, and the docstring warns consumers about them. `peat/device.py` is unchanged.
  - The new opt-in option `sel.rtac_probe_tunnel_ports` (default `false`, mirrored in the three example configs) adds `probe_tunnel_ports(dev)` after the PostgreSQL pull:
    - TLS ports get one handshake through #50's `peat/protocols/tls.py`, with its legacy retry. The result has the fingerprints, factory-default/self-signed/expiry flags, `same_as_web_certificate`, and `engineering-access-tcp-<port>-certificate.pem` (hashed into `files`).
    - SSH ports get one key exchange. The host key is stored in `ssh_keys` with its `SHA256:` fingerprint as the `id`.
    - Results are in `extra.engineering_access_probes["tcp/<port>"]`, `related.hash`, and the port's service (status `verified`).
    - Ports are allow-listed: a port is probed only if every path on it is a SEL server (which needs `PORT n` to reach a device) or an `interleaved` route. Ports with a direct or unknown route are never probed, and neither are ports whose paths disagree on the transport. Telnet and raw ports a

author: adampluth
body:
## Reason

The shared `DataTable` component is built on TanStack Table 8, and 9 has been out since August 2026. Staying a major version behind makes each later upgrade bigger, and newer React tooling expects the newer version.

## Design

`DataTable.tsx` is the only file that imports TanStack Table. Its props don't change, so the two screens that use it (Project Management's team table and Data Management's artifacts table) are unchanged.

- `useReactTable` becomes `useTable`. Version 9 only bundles the features a table registers, so `DataTable` registers sorting, column filters and search with their row models.
- In v8, sorting picked a sort function from the column's values: text, alphanumeric or datetime. Those three are registered, so columns sort the same way they did.
- Two v8 workarounds are gone:
  - The `getColumnCanGlobalFilter` override. v8's search skipped columns whose first value wasn't a string or number, and v9 doesn't.
  - Reading cells through `getValue()`. Cells now read the column's `value` directly, which gives the same result with simpler types.
- **The `react-hooks/incompatible-library` eslint-disable is removed.** Lint passes without it on `useTable`. That's the line questioned on PPLT-320.
- New packages: `@tanstack/table-core` 9.3.1 (released 2026-10-12), and `@tanstack/react-store` and `@tanstack/store` 0.11.2 (released 2026-09-29). All are older than two weeks.

## Impact

- **No visible change.** I ran a scripted Playwright check against both screens on v8 and on v9, with `/api` stubbed. The headers, rows and sort buttons matched, the table screenshots were byte-identical, and there were no console errors.
- **New test:** `DataTable.dom.test.tsx` clicks a header and checks that sorting goes ascending, then descending, then off, and that an empty value stays last. It passes on v8 and v9. The existing `DataTable.test.ts` passes unchanged.
- **Conflicts with PPLT-319 (#374):** both PRs change `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. Whichever merges second needs a rebase and a fresh `npm install`.
- **For the docker dev profile:** dependencies changed, so `frontend-dev` needs a rebuild with fresh `node_modules` (`--renew-anon-volumes`).

## Checklist
- [x] This PR targets `devel` and contains a single logical change
- [x] Checks for the touched components pass locally (see CONTRIBUTING.md): lint, typecheck, 76 tests, build
- [x] Tests were added or updated (`DataTable.dom.test.tsx`)
- [ ] Documentation was updated, if behavior or configuration changed (no behavior or configuration change)
- [x] New `.py` / `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.jsx` files carry the copyright marking
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files are included

## AI assistance
- [x] AI tools were used to prepare this PR

Claude Code ported `DataTable`, wrote the new test, and ran the v8 and v9 comparison.

author: nyeinchanaung75299-eng
body:
## Problem
PR #117 only added a known-name mapping. YYZB feed snapshot contains 3,837 football fixtures and 3,671 still show `Home team (id)` or `Away team (id)`, although original club names were retained. Soco UI also shows a distracting 'Streamer rooms are listed...' disclaimer, and raw Soco league codes such as `ITA D1` are not normalized.

## Fix
- Preserve meaningful original club and competition names when a confirmed English alias is missing, rather than fake 'Home/Away team (id)' names. Known English names remain preferred; no guessed translations.
- Fix cached/mirrored legacy YYZB rows to retrieve `original_home_team`, `original_away_team` and `original_league`, skipping numeric placeholders. Sync 159 curated European Chinese aliases into the Dart client fallback.
- Add English translations for reported Swedish clubs (GAIS Gothenburg, AIK Solna, Mjallby AIF, Kalmar FF) and common Soco league codes (`ITA D1` → Italian Serie A etc.).
- Keep every football league in Soco/YYZB, not only top five or UEFA; reject basketball and other explicitly non-football category IDs or names, and support nested football team objects.
- Remove Soco 'Streamer rooms are listed, but video availability is checked when opened' match-card banner.
- Update JS regression coverage for unknown lower-league identities, Allsvenskan, leagues and basketball exclusion.

## Scope / limitations
This **does not** claim all 3,837 Chinese fixture names are translated to English. Unmapped teams retain their REAL source name for identification, never an invented English name. Team-logo URLs, room identities, playback/DRM, EPG and kickoffs are unchanged. UI/Backend deployment and real-device check required after CI.

author: kurtl9862
body:
## What this does

Replaces the "git pull, npm run setup, npm run build, npm start, open Chrome" routine with an **OBD2** app you open like any other.

**One-time install** (after this is merged):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kurtl9862/obd2/main/scripts/mac/install.sh | bash
```

The installer (`scripts/mac/install.sh`):
- finds the existing OBD2 folder in the usual places (or `OBD2_DIR=...`), otherwise clones it to `~/obd2`
- switches it to `main` if it's on another branch with no local edits
- installs Node with Homebrew if it's missing or older than 22.18 (or points to nodejs.org)
- creates `~/Applications/OBD2.app` with a gauge icon, then runs it once so packages and the build are ready

Opening the app runs `scripts/mac/launch.sh`, which lives in the repo so it updates itself:
1. fetches `main` with a ~15 s stall timeout; no internet just means "use what's here"; skipped when not on `main` or with local edits
2. `npm run setup` only when a `package.json` changed; `npm run build` only when the commit changed
3. reuses the running helper if it's the same version, otherwise restarts it in the background (log at `~/Library/Logs/OBD2/obd2.log`)
4. opens `http://localhost:35001` in Chrome (then Edge, then the default browser)

Progress shows as macOS notifications; failures show a dialog with a **Show log** button. `launch.sh --stop` and `--sim` are there for when they're needed.

## Testing

On Linux with `open`, `uname` and `xcode-select` stubbed: first run (setup + build + start), second run (reuses helper in under 0.1 s), `--sim` restart, an upstream commit (pulls, rebuilds, restarts), unreachable remote (carries on), `--stop`, and the installer piped through `bash` from a feature branch. Not yet run on a real Mac, so the icon conversion (`sips`/`iconutil`) and the Finder/notification bits are untested.

author: jvallery
body:
Part of #1147 (program epic VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform#1120).

## Summary

Adds `verdify_services`, the one service layer that the operator API (#1148) and MCP share. It sets the conventions every later service follows (architecture §6, §5.3 and §5.6). Nothing calls it yet, so the next `verdify-prod-dark` sync changes no live behaviour. There is no migration, manifest, grant or device write.

- `verdify_services/actor.py`: `Actor(source, name, role)`. It is frozen and accepts only the R4 sources (`dashboard`, `iris`, `system`, `agent:<name>`). A `dashboard` actor needs the role `operator` or `viewer`; every other source has no role. The constructors are `person`, `iris`, `agent` (`Actor.agent("admin")` for the admin token) and `system`. `ActorRef` is the OpenAPI `Actor` (source and name) that responses carry.
- `verdify_services/problems.py`: the 24 OpenAPI `ProblemCode` values verbatim, `Problem` field for field, `ServiceError` and `problem()`.
  - The title is the code in words.
  - The status follows the code: 400, 401, 403, 404 and 503 where the OpenAPI lists them, 422 for every other code.
  - `retryable` is true only for `line_busy`, `manifold_busy`, `query_timeout` and `unavailable`. The model refuses `retryable=true` for any other code.
  - An irrigation `Refusal` converts with `Problem.model_validate(refusal.problem())`.
- `verdify_services/activity.py`:
  - `append` writes one `activity_log` row.
  - `list` serves API-17: newest first, `source='agent'` matching every agent, a prefix match on `action`, an opaque base64url cursor and `limit` from 1 to 200.
  - `recorded_write` is the one write convention. It checks the actor and hashes the canonical request. On (`source`, `request_id`) it replays a match or raises `request_id_reused`. It stamps the armed experiment id from `fn_mcp_armed_assignment_context()`, writes the domain row and its activity row in one transaction, and retries once after a concurrent duplicate hits `UNIQUE (source, request_id)`.
  - `WriteResult` gives the REST body, the `Idempotency-Replayed: true` header and the MCP payload with `replayed: true`.
- `verdify_schemas/activity.py`: `ActivityLogRow` and `DesiredStateRow` for migration 280's tables, both added to the drift guard's `DB_BACKED`. It also defines `ACTOR_SOURCE_PATTERN` and `ACTIVITY_ACTION_PATTERN` (the architecture §9 actions; `irrigation.*` is open).
- `api/operator_routes/__init__.py`: the route-module rules, as a docstring only.
- `api/Dockerfile` and `mcp/Dockerfile`: a plain `COPY verdify_services/ ./verdify_services/` and `RUN python -c "import verdify_services.activity"`. The ingestor image does not get the package.
- `scripts/ci-local.sh`: ruff now covers `verdify_services/`, and `tests/test_verdify_services_core.py` joins the curated list.
- Docs: `verdify_services/README.md` holds the conventions on one page. Architecture §6 now says that reads take no actor, that every write runs through `recorded_write`, and that the api Dockerfile copies the package.

**For L4 (#1177), L6 and L7:**
- `recorded_write` takes one argument that the issue's signature lacks: `action`, the activity action (`setting.write`, `irrigation.run` and so on). The operation id alone cannot supply it: API-20 covers both `light.on` and `light.off`, and MCP `set_setting` maps to API-10 or API-11.
- `request` must hold every input that `target` does not carry: the body, plus any path or query value such as API-20's `{state}`. Otherwise two writes that differ only there would replay each other.

Other choices beyond the issue text, each small:
- `recorded_write` and `append` also refuse a dashboard viewer with `forbidden`.
- `recorded_write` refuses a `request_id` that is not a UUID, or a reason over 500 characters, with `invalid_request` before it opens its transaction.
- `recorded_write` raises `RuntimeError` when called inside an open transaction, because it must own its transaction.
- `ActivityLogRow` checks the action against the §9 list and requires `request_id` and its 32-byte hash together. A lane that adds a new kind of action extends `ACTIVITY_ACTION_PATTERN`, which is a rule-7 change.
- `DesiredStateRow` enforces migration 280's two CHECKs.
- `ReadbackState`, the OpenAPI enum behind `ActivityEntry.state`, lives in `verdify_services/activity.py`; VD-67 can move it.

Review fixes (second commit):
- **Hash:** the canonical hash wrote a UTC time as `+00:00` when the request was a dict of typed arguments, but as `Z` when it was the model that dict validates into. The two surfaces would therefore disagree on one request. Times, dates and UUIDs now hash in Pydantic's JSON form.
- **Reason length:** `ActivityLogRow` capped `reason` at 500 characters, but the `activity_log` column has no limit. Iris's unchanged `set_tunable` takes a reason of any length and must never gain a refusal (R5), so the cap is gone. `recorded_write` still refuses a REST or MCP reason over 500, as the request bodies do.
- **`limit` refusal:** `activity.list` refused an out-of-range `limit` with 422 `out_of_range`. The operator API answers the same query with 400 `invalid_request` (#1148), so the service now does too, still with `min`, `max` and `current`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **Replay and `request_id_reused`:** met in code and tests.
  - A request with the same source, `request_id` and payload returns the stored object with `replayed` true (REST header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, MCP top-level `replayed: true`) and appends no row.
  - The same key with another payload raises 422 `request_id_reused`, with `retryable` false.
  - Tested against a fake connection in `tests/test_verdify_services_core.py`, and on PostgreSQL in `tests/test_dashboard_db_services.py` (campaign step), including a real two-connection race.
- [x] **Experiment stamp:** met in code and tests. An append while a fixture experiment is armed carries its `experiment_id`; with none armed it is null; nothing is refused. The fake-connection test covers it, and the database test arms, runs and completes a fixture experiment.
- [x] **`Actor` vocabulary:** met in code and tests. `admin`, `agent:`, `Agent:Steward` and `system-x` are rejected, along with `agent:Steward`, a trailing newline and an empty source. A `dashboard` actor without a role is rejected too.
- [x] **`Problem`:** met in code and tests. Every code's body validates against the committed OpenAPI `Problem` schema. The field set, the required set, the `ProblemCode` enum and the `result` enum match the file. `retryable` is true only for the four waiting codes, unless the caller sets it false.
- [ ] **Both images build and import the package:** verified at release. The in-cluster build of the merge commit must pass `RUN python -c "import verdify_services.activity"` in `verdify-api` and `verdify-mcp`. Before the PR, the import was checked in a copy laid out like `/app`, on Python 3.13 with only the images' packages (asyncpg, pyyaml, and pydantic at both the newest 2.x and the pinned floor, 2.8).

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_verdify_services_core.py`: 82 passed.
- `python -m pytest -q verdify_schemas/tests/test_activity.py`: 39 passed.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_dashboard_db_services.py`: 5 skipped here, because it needs `VERDIFY_ISOLATED_TEST_DSN`. It runs in the jvallery/agents#5994 campaign step.
- A wider run of the related suites passed: 1265 passed and 190 skipped (the database-backed guards). It covered `verdify_schemas/tests/`, `test_build_provenance`, `test_public_output_guard`, `test_release_dockerfile_base_pins`, `test_ha_trim`, `test_280_desired_state_delivery`, `test_dashboard_db_280` and the new files.
- The tests for the three review fixes fail when the pre-fix logic is restored: the dict-versus-model hash, the time form in `detail`, and the reason cap.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on every changed Python file: clean. `bash -n scripts/ci-local.sh`: OK. `scripts/check-service-restart-drift.sh origin/main HEAD`: OK.

## Intent To the existing Resend draft PR, add manual opt-in live Resend tests for digest delivery and every outbound email category using synthetic data in a disposable local PostgreSQL database. Redirect every test email to the approved Gmail inbox only, never real students; verify provider acceptance and durable job/outbox states without claiming inbox receipt. Keep mocked network-drop, retry, and privacy-failure tests in normal CI. Preserve one commit on the draft PR and update its description with results. ## What Changed - Add Resend HTTPS delivery while retaining SMTP, with frozen email payloads, stable idempotency keys, and send-time eligibility checks for queued jobs and digests. - Add manual opt-in live tests for auth, queued, and digest email that use synthetic data in a disposable local PostgreSQL database, redirect sends to the approved inbox, and check provider acceptance and durable job/outbox states—not inbox receipt. - Add mocked failure, retry, and privacy regression coverage, plus configuration, migration, specification, and documentation updates. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The review found no substantiated defect, but the change spans sensitive email delivery, durable retries, and privacy checks, making its residual implementation risk greater than a routine change. ## Testing After installing missing worktree dependencies, focused tests passed and the real manual command rejected both missing opt-in and an unapproved recipient. author: costajohnt
body:
## Change

The Local security result list (`LocalSecurityRows.svelte`) shows its matching-record count and current page as plain text, so a screen reader user who filters or changes page hears nothing about the result.

- Adds one visually hidden `role="status"` (polite) line under the toolbar. It reads "25 of 25 records, page 1 of 2", or just "0 of 25 records" when everything fits on one page. It only interpolates counts, never row titles or paths. Both messages are in `pt-BR.json`.
- Previous and Next now use `aria-disabled` with a guard in the click handler, the same way `ResultReviewChanges.svelte` does. In Chromium, pressing Next onto the last page with native `disabled` dropped keyboard focus to `body`, and the next Tab went back to the section tabs. With `aria-disabled` focus stays on the button. The dimmed style matches the global `button:disabled` look.
- The 20-row bound, native `details` rows, filter behaviour and retained results are unchanged. No new endpoints, persistence or dialogs.

Closes #1218

## Verification

On Linux, Node 24.21.0, at this branch on top of `33aa0c15`:

- `npx vitest run --project components`: 113 files, 881 tests passed. The two new tests in `ObservatoryLocalSecurity.test.ts` fail against the current `LocalSecurityRows.svelte` and pass with this change. They cover filtering to zero, clearing the filter, paging forward, pressing Next again on the last page, paging back, the status not containing row paths, and the Portuguese text.
- `npx vitest run tests/renderer/observatory-i18n.test.ts`: 6 passed (the new keys keep their placeholders).
- `npm run frontend:check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings. `npm run build:renderer` builds. eslint and prettier are clean on the changed files.
- Rendered keyboard journey: ran the preview (`vite --mode preview`) in headless Chromium through Playwright, with the demo findings temporarily padded to 25 rows so the list paginates (that padding is not part of this PR). Using the keyboard only: focus stayed in the search box while filtering to zero and clearing, the status read "0 of 25 records" and then "25 of 25 records, page 1 of 2", Tab reached Next, Enter moved to "page 2 of 2" with focus still on Next, and Shift+Tab reached Previous. Before the `aria-disabled` change the same journey left focus on `body` after Next.

Not checked: a real screen reader, Electron/Windows, and the packaged app.

## Limits and review

- A single match reads "1 of 1 records"; the existing record strings don't have plural forms either.
- Tool-assisted checks are the ones listed under Verification.

author: simitchell
body:
## Problem
On a phone, a signed-out visitor had to scroll past the long welcome paragraph, the "New here?" list, and the full login form before reaching any listings, which started around 1,000px down. The login card was also stuck to the left. Two causes:
- `HomeWrapper` used `${(justifyContent) => justifyContent}`. styled-components passes that function the whole props object, so the CSS came out as `[object Object]`. The browser dropped it and the row fell back to `flex-start`. The prop also leaked onto the DOM `<div>`.
- `HomeLogin` is `flex: 0 0 280px`, so on a wrapped phone row it stayed 280px wide.

## Changes
- **Alignment fix:** the prop is now a transient `$justify`, read as `justify-content: ${({ $justify }) => $justify}`, so it no longer reaches the DOM. Added `gap: 24px` between the welcome text and the login form.
- **Compact welcome card on phones (≤640px, signed out only):** headline, one-line tagline, Log In / Register buttons (MUI `Button component={Link}`, 46px tall), and "New here? How it Works · About Us" links. Both layouts are always in the page and CSS media queries pick one: no JS state, no resize listener, and no flash of the wrong layout. Signed-in visitors see the same page as before.
- **"Current Listings" heading row on phones:** heading on the left and an "N listings" count on the right, shown only after loading finishes. The count is hidden on desktop. The listings grid's top padding is removed on the homepage only, so the gap under the heading is 12px.
- **About Us:** the old homepage paragraph becomes the page's intro, reworded from a homepage pitch into an About Us introduction.
- Desktop `<ul>` indent fixed (`padding-left: 0`).

## Testing (local, Chrome; phone checks in a 390×844 viewport)
| | Phone, signed out | Phone, signed in | Desktop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layout | Compact card; long text and login form hidden | Unchanged (long text, no form, no card) | Unchanged; login form now right-aligned |
| First listing card | **517px** from the top (was ~1,000), visible without scrolling | 793px (unchanged) | unchanged |
| Buttons | Log In / Register 46px tall | — | — |
| Horizontal scroll | None | None | None |

About Us at 390px: the new intro renders first, with no horizontal scroll.

author: ghostofgoes
body:
# refactor(sel): split SELHTTP fetching from parsing and add parser tests

## Description

tl;dr: SELHTTP only fetches pages; new pure, tested parsers handle relay, RTAC and SEL-3620 pages; many parsing bugs fixed.

**I5b: "Split SELHTTP into separate methods for parsing and pulling"**

Every relay, RTAC and SEL-3620 method in `sel_http.py` now does fetch, then a pure `parse_*()`, then `process_*(parsed, dev)`. Method names and return contracts are unchanged:
- relay methods return `bool` (`SELRelay.pull_http`);
- RTAC methods return dicts (`SELRTAC.pull_web` checks for truthy values);
- `SEL3620._pull` still finds the same 22 `gateway_*` methods by reflection. A test pins that set.
- one exception: the relay `login()` raises `PeatError` when the relay didn't reject the credentials but the session can't be determined (see Relay login below). The old code raised `TypeError` in one of these cases (a SEL-351 response without a link).

New `peat/modules/sel/relay_command_parse.py` (relay command output):
- `parse_ver_output()` + `process_ver_info()`: sections are found by name and indentation, not by their order or fixed end markers. So the SEL-421 layout works (`Fiber Port`, `Communications Card`, a different closing note), and so does the two-space indentation of the 311L/351S. It adds the 351S `Analog Input Voltage/Current`, `Main Board I/O` and `Additional I/O` (old TODOs), and `hardware_warnings`. It replaces the unused `parse_ver_output()` in `relay_parse.py`.
- `parse_eth_output()` + `process_eth_info()`, and `parse_mac_output()`, which reads both MAC formats (`Port 1 MAC Address:` and `(IP) MAC`/`(GOOSE) MAC`), plus `MAC:` / `MAC 1:`. Both use one regex, `MAC_LINE_RE`. The web interface has no MAC page, so `parse_mac_output()` has no caller in this PR (see Decisions).
- `parse_show_groups()`: `SHO` output grouped by heading. It's built on `parse_show_output()` from #20 (both `=` and `:=`, continuation lines, quoted values). It's used for port settings, front panel, outputs and logic.
- `parse_meter_values()` and `parse_meter_energy()`.
- `parse_simple_line()`, `normalize_keys()` and `parse_comments()` moved here. They can still be imported from `sel_http`.

New `peat/modules/sel/sel_web_parse.py` (HTML/CSV):
- helpers: `extract_pre_text()`, `extract_login_token()`, `derive_relay_session_url()`, `read_html()`/`parse_html_table()`;
- RTAC: `parse_rtac_device_info`, `parse_rtac_diagnostics`, `parse_rtac_post_summary`, `parse_rtac_files`, `parse_soe_csv`, `classify_soe_event`;
- shared: `parse_web_accounts`;
- SEL-3620: `parse_gateway_index`, `parse_gateway_syslog`, `parse_x509_export_links`;
- each with a `process_*()` counterpart where data goes into the data model.

The 19 SEL-3620 stub pages are now one `GATEWAY_PAGES` table plus `SELHTTP._pull_gateway_page()`. The helper's name doesn't start with `gateway_`, so the reflection in `SEL3620._pull` never calls it. Each `gateway_*` method is a one-line wrapper with the same page, `dev.extra` key and result key as before (tested per page). The pages are still fetched and saved, and not parsed.

**I5a: "Reduce duplication with SELHTTP and SELTelnet"**

- Relay pages run an ASCII command and show its output in `<pre>`. That text now goes through parsers that only take text (`relay_command_parse`, `relay_parse`). This is only partly done for I5a:
  - `STA`, `SER` and `HIS` output is already parsed by the same functions for the web interface and for Telnet/serial. The web interface doesn't fetch or parse `ID` yet (see Not in this PR).
  - `parse_ver_output`, `parse_eth_output` and `parse_mac_output` accept Telnet captures (command echo, prompts, CRLF), and are tested with SEL-421- and SEL-751A-style ASCII output. But the Telnet/serial code doesn't use them yet: `sel_ascii.py` isn't touched, and wiring them into `SELAscii.show_eth`/`show_mac` and `pull_more_commands` is left to #60.
- One `SELHTTP._extract_login_token()` serves `login`, `login_rtac` and `login_3620` (there were 3 copies).
- One `process_firmware_checksum()` (in `relay_parse.py`, next to `process_fid`) handles the RTAC `Firmware Checksum` and the relay `VER` checksum (there were 2 copies).
- One `parse_web_accounts()`/`process_web_accounts()` handles RTAC `user_table.sel` and SEL-3620 `Users.sel` (the two copies were identical).
- One `login_with_web_credentials()` holds the web login loop: cached credentials, otherwise each user with each password.
  - `SEL3620._verify_http` uses it.
  - `SELRTAC._verify_http` has the same loop. It can switch to this helper after #21, which rewrites `sel_rtac.py`, so `sel_rtac.py` isn't changed here.
- A `_post_rtac()` helper covers the repeated RTAC POST with session parameters.

**I5c: "Unit tests for SELHTTP parsing code"**

- Characterization tests came first. They were written against the code before the split, drive the `SELHTTP` methods against a fake web server, and passed on the base branch. They stay green after the refactor, except for one intentional change, noted in the test (RTAC sizes, see Decisions). Login session-URL derivation for the 351, 351S and 451 is tested with `requests_mock`.
- Then unit and regression tests for every pure parser and every bug fixed below.
- 183 tests in two new files: `tests/modules/sel/test_sel_http_relay_parse.py` (relay pages, login, command parsers) and `tests/modules/sel/test_sel_web_parse.py` (RTAC, SEL-3620, login loop).
- Fixtures: 25 synthetic pages in `tests/modules/sel/data_files/web/`. The README states their provenance:
  - The relay pages follow the layout of the command examples in public SEL manuals, with made-up values.
  - The RTAC/3620 pages are minimal HTML with the structure the parsers read.
  - All values are made up (RFC 5737 IP addresses). There are no device captures.

**Bugs fixed** (each has a regression test)
- `parse_page_data` used `pre.string`, which is `None` when the `<pre>` contains tags (e.g. links on the `his` page), so it raised `AttributeError`. It now uses `get_text()`, and multiple `<pre>` sections are joined.
- `parse_simple_line`:
  - missed a value on the first line of the text;
  - didn't escape the name;
  - treated `|` as a separator.
- VER:
  - Values on the first line of a page were missed (the 351S/421 output starts with them).
  - A missing part number replaced the current one with `""`.
  - Empty `FID`/`BFID` keys were added to `extra`.
- ETH:
  - A subnet mask on its own line (351S/751A) was ignored.
  - An invalid `IP ADDRESS: x/y` value raised `ValueError`, which lost all of the output. The value is kept as it is.
  - `PRIMARY PORT: PORT 1A` became `PORT`.
  - `--` wasn't treated as unknown.
  - The MAC order was random (it came from a set).
  - The 351S GOOSE port counters were lost. They're now in the new `port_sections`.
- SHO:
  - `parse_multiple_lists` returned `{}` for a page with an odd number of blocks, e.g. one with a `Port 5` title.
  - The 351-style parser split values on spaces (`FTP SERVER:` became `FTP`).
  - `get_front_panel_settings` raised `KeyError` when the page had no `Front Panel Settings` heading.
  - The port-format probe accepted an `Invalid Command` page as the URL format. It now tries the other format and falls back to the first one if both say `Invalid Command`.
- MET:
  - A `$$$$$$` value raised `ValueError` and failed the whole page.
  - 351S/351 energy values (old TODO) now parse, as do layouts without a total row.
  - The reset time uses `DATE_F`.
- Relay login:
  - The SEL-351 path raised `TypeError` when the response had no link. It now raises `PeatError` with a clear message. It raises (instead of returning `False`) whenever the relay didn't reject the credentials but the session can't be determined, so the credential loop in `SELRelay._verify_http` stops, as it did with the `TypeError`. Returning `False` would make it try the other default credentials, which are failed logins on a relay that already accepted the first ones (failed-access alarm, lockout). A test checks that

author: dodgeblaster
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** When saving a cron job edit fails, the edit is undone but a run that finished meanwhile keeps its result.

`CronService._update_job_locked` undoes a failed save by copying the whole job record back from a copy taken before the edit. A run of the same job can finish during that save. It writes its failure count, its auto-pause, the one-shot park and its last status onto the same job, and the whole-record copy wipes those out. Then the run's final record, taken from that object, can persist the wiped values. A job that just reached its auto-pause threshold comes back enabled with a failure count of 0 and keeps firing.

## Why it matters

The auto-pause is what stops a failing job from running (and spending) forever, and the one-shot park is what stops a fired one-shot from firing again. A failed save of an unrelated edit, such as a rename, silently undoing either one is a cost and correctness bug that nobody sees. It needs a disk-full or I/O-error save at the moment a run of that job finishes, so it is rare, but the damage lasts.

## Not a goal

- Any change to `enable_job` (pause/resume), which reloads the store after a failed save.
- Any change to what a successful edit writes, or to the other mutators' rollbacks.
- A revision fence or a per-job lock on run-owned fields.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

The edit owns some fields of the job and a run owns others. The edit never writes `enabled`, `auto_paused`, `consecutive_failures` or a run's status fields. The bug is only that the undo restored every field. So the undo now covers exactly the fields the edit changed.

`_update_job_locked` applies the edit to a private copy of the job, which no other thread can reach. The fields that differ from the copy's starting values are the edit's changes. Only those are written to the live job, which stays the same object readers already hold. If the save fails, each changed field is put back only while it still holds the edit's own value, so a later write to it stands. Every other field, including everything a run in flight wrote, is left alone.

`docs/system-specs/modules/learn-cron-dashboard.md` now describes this in its save-failure paragraph, in place of the whole-record restore.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: only an edit whose save already raised behaves differently; a successful edit writes the same fields as before, and the caller still gets the same exception.

Removes nothing: no field, record, key or function is removed; the failed-save path just restores fewer fields.

## Tests

`test/test_cron_save_failure_rollback.py` adds four `update_job` cases, each with a real `OSError` from the atomic write:

- A run that fails into its auto-pause during the failed save keeps `enabled=False`, `auto_paused=True`, the failure count and its status, while the edit is undone on the same object.
- A one-shot the run parks during the failed save stays parked.
- Every field the edit changed is restored (name, message, schedule, silent, skip dates), on the same object and on disk.
- A field the edit changed that another writer changed again keeps the later write.

The healthy-save control now also checks that a successful edit lands in memory, on the same object, and on disk.

Proof: PROVEN test/test_cron_save_failure_rollback.py::test_a_failed_update_keeps_a_concurrent_runs_auto_pause, test/test_cron_save_failure_rollback.py::test_a_failed_update_keeps_a_concurrent_one_shot_park, test/test_cron_save_failure_rollback.py::test_a_failed_update_keeps_a_field_another_writer_changed_since (head b5e290d45fb0)

The restore-every-field case passes on main too. It guards the edit's own undo, which a narrower rollback could drop.

## Manual verification

N/A — unit coverage sufficient: the fault is injected at the real `atomic_write` call, and the run's writes land on the live job inside that failing save, which is the race window.

## Screenshots / video

N/A — no user-visible UI change.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22350

## Sibling sweep

Swept: git grep -nE "__dict__\.update|copy\.copy\(" -- src/kiro_crew/cron.py src/kiro_crew/cron_service/
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/cron.py -- changed here
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/cron_service/execution.py -- not affected -- copies the job to freeze a run's terminal record, nothing is restored from it
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/cron_service/settlement.py -- not affected -- copies the job to build a held settlement record, nothing is restored from it
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/cron_service/service/run_merge.py -- not affected -- copies a held record before applying it, nothing is restored from it

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: rolling back a failed write by restoring a whole object snapshot when another thread writes other fields of the same object

author: rgdevment
body:
## What it changes

Each version Tisty shares now carries the page it drew from the words, beside the Markdown, so the web can show it without drawing it. Nothing changes on screen yet: the web keeps drawing from the Markdown until the light `show` door arrives (4b-5).

## Why

Tasks «Tisty Share 4b-3» and «4b-4», decision 91: the page is drawn when it is put up, never when it is opened.

## How

**Envelope v3** (`tisty-share-proto`):
- Format byte 2 and manifest `v = 3` carry a sealed `Html` part between what the words cite and the pictures.
- An index frame follows the manifest with the SHA-256 of each sealed part. The sender signs the manifest and the index only, so who sent it is known before any part arrives, and each part is checked against its hash as it comes.
- The writer signs the words, what they cite, the page and each picture's hash, so a picture can arrive later and still be checked on its own.
- v1 and v2 envelopes are byte for byte what they were; an older reader says `newer` for v3.

**After an Opus security audit** (no way found for a server, a man in the middle or a link holder to break integrity or authorship):
- The writer's signature part grows by 48 bytes per picture in v3. Before, a signed v3 with about 30 pictures could not be sealed. The Worker's ceiling grows by 96 bytes per picture to match.
- `Limits.html` is 0 when a server leaves it out, so Tisty seals v3 only for a server that says it takes a page. Today's tisty.cl does not say so, so this can ship before or after the `share-v` tag.
- `drawn_content` refuses when the picture and hash counts differ, and prefixes each media type with its length.
- Text and page are checked as UTF-8 before they are copied. The cited list is zeroized, and each part is sealed in a buffer with room for its tag.
- `HtmlTooBig` is told apart from `TextTooBig`.

**Tisty** (`sharing.rs`): `put_up`, which all four ways of putting a version up go through, draws the page with `tisty_markdown::html` over the text `pictured()` already rewrote. It uses the same features as the wasm, so the page is the one the web draws today.

## How it was checked

- **proto:** 144 tests. New ones cover:
  - a format byte against the manifest;
  - an index flipped, framed wrong or cut short;
  - a page or pictures changed, reordered, dropped or added by a link holder;
  - a writer's signature carried between v2 and v3;
  - Html out of place;
  - unsigned v3 with citations;
  - 60 signed pictures;
  - limits without `html`.
- **Fuzz:** `envelope_tamper` now also checks the page and the writer before tampering; the fuzz crate builds.
- **Workspace:** `cargo test` for the whole workspace, with the app at 653; clippy on all targets with `-D warnings`; the wasm crate checked for `wasm32`; `scripts/rules.sh`.

Diagrams still travel as the web draws them; sending the SVG the app drew is left for 4b-5.

- [x] The issue was discussed first, if this is more than a bug fix
- [x] Both languages carry the same texts
- [x] I signed the [CLA](../CLA.md), or I will when the bot asks

author: rogerhu12
body:
## 改动原因

按要求，将仓库当前全部 workflow 的 `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` 统一为 `true`，让同一 workflow、同一 ref 上的新运行取消过时运行。

当前默认分支共有三份 workflow。`integration-build.yml` 和 `lake-cache-test.yml` 已为 `true`；本 PR 修改唯一仍为 `false` 的 `lake-cache-release.yml`，保留原有按 workflow/ref 分组的 key。

## 缓存续跑

缓存发布流程原先在普通 step 中自行派发续跑，而部分构建产物在 job 的 post 步骤才保存。直接启用取消会让续跑抢在缓存保存之前取消原 run。

本 PR 将派发移到依赖 `release` 的 `continue-build` job，通过原构建步骤的 `timed_out` output 决定是否续跑。这样原日志上传及缓存保存尝试先完成，随后再派发。新 job 还核对分支当前 SHA：分支已前进时跳过旧提交的续跑，并在 workflow 被取消时停止。

原构建、发布、缓存、日志步骤和权限保持相同；`release` job id 保持不变，以保留现有缓存 lineage。正常流程仍最多自动续跑两次。自派发的新 run 可能将正在结束的辅助 job 标为 cancelled，但此前的 `release` job 已完成。

## 验证

- 逐一读取提交 `19a1e38` 的三份远端 workflow，确认全部为 `cancel-in-progress: true`。
- 三份 YAML 均成功解析；所有内嵌 shell 脚本通过 `bash -n`。
- 结构比较确认原构建、缓存、发布及日志步骤未被改写。
- 对实际续跑脚本使用模拟 GitHub CLI 检查：同一 head 的计数 0→1、1→2 均派发正确；分支前进时不派发。
- 本地检查没有实际触发缓存发布或等待完整编译超时；真实 GitHub Actions 运行状态由本 PR checks 单独记录。

本 PR 仅修改一份 workflow，不包含 Lean 源码变更。

body:
## Summary
Ticket #4509: on **Bench › Runs › run › QC review › Assessments**, Whole run appeared in the grid with the analytes and showed "Not assessed" like them, so it looked required. Accepting it did not clear "QC for this analyte is not assessed", the page explained none of this, and every analyte had to be assessed one at a time.

- **Summary line**, for example `3 of 3 analytes accepted · Whole run not assessed (optional)`. An analyte counts only while its acceptance cites exactly its current observations.
- **Whole run section** above the grid:
  - History and Assess QC buttons;
  - the note "Optional. Reject to block every analyte on this run. Accepting it doesn't accept the analytes.";
  - status "Not assessed (optional)", in a neutral tone;
  - its side panel and dialog are titled "QC for the whole run".
- **Bulk accept** (new `AcceptQcDialog.tsx`):
  - check column, Select all rows, then **Accept QC**;
  - one `assess_qc` call per selected analyte, citing that analyte's current observations shown and the same reason, so each one is recorded and audited separately;
  - the reason is optional, unless a selected analyte replaces an earlier acceptance whose evidence changed;
  - the calls run one after another. If the engine refuses one, the dialog names that analyte and shows the engine's message. Analytes already recorded stay recorded, and **Accept the rest** continues with the others. The selection clears on success.
- **Rows that can't be selected** have no check box and are skipped by Select all. The new "Accept with others" column says why:
  - No QC observations.
  - A changed QC row awaits a decision.
  - An open deviation applies.
  - Already accepted.
  - Rejected; this is final.
  - Assessed on its own. (preparation batches)
- Reject stays one scope at a time, through Assess QC.
- `DataGrid`: `GridSelection` takes an optional `isSelectable(id)`. A row that may not be selected shows no check mark, has no `aria-selected`, and is skipped by Space and Select all.
- Docs:
  - help `run-qc.json` describes the summary, Whole run, Accept with others, bulk Accept QC and a troubleshooting entry; `reviewedOn` is 2026-11-02;
  - `ui-standards.md` adds the selection rule for rows that may not be selected.

Design note: there is no engine change. Bulk accept reuses `assess_qc` (engine authorization, one audit event per assessment), so it is not all-or-nothing. A partial result is shown and can be resumed.

author: decksx
body:
Implements blocker **B1** of #158: opt-in scoped planning, so a live library that the watcher writes to doesn't void the whole canonical naming plan.

## What changed
- `canonical_plan.build_plan(..., scoped=False, scopes=None)`. In **strict mode (the default, unchanged)** any change under the root refuses the plan. I checked that strict plans are byte-identical to `origin/master`'s, digest included, on a 3-book fixture.
- `scoped=True` compares the before/after inventory **per series folder** (a folder directly under the root plus everything inside it, including its own directory row, because an arrival changes that folder's mtime). A folder that changed, appeared or disappeared is listed in `skipped_scopes` (`scope`, `path`, `reason`). Every rename, family, review hold and unchanged row inside it is dropped. All other folders keep their actions.
- `scopes=[...]` (CLI `--scope NAME`, repeatable, implies `--scoped`) plans only the named folders. Names must be exact spellings directly under the root. Other series folders are neither walked nor planned.
- **Root-level changes still refuse in scoped mode.** That covers a loose file, a history dir or a reparse point directly under the root. Root books are planned under root-wide authority (`--series-folder-root` or the root's number-style registry entry), and a root arrival belongs to no single series, so there's no scope to confine it to. With `--scope`, the root level is still watched but its loose books aren't planned.
- `skipped_scopes` and `planning_scope` are top-level keys, so `plan_digest` seals them. The executor's five `counts` don't change, and `diagnostics.skipped_scopes` gives the number. The CLI exits 1 when any folder was skipped.
- Apply (`canonical_apply/executor.py`) is untouched.
- Docs: `docs/canonical_naming_plan.md` (protocol) and `docs/engineering_decisions.md` (decision).

## Tests
I added 17 tests to `tests/test_canonical_plan.py`: one-folder mutation keeps the others' renames, holds dropped from a skipped folder, a nested change, a folder appearing, strict mode still refusing, strict docs carrying no new keys, root-level arrivals refusing (3 kinds), named scopes ignoring other folders, scope-name validation (5 cases), the digest sealing `skipped_scopes`, and CLI exit codes.

I mutation-tested 8 guards, and each mutation failed at least one named test: per-scope comparison disabled (5 tests fail), series dir row counted as root level (5), root-level check removed (3), dropping disabled (2), strict comparison removed (2), unnamed folders walked (1), loose root books planned under `--scope` (1), appeared folder not reported (1).

## For review
- Should root-level changes refuse even when `--scope` names only series folders? I chose refuse (conservative), but it puts back some brittleness if anything writes loose files at the root.
- A review hold inside a skipped folder is dropped rather than carried. The folder must be replanned anyway.
- Collision checks run before dropping. I argue in a code comment that this is safe (sibling destinations, quarantine paths unique per family).

David hasn't opted in to scoped mode. Nothing here touches the live library.
